The album's title refers to its sound, the deep, low-end frequencies that drive it, and songs like 'Check the Rhime', 'Buggin' Out', 'Scenario', with its legendary guest verse from Busta Rhymes, and the title track, which features a guest appearance from the jazz bassist Ron Carter, became classics. The album was a landmark of the Native Tongues movement, hip-hop's most intelligent and positive wing, and it remains one of the most influential records in the genre, the sound of hip-hop at its most musical and its most wise.

name: The Chronic
teaser: Dr. Dre 1992 — the album that invented G-funk and made the West Coast the center of hip-hop. Recorded at Death Row Studios with a young Snoop Doggy Dogg writing most of the lyrics. Dre used a live band to replay Parliament-Funkadelic samples, creating a sun-drenched, low-rider sound that dominated the 90s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Nuthin' but a G Thang' — the synthesizer whine was played on a Minimoog by Dre himself. Then 'Let Me Ride' — the chorus samples a Parliament track at half-speed. Dre's secret was the low-end: he mixed the bass frequencies higher than anyone else at the time, making the album literally shake car speakers.

synopsis: The Chronic (1992) is the album that invented G-funk and made the West Coast the center of the hip-hop universe, a record of slow, bass-heavy beats and languid synth melodies that sounded like nothing else in rap. Dr. Dre had left N.W.A. after a bitter dispute, and The Chronic, named after a particularly potent strain of marijuana, was his declaration of independence, recorded at his new Death Row Records with a young Snoop Doggy Dogg, whose laid-back, melodic flow was the perfect counterpoint to Dre's meticulous production. 'Nuthin' but a 'G' Thang', a duet with Snoop built on a Leon Haywood sample, became one of the biggest rap hits of all time, and the album is full of similar gems: 'Dre Day', 'Let Me Ride', 'Fuck wit Dre Day' and the ominous 'Lil Ghetto Boy'. The album sold millions, turned Death Row into the most powerful label in hip-hop and made Dre, a decade after he started with N.W.A., the most influential producer in the genre.

name: Doggystyle
teaser: Snoop Doggy Dogg 1993 — the fastest-selling debut album in hip-hop history at the time. Recorded while Snoop was on trial for murder (he was acquitted). Dr. Dre's production is G-funk at its silkiest. The album was recorded almost entirely at night because the studio's daytime clients were intimidated by Death Row's reputation.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Gin and Juice' — Snoop wrote the chorus in 10 minutes. The laid-back delivery was not an act; Snoop recorded most of his vocals while high, and Dre liked the looseness. Then 'Murder Was the Case' — Snoop narrates his own fictional death, which became eerily prescient given his legal situation at the time.

tracks.title: Ain't No Fun (If the Homies Can't Have None)

synopsis: Doggystyle (1993) is the debut album that made Snoop Doggy Dogg the most famous rapper in the world, a record of such effortless charisma that it sounded like Snoop was barely trying. Produced entirely by Dr. Dre, who built the album's beats from funk samples and gave Snoop the perfect setting for his unique flow, Doggystyle is full of the slow, luxurious grooves of G-funk at its peak. Snoop's delivery was unlike anything hip-hop had heard, a relaxed, melodic mumble that could switch to a sharp bark in a second, and his lyrics, full of humor, menace and an almost supernatural cool, made songs like 'Gin and Juice', 'What's My Name?', 'Doggy Dogg World' and 'Murder Was the Case' instant classics. The album was recorded while Snoop was facing a murder trial, which only added to his mystique, and it debuted at number one, the fastest-selling debut in hip-hop history at the time. It remains one of the defining albums of the West Coast era and the high-water mark of Dre and Snoop's partnership.

name: All Eyez on Me
teaser: 2Pac 1996 — the first double album in hip-hop history. Recorded in just 2 weeks after Suge Knight bailed Pac out of prison. Pac was living at the studio, writing and recording 3-4 songs a day. The album documents his transformation from political poet to thug icon in real time. He was dead 7 months after its release.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'California Love' — Dr. Dre produced it; the talkbox hook is Roger Troutman of Zapp. Then 'Ambitionz Az a Ridah' — Pac recorded it at 4 AM on his first night out of prison. The album's 27 tracks capture a man who knew he was running out of time and was determined to say everything.

tracks.title: Wonda Why They Call U Bytch

synopsis: All Eyez on Me (1996) is the double album where Tupac Shakur, newly signed to Death Row Records after Suge Knight bailed him out of prison, made the most extravagant statement of his career, and it remains the biggest-selling hip-hop double album ever released. Pac recorded the 25 songs in just two weeks, working at a furious pace with Dr. Dre, Johnny J and the rest of the Death Row production team, and the album captures him at his most confident and contradictory: 'California Love', with Dre, became one of the defining anthems of the West Coast, 'How Do U Want It' and '2 of Amerikaz Most Wanted' are full of swagger, while 'Life Goes On' and 'I Ain't Mad at Cha' show the reflective, vulnerable side of a man who knew his life was short. The album went to number one and sold millions, and it turned Tupac into the biggest star in hip-hop, a status he would hold until his murder later that year. It stands as the ultimate document of his Death Row era.

name: Me Against the World
teaser: 2Pac 1995 — released while Pac was in prison serving a sentence for sexual assault. It debuted at #1, making him the first artist to have a #1 album while incarcerated. The album's introspection and vulnerability set it apart from the gangsta rap dominating the charts.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dear Mama' — a tribute to his mother Afeni Shakur, a Black Panther who was pregnant with Pac while defending herself in court. Then 'So Many Tears' — Pac wrote it on his 23rd birthday after being shot 5 times in a robbery attempt. The album reads like a suicide note from someone who survived.

synopsis: Me Against the World (1995) is Tupac Shakur's most introspective album, recorded while he was in prison and facing a possible sentence of years, and it captures him at his most vulnerable and most defiant. Pac was serving time for sexual assault when the album was released, and it debuted at number one, making him the first artist to top the chart while incarcerated. The album is full of the fear and paranoia of a man who had recently been shot five times and was now watching his life fall apart: 'Dear Mama', a tribute to his mother, became his most beloved song, 'So Many Tears' and 'Temptations' show his tenderness, and 'Me Against the World' and 'Fuck the World' capture his fury. The album was hailed by critics as his most mature work, and it won the Soul Train award for best rap album. It is the sound of an artist at a crossroads, and it remains one of the most honest and moving records in hip-hop history.

name: AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted
teaser: Ice Cube 1990 — his solo debut after leaving N.W.A. over a financial dispute. Recorded in New York with Public Enemy's production team The Bomb Squad, creating a West Coast/East Coast fusion that shouldn't have worked but became iconic. Cube was 21 and angrier than any rapper had ever been on record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Cube narrates America from the perspective of its most wanted citizen. Then 'The Nigga Ya Love to Hate' — the chorus sarcastically thanks the listener for their voyeurism. Cube wrote the whole album in 3 weeks and recorded it in 6.

tracks.title: The Nigga Ya Love to Hate
Once Upon a Time in the Projects
I'm Only Out for One Thang
Get Off My Dick and Tell Yo Bitch to Come Here

synopsis: AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted (1990) is the solo debut that proved Ice Cube was the most gifted lyricist in rap, a furious, brilliant record that he made after walking out of N.W.A. over money. Cube left the group at the height of their fame, and his debut, recorded in New York with Public Enemy's production team, the Bomb Squad, was a declaration of war: over their dense, chaotic, sample-heavy beats, Cube delivered the most politically charged rhymes of his career, full of rage at racism, police brutality and the failures of America. 'The Nigga Ya Love to Hate' opens the album with a defiant statement, 'AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted' and 'Who's the Mack' show his storytelling gifts, and the skits, featuring Cube's friend Yo-Yo, add a layer of dark satire. The album was a massive success and is now regarded as one of the greatest political rap records ever made, the moment Cube established himself as a solo star of equal stature to his former group.

name: Straight Outta Compton
teaser: N.W.A. 1988 — the album that put gangsta rap on the map and got the FBI to send a warning letter to the record label. Recorded for $12,000 in a small Torrance studio. The group's lyrics about police brutality, drug dealing, and life in Compton were so controversial that radio stations refused to play them and they still went platinum.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Fuck tha Police' — the song that prompted the FBI letter. Dr. Dre built the beat from a single drum loop and a siren sound. Then 'Express Yourself' — a track Dre produced as a counterpoint, sampling Charles Wright. The album's impact went beyond music: it forced America to confront what police were doing in Black neighborhoods.

synopsis: Straight Outta Compton (1988) is the album that put gangsta rap on the map and terrified America, a record so raw and confrontational that the FBI sent a warning letter to the group's label. N.W.A, five young men from Compton and the surrounding Los Angeles area, were the first group to rap about life in the inner city with no filter: violence, police brutality, drugs and rage, delivered with a fury that had never been heard on record. The title track is a declaration of war, 'Fuck tha Police' became an anthem that got the group banned from venues and investigated by the FBI, and 'Gangsta Gangsta' and 'Straight Outta Compton' showed the storytelling gifts of Ice Cube, who wrote most of the lyrics, while Eazy-E's high, menacing voice and Dr. Dre's pioneering production completed the sound. The album sold millions despite being banned from many radio stations, and it changed hip-hop forever, turning the West Coast into the genre's new center and making N.W.A the most controversial and influential group in rap history.

name: It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back
teaser: Public Enemy 1988 — the album that turned hip-hop into a revolutionary force. The Bomb Squad's production was unlike anything before: layers of sirens, speeches, funk samples, and noise compressed into a sonic assault. Chuck D called rap 'the Black CNN.' The album made the case.

exploreAction.targetName: It Takes a Nation of Millions (1988) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Bring the Noise' — the opening siren is a recording from an actual police car. Then 'Rebel Without a Pause' — the squealing horn sample was pitched up so high it sounds like a fire alarm. Chuck D's baritone was a deliberate contrast to the high-pitched production, anchoring the chaos.

tracks.title: Terminator X to the Edge of Panic
Caught, Can We Get a Witness?
Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos
Party for Your Right to Fight

synopsis: It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back (1988) is the album that turned hip-hop into a revolutionary force, a record of such density and fury that it sounded like the end of the world and the beginning of a new one at the same time. Public Enemy, led by the charismatic Chuck D, whose booming voice was once called 'the greatest voice in hip-hop', and the provocation of Flavor Flav, were backed by the Bomb Squad, a production collective who built their beats from dozens of overlapping samples, sirens, noise and fragments of speeches, creating a sound that was as political as the lyrics. 'Bring the Noise', 'Don't Believe the Hype', 'Rebel Without a Pause' and 'Night of the Living Baseheads' are relentless attacks on racism, the media and the American establishment, and the album's title is a direct rebuke to the idea that black people needed anyone's permission. It is now regarded as one of the most important albums ever made, the record that proved hip-hop could be the most powerful political music of its time.

name: Fear of a Black Planet
teaser: Public Enemy 1990 — recorded during the controversy over Professor Griff's antisemitic remarks, which nearly destroyed the band. The album's denser, darker production reflected the internal chaos. 'Fight the Power' had premiered in Spike Lee's Do the Right Thing a year earlier and became an anthem.

exploreAction.targetName: Fear of a Black Planet (1990) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Fight the Power' — the song references Elvis, John Wayne, and the entire white power structure in under 5 minutes. Then '911 Is a Joke' — Flavor Flav's solo track about ambulance response times in Black neighborhoods. The Bomb Squad reportedly used 150 different samples across the album.

tracks.title: Contract on the World Love Jam
Meet the G That Killed Me
Can't Do Nuttin' for Ya Man
Leave This Off Your Fuckin' Charts
Final Count of the Collision Between Us and the Damned

synopsis: Fear of a Black Planet (1990) is the album where Public Enemy, at the peak of their powers and in the middle of a crisis that nearly destroyed them, made their most ambitious and prescient record. The band recorded the album during the controversy over Professor Griff's antisemitic remarks, which led to Griff's departure and left the group fighting for survival, but the music that emerged is a sprawling, brilliant exploration of race, culture and the fear that black self-determination inspired in white America. The Bomb Squad's production reached its most extreme: layers of samples, noise and found sound create a dense, almost overwhelming soundscape. 'Fight the Power', originally made for Spike Lee's Do the Right Thing, became one of the most iconic protest songs ever recorded, and 'Welcome to the Terrordome', '911 Is a Joke' and 'Brothers Gonna Work It Out' are furious, brilliant statements. The album was a huge hit and is now regarded as Public Enemy's masterpiece, the sound of hip-hop at its most militant and its most musical.

name: Paid in Full
teaser: Eric B. & Rakim 1987 — the album that changed how rappers rapped. Before Rakim, hip-hop flow was relatively simple; after Rakim, internal rhyme schemes, multi-syllabic patterns, and relaxed delivery became the standard. Eric B.'s production was built from James Brown samples slowed to a crawl.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Ain't No Joke' — Rakim's opening verse contains 16 bars with 14 internal rhymes. Then 'Eric B. Is President' — recorded in one take in Marley Marl's living room. Rakim was 18. The album cost $5,000 to make and became the blueprint for every rapper who followed.

tracks.title: Eric B. Is on the Cut

synopsis: Paid in Full (1987) is the album that changed how rappers rapped, the record where Rakim transformed hip-hop from a music of simple rhymes into an art form of complex, flowing poetry. Before Rakim, most rappers followed the beat with simple, rhythmic couplets; Rakim, a Muslim convert who had studied the Five Percent Nation's teachings, brought a new level of intelligence and technique to the mic, rapping in long, complex sentences with an internal rhyme scheme that had never been heard. Over the sparse, minimal beats of DJ Eric B., songs like 'I Ain't No Joke', 'Paid in Full', 'Eric B. Is President' and 'My Melody' showed off his revolutionary style, and the title track's remix, built on a sample of an Israeli funk song, became one of the most famous beats in hip-hop history. The album is now universally regarded as one of the most important records ever made, the moment hip-hop lyricism grew up, and its influence on every rapper who followed is immeasurable.

name: The Infamous
teaser: Mobb Deep 1995 — recorded in a Queensbridge apartment by two teenagers, Havoc and Prodigy. Havoc, who had never produced before, taught himself on an Akai MPC and a cheap keyboard. The album's sound — minor-key piano loops, sparse drums, whispered threats — defined East Coast hardcore hip-hop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Shook Ones, Pt. II' — Havoc found the piano sample on a Herbie Hancock record and slowed it down until it sounded haunted. Then 'Survival of the Fittest' — the beat is two notes and a snare. Prodigy was 19 when he wrote 'I'm only 19 but my mind is old.' The album made Queensbridge the most famous housing project in music.

tracks.title: The Start of Your Ending (41st Side)
Eye for a Eye (Your Beef Is Mines)

synopsis: The Infamous (1995) is the album where two teenagers from the Queensbridge housing projects made the definitive record of New York street rap, a dark, haunting masterpiece of beat poetry. Havoc and Prodigy were just out of their teens when they recorded it, and Havoc, who had never produced before, taught himself by making beats in a Queensbridge apartment, building a sound of eerie piano loops, sparse drums and bass that felt like a threat. Prodigy's voice, cold and precise, delivered some of the most memorable verses in hip-hop history, and songs like 'Shook Ones Part II', with its immortal opening line, 'Survival of the Fittest', 'Temperature's Rising' and 'Eye for a Eye' painted a portrait of project life that was both terrifying and hypnotic. The album was a critical and commercial success, and it established Mobb Deep as the most respected duo in New York hip-hop, the sound of the streets made into art. It remains a touchstone of East Coast rap, as influential as any record of its era.

name: Reasonable Doubt
teaser: Jay-Z 1996 — recorded when no label would sign him, so he started Roc-A-Fella Records with Damon Dash and Kareem Burke. The album was recorded in various New York studios, often at night after other sessions had finished. Jay-Z was 26, a former drug dealer who'd decided rap was his way out.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Can't Knock the Hustle' — Mary J. Blige sings the hook. Jay-Z's flow is so relaxed it sounds like a conversation. Then 'Dead Presidents II' — the Nas sample was a deliberate homage to Illmatic. The album's mafioso-rap style — all Italian suits, Cuban cigars, and champagne — created Jay-Z's persona as hip-hop's CEO.

synopsis: Reasonable Doubt (1996) is the debut album of Jay-Z, and it remains one of the greatest first records in hip-hop history, a portrait of a drug dealer's life in Brooklyn made with stunning sophistication. Jay-Z had been unable to get a record deal, so he started his own label, Roc-A-Fella Records, with Damon Dash and Kareem Burke, and recorded the album with some of the era's best producers, including DJ Premier, Ski and the Trackmasters. The result is a record of luxurious, soulful beats and Jay-Z's effortless, intricate flow, full of the details of his life selling drugs in the Marcy Houses: 'Dead Presidents' and 'Can't Knock the Hustle' are about ambition and survival, 'Regrets' and 'Feelin' It' show his reflective side, and the album's masterpiece, 'D'Evils', is a chilling portrait of the moral compromises of the game. The album sold respectably but was not an immediate smash, yet its reputation has grown steadily, and it is now regarded as one of the finest hip-hop albums ever made, the sound of a genius arriving fully formed.

name: The Blueprint
teaser: Jay-Z 2001 — released on September 11, 2001. Despite the attacks, it debuted at #1 and sold 427,000 copies in its first week. Recorded in just 30 days with producers Kanye West (then unknown) and Just Blaze. Jay-Z was simultaneously preparing for a trial on assault charges; he recorded vocals during court recesses.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Izzo (H.O.T.A.)' — Kanye built the beat from a Jackson 5 sample pitched up to chipmunk speed, a technique that would define 2000s hip-hop. Then 'Song Cry' — Jay-Z's vulnerability here was unprecedented for a rapper at his commercial peak. The album's soul-sample production was Kanye's audition for his own career.

tracks.title: Heart of the City (Ain't No Love)

synopsis: The Blueprint (2001) is the album where Jay-Z, already the biggest rapper in the world, proved he was also the best, a record of effortless mastery that has become one of the most influential hip-hop albums of the 2000s. Jay-Z recorded the album in just two weeks, working with producers Kanye West, who was then an unknown, and Just Blaze, who built the album's soulful, sample-heavy sound, and the speed of the sessions gave the record a relaxed, confident energy. 'Takeover' is a vicious diss track aimed at his rivals Nas and Prodigy, 'Izzo (H.O.V.A.)' became an anthem built on a Jackson 5 sample, 'Song Cry' and 'Never Change' are tender, reflective songs, and 'Renegade', a duet with Eminem, is one of the greatest posse cuts ever recorded. The album was released on September 11, 2001, and still debuted at number one, selling over 400,000 copies in its first week. It is now regarded as Jay-Z's masterpiece and one of the most important rap albums of its decade.

name: Aquemini
teaser: OutKast 1998 — the album where André 3000 and Big Boi proved the South could make art as ambitious as anyone. The title combines their zodiac signs (Aquarius and Gemini). Recorded in Atlanta with live instrumentation when most hip-hop relied on samples. George Clinton called it 'the funkiest album I've heard in years.'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Rosa Parks' — the song's energy is so infectious that Rosa Parks herself sued for using her name (the case was eventually settled). Then 'SpottieOttieDopaliscious' — a 7-minute track with no chorus, just horn stabs and spoken-word verses about Atlanta nightlife. André's verse about the club shooting is one of the most vivid stories in hip-hop.

synopsis: Aquemini (1998) is the album where OutKast proved that the South could make hip-hop as ambitious and artful as anything from New York or Los Angeles, and it remains their most revered record. The album's title combines their astrological signs, Aquarius and Gemini, and the record is a meditation on duality, change and staying true to yourself: André 3000 and Big Boi were growing apart artistically, and the album captures both their visions, from André's increasingly experimental, psychedelic leanings to Big Boi's funk and soul foundations. 'Rosa Parks', built around a horn sample, became a hit and led to a lawsuit from the civil rights icon, 'Da Art of Storytellin' (Part 1)' shows their narrative gifts, 'SpottieOttieDopaliscious' is a masterpiece of Southern funk, and 'Liberation', featuring a stunning guest verse from CeeLo Green, is a gorgeous, reflective closer. The album was a huge success and won a Grammy, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest hip-hop albums ever made, the moment the South claimed its place at the center of the genre.

name: Stankonia
teaser: OutKast 2000 — recorded in a converted Atlanta warehouse they called Stankonia Studios. The album broke every rule: funk, psychedelia, drum & bass, gospel, and Prince-influenced freak-outs. 'B.O.B.' was recorded at 165 BPM when most rap was under 100. It became their commercial breakthrough.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'B.O.B. (Bombs Over Baghdad)' — the drum programming by André 3000 was inspired by UK jungle music. The guitar solo was played through a wah-wah pedal by a session guitarist who'd never heard OutKast before. Then 'Ms. Jackson' — André wrote it as an apology to Erykah Badu's mother after their breakup.

synopsis: Stankonia (2000) is the album where OutKast, already the South's greatest rap group, blew up the genre's boundaries completely, a record of such wild invention that it sounded like nothing else in music. The title comes from the name of the converted Atlanta warehouse the duo turned into their studio, and the album has the feeling of a laboratory of sound: André 3000 and Big Boi rapped, sang, shouted and whispered over production that mixed funk, psychedelia, rock, gospel and pure noise into something entirely new. 'Ms. Jackson', a song about apologizing to an ex's mother, became their biggest hit and a global phenomenon, 'B.O.B.', with its breakneck tempo and gospel choir, is regarded as one of the most exciting songs ever recorded, and 'So Fresh, So Clean' and 'Humble Mumble' showed the duo's range. The album went to number one, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest and most influential hip-hop albums of all time, the sound of two geniuses at the peak of their powers refusing to be contained.

name: Ridin' Dirty
teaser: UGK 1996 — Bun B and Pimp C's masterpiece. Pimp C, incarcerated at the time of release, produced most of the album from prison using a cassette recorder to sketch ideas. The album's title refers to driving with illegal substances or weapons, a constant reality for the Port Arthur, Texas duo.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'One Day' — Pimp C's production layers a Gospel sample over a slow-rolling bassline. Then 'Murder' — Bun B's verse is a masterclass in Southern storytelling, delivered with the authority of someone who saw everything he describes. The album defined Southern hip-hop's independent spirit before the mainstream caught on.

synopsis: Ridin' Dirty (1996) is the masterpiece of UGK, the duo of Pimp C and Bun B who had spent years as the kings of the underground Southern rap scene, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest hip-hop albums ever made. Pimp C, who produced most of the record, built a sound of slow, luxurious funk, full of live instrumentation and thick bass lines that sounded like nothing coming out of New York or Los Angeles at the time, while Bun B's steady, commanding flow provided the perfect counterweight to Pimp C's more laid-back, melodic style. The album was recorded while Pimp C was in prison, using a small keyboard he was allowed in his cell, and songs like 'One Day', 'Murder', 'Diamonds & Wood' and the iconic 'Ridin' Dirty' painted a portrait of life in Port Arthur, Texas, that was both gritty and soulful. The album sold slowly at first but its reputation grew enormously, and it is now heard as the record that laid the foundation for the entire Southern rap era that followed.

name: The Diary
teaser: Scarface 1994 — the Geto Boys member's third solo album, recorded during a period of severe depression. Scarface's storytelling — about poverty, mental illness, and survival — brought literary depth to gangsta rap. The album's production by N.O. Joe and Mike Dean created the template for Southern hip-hop's dark, soulful sound.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Seen a Man Die' — Scarface narrates a death from three perspectives: the victim, the shooter, and God. Then 'Mind Playin' Tricks on Me' (originally a Geto Boys track) — Scarface's verse about paranoia and hallucinations is based on his own experiences with depression. He later checked himself into a psychiatric hospital.

synopsis: The Diary (1994) is the album where Scarface, already the most respected storyteller in Southern rap as a member of the Geto Boys, made his solo masterpiece, a dark, brooding record of stunning emotional power. Scarface recorded the album during a period of severe depression, and the record is full of that darkness: it is an album about death, despair, faith and survival, told with a literary precision that few rappers have ever matched. 'I Seen a Man Die' is one of the most chilling songs ever recorded, a detailed account of watching someone die that Scarface has said was inspired by his own experiences, while 'Hand of the Dead Body', a collaboration with Ice Cube, and the gospel-tinged 'Smile', which featured a posthumous verse from Tupac, showed his range. The album was a huge success, going platinum, and it is now regarded as a landmark of Southern hip-hop, the record that proved rappers from Texas could make art as profound as anything from the coasts.

name: Tha Carter III
teaser: Lil Wayne 2008 — recorded during what Wayne called his 'mixtape era', when he was releasing a new track almost daily. The album sold 1 million copies in its first week, the last hip-hop album to do so for nearly a decade. Wayne's wordplay — puns, metaphors, free association — rewired what rap lyrics could be.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'A Milli' — the beat is a single vocal sample repeated for 3 minutes. Wayne recorded his verse in 20 minutes without writing anything down. Then 'Lollipop' — the Auto-Tuned hook was Wayne's first experiment with singing, which would define the next decade of hip-hop. Static Major, who co-wrote the hook, died a week before the album's release.

synopsis: Tha Carter III (2008) is the album where Lil Wayne, already the most mixtape-obsessed rapper of his era, finally released the studio album that matched his legend, and it became one of the biggest-selling rap records of the decade. Wayne recorded the album during what he called his mixtape era, when he was releasing new songs almost daily and rapping circles around every competitor, and Tha Carter III captured that endless, improvisational brilliance. 'A Milli', built on a sparse, percussive beat, became one of the most imitated rap songs ever recorded, 'Lollipop' was a massive pop hit, '3 Peat' and 'Mr. Carter' showed his technical mastery, and 'Tie My Hands' and 'DontGetIt' revealed the reflective side beneath the bravado. The album sold over a million copies in its first week, making Wayne the biggest rapper in the world, and it won a Grammy for Best Rap Album. It stands as the definitive statement of his genius and one of the most influential hip-hop albums of the 2000s.

name: King
teaser: T.I. 2006 — the album that crowned him 'King of the South.' Recorded in Atlanta with a roster of producers including Just Blaze, Toomp, and Swizz Beatz. T.I.'s cocky, conversational flow — half-rapping, half-talking — bridged the gap between Southern trap and mainstream hip-hop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'What You Know' — the synth line was played by DJ Toomp on a Roland Juno-106. T.I.'s opening line 'Don't you know I got the key by me?' is delivered with the confidence of someone who doesn't need to raise his voice. Then 'Why You Wanna' — the song samples a Crystal Waters house track, proving Southern hip-hop could make dance records too.

synopsis: King (2006) is the album where T.I., who had spent years calling himself the King of the South, finally delivered a record worthy of the title, and it remains his masterpiece. Recorded in Atlanta with a who's who of producers, including Just Blaze, DJ Toomp and the Neptunes, the album is a grand, confident statement of dominance from an artist at the absolute peak of his powers. 'What You Know', with its hypnotic beat, became his signature song and one of the defining Southern rap anthems of the decade, 'Why You Wanna' and 'Live in the Sky', featuring a soaring chorus from Jamie Foxx, were huge hits, and 'King Back', 'Front Back' and the title track showed T.I.'s effortless charisma and technical skill. The album sold over half a million copies in its first week, and it is now regarded as one of the essential albums of the Southern rap golden age, the record that made good on every promise T.I. had ever made.

name: Let's Get It: Thug Motivation 101
teaser: Young Jeezy 2005 — the album that made trap music a national phenomenon. Recorded in Atlanta with Shawty Redd's minimalist production: 808 drums, church bells, and synth strings. Jeezy's ad-libs ('yeahhh', 'that's riiight') became as quotable as his verses.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Soul Survivor' — Akon sings the hook about surviving the streets. Jeezy's verse is a checklist of everything he overcame. Then 'Go Crazy' — the beat is an 808 kick and a single synth note. Jay-Z's guest verse was recorded in 15 minutes in a hotel room. The album's snowman logo became a cultural symbol.

tracks.title: Let's Get It / Sky's the Limit

synopsis: Let's Get It: Thug Motivation 101 (2005) is the album that introduced trap music to the mainstream and made Young Jeezy the voice of a new generation of Southern street rap. Jeezy had spent years as a mixtape legend in Atlanta, and his major-label debut, recorded with the producer Shawty Redd, whose minimalist, menacing beats defined the early trap sound, turned his hustler's gospel into a national phenomenon. The album is built on Jeezy's signature delivery, a low, raspy growl that sounds like he is telling secrets and threats at the same time, and its songs, from the anthemic 'Soul Survivor', featuring Akon, and 'Go Crazy' to the menacing 'Trap or Die' and the triumphant 'And Then What', are all variations on the same theme: the grind, the trap, the come-up. The album went double platinum and made Jeezy a star, and its influence on the next decade of hip-hop, from Gucci Mane to Future to every trap artist since, is incalculable.

name: The State vs. Radric Davis
teaser: Gucci Mane 2009 — his major-label debut, named after his ongoing legal case. Gucci's stream-of-consciousness delivery and unpredictable punchlines made him a cult hero. The album was recorded between jail stints. The cover is a literal mugshot.

exploreAction.targetName: The State vs. Radric Davis (2009) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Wasted' — featuring Plies, the chorus about getting drunk became a college anthem. Then 'Lemonade' — the beat sounds like a carnival ride breaking down. Gucci's influence on the next decade of hip-hop — from Migos to 21 Savage — is hard to overstate.

synopsis: The State vs. Radric Davis (2009) is Gucci Mane's major-label debut, the album where the most prolific and unpredictable figure in Southern rap finally got his shot at the mainstream, and it remains the definitive statement of his early genius. The album's title refers to Gucci's ongoing legal troubles, and the record is full of the tension between his enormous talent and his chaotic life: Gucci's delivery was stream-of-consciousness, loose and hypnotic, full of non-sequiturs and sudden flashes of brilliance, and his flow over the album's cold, minimalist trap beats was unlike anything else in hip-hop. 'Lemonade', 'Wasted', featuring Plies, and 'I Be Loving You' became hits, but the album's real power is in its smaller moments, where Gucci's unpredictable genius shines. The album was a commercial success and is now regarded as a landmark of the trap era, the record that proved Gucci Mane, for all his chaos, was one of the most important and influential rappers of his generation.

name: DS2 (Dirty Sprite 2)
teaser: Future 2015 — the album that perfected the sound of narcotic melancholy. Recorded with Metro Boomin, Southside, and Zaytoven in Atlanta. Future's Auto-Tuned voice, half-sung and half-cried, captured a specific kind of post-success emptiness. The album's influence is audible in almost every rap record made since.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Thought It Was a Drought' — Future mumbles the chorus through a fog of cough syrup, and somehow it's a hit. Then 'Where Ya At' — Drake's guest verse was recorded via email. The album's production is built almost entirely from 808s, hi-hats, and atmospheric synths — the definitive trap sound.

synopsis: DS2 (Dirty Sprite 2) (2015) is the album where Future perfected his signature sound of narcotic melancholy, a record of such druggy, exhausted beauty that it redefined what rap could sound like. The Atlanta rapper had spent years building toward this moment, and DS2, recorded with Metro Boomin, Southside and Zaytoven, distilled his genius into its purest form: slow, hypnotic beats, melodies that hover between singing and rapping, and lyrics about codeine, heartbreak and numbness delivered with a kind of beautiful detachment. 'Thought It Was a Drought' opens the album with one of the great opening lines in trap history, 'Where Ya At' and 'Stick Talk' are menacing classics, and 'I Serve the Base', 'Rich Sex' and the closing 'Codeine Crazy', a stunning seven-minute confession, show the range of his pain. The album was hailed as a masterpiece on release, and it is now regarded as the most influential rap album of its era, the record that taught a generation how to turn sadness into a sound.

name: Culture
teaser: Migos 2017 — the album that turned the triplet flow into a global phenomenon. Recorded in Atlanta and Los Angeles over a year. The trio — Quavo, Offset, and Takeoff — traded verses with a chemistry that felt telepathic. 'Bad and Boujee' became a meme, a #1 single, and the cultural moment when trap officially conquered pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Bad and Boujee' — Lil Uzi Vert's ad-libbed verse was recorded in 10 minutes. The 'raindrop, drop-top' opening couplet became one of the most-quoted lyrics of the decade. Then 'T-Shirt' — the triplet flow on the verses turns the English language into pure rhythm. Offset's verse on 'Deadz' was widely considered the best rap verse of 2017.

synopsis: Culture (2017) is the album that turned the Migos' triplet flow, the rapid-fire rhythmic pattern they had popularized on their mixtapes, into a global phenomenon, and it made the trio from suburban Atlanta the most influential group in hip-hop. Quavo, Offset and Takeoff had spent years perfecting their chemistry, and Culture, recorded in Atlanta and Los Angeles over the course of a year, captured them at the peak of their powers. 'Bad and Boujee', which had already become a viral sensation, made the album a number one hit, and songs like 'T-Shirt', 'Slippery', featuring Gucci Mane, and 'Call Casting' showed the trio's effortless cool and their gift for hooks. The album was hailed by critics as the moment trap music fully entered the mainstream, and its influence on the next wave of rap, from the triplet flow to the ad-libs to the production style, is incalculable. It remains the Migos' defining statement.

name: Astroworld
teaser: Travis Scott 2018 — named after the demolished Houston amusement park, an album-length nostalgia trip. Recorded over two years with dozens of producers. Scott's production philosophy — maximalist, atmospheric, deliberately disorienting — made the album feel like a theme park ride itself.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sicko Mode' — the song has three distinct beat switches, each produced by a different team. Drake's verse appears at a seemingly random moment. Then 'Stop Trying to Be God' — Stevie Wonder plays harmonica and James Blake sings the bridge. Scott's genius is making chaos feel like inevitability.

synopsis: Astroworld (2018) is Travis Scott's grandest statement, a psychedelic, maximalist album named after the Houston amusement park of his childhood that was demolished in 2005, and it turned him into one of the biggest stars in music. Scott recorded the album over two years with dozens of collaborators, building a sound that mixed trap drums with psychedelic rock textures, auto-tuned melodies and enormous, cinematic production. The album is designed to be an experience rather than a collection of songs, full of transitions, skits and sound effects that make it feel like a ride through an amusement park built inside Scott's head. 'Sicko Mode', a three-part epic that became his biggest hit, 'Stargazing', 'Butterfly Effect' and 'Stop Trying to Be God' showed his range, and guest appearances from Drake, Kid Cudi, Frank Ocean, the Weeknd and Stevie Wonder added to the record's sense of event. The album debuted at number one and is now regarded as one of the defining rap albums of the late 2010s.

name: Resurrection
teaser: Common 1994 — recorded when he was 22, still called Common Sense (he later dropped 'Sense' after a lawsuit from a reggae band). The album's production by No I.D. (then unknown, later Kanye's mentor) established the soul-sampling Chicago sound. Common's battle-rap skills and social consciousness made him the Midwest's answer to Nas.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Used to Love H.E.R.' — the 'her' in question is hip-hop itself, personified as a woman who's lost her way. The extended metaphor runs for the entire song. Then 'Resurrection' — the title track's opening bars are a direct response to Ice Cube dissing him. No I.D. built the beat from a single Ahmad Jamal piano loop.

tracks.title: In My Own World (Check the Method)

synopsis: Resurrection (1994) is the album where Common, then performing as Common Sense, established himself as one of the most thoughtful and skilled lyricists in hip-hop, a record of quiet brilliance made when he was just 22. Recorded in Chicago with his partner No I.D., who built the album's soulful, jazzy beats, Resurrection was a conscious reaction to the violent gangsta rap that dominated the era: Common rapped about love, family, black history and his own insecurities with a sincerity that felt revolutionary. 'I Used to Love H.E.R.', the album's centerpiece, is a brilliant extended metaphor in which hip-hop itself is portrayed as a woman who has been corrupted by the industry, and it became one of the most celebrated rap songs of the decade. The album also contains 'Resurrection', 'Nuthin' to Do' and the reflective 'Book of Life'. It is now regarded as a classic of conscious hip-hop, the record that put Chicago on the rap map and launched one of the most respected careers in the genre.

name: Black on Both Sides
teaser: Mos Def 1999 — a solo debut that ranges from Afrocentric poetry to jazz-inflected rap to straight-up rock. Recorded in New York with a live band on several tracks. Mos Def sang and played drums, bass, and keyboards himself. The album is a deliberate argument that hip-hop could be as musically sophisticated as any genre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Mathematics' — DJ Premier's beat is built from a single 2-bar loop. Mos Def packs references to statistics, history, and street mathematics into every verse. Then 'Umi Says' — the wordless chorus was improvised in the studio. Mos Def later said the album was his attempt to 'make hip-hop that my mother could listen to.'

synopsis: Black on Both Sides (1999) is the solo debut of Mos Def, and it announced him as one of the most gifted and versatile artists in hip-hop, a record that moves effortlessly between Afrocentric poetry, jazz-inflected rap, social commentary and even straight-up rock. Mos Def, born Dante Smith in Brooklyn, had already made his name as one half of Black Star with Talib Kweli, and his solo album expanded his range even further, showing off his skills as a rapper, singer and actor. 'Ms. Fat Booty', built on a gorgeous soul sample, became his signature song, 'Mathematics' is a brilliant lesson in the numbers behind American inequality, 'Umi Says' is a gorgeous, gospel-tinged plea for freedom, and 'Rock n Roll', with its funny, incisive history of the genre, showed his wit. The album was hailed as a masterpiece of conscious hip-hop, and it established Mos Def, later known as Yasiin Bey, as one of the most important voices of his generation.

name: Quality
teaser: Talib Kweli 2002 — the Brooklyn rapper's most fully realized solo album. Produced primarily by Kanye West (pre-fame) and Hi-Tek. Kweli's lyrical density — five-syllable internal rhymes packed into every bar — made the album a Rosetta Stone for aspiring MCs.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Get By' — Kanye's beat samples Nina Simone's 'Sinnerman' pitched to a frantic tempo. Kweli's three verses each describe different paths to survival: hustling, education, and faith. Then 'The Proud' — produced by Ayatollah, the song is a roll call of Black pride references woven into a love song.

synopsis: Quality (2002) is the album where Talib Kweli, already beloved by underground hip-hop fans as half of Black Star, proved he could carry a solo record, and it remains the most fully realized album of his career. Recorded primarily with Kanye West, then a rising producer still a few years from fame, and Hi-Tek, his longtime collaborator, Quality is a showcase for Kweli's extraordinary lyrical gifts: his dense, multisyllabic rhymes about race, love, faith and politics are among the most technically impressive in hip-hop. 'Get By', produced by Kanye, became a massive underground hit, a gorgeous meditation on survival and hope built on a Nina Simone sample, and songs like 'Waitin' for the DJ', 'Push Thru' and 'Put It in the Air' showed his range. The album was a critical triumph, and it is now regarded as a classic of the conscious hip-hop movement, the record that proved Kweli was one of the greatest pure lyricists of his generation.

name: Let's Get Free
teaser: Dead prez 2000 — recorded in New York by stic.man and M-1, two activists who met at a Black Panther event. The album's revolutionary politics — veganism, Black nationalism, anti-capitalism — were so far left of mainstream hip-hop that they made Public Enemy sound moderate. The production, dark and minimal, matched the urgency.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hip-Hop' — the chorus is a single repeated phrase: 'It's bigger than hip-hop.' The song became an activist anthem. Then 'Mind Sex' — a love song about intellectual and emotional intimacy as political resistance. The album was produced by Lord Jamar of Brand Nubian, who gave it a gritty East Coast foundation.

synopsis: Let's Get Free (2000) is the debut album of dead prez, the duo of stic.man and M-1, and it remains one of the most politically radical records in hip-hop history, an album that treated rap not as entertainment but as a weapon. The two activists met at a Black Panther event and shared a vision of hip-hop as a tool for revolution, and their debut, recorded in New York, is full of that fire: 'Hip Hop', the album's centerpiece, declares that hip-hop should be a way of life, not a product, and attacks the industry for turning the culture into commerce, while 'It's Bigger Than Hip Hop' and 'I'm a African' connect the struggle to a larger history of oppression. The album is built on spare, funky beats and the duo's urgent, chanting delivery, and its politics are uncompromising. It became a landmark of underground hip-hop, and its influence can be heard in everything from the Occupy movement to the conscious rap revival of the following decades.

name: Boy in da Corner
teaser: Dizzee Rascal 2003 — the album that invented grime. Recorded in a bedroom in Bow, East London, on a PlayStation and a cheap PC. Dizzee was 18, processing knife crime, teenage pregnancy, and inner-city London life into something entirely new. The beats — built from video game sounds, ringtones, and distorted bass — sounded like nothing else.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Luv U' — the beat is a single distorted bass note and a snare. The call-and-response between Dizzee and the female vocalist narrates a teenage pregnancy argument. Then 'Fix Up, Look Sharp' — the Billy Squier sample was Dizzee's idea after hearing it in a Nike commercial. The album won the Mercury Prize; Dizzee was 19.

synopsis: Boy in da Corner (2003) is the album that invented grime, and it remains the genre's greatest record, a stunning debut made by a teenager in a bedroom in East London. Dizzee Rascal, born Dylan Mills, was just 18 when he recorded the album, using a PlayStation and a cheap PC to build beats that sounded like the future of British music: frantic, skeletal, full of static and bass, drawing on garage, jungle and the sounds of the East London streets. His lyrics were just as extraordinary, moving from boastful fury to vulnerable confession in a single song, and tracks like 'I Luv U', with its raw depiction of a toxic relationship, 'Fix Up, Look Sharp', built on a sample of an old Billy Squier rock song, and the eerie 'Jus a Rascal' showed a talent that seemed to arrive fully formed. The album won the Mercury Prize, the first grime record to do so, and it is now regarded as one of the most important British albums ever made.

name: Treddin' on Thin Ice
teaser: Wiley 2004 — the godfather of grime's debut album. Recorded in Bow, East London, the same neighborhood as Dizzee Rascal. Wiley's production — sparse, cold, built from video game soundtracks and pirate radio static — created the sonic template for grime. The album was released on XL Recordings after a bidding war.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Wot Do U Call It?' — Wiley addresses the question everyone was asking: what is this music? The answer: 'It's not garage, it's not hip-hop, it's just... this.' Then 'Eskimo' — the instrumental track that became the foundation of grime production. Wiley's Eskibeat sound — cold synth lines over 140 BPM drums — influenced Skepta, Stormzy, and an entire scene.

synopsis: Treddin' on Thin Ice (2004) is the debut album of Wiley, the man widely credited as the godfather of grime, and it captures the genre at the moment of its birth. Wiley, born Richard Cowie in East London, had been at the center of the garage and grime scenes for years, both as a solo artist and as a member of the legendary Roll Deep crew, and his debut album, recorded in the same neighborhood as Dizzee Rascal's breakthrough, is a document of a new sound being invented in real time. The album is built on Wiley's production, which mixed the dark, skeletal energy of grime with moments of unexpected melody, and his delivery, which could switch from a rapid-fire flow to a singsong melody in a second. 'Wot Do U Call It?' is a playful history of the genre itself, while tracks like 'Pick Your Self Up' and the eerie 'Ice Rink' show his range. The album is raw and uneven, but its influence is enormous, and it is now regarded as an essential document of grime's founding era.

name: Konnichiwa
teaser: Skepta 2016 — the album that brought grime to the global mainstream. Recorded in London and Tokyo. Skepta produced most of the album himself on a laptop. The album won the Mercury Prize. Drake and Kanye West both publicly championed it, but Skepta refused to dilute the sound for American audiences.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Shutdown' — the opening line 'truss me daddy' became a catchphrase. The video, shot on a London estate, was banned from some platforms for being 'too provocative.' Then 'Man (Gang)' — the beat is a single bass note and an air horn. Skepta's delivery makes 'I said real gangsters don't flex' sound like a universal truth.

synopsis: Konnichiwa (2016) is the album that brought grime, the British genre that had spent years as an underground phenomenon, to the global mainstream, and it made Skepta, already a legend in the scene, an international star. Skepta produced most of the album himself, returning to the raw, minimal sound of grime's early years after experimenting with American trap, and the result is a record that sounds like a declaration of war on the music industry's expectations. 'Shutdown' became an anthem, a defiant response to the police shutting down grime events, 'Man' and 'Crime Riddim' showed his technical mastery, and 'Konnichiwa', recorded partly in Tokyo, gave the album its global perspective. The album won the Mercury Prize, the first grime album to do so, and it is now regarded as the record that proved grime could conquer the world without compromising its identity, the sound of a genre and its king arriving at the same time.

name: Gang Signs & Prayer
teaser: Stormzy 2017 — the first grime album to debut at #1 on the UK charts. Recorded over two years in London. Stormzy's range — from gospel-choir choruses to hard-edged grime bars — showed that British rap could be commercially massive without compromise. The album cover is Stormzy in a suit, holding a Bible.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Blinded by Your Grace, Pt. 2' — the song is a gospel hymn featuring a full choir, and it became a festival singalong. Then 'Big for Your Boots' — a straight grime track produced by Sir Spyro. The album's title is literal: it alternates between street narratives and spiritual searching.

synopsis: Gang Signs & Prayer (2017) is the debut album of Stormzy, and it made him the biggest star British grime had ever produced, the first grime album to debut at number one on the UK charts. Stormzy had spent years as the most popular freestyler in Britain, and his debut, recorded over two years in London, showed the full range of his talent: the album moves from gospel-tinged anthems to raw grime workouts to confessional ballads, all held together by Stormzy's commanding presence and his gift for writing hooks that the whole country could sing. 'Big for Your Boots' became his signature anthem, 'Cold' and 'Shut Up' showed his grime roots, 'Blinded by Your Grace, Pt. 2', a gospel duet with MNEK, was a massive hit, and 'Cigarettes & Cush' revealed a more vulnerable side. The album was hailed as a landmark for British music, and it established Stormzy as not just a rapper but a cultural figure, the voice of a generation of young Britons.

name: Original Pirate Material
teaser: Mike Skinner (The Streets) 2002 — the album that proved British rap didn't need to sound American. Recorded in a Brixton bedroom on a laptop. Skinner narrated the mundane details of British working-class life — kebabs, minicabs, PlayStation, cheap lager — over garage-influenced beats. His Birmingham accent was so thick Americans needed subtitles.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Has It Come to This?' — Skinner's deadpan delivery of observations about pub life, Nokia phones, and Channel 4. Then 'Weak Become Heroes' — a 5-minute story about a night out at a club, taking ecstasy, and the sunrise after. The piano sample is from a 1970s library music record Skinner found at a car boot sale.

synopsis: Original Pirate Material (2002) is the debut album of Mike Skinner, performing as the Streets, and it proved that British rap did not need to imitate America to be brilliant, a record that sounded like nothing else in music. Skinner recorded the album in a bedroom in Brixton on a laptop, and his music was a strange, wonderful hybrid: two-step garage beats, video game bleeps and piano lines, all underneath Skinner's spoken-sung delivery, which sounded less like rapping and more like a mate telling you stories down the pub. The album is a portrait of ordinary British life, full of nights out, kebab shops, fights and the mundane details of being young and broke: 'Weak Become Heroes' is a beautiful account of the rave scene, 'Let's Push Things Forward' is a statement of intent, and 'Has It Come to This?' is a melancholy anthem for the disaffected. The album was a massive critical and commercial success, and it is now regarded as one of the most important British albums of the decade.

name: Psychodrama
teaser: Dave 2019 — the album that won the Mercury Prize and made British rap feel like literature. Recorded over a year in London and Los Angeles. Dave plays piano on nearly every track. The album is structured as a therapy session, which is literal: Dave's brother is serving a life sentence, and the album processes that trauma.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Black' — Dave lists the experience of being Black in Britain in a single verse that runs for 3 minutes without a chorus. Then 'Lesley' — an 11-minute narrative about an abusive relationship, told from the perspective of a concerned friend. The album's therapy-session framing gives it a structure no other rap album has attempted.

synopsis: Psychodrama (2019) is the album where Dave, still only 20 years old, made British rap feel like literature, a stunningly ambitious concept record that won the Mercury Prize and established him as the most important young voice in British music. The album is structured as a therapy session, with spoken-word interludes from a therapist guiding the listener through Dave's mind, and its songs deal with mental health, grief, racism, knife crime and the legacy of his older brother's imprisonment with a maturity that belied his age. 'Streatham' is a devastating account of his brother's trial, 'Black' is a brilliant history lesson about the treatment of black people in Britain, 'Location' became his biggest hit, and 'Psycho', featuring the rapper Headie One, is a chilling duet about the trauma of growing up in London. The album won the Mercury Prize and was hailed as a masterpiece, and it is now regarded as the record that proved British rap could make art as profound as any music in the world.

name: Finally Rich
teaser: Chief Keef 2012 — the album that invented drill music. Recorded in Chicago when Keef was 16 and already a legend on the South Side. The production by Young Chop — sparse, menacing, built from 808s and horror-movie synths — created a new sonic language. Keef's delivery, which sounded half-asleep, was actually a refusal to perform emotion.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Don't Like' — the song that got Kanye West's attention, leading to a remix that introduced drill to the world. Then 'Love Sosa' — the call-and-response chorus was recorded at 3 AM after Keef had been up for two days. The album's influence on modern hip-hop — from the ad-libs to the production style — is impossible to overstate.

synopsis: Finally Rich (2012) is the album that introduced drill music to the world, a record of such cold, menacing minimalism that it changed the sound of hip-hop forever. Chief Keef was just 16 when he recorded it, already a legend on the South Side of Chicago, and his music, built on the spare, skeletal beats of producers like Young Chop, sounded like nothing else in rap: slow, dark, almost hypnotic, with Keef's deadpan, auto-tuned delivery floating above it. 'I Don't Like', which had already become a viral phenomenon and been remixed by Kanye West, 'Love Sosa', 'Hate Bein' Sober' and 'Faneto' became anthems of the drill movement, and the album's portrait of Chicago's violence and poverty was both terrifying and mesmerizing. Keef was still a teenager when the album came out, and his legal troubles and unpredictable behavior made him as famous for his chaos as for his music. Finally Rich is now regarded as one of the most influential rap albums of the 2010s, the sound of a new genre being born.

name: Shoot for the Stars, Aim for the Moon
teaser: Pop Smoke 2020 — released posthumously after the 20-year-old was murdered in a home invasion. The album bridges Brooklyn drill with mainstream hip-hop. 50 Cent executive-produced it. Pop Smoke's gravelly voice — he sounded at least a decade older than he was — made drill radio-friendly without losing its edge.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dior' — the song that became a global anthem after Pop Smoke's death. The 808 pattern was created by producer 808Melo in 15 minutes. Then 'What You Know Bout Love' — a pop-rap love song that samples a UK garage track, proving drill could be tender. The album debuted at #1; Pop Smoke never lived to see it.

synopsis: Shoot for the Stars, Aim for the Moon (2020) is the posthumous debut album of Pop Smoke, the Brooklyn rapper who was murdered at the age of 20 just as he was becoming one of the biggest stars in hip-hop, and it stands as a monument to his extraordinary promise. Pop Smoke had spent a year revolutionizing New York rap with his deep, menacing voice and his fusion of Brooklyn drill with the sounds of his father's Jamaican heritage, and his debut album, completed after his death by his producers and collaborators, captured him at the peak of his powers. 'Dior' had already become an anthem, 'The Woo', featuring 50 Cent, and 'For the Night', featuring Lil Baby and DaBaby, were massive hits, and the album, with its guest appearances from Quavo, Future, Roddy Ricch and many more, was designed to show the range of a star who never got to see his own success. It debuted at number one and is now regarded as a landmark of the Brooklyn drill era, a heartbreaking reminder of what was lost.

name: The Marshall Mathers LP
teaser: Eminem 2000 — the fastest-selling rap album in history at release (1.76 million first week). Recorded in a Detroit studio while Em was fighting a custody battle and a lawsuit from his mother. Dr. Dre produced the singles; Eminem himself produced much of the rest. The album made Slim Shady a household name and got the FTC involved over lyrical content.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Stan' — the Dido sample was lifted from her debut album, which Dre heard playing in a car at a stoplight. The song's epistolary structure (letters back and forth) was Eminem's idea. Then 'The Way I Am' — recorded in one take at 3 AM after Em's label demanded a radio single. The Marilyn Manson remix of 'The Way I Am' was recorded at 4 AM after Manson showed up unannounced at the studio.

synopsis: The Marshall Mathers LP (2000) is the album where Eminem, already the most controversial figure in music, became the biggest star in the world, and it remains the fastest-selling rap album in history. Eminem recorded the album at the height of his fame, when every word he said was being dissected by the media, and the record is his response: a furious, hilarious, deeply personal document that veers between savage attacks on his critics and heartbreaking confessions about his family. 'The Real Slim Shady' and 'The Way I Am' are brilliant statements of defiance, 'Stan', a stunning story-song about an obsessed fan told through letters, is regarded as one of the greatest rap songs ever recorded, and 'Kim' and 'Marshall Mathers' are terrifyingly raw. The album sold 1.76 million copies in its first week in the US, a record that stood for years, and it is now regarded as Eminem's masterpiece, the sound of a genius at war with the world and himself.

name: The Slim Shady LP
teaser: Eminem 1999 — his major-label debut, recorded after Dr. Dre heard Em's demo at Interscope and said 'Find him. I don't care where he is.' Dre produced three tracks in one night at Em's Detroit trailer. The album's cartoon violence and Slim Shady alter-ego introduced the world to a white rapper who didn't sound like any white rapper before him.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'My Name Is' — the sample is Labi Siffre's 'I Got The…', used with the condition that Siffre's openly gay status wasn't mocked. Dre built the beat in 20 minutes. Then '97 Bonnie & Clyde' — Em recorded himself doing both his voice and his baby daughter's voice, telling a bedtime story about killing her mother. He recorded her parts by pitching his voice up.

synopsis: The Slim Shady LP (1999) is the major-label debut that turned Eminem from an underground battle rapper into the most talked-about artist in music, a record of such outrageous humor and technical brilliance that it changed hip-hop forever. Dr. Dre, who had heard Eminem's demo and immediately signed him, produced much of the album, giving Eminem's chaotic alter ego Slim Shady the perfect backdrop: a cartoonish, horror-movie world of dark beats and twisted samples. 'My Name Is', with its unforgettable hook, became a massive hit, 'Guilty Conscience' is a brilliant duet with Dre about moral choices, 'Role Model' and 'Still Don't Give a Fuck' are full of Slim Shady's anarchic energy, and 'Rock Bottom' and 'If I Had' reveal the poverty and frustration beneath the jokes. The album won the Grammy for Best Rap Album and made Eminem a superstar, and it is now regarded as one of the most important hip-hop albums of its era, the record that introduced one of the greatest rappers of all time.

name: The Eminem Show
teaser: Eminem 2002 — the album where he became the biggest artist in the world. Self-produced almost entirely (Dre stepped back). Recorded during a period when Em was fighting for custody of his daughter Hailie and facing felony gun charges. The album is structured like a TV show with Em as both host and prisoner of his own fame.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sing for the Moment' — the Aerosmith sample is from 'Dream On', and Steven Tyler recorded new vocals for the chorus. The third verse addresses the Columbine shooting. Then 'Cleaning Out My Closet' — Em's vocal is a single continuous take, no punch-ins. The apologies to his mother are embedded in accusations.

synopsis: The Eminem Show (2002) is the album where Eminem, now the biggest artist in the world, turned his attention from shock value to something more substantial, and it stands as his most mature and ambitious record. Unlike his earlier albums, which were largely produced by Dr. Dre, Eminem produced most of The Eminem Show himself, and the album has a darker, more personal feel: it was recorded during his legal battles and the fallout from his divorce, and songs like 'Cleanin' Out My Closet', a devastating account of his childhood, and 'Hailie's Song', a tender tribute to his daughter, show a new level of emotional honesty. 'Without Me' became his biggest hit, a hilarious attack on the music industry, 'Sing for the Moment' brilliantly samples Aerosmith, and 'Till I Collapse' and 'Business' show his technical mastery. The album debuted at number one and sold over a million copies in its first week, and it is now regarded as the peak of Eminem's commercial and artistic power.

name: The College Dropout
teaser: Kanye West 2004 — the producer's debut that changed hip-hop's sound from hard-edged to soulful. Kanye recorded much of it while his jaw was wired shut after a near-fatal car crash. The chipmunk-soul samples were a deliberate rebellion against gangsta rap's dominance. The album opens with a skit asking for a degree, then immediately rejects the premise.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Jesus Walks' — Kanye wrote it as a gospel-rap song at a time when labels said Christian rap didn't sell. The opening chain-gang chant is actually a sample of a 1950s prison recording. Then 'Through the Wire' — recorded while Kanye's jaw was literally wired shut; you can hear his slurred delivery. He shot the music video two weeks after the crash.

synopsis: The College Dropout (2004) is the debut album of Kanye West, and it changed the sound of hip-hop, replacing the hard-edged gangsta rap that dominated the charts with a soulful, witty, deeply personal style that made Kanye the most important artist in the genre. Kanye had spent years as one of hip-hop's most successful producers, but labels refused to let him rap, and his debut, recorded partly while recovering from a near-fatal car accident that left his jaw wired shut, is full of that frustration and determination. 'Jesus Walks', a gospel-tinged meditation on faith, became one of the most unlikely hits in rap history, 'Through the Wire', recorded with his jaw still wired shut, is a stunning statement of survival, 'All Falls Down' and 'Slow Jamz' are brilliant, soulful songs, and 'Never Let Me Down' and 'Family Business' reveal his tenderness. The album won the Grammy for Best Rap Album and is now regarded as one of the greatest debuts in hip-hop history.

name: Late Registration
teaser: Kanye West 2005 — the album where he spent $2 million on production and brought in film composer Jon Brion to arrange live strings. The result was baroque hip-hop: 20-piece orchestras over sample-based beats. The album was recorded partly in the same studio where Michael Jackson recorded 'Thriller'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Gone' — the song has five verses by five different MCs, each one trying to out-rap the last. Cam'ron's verse was written in the studio in 15 minutes while Kanye laughed at every line. Then 'Roses' — Kanye wrote it about his grandmother in the hospital; the strings swell exactly at the point where he admits he was wrong.

synopsis: Late Registration (2005) is the album where Kanye West, determined to prove his debut was no fluke, made a record of even greater ambition, and it confirmed him as the most important artist in hip-hop. Kanye spent a reported $2 million on production and brought in film composer Jon Brion to arrange live strings and orchestral textures, giving the album a cinematic grandeur that no rap record had ever attempted. 'Gold Digger', built around a Jamie Foxx vocal, became one of the biggest hits of the decade, 'Touch the Sky' and 'Heard 'Em Say' are gorgeous, uplifting songs, and 'Diamonds from Sierra Leone' and 'Crack Music' show Kanye's willingness to tackle serious subjects, while 'Gone' and 'Roses' are among the most personal songs he has ever written. The album debuted at number one and won the Grammy for Best Rap Album, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest hip-hop albums of the 2000s, the record where Kanye's ambition and his talent finally met.

name: Graduation
teaser: Kanye West 2007 — the third in the dropout trilogy, recorded partially in a Hawaiian mansion. Kanye deliberately moved away from soul samples toward stadium-sized electronic production inspired by Daft Punk and U2. The album outsold 50 Cent's 'Curtis' in the famous same-day release battle, marking the moment when hip-hop shifted from gangsta to art-school.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Stronger' — the Daft Punk sample was cleared only after Kanye flew to Paris and played them the track in person. Then 'Flashing Lights' — the synth arrangement by DJ Toomp was inspired by 80s cop-show themes. Kanye insisted the album cover be designed by Takashi Murakami; the cartoon bear became the era's visual shorthand.

synopsis: Graduation (2007) is the final album in Kanye West's dropout trilogy, and it is the record where he made the leap from hip-hop star to global pop phenomenon, deliberately moving away from the soul samples that had defined his earlier work toward a colder, more electronic sound inspired by the bands he had been listening to, from Daft Punk to U2. The album was recorded partly in a Hawaiian mansion and it sounds like it: huge, anthemic, stadium-sized, full of synthesizers and grand gestures. 'Stronger', built on a Daft Punk sample, became one of the defining songs of the decade, 'Good Life' and 'Can't Tell Me Nothing' were massive hits, and 'Flashing Lights' and 'Homecoming' showed his range. The album's release was scheduled for the same day as 50 Cent's Curtis, and the chart battle between them became one of the most talked-about events in hip-hop history; Graduation won easily, selling over a million copies in its first week, and it is now regarded as the record that ended the gangsta rap era and made Kanye the biggest star in music.

name: Take Care
teaser: Drake 2011 — the album that merged hip-hop with late-night R&B confessions and made vulnerability a commercial strategy. Recorded mostly in Toronto with Noah '40' Shebib, who recorded Drake's vocals in a room literally filled with candles. The album's emotional palette — loneliness, fame, regret, longing — defined the sound of 2010s pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Marvins Room' — Drake recorded the vocal lying on a studio floor at 4 AM, drunk-dialing his ex on the song itself. The phone call at the end is real. Then 'The Motto' — the 'YOLO' hook was added as a last-minute bonus track and became a global catchphrase. The Weeknd contributed four songs but insisted on no feature credit.

synopsis: Take Care (2011) is the album where Drake merged hip-hop with late-night R&B confession and made vulnerability a commercial strategy, and it turned him from a promising star into the defining artist of his generation. Recorded mostly in Toronto with his producer Noah '40' Shebib, whose signature sound, slow, atmospheric, full of haunting melodies and muffled drums, gave the album its nocturnal feel, Take Care is a record about the pleasures and pains of fame, love and loneliness. 'Headlines' and 'Marvin's Room' became anthems of sad-boy hip-hop, 'The Motto', with its celebration of YOLO, was a cultural phenomenon, 'Take Care', featuring Rihanna, and 'Crew Love' showed his gift for collaboration, and 'Doing It Wrong' and 'Look What You've Done' revealed his tenderness. The album won the Grammy for Best Rap Album and is now regarded as Drake's masterpiece, the record that proved rappers could be sensitive and still rule the world.

name: Nothing Was the Same
teaser: Drake 2013 — the album where he stopped apologizing for being both a rapper and a singer. 40's production is aqueous and claustrophobic, trapping Drake's confessions in reverb. The album cover, a painting by Kadir Nelson of young Drake and adult Drake facing each other, is about not recognizing your past self.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Tuscan Leather' — a six-minute track with no hook, three beat switches, and a sample from Whitney Houston that repeats 'I have nothing.' Then 'Hold On, We're Going Home' — originally written for a female singer; Drake kept it and turned it into a new-wave-reggae hybrid that his rap fans initially rejected.

synopsis: Nothing Was the Same (2013) is the album where Drake stopped apologizing for being both a rapper and a singer, and it is the record where his vision of hip-hop, moody, melodic, deeply personal, fully came into focus. Recorded with his longtime collaborator 40, whose production here is even more atmospheric and claustrophobic than on Take Care, the album is a portrait of an artist at the height of his powers and the peak of his paranoia. 'Started from the Bottom' became an anthem of self-made success, 'Hold On, We're Going Home', a gorgeous slice of 80s-influenced R&B, was his biggest hit, 'Wu-Tang Forever' pays homage to his influences, and 'Too Much' and 'Pound Cake', featuring Jay-Z, show his ambition. The album debuted at number one and is now regarded as one of Drake's finest records, the sound of an artist who had finally figured out exactly who he was and what he wanted to say.

name: If You're Reading This It's Too Late
teaser: Drake 2015 — released as a surprise mixtape/album to fulfill his contractual obligation to Cash Money Records. Recorded mostly in a Toronto forest cabin. The album is leaner than 'Take Care': fewer features, darker production, more paranoia. The cover is a handwritten note in Drake's own handwriting, as if left on a kitchen table.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Energy' — the beat is built from a single vocal sample slowed to a growl. Then 'Jungle' — a song about a friendship ending, with the line 'these days, I'm letting God handle all things above me.' Drake's pen game here is sharper than anything he'd written before: every bar is a tweet waiting to happen.

synopsis: If You're Reading This It's Too Late (2015) is the album that Drake released as a surprise in the middle of the night, ostensibly a mixtape to fulfill his contractual obligations to Cash Money Records, and it turned out to be one of the most influential rap releases of the decade. Recorded mostly in a Toronto hotel room with his producer 40 and the young producer Boi-1da, the album has a darker, more paranoid sound than Drake's earlier work, full of muted beats and references to his legal battles with his label. 'Energy', 'Know Yourself' and 'Legend' became anthems, '6 Man' and 'Company' showed his versatility, and the album's overall mood, cold, bitter, defiant, felt like a message from an artist who was done playing nice. The album was certified platinum within a week of its surprise release, and its influence on the wave of dark, atmospheric rap that followed, from the sound of the late 2010s, is enormous.

name: Madvillainy
teaser: MF DOOM and Madlib 2004 — two reclusive geniuses who never met in person during the album's creation. Madlib sent DOOM beat CDs from Los Angeles; DOOM recorded verses in a Brazilian hotel room and mailed them back. The album is 22 tracks in 46 minutes, each one a self-contained universe of comic-book references and internal rhyme schemes.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Accordion' — Madlib's beat is just an accordion sample, a bass note, and a snare. DOOM packs 18 different rhyme sounds into 16 bars. Then 'All Caps' — Madlib sampled the same note from a 1970s cartoon theme and built an entire song around it. DOOM's insistence on all-caps spelling wasn't stylistic: it was a legal tactic against impostors.

synopsis: Madvillainy (2004) is the album where two of hip-hop's most reclusive geniuses, the rapper MF DOOM and the producer Madlib, joined forces to create one of the most beloved and influential underground records of all time, and the fact that they barely communicated during its creation only adds to the legend. Madlib sent DOOM beat CDs from Los Angeles, and DOOM, in New York, rapped over them and sent them back, and the two never even met in person during the making of the album. The result is a record of astonishing density and invention: Madlib's beats, built from obscure jazz and soul samples chopped into strange, beautiful patterns, and DOOM's flow, full of wordplay, cartoon references and a kind of weary genius, are a perfect match. 'Accordion', 'All Caps', 'Rhinestone Cowboy' and 'Figaro' are regarded as masterpieces of underground hip-hop, and the album has only grown in reputation, becoming one of the most influential rap records of the 2000s.

name: Operation: Doomsday
teaser: MF DOOM 1999 — his debut under the metal-masked villain persona, recorded after his brother and KMD partner Subroc was killed by a car. DOOM retreated from music for five years, sleeping on park benches, then re-emerged in a mask based on Doctor Doom. The album was recorded in a basement on borrowed equipment, DOOM producing, rapping, and engineering everything.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Doomsday' — the beat is a looped Sade sample pitched to sound underwater. DOOM's rhyme scheme is so dense that deciphering one verse takes multiple listens. Then 'Rhymes Like Dimes' — DOOM recorded his verses in a single night while wearing the mask. The skit about a failed meeting is based on an actual interaction with a confused A&R.

synopsis: Operation: Doomsday (1999) is the album where MF DOOM, a rapper who had seemed destined for mainstream success before tragedy derailed his career, reinvented himself as the masked supervillain who would become one of the most revered figures in underground hip-hop. DOOM had been known as Zev Love X, a member of the group KMD, until his brother and partner Subroc was killed by a car in 1993, and the group's label dropped them, seemingly ending his career. Six years later, DOOM returned wearing a metal mask inspired by the Fantastic Four villain, and Operation: Doomsday is his origin story: a record built on obscure soul samples, cartoon sound effects and DOOM's new persona, a supervillain rapper who rhymes about his own genius with deadpan humor. 'Doomsday', 'Rhymes Like Dimes' and 'Hey!' are underground classics, and the album established the persona and the sound that DOOM would refine for the rest of his career, making him one of the most influential and beloved figures in underground hip-hop.

name: Mm..Food
teaser: MF DOOM 2004 — a concept album where every track is named after food, but every metaphor is about the music industry consuming artists. DOOM produced all but two tracks himself, sampling cartoons, cooking shows, and obscure jazz records. The cover is a parody of an old soul-food restaurant menu.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Rapp Snitch Knishes' — the beat is three notes from a David Matthews funk record, and DOOM and guest Mr. Fantastik trade verses about not cooperating with investigations.
