Then 'Beef Rapp' — the opening track explains the album's thesis: 'Beef is not what you want, it's what you covet.' DOOM's food metaphors are a meal plan for surviving the industry.

synopsis: Mm..Food (2004) is the concept album where MF DOOM, already a legend of underground hip-hop after his persona-defining Operation: Doomsday and the masterpiece Madvillainy, turned every track into a meditation on food, and made one of the most inventive and beloved records of his career. Each song is named after food, from 'Beef Rapp' to 'One Beer' to 'Kon Karne', and the metaphors are consistent: the music industry consumes artists the way people consume food, and DOOM, the supervillain chef, is serving up the truth. The album is full of DOOM's trademark wordplay, humor and dizzying rhyme schemes, and its production, a mix of his own beats and obscure samples, matches the playful concept. Songs like 'One Beer', 'Hoe Cakes' and 'Rapp Snitch Knishes', featuring Mr. Fantastik, have become underground anthems. Mm..Food is now regarded as one of DOOM's finest albums, a record that rewards endless listening.

name: Flower Boy
teaser: Tyler, the Creator 2017 — the album where the enfant terrible of Odd Future grew up. Recorded in Tyler's own studio with production entirely self-handled. The album's cover — Tyler in a field of sunflowers surrounded by bees — was painted by artist Eric White. The lyrics cycle through loneliness, sexuality, and the fear of being forgotten.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'See You Again' — Kali Uchis sings a chorus that Tyler wrote in 10 minutes while driving. Then 'Garden Shed' — the verse where Tyler comes out is embedded so deeply in the mix that most listeners missed it on first play. The chords on the album are jazz-influenced sevenths and ninths; Tyler taught himself piano specifically for this project.

synopsis: Flower Boy (2017) is the album where Tyler, the Creator, the provocateur who had built his career on shock humor and outrage as the leader of Odd Future, grew up in public, and it turned out he had been hiding one of the most tender and gifted songwriters in hip-hop all along. The album, recorded in Tyler's own studio with a huge cast of collaborators, including Frank Ocean, A$AP Rocky, Estelle and Rex Orange County, is a lush, gorgeous record full of soul, funk and psychedelic pop, and its lyrics are startlingly honest: Tyler raps and sings about loneliness, insecurity and, most strikingly, his romantic feelings for men, which he had never addressed directly before. 'See You Again' and 'Boredom' became hits, '911 / Mr. Lonely' is a stunning meditation on isolation, and 'Garden Shed' and 'Glitter' show his new emotional range. The album was hailed as a masterpiece and nominated for the Grammy for Best Rap Album, and it marked the beginning of Tyler's transformation into one of the most respected artists of his generation.

name: IGOR
teaser: Tyler, the Creator 2019 — a breakup album told through a character named Igor, a mad-scientist archetype with a low hairline and a broken heart. Tyler sings more than he raps, processing his voice through a chorus of pitched-up and slowed-down selves. The album won Best Rap Album at the Grammys; Tyler called the category a 'backhanded compliment'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'EARFQUAKE' — the beat was originally written for Justin Bieber, who didn't respond. Playboi Carti's verse was recorded in one take while Carti was on FaceTime with his girlfriend. Then 'A BOY IS A GUN' — the Kanye-style sample manipulation is Tyler's own; the song's central metaphor is from Toni Morrison's 'Song of Solomon'.

tracks.title: Exactly What You Run from You End Up Chasing

synopsis: IGOR (2019) is the album where Tyler, the Creator completed his transformation from provocative oddball to visionary artist, a stunningly ambitious concept record about a doomed romance that won the Grammy for Best Rap Album. The album tells the story of Igor, a mad-scientist archetype, who falls in love with someone who does not love him back, and Tyler sings almost the entire record, abandoning rapping for a vulnerable, cracked falsetto that he pushes to its limits. The music is extraordinary, a fusion of funk, soul, gospel, R&B and psychedelic pop, built on layers of synthesizers, drum machines and vocal harmonies, with guest appearances from Kanye West, Lil Uzi Vert, Solange and Pharrell woven into the fabric of the songs. 'Earfquake' became his biggest hit, 'New Magic Wand' and 'A Boy Is a Gun' are masterpieces of heartbreak, and the album's closing trilogy, 'Gone, Gone / Thank You' and 'Are We Still Friends?', is devastating. IGOR is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 2010s, the record where Tyler fully realized his vision.

name: Call Me If You Get Lost
teaser: Tyler, the Creator 2021 — framed as a mixtape hosted by DJ Drama, reviving the Gangsta Grillz format. Tyler raps over beats that sample everything from Ghanaian highlife to Japanese city pop. The album's alter-ego, Sir Baudelaire, is a globetrotting aristocrat who travels by boat because he's been banned from flying (Tyler is afraid of flying).

exploreAction.targetName: Call Me If You Get Lost (2021) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'WUSYANAME' — the sample is from H-Town's 90s R&B, layered with a bassline Tyler played himself. Then 'SWEET / I THOUGHT YOU WANTED TO DANCE' — the song switches genres three times in 10 minutes: rap, then reggae, then bossa nova. Tyler rapped the opening verse in one breath to prove a point about his technical ability.

tracks.title: Sweet / I Thought You Wanted to Dance

synopsis: Call Me If You Get Lost (2021) is the album where Tyler, the Creator, at the absolute peak of his powers, made a love letter to the mixtape era and won his first Grammy for Best Rap Album. Framed as a gangsta-grillz mixtape hosted by DJ Drama, the album is a showcase for Tyler's versatility: he raps with a new confidence and density over beats that range from boom-bap to jazz to soul, and the record is full of the luxurious travelogue imagery, yacht-rock samples and spoken interludes that had become his signature. 'Lumberjack' and 'Wusyaname' open the album with swagger, 'Sweet / I Thought You Wanted to Dance' is a stunning nine-minute soul odyssey, and 'Massa', 'Manifesto' and the closing 'Wilshire', a solo track about a complicated relationship, show his storytelling gifts. The album was hailed as one of his best, and it confirmed Tyler as one of the most complete artists in hip-hop, a genius who could do absolutely anything.

name: Atrocity Exhibition
teaser: Danny Brown 2016 — named after a JG Ballard novel about psychological fragmentation. Recorded while Brown was drinking heavily and barely sleeping. The beats — by Paul White, Evian Christ, and others — sound like industrial machinery breaking down. Brown's voice is a weapon: a nasal shriek that makes every bar feel like it's hitting a different frequency.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Ain't It Funny' — the beat is a distorted brass sample that sounds like a marching band falling down stairs. Brown raps about using drugs to cope with depression. Then 'Really Doe' — Kendrick, Ab-Soul, and Earl Sweatshirt all deliver career-best guest verses. The album's title track samples Joy Division's 'Atrocity Exhibition' with permission from the band.

tracks.title: Tell Me What I Don't Know

synopsis: Atrocity Exhibition (2016) is the album where Danny Brown, already one of the most distinctive voices in rap, made a record of such fractured brilliance that it sounded like a nervous breakdown set to music, and it is now regarded as his masterpiece. The album's title comes from the JG Ballard novel about psychological fragmentation, and the record lives up to it: Brown, struggling with depression and drinking heavily at the time, raps with a new rawness over beats, from the producers including Black Milk and the Alchemist, that lurch between jazz, punk, industrial and experimental hip-hop. 'When It Rain' is a stunning, paranoid epic, 'Ain't It Funny' is built on a jazz sample that Brown makes sound terrifying, 'Pneumonia' and 'Really Doe', featuring Kendrick Lamar, Ab-Soul and Earl Sweatshirt, are showcases for his extraordinary technical skill, and 'Hell for It' is a desperate scream. The album was hailed as a masterpiece of experimental hip-hop, the sound of an artist pushing himself to the edge and bringing back something extraordinary.

name: XXX
teaser: Danny Brown 2011 — a mixtape/album recorded in Detroit basements after Brown turned 30 and decided his window was closing. The beats are split between classic boom-bap and experimental electronic. Brown's voice alternates between a high-pitched yelp (the party persona) and a low baritone (the depressed reality). The album turns 30 into a crisis more than a celebration.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to '30' — the opening track where Brown confronts his age over a beat that samples This Heat's '24 Track Loop'. Then 'DNA' — produced by Frank Dukes, who built the beat from a 0.3-second sample of an obscure 70s jazz record. Brown's verse about his family's genetic predisposition to addiction hits differently knowing he wrote it sober.

synopsis: XXX (2011) is the album that made Danny Brown, a Detroit rapper who had been grinding for over a decade, into one of the most exciting and unconventional voices in hip-hop. Brown was about to turn thirty when he recorded it, convinced his window was closing, and the album has the energy of a man with nothing to lose: over beats from a team of underground producers, Brown raps with a voice that veers between a high-pitched, manic shriek and a low, gravelly growl, and his lyrics move between filthy humor and devastating honesty. 'Blunt After Blunt' and 'I Will' show his party side, but 'Radio Song', 'Monopoly' and 'Scrap or Die' are portraits of poverty, addiction and desperation that are as real as anything in hip-hop. The album, released as a free mixtape, became an underground phenomenon and made Brown a cult star. It remains the record where one of rap's strangest and most gifted voices announced himself.

name: Run the Jewels 2
teaser: Killer Mike and El-P 2014 — the second collaboration between the Atlanta rapper and the Brooklyn producer, released as a free download. Recorded in 3 intense months in El-P's Brooklyn apartment. The album was so politically charged that it accidentally predicted the Ferguson protests; tracks were literally playing at demonstrations within weeks of release.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Close Your Eyes (And Count to Fuck)' — Zack de la Rocha's guest verse was his first recording in 6 years. He tracked it at 1 AM after driving to El-P's apartment from a Rage Against the Machine rehearsal. Then 'Angel Duster' — the closing track where Mike and El literally pass the mic back and forth, each trying to out-rap the other in real time.

tracks.title: Close Your Eyes (And Count to Fuck)

synopsis: Run the Jewels 2 (2014) is the album where Killer Mike and El-P, already a formidable duo after their first collaboration, became one of the greatest partnerships in hip-hop history, a record of such ferocious energy and righteous anger that it felt like a shot of adrenaline to the genre. The pair, an Atlanta rapper and a Brooklyn producer who had spent years in the underground, recorded the album quickly, feeding off each other's energy, and the result is a record of astonishing chemistry: Mike's booming, streetwise delivery and El-P's dense, science-fiction production, full of pounding drums and eerie synths, are a perfect match. 'Close Your Eyes (And Count to Fuck)', featuring Zack de la Rocha, is a furious statement, 'Oh My Darling Don't Cry' and 'Blockbuster Night Part 1' are relentless attacks, and 'Early' and 'Lie, Cheat, Steal' show the duo's range. The album was released as a free download, and it made Run the Jewels one of the most beloved and important acts in hip-hop.

name: Run the Jewels 3
teaser: Killer Mike and El-P 2016 — released on Christmas Day as a gift to fans, just weeks after Trump's election. The album's paranoia and anger feel like a document of a specific historical moment. El-P's production is denser than ever; Mike's verses are sermons disguised as battle raps. The album features Danny Brown, Tunde Adebimpe from TV on the Radio, and Kamasi Washington on sax.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Legend Has It' — the 'RTJ' chant was recorded by Mike and El screaming into the same microphone until their voices clipped. The beat is built from a single piano sample pitched into three different keys. Then 'Thursday in the Danger Room' — a eulogy for a friend who died of cancer, with El-P rapping about watching someone 'wither into a whisper.'

tracks.title: A Report to the Shareholders" / "Kill Your Masters

synopsis: Run the Jewels 3 (2016) is the album that Killer Mike and El-P released on Christmas Day 2016, just weeks after the election of Donald Trump, and its fury and paranoia captured the mood of a country in crisis. The album is the darkest of the Run the Jewels series, its production, by El-P, full of ominous synths and pounding, industrial drums, and its lyrics full of anger at racism, police violence and the rising tide of fascism. 'Talk to Me' and 'Legend Has It' are among the hardest tracks the duo has made, 'Kill Your Masters' and 'Panther Like a Panther' are full of revolutionary energy, and '2100', featuring Boots, and 'Thursday in the Danger Room', a stunningly vulnerable song about losing friends, show the duo's range. The album was hailed as their best yet, and its timing, arriving in the anxious weeks after the election, made it feel like a necessary document of the moment, the sound of two artists channelling their generation's fear and rage.

name: RTJ4
teaser: Run the Jewels 2020 — released two days early amid global protests after George Floyd's murder. The album opens with Killer Mike's pre-recorded speech at a Bernie Sanders rally. El-P's production incorporates punk, industrial, and trap. The feature list includes Mavis Staples, Josh Homme, 2 Chainz, and Pharrell. It was the first RTJ album to debut at #1 on any chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'walking in the snow' — Killer Mike's verse about police brutality was recorded in 2019, but its description of a man being choked to death was eerily predictive. Then 'JU$T' — Pharrell's hook 'look at all these slave masters posing on your dollar' was originally written for a different project. Zack de la Rocha's verse was recorded in one 20-minute session.

tracks.title: A Few Words for the Firing Squad (Radiation)

synopsis: RTJ4 (2020) is the album that Run the Jewels released two days early in June 2020, as protests over the murder of George Floyd swept the world, and it turned out to be exactly the record the moment needed. Killer Mike, who had spent years speaking about police violence, delivered the album's opening track, a stunning spoken-word monologue about racism and revolution recorded before the protests began, and the rest of the record lives up to its fury: 'Ooh LA LA' and 'Out of Sight' are as hard as anything the duo has made, 'Walking in the Snow' is a devastating account of police brutality, and 'JU$T', featuring Pharrell, attacks capitalism itself. The album also contains some of the duo's most personal music: 'A Few Words for the Firing Squad' is a stark, spoken reflection on mortality and legacy. Released amid a global uprising, RTJ4 was immediately hailed as the definitive protest record of 2020, the sound of two artists perfectly in sync with their moment.

name: Landlord
teaser: Giggs 2016 — the Peckham rapper's major-label breakthrough after a decade of mixtapes and a prison sentence. Giggs's voice is a glacier-slow baritone that makes every bar feel physically heavy. The album features Drake, Stormzy, and 2 Chainz, but Giggs remains the undeniable gravitational center: his delivery redefined what UK rap could sound like.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Whippin Excursion' — the beat is 808-heavy trap, but Giggs's flow sits behind it, not on it. Then 'Lock Doh' — the song that introduced Giggs to American audiences when Drake remixed it. Giggs recorded the original in his home studio; the vocal was so raw they considered re-recording it but decided the roughness was the point.

synopsis: Landlord (2016) is the album where Giggs, the Peckham rapper who had spent a decade as one of the most respected voices in British rap, finally made his major-label breakthrough, and it stands as the definitive statement of his cold, menacing style. Giggs had built his reputation on mixtapes and a prison sentence that only added to his legend, and his voice, a slow, deep, almost glacial growl, is one of the most recognizable in British music. The album, produced by a team that included some of the best beatmakers in UK rap, is built on dark, sparse production and Giggs's unhurried, hypnotic delivery, and songs like 'Whippin' Excursion', 'Linguo' and the title track became anthems of the UK rap underground. The album was a critical and commercial success, and it established Giggs as the elder statesman of British street rap, the artist whose influence can be heard in nearly every UK rapper who came after him.

name: good kid, m.A.A.d city
teaser: Kendrick Lamar 2012 — a cinematic concept album about a single day in Compton. Each track is a scene; the skits are a prayer circle that bookends the story. Dr. Dre's presence is minimal, which was deliberate: Kendrick wanted to prove he didn't need a co-sign. The album's narrative arc follows teenage Kendrick from a stolen van to a baptism.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sing About Me, I'm Dying of Thirst' — two characters speaking from beyond the grave over a 12-minute track. Then 'm.A.A.d city' — the beat was produced by Sounwave on an MPC in a hotel room. MC Eiht's verse was recorded in a single take. The album's voice-mail skits are real messages from Kendrick's parents.

tracks.title: Sing About Me, I'm Dying of Thirst

synopsis: good kid, m.A.A.d city (2012) is the album where Kendrick Lamar, already the most hyped young rapper in America, delivered a debut masterpiece that more than lived up to the expectations, a cinematic concept record that is now regarded as one of the greatest hip-hop albums of all time. The album tells the story of a single day in Kendrick's life as a teenager in Compton, and each track is a scene in a larger narrative: 'Sherane a.k.a Master Splinter's Daughter' sets up the day's mission, which goes wrong when Kendrick's friends get into a shootout, and the record follows him through the violence, temptation and faith of his neighborhood. The skits, including a voicemail from his mother and a prayer with his friends, ground the story in heartbreaking realism, and songs like 'Bitch, Don't Kill My Vibe', 'Swimming Pools (Drank)', 'The Art of Peer Pressure', 'm.A.A.d city' and the stunning closer 'Sing About Me, I'm Dying of Thirst' are among the best of the decade. The album was nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys and made Kendrick the defining rapper of his generation.

name: 2014 Forest Hills Drive
teaser: J. Cole 2014 — named after his childhood home address in Fayetteville, North Carolina. No features, no singles released ahead of time, no promotion. Cole produced most of the album himself. It went double platinum anyway. The album is structured as a journey from childhood to fame and back to the realization that neither satisfied him.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Wet Dreamz' — the first verse was written when Cole was 19, found in an old notebook. The second verse was written at 29, responding to his younger self. Then 'Love Yourz' — recorded in a single take at 2 AM in Cole's home studio. The track has no drums for the first 90 seconds. Cole later said it was the most honest song he'd ever written.

synopsis: 2014 Forest Hills Drive (2014) is the album where J. Cole, who had spent years being dismissed as the third wheel of the great 2010s rappers, made a deeply personal masterpiece that silenced his critics and became one of the best-selling rap albums of the decade. The album is named after the address of the house in Fayetteville, North Carolina, where Cole grew up, and it is a portrait of his journey from poverty to fame: his mother's struggles, his own ambitions, the girls he loved and the friends he lost. Cole released the album with no features and no advance singles, a defiant statement of confidence, and it debuted at number one and went platinum without any radio hits. 'Wet Dreamz' and 'No Role Modelz' became anthems, 'Love Yourz' is a stunning meditation on gratitude, 'Apparently' and 'A Tale of 2 Citiez' show his storytelling gifts, and 'Note to Self' closes the record with a raw, unpolished confession. It is now regarded as Cole's masterpiece.

name: Swimming
teaser: Mac Miller 2018 — his final album released in his lifetime, completed just a month before his accidental overdose. Recorded after a breakup with Ariana Grande and a DUI arrest. Jon Brion (who worked on Kanye's Late Registration) produced many tracks. The album is about learning to swim through depression rather than fighting the current.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Self Care' — the music video features Mac literally buried alive, breaking out of a coffin. The beat switch at 1:35 was Mac's idea: he wanted the song to feel like a panic attack that resolves into calm. Then '2009' — recorded with a string quartet in a single session. Mac's vocal was his first take; Brion told him he'd never beat it.

synopsis: Swimming (2018) is Mac Miller's fifth studio album and the last one released in his lifetime, a gorgeous, understated record about trying to keep your head above water, completed just a month before his accidental overdose at the age of 26. Miller had spent years battling addiction and heartbreak, and Swimming, recorded with producer Jon Brion after Miller went through a painful public breakup, is his most mature and vulnerable work: over mellow, jazzy production that blends hip-hop, R&B and soft rock, he sings and raps about the struggle to heal, to keep going, to find peace. 'Self Care' became his biggest solo hit, 'What's the Use?' and 'Ladders' are gorgeous, sunlit songs, and 'Come Back to Earth', the opening track, and '2009', the closer, are devastatingly honest. The album was nominated for a Grammy after his death, and it now stands as a heartbreaking final statement from an artist who was just beginning to find his most personal voice.

name: Circles
teaser: Mac Miller 2020 — released posthumously, the companion to 'Swimming' that Mac was finishing when he died. Jon Brion completed the album from Mac's notes. The sound is almost entirely sung, fingerpicked acoustic guitars over soft beats, as if 'Swimming' was the struggle and 'Circles' was the peace that followed.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Good News' — the opening line 'I spent the whole day in my head' was one of the last things Mac recorded. Then 'Hand Me Downs' — the bar featuring Mac's brother rapping about family addiction cycles hits devastatingly hard in retrospect. Brion said finishing the album was 'the hardest thing I've ever done.'

synopsis: Circles (2020) is the album that Mac Miller was finishing when he died in 2018, released posthumously as the companion piece to Swimming, and it stands as a beautiful, heartbreaking farewell from one of the most beloved artists of his generation. Miller had conceived Swimming and Circles as a pair of albums, one about swimming against the current, the other about the possibility of finding peace, and he had enlisted producer Jon Brion to help him complete the second before his overdose. The album that emerged is a gorgeous, understated record of soft rock, R&B and gentle hip-hop, with Miller singing more than rapping: 'Good News', the album's centerpiece and first single, is a devastating meditation on depression and the pressure of fame, while 'Circles', 'Blue World' and 'That's on Me' show his gift for melody and his wry humor. The album was completed by Brion after Miller's death, with Miller's family's blessing, and it was released to universal acclaim as a fitting, tender farewell.

name: Live.Love.A$AP
teaser: A$AP Rocky 2011 — the mixtape that made Harlem cool again. Recorded for $2,000 in a Bronx basement. Rocky rapped over cloud-rap beats (Clams Casino's hazy samples) and Houston screw music simultaneously, creating a sound that was half New York, half Texas, fully hypnotic. The mixtape became his major-label audition; RCA signed him within a year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Peso' — the beat is Clams Casino sampling a Sia B-side pitched to sound like a ghost. Rocky's verse was freestyled in one take while sitting on a studio couch. Then 'Purple Swag' — the song that made 'trill' a national term for white teenagers. The Houston influence on every beat is a deliberate love letter to Rocky's Texas family.

synopsis: Live.Love.A$AP (2011) is the mixtape that made A$AP Rocky the most exciting new rapper in America and put the Harlem scene back on the map, a record of such effortless cool that it felt like a new genre arriving fully formed. Rocky, born Rakim Mayers in Harlem, recorded the mixtape for almost nothing in a Bronx basement, and its sound, built on the spaced-out, slowed-down beats of the cloud-rap movement and Rocky's smooth, melodic flow, was unlike anything in mainstream rap. 'Peso' became an underground phenomenon and got Rocky signed within months, 'Purple Swag' and 'Houston Old Head' showed his range, and 'Palace' and 'Brand New Guy', featuring his A$AP Mob partner A$AP Twelvyy, displayed his charisma and his gift for hooks. The mixtape was hailed as a landmark of the new decade's rap, and it established Rocky as a style icon and a star, the record that proved hip-hop could be dreamy, druggy and glamorous.

name: Summertime '06
teaser: Vince Staples 2015 — a double album named after the summer of 2006 in Long Beach, when Vince was 13 and several friends were killed. Produced almost entirely by No I.D. The album's cruelty is never gratuitous: every violent image is a fact of the environment Vince is reporting from, not celebrating.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Norf Norf' — the beat is a single piano loop that sounds like a funeral march. The video was filmed in black and white in Vince's actual neighborhood. Then 'Summertime' — the closing track where Vince's monologue about the summer of 2006 is the album's thesis statement: 'They want a real nigga 'til they get one.' Then silence.

synopsis: Summertime '06 (2015) is the double album where Vince Staples, a rapper from Long Beach who had spent years as a sharp-eyed observer on other people's records, made his full debut, a stunningly bleak and brilliant portrait of the summer he turned thirteen and the violence that defined it. The album is named after 2006, when Vince was 13 and several of his friends were killed, and it is not nostalgic: it is a cold, detailed account of the world that shaped him, full of gang life, police, poverty and the constant presence of death. The production, from No I.D., DJ Dahi and others, is spare and menacing, and Vince's delivery, flat and precise, makes the horror of his stories even more chilling. 'Norf Norf' became an anthem, 'Summertime' and 'Lift Me Up' are gorgeous, and 'Seniors' and '33rd Blakk Glass' are among the most harrowing songs ever recorded about American street life. The album was hailed as a masterpiece, the sound of a brilliant young artist refusing to romanticize his past.

name: The Never Story
teaser: JID 2017 — the Atlanta rapper's debut, signed to J. Cole's Dreamville after Cole heard a demo and flew him to North Carolina the next day. JID's flow is impossibly fast without sacrificing clarity; his verses pack internal rhyme stacks that take three listens to decode. The album title refers to Peter Pan: JID is the lost boy who never had to grow up.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Never' — the opening track where JID raps over a beat that changes tempo three times in under four minutes. Then 'Lauder' — the song's structure mirrors a trauma spiral: calm reflection, eruption, exhaustion, calm. JID's enunciation at his fastest speed is cleaner than most rappers at half his pace.

synopsis: The Never Story (2017) is the debut album of JID, the Atlanta rapper whose dizzying technical skill made him the most exciting young lyricist in hip-hop, and it announced the arrival of a generational talent. JID had spent years honing his craft, and when J. Cole heard his demo, he signed him to Dreamville and flew him to North Carolina the next day; the album that emerged justifies every bit of the hype. JID's flow is breathtaking, a rapid-fire, shape-shifting style that he bends around beats from producers including Christo and Childish Major, and his lyrics are dense with wordplay and storytelling. 'Never' and 'Never Story' announce his ambition, 'EdEddnEddy' and '151 Rum' are showcases for his technical brilliance, and 'Never Fold', 'D/vision' and the gorgeous 'All Bad' show his range. The album was hailed as one of the best debuts of the year, and it established JID as the heir to the throne of technically brilliant Southern rappers.

name: TA13OO
teaser: Denzel Curry 2018 — a three-act concept album structured as Light, Gray, and Dark, tracking a descent from upbeat pop-rap into psychological horror. Curry was 23, processing the murder of his brother and the online abuse he received after a friend's death. The album features JPEGMAFIA, GoldLink, and Twelve'len. The title is a stylized 'Taboo.'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'CLOUT COBAIN | CLOUT CO13A1N' — the beat switches mid-track from trap to industrial noise, and Curry's voice pitches from melodic to demonic. Then 'BLACK BALLOONS | 13LACK 13ALLOONZ' — GoldLink's verse is a single breathless run. The album's Light section is deliberately disorienting: the pop songs feel like they're rotting from the inside.

synopsis: TA13OO (2018) is the album where Denzel Curry, a Florida rapper who had spent years making some of the hardest music in the underground, revealed his full range, a three-act concept record that is now regarded as his masterpiece. The album is structured in three acts, Light, Gray and Dark, tracking a descent from upbeat, radio-friendly pop-rap into psychological darkness, and Curry moves between them with total command: the first act, with songs like 'Sumo' and 'Super Saiyan Superman', is bright and aggressive, the second act, including the massive hit 'Clout Cobain', a stunning critique of the toll of fame, is murky and introspective, and the third act, with the terrifying 'Percs', 'Vengeance' and 'Black Balloons', is a descent into paranoia and rage. The album was hailed by critics as a landmark of modern rap, and it proved that Curry, still in his early twenties, was one of the most ambitious and talented artists of his generation.

name: Nothing Great About Britain
teaser: Slowthai 2019 — a Northampton council-estate kid's debut that became a political document of post-Brexit Britain. The album title is literal: slowthai's Britain is food banks, xenophobia, class warfare, and a Queen on the currency. Production flips between grime, punk, and industrial; slowthai's accent is so thick the CD came with a lyric booklet.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Doorman' — the beat was produced by Mura Masa, who built it from a single distorted guitar riff and a 2-step drum pattern. Then 'Gorgeous' — the song is a love letter to a woman while detailing every reason the country treats her terribly. slowthai's performance at the Mercury Prize — where he held up a fake severed head of Boris Johnson — got him banned from several venues.

synopsis: Nothing Great About Britain (2019) is the debut album of Slowthai, a rapper from a council estate in Northampton, and it became an instant political document of post-Brexit Britain, a furious, funny and tender portrait of the country's forgotten working class. The album's title is a pun on the patriotic song 'There'll Always Be an England', and Slowthai, born Tyron Frampton, spends the record dismantling every myth of British greatness: the class system, the royal family, the failure of the state to protect its own people. His delivery is raw and theatrical, switching between rage and vulnerability, and the production, from Kwes Darko and others, blends grime, punk and British hip-hop. 'Doorman' is a furious attack on the classism of nightlife, 'Gorgeous' and 'Crack' are tender portraits of his community, and 'T N Biscuits' shows his humor. The album was nominated for the Mercury Prize and announced Slowthai as the most exciting and important new voice in British music.

name: GREY Area
teaser: Little Simz 2019 — a London rapper's third album, written and recorded after a breakup with her long-term manager. The production is live instrumentation (bass, drums, strings) played by Simz's touring band; no samples. The album's title refers to her lifelong feeling of not fitting in: too hip-hop for the indie scene, too indie for hip-hop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Offence' — the beat is a single bass riff played by her bassist. Simz's verse references Jay-Z, Biggie, and Big L while sounding like none of them. Then '101 FM' — a song about her childhood watching her Nigerian mother work double shifts. The music video was shot in Simz's actual childhood home on a council estate in Islington.

synopsis: GREY Area (2019) is the album where Little Simz, a London rapper who had spent years building her reputation, delivered the masterpiece that made her one of the most acclaimed artists in British music, winning the Mercury Prize and universal critical praise. The album was written and recorded after a painful breakup with her long-term manager, and the anger and catharsis of that experience runs through the whole record: Simz raps with a new ferocity over sharp, cinematic production from her longtime collaborator Inflo, whose beats mix strings, soul and hard drums into something entirely her own. 'Offence' is a stunning statement of intent, 'Selfish', 'Boss Up' and the devastating 'Venom' show her range, and '101 FM', 'Therapy' and 'Flowers' reveal her vulnerability. The album is tight, focused and utterly confident, and it established Simz, already respected as one of the finest lyricists in Britain, as a true star, the sound of an artist arriving at her peak.

name: Kind of Blue
teaser: Miles Davis 1959 — recorded in one session of about 9 hours. Davis gave the band only sketches of scales and modes, not full charts. The result sold millions and became the best-selling jazz album of all time, the touchstone of modal jazz.

exploreAction.instruction: Put it on once as background and once as the only sound in the room. The opening of 'So What' is a modal scale you'd never guess from the chord chart. Bill Evans's piano intro was written on a napkin in the taxi on the way to the studio. Most of the album was first takes.

synopsis: Kind of Blue (1959) is the best-selling jazz album of all time and the record that changed the course of the music, a masterpiece of modal jazz that has never been out of print. Miles Davis had been moving away from the dense, complex harmonies of bebop, and for this session he gave his band, which included John Coltrane, Cannonball Adderley, Bill Evans and the rhythm section of Paul Chambers and Jimmy Cobb, only sketches of scales and modes rather than full chord charts, asking them to improvise on the scales themselves. The result is music of unprecedented freedom and beauty: 'So What' opens the album with one of the most famous bass lines in jazz, 'Freddie Freeloader' is a blues of effortless cool, 'Blue in Green' is a gorgeous, haunting ballad, and 'All Blues' and 'Flamenco Sketches' complete a record that sounds like it was recorded in a single breath. It was actually recorded in just two sessions in March and April 1959, and it remains the essential jazz album, the door through which most listeners first enter the music.

name: A Love Supreme
teaser: John Coltrane's 1965 suite — his 'gift to God' after getting sober from heroin. Recorded in one evening at Van Gelder Studio, four parts, ~33 minutes. The handwritten poem in the liner notes is a prayer. Coltrane chants 'A Love Supreme' at the end of Part 1.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Resolution' twice. First time, follow the saxophone. Second time, follow Jimmy Garrison's bass. The album does both, and most people only hear half. Then 'Acknowledgement' — the four-note 'A Love Supreme' motif is the foundation; Coltrane plays it in every key.

synopsis: A Love Supreme (1965) is John Coltrane's most celebrated album, a four-part suite that he called his gift to God, made after he had overcome his heroin addiction, and it is one of the most profound documents in all of music. Coltrane, who had undergone a spiritual awakening in 1957, composed the suite as a testament to his faith, and the album's four movements, 'Acknowledgement', 'Resolution', 'Pursuance' and 'Psalm', trace a journey from declaration to devotion. Recorded in a single evening at Van Gelder Studio in New Jersey with his classic quartet, McCoy Tyner on piano, Jimmy Garrison on bass and Elvin Jones on drums, the album is music of extraordinary intensity and beauty: the opening chant of the words 'a love supreme' in 'Acknowledgement', the ferocious soloing of 'Pursuance', and the final movement, where Coltrane plays a musical recitation of a poem he wrote. It sold well and won wide acclaim, and it is now regarded not just as a jazz masterpiece but as one of the greatest spiritual statements in any art form.

name: Bitches Brew
teaser: Miles Davis 1970 — recorded at Columbia's 52nd Street studio with two keyboardists, two bassists, two drummers, and a percussionist. By accident (or design), it invented jazz-rock fusion. The album was assembled from long improvisations edited by producer Teo Macero.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track's first 5 minutes. Then skip to 18 minutes in. Davis creates electronic space before there were electronic instruments — the mood is built from echo and silence. Macero's edit cuts are audible if you listen for them; the album is as much a production artifact as a performance.

synopsis: Bitches Brew (1970) is the album where Miles Davis electrified jazz and blew up its conventions entirely, a record of such radical experimentation that it is now regarded as the founding document of jazz fusion. Davis had been moving toward electric instruments, and for this album he assembled a huge ensemble, including Wayne Shorter, Chick Corea, Joe Zawinul, John McLaughlin and two bassists, two drummers and a percussionist, and gave them only loose themes to work with, encouraging them to play through and past the music's structures. The result is music that is dense, dark, funky and almost psychedelic, built on grooves that stretch for fifteen minutes or more, full of electric piano, wah-wah guitar and trumpet lines that float above the churn. The title track and 'Spanish Key' are the album's centerpieces, and the record sold remarkably well, introducing a generation to electric jazz. It is now regarded as one of the most influential jazz albums ever made, the record that dragged jazz into the rock era whether it wanted to go or not.

name: Giant Steps
teaser: John Coltrane 1960 — the album that introduced 'Coltrane changes', a harmonic progression so complex that Tommy Flanagan (the pianist) could barely solo over the title track. Coltrane had practiced the changes for months in secret before the session.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Coltrane's solo moves through three keys so fast that music theorists named the progression after him. The original take was even faster; they slowed it down for the album. Then 'Naima' — a ballad named for Coltrane's first wife, built on a single pedal tone that never resolves.

synopsis: Giant Steps (1960) is the album that made John Coltrane a legend, the record that introduced the dizzying harmonic progression now known as 'Coltrane changes' and instantly became required listening for every jazz musician. The title track is one of the most demanding compositions in jazz, its rapid-fire chord changes moving through three keys in a pattern that even the album's pianist, Tommy Flanagan, struggled to keep up with, and Coltrane's solo on it is one of the most famous in the music's history. The album, recorded over several sessions in 1959 and 1960 with a rotating cast that included Cedar Walton, Wynton Kelly and the rhythm section of Paul Chambers and Art Taylor, also contains gorgeous ballads like 'Naima', written for his wife, and 'Mr. P.C.', a tribute to bassist Paul Chambers. Giant Steps marked the moment Coltrane, who had spent years in the shadow of Miles Davis and Thelonious Monk, fully emerged as one of the most important and innovative forces in jazz.

name: Time Out
teaser: Dave Brubeck Quartet 1959 — the first jazz album to sell a million copies. Every track is in an unusual time signature: 9/8, 5/4, 6/4. Columbia executives thought it was a terrible idea. 'Take Five' became the best-selling jazz single of all time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Take Five' — the 5/4 time signature was inspired by Turkish street musicians Brubeck heard on a State Department tour. Joe Morello's drum solo was improvised; the band kept playing because he was on fire. Then 'Blue Rondo à la Turk' — it shifts from 9/8 to 4/4 and back without announcing the change.

synopsis: Time Out (1959) is the album that made jazz with unusual time signatures a hit, the first jazz album to sell over a million copies, and it remains one of the most beloved records in the genre's history. Dave Brubeck, who had studied with the composer Darius Milhaud and was fascinated by the rhythms of classical and world music, composed most of the album's pieces in meters that jazz had rarely attempted: 9/8, 5/4, 6/4 and the like, with saxophonist Paul Desmond's lyrical playing floating effortlessly over the odd meters. 'Take Five', written by Desmond in 5/4 time, became the biggest jazz single ever recorded and one of the most recognizable pieces of music in the world, while 'Blue Rondo à la Turk', inspired by Turkish street musicians, and 'Strange Meadow Lark' complete a record of effortless sophistication. The album made Brubeck a household name and proved that jazz could be intellectually adventurous and commercially successful at the same time.

name: Head Hunters
teaser: Herbie Hancock 1973 — after years of acoustic jazz, he went electric. The album opens with 'Chameleon', a 15-minute funk groove built on a two-note bassline. Hancock played all the synthesizers himself, including a custom ARP that he had just bought.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Chameleon' — the bassline is two notes for the first 6 minutes. The groove never gets boring because the textures keep shifting: clavinet, ARP synth, and layers of percussion. Then 'Watermelon Man' — a reworking of Hancock's 1962 hit, but played through a beer bottle and an African percussion ensemble.

synopsis: Head Hunters (1973) is the album where Herbie Hancock, one of the most respected pianists in jazz, plugged in his electric piano and made the best-selling jazz record of its era, a stunning fusion of funk and jazz that changed the music forever. Hancock had been experimenting with electronic instruments, and for this album he assembled a new band, the Head Hunters, including the bassist Paul Jackson, drummer Harvey Mason, saxophonist Bennie Maupin and the young Bill Summers on percussion, and set out to make music that was as funky as anything on the radio but as sophisticated as anything in jazz. The album opens with 'Chameleon', a fifteen-minute groove built on one of the most famous bass lines ever recorded, and also contains 'Watermelon Man', a Hancock classic reinvented as Afro-Cuban funk with the astonishing percussion work of Summers, who played beer bottles as part of the rhythm. The album sold over a million copies and made Hancock a star, and it is now regarded as a landmark of jazz fusion.

name: Mingus Ah Um
teaser: Charles Mingus 1959 — one of the most emotionally direct jazz albums ever made. 'Fables of Faubus' was meant to have lyrics mocking Arkansas governor Orval Faubus, but Columbia censored them. Mingus re-recorded the vocal version a year later on a different label.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Goodbye Pork Pie Hat' — a eulogy for Lester Young recorded just two months after his death. The saxophone solo by John Handy was his first recording session. Then 'Better Git It in Your Soul' — the handclaps and shouts were improvised by the band during the take.

tracks.title: Better Git It in Your Soul

synopsis: Mingus Ah Um (1959) is the album where Charles Mingus, the great bassist, composer and bandleader, made his most emotionally direct and enduring statement, a record that captures both his fury and his tenderness in equal measure. Mingus was one of the most volatile figures in jazz, a man who once fired a gun at a bandmate and who poured every feeling he had into his music, and Mingus Ah Um is the purest distillation of his genius. 'Better Git It in Your Soul' opens the album with a gospel shout, 'Goodbye Pork Pie Hat', his tribute to the saxophonist Lester Young, who had died weeks before the session, is one of the most beautiful elegies in jazz, and 'Fables of Faubus', a furious attack on the segregationist governor of Arkansas, was so political that Columbia refused to let Mingus record the original lyrics, which mocked Faubus directly. The album also contains tributes to Duke Ellington and Jelly Roll Morton, and it is now regarded as Mingus's masterpiece, the record where his rage and his love became one.

name: Selected Ambient Works 85-92
teaser: Richard D. James' 1992 compilation of ambient techno tracks recorded while he was a teenager in Cornwall. The master tape was damaged — one channel is subtly quieter than the other through the entire album. James decided to leave it that way; it became part of the sound.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen for the moments that sound broken — a synth that doesn't resolve, a sample that loops fractionally late. That's the texture Aphex Twin is building. 'Xtal' opens the album with a vocal sample from an obscure 1970s library record. The whole thing feels like a field recording from a place that never existed.

synopsis: Selected Ambient Works 85-92 (1992) is the album that introduced the world to Aphex Twin, the teenage genius Richard D. James, and it remains one of the most influential electronic records ever made, a collection of tracks of such strange, dreamlike beauty that they sounded like they came from another planet. James recorded most of the tracks as a teenager in Cornwall, using a small collection of synthesizers and drum machines, and the album collects his early experiments in what would come to be called ambient techno: melodies that float and drift over gentle, insistent beats, full of the warmth and weirdness of the analog equipment he used. Tracks like 'Xtal', 'Pulsewidth', 'Ageispolis' and 'Tha' are masterpieces of the form, and the album's overall mood, somewhere between bliss and melancholy, has never been matched. The master tape was reportedly damaged, which added to the album's legend. It is now regarded as one of the most important electronic albums ever made, the record that proved electronic music could be as emotional as any other.

name: Music Has the Right to Children
teaser: Boards of Canada's 1998 debut — brothers Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin recording in their Pentland Hills hideaway in Scotland. The album samples 1970s children's TV shows, NASA transmissions, and deteriorating VHS tapes. The result sounds like a memory of a TV show from a parallel universe.

exploreAction.targetName: Music Has the Right to Children (1998) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen on headphones with the lights low. 'Telephasic Workshop' contains a sample of US President Eisenhower from an obscure 1950s broadcast, chopped into syllables. Then 'Roygbiv' — an ambient lullaby in two chords that has become the most-sampled Boards of Canada track without anyone knowing they're sampling it.

synopsis: Music Has the Right to Children (1998) is the debut album of Boards of Canada, the Scottish duo of brothers Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin, and it is one of the most influential electronic albums ever made, a record of warm, nostalgic, strangely familiar music that sounds like memories of a childhood you never had. The brothers recorded the album in their studio in the Pentland Hills of Scotland, and their music is built on vintage synthesizers, dusty beats and, most distinctively, layers of degraded tape hiss and fragments of old educational films, which give the record its uncanny sense of time and place. Tracks like 'Roygbiv', 'An Eagle in Your Mind', 'Turquoise Hexagon Sun' and 'Amo Bishop Roden' have become touchstones of the genre, and the album's gentle melodies and hypnotic rhythms made it a favorite of everyone from electronic fans to ambient listeners to hip-hop producers. It is now regarded as a landmark, the record that proved electronic music could be pastoral, nostalgic and deeply human.

name: Discovery
teaser: Daft Punk's 2001 second album — recorded on a four-track with no computer sequencing. Every song was made from samples played by the duo themselves, then processed until the source was unrecognizable. The album has a companion anime film, 'Interstella 5555', with no dialogue.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'One More Time' — a sample from Eddie Johns' 'More Spell on You' plus a vocoded vocal by Romanthony. The song took 8 months to produce because they kept restarting. Then 'Aerodynamic' — the guitar solo in the middle was played by Thomas Bangalter on a synthesizer routed through a guitar amp, meant to sound like Eddie Van Halen.

synopsis: Discovery (2001) is the album where Daft Punk, the French duo who had conquered the world's dance floors with their debut, made a record of pure, unashamed pop joy, and it is now regarded as one of the most influential albums of the 2000s. Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo recorded the album using only samples, played live by the duo into a four-track recorder rather than sequenced on a computer, and they drew on the disco, rock and funk of the 1970s and 80s to create a sound that was both nostalgic and completely new. 'One More Time', with its auto-tuned vocals and euphoric energy, became an anthem for a generation, 'Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger' and 'Digital Love' are masterpieces of sampled pop, and 'Something About Us' and 'Veridis Quo' show the duo's more melancholy side. The album was accompanied by the animated film Interstella 5555, and its influence on pop, electronic and hip-hop music, from Kanye West's Graduation to countless others, is incalculable.

name: Homework
teaser: Daft Punk's 1997 debut — recorded in Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo's bedroom in Paris on a 4-track cassette recorder. The album made French house music credible to American audiences almost overnight. The title is literal: they treated it like schoolwork, recording every night after their day jobs.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Da Funk' — the bass riff is a 4-bar sample from a G-funk record, looped for 5 minutes without changing once. Then 'Around the World' — a 7-minute song built around a single vocal phrase repeated 144 times. The groove is in the slight variations, not the pattern.

synopsis: Homework (1997) is the debut album of Daft Punk, the record that made French house music a global phenomenon and introduced the world to the most influential electronic duo of their era. Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo recorded the album in a bedroom in Paris on a four-track cassette recorder, using drum machines, synthesizers and an obsessive attention to the sounds of Chicago house and Detroit techno, and the result was a record of raw, funky, irresistible dance music. 'Around the World' and 'Da Funk' became massive hits, 'Revolution 909' and 'Teachers', a tribute to the producers who inspired them, showed their roots, and the album's overall energy, loose and live-sounding, made it a favorite of DJs and dancers everywhere. The album made Daft Punk stars before they had even adopted the robot helmets that would make them icons, and it remains a landmark of electronic music, the record that proved house music could be art.

name: Music for Airports
teaser: Brian Eno's 1978 ambient landmark — composed to be heard (and ignored) in public spaces. The first record to call itself 'ambient'. Eno was inspired after being stuck at an airport listening to the terrible Muzak, thinking: what if background music was actually beautiful?.

exploreAction.instruction: Put it on low while doing something else. The piece reveals itself only when you half-listen — try to catch each loop as it phases out of alignment with the others. Eno described it as 'music designed to be as ignorable as it is interesting.' Each of the four tracks is a tape loop of different lengths, drifting in and out of sync.

synopsis: Music for Airports (1978) is the album that gave ambient music its name and its purpose, a record by Brian Eno, the former Roxy Music keyboardist, that was designed to be heard and ignored at the same time, music that would calm the anxiety of a public space without demanding attention. Eno had been experimenting with the idea of music as atmosphere since an accident left him bedridden, listening to a record so quietly that he could barely hear it, and he coined the term 'ambient' for this album's liner notes, defining it as music that could be 'as ignorable as it is interesting'. The album's four pieces are built on tape loops of piano, voices and synthesizers, arranged so that the loops shift in and out of sync, creating music that seems to float and breathe. It was originally installed in airports, most famously at the Marine Midland Building in Buffalo, and its influence on everything from film scores to meditation apps to ambient pop is immeasurable. It remains the definitive statement of ambient music.

name: Trans-Europe Express
teaser: Kraftwerk 1977 — the album that convinced a generation of Detroit teenagers to buy drum machines. The title track mimics a train journey across Europe using only synthesizers and a vocoder. Afrika Bambaataa sampled 'Trans-Europe Express' for 'Planet Rock', birthing electro.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Europe Endless' — the 10-minute opening track that never changes tempo but constantly shifts texture. Then the title track — the train rhythm was created by running a sequencer at a mathematically precise tempo matching actual train wheel clicks. Kraftwerk built their own electronic drum kit because none existed in 1977.

synopsis: Trans-Europe Express (1977) is the album where Kraftwerk, the Dusseldorf quartet who had spent years building the sound of electronic music, made their masterpiece, a record that imagined a futuristic, fully mechanized Europe and predicted the entire electronic dance era. The title track mimics the rhythm of a train journey, its relentless, hypnotic beat and simple, memorable melody evoking the romance and precision of the great European express trains, and the album is full of the band's signature coldness and wit: 'The Hall of Mirrors' is about the vanity of fame, 'Showroom Dummies' is a deadpan meditation on being watched, and 'Europe Endless' opens the record with a stately, beautiful anthem to the continent. The album was a huge influence on the nascent hip-hop scene in New York and Detroit, and it is often credited with helping to inspire techno and electro. It is now regarded as one of the most important albums ever made, the record where electronic music grew up.

name: Mezzanine
teaser: Massive Attack 1998 — recorded in a Bristol basement over 18 months. The band was falling apart; three members recorded in separate rooms. The cover art is a black beetle photographed by Nick Knight. The album's darkness consumed two years of their lives.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen on headphones in the dark. 'Angel' opens with a bassline that sounds like it's crawling toward you — it was recorded by playing a bass guitar through three distortion pedals in series. Then 'Teardrop' — the heartbeat rhythm is a sample of a fetal heartbeat; the vocal is by Cocteau Twins' Elizabeth Fraser, recorded in a single take at 3 AM.

synopsis: Mezzanine (1998) is the album where Massive Attack, the Bristol group who had invented trip-hop with their debut Blue Lines, made their masterpiece, a dark, brooding, utterly hypnotic record that is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 1990s. The band recorded the album over eighteen months in a basement studio in Bristol, and the sessions were fraught: the group's three core members were barely speaking, recording in separate rooms, and the tension seeped into the music, which is darker and heavier than anything they had made before, full of slow, crushing beats, eerie guitars and the deep, foreboding bass lines that became the record's signature. 'Teardrop', with its gorgeous vocal from Elizabeth Fraser of the Cocteau Twins, became one of the defining songs of the decade, 'Angel' is a menacing masterpiece built on a sample of a song by the group the Incredible String Band, and 'Inertia Creeps', 'Risingson' and 'Group Four' complete a record of astonishing consistency. It sold millions and its influence is everywhere, from film and television soundtracks to the entire genre of dark electronic pop.

name: Crush
teaser: Sam Shepherd's 2019 album — a neuroscientist-turned-producer builds dance music where the breakdown is the song. Recorded over five years between DJ sets and research. The album refuses to climax in the way dance music is supposed to.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen for phrases that repeat one bar longer than expected. Shepherd builds grooves that go past the obvious exit — those are the hooks. Resist skipping to the drop; the drop is buried. The album was mixed to reveal detail on headphones that get lost on speakers.

synopsis: Crush (2019) is the album where Floating Points, the British producer and neuroscientist Sam Shepherd, made his most complete and celebrated record, a stunning fusion of his two great loves, the intellectual rigor of electronic music and the warmth of live musicians. Shepherd, who had spent years making experimental electronic music and also leading an ensemble of live players, brought the two worlds together on Crush, working with a team of musicians and processing their playing through his modular synthesizers, and the result is music of extraordinary energy and invention. 'Last Bloom' and 'Anasickmodular' are overwhelming, ecstatic tracks, 'Apoptose' and 'Birth4000' show his gift for building enormous, cinematic climaxes, and the album's blend of jungle, techno, ambient and classical music is entirely his own. The album was hailed as one of the best electronic records of the year, and it confirmed Shepherd as one of the most important figures in contemporary electronic music.

name: Untrue
teaser: Burial's 2007 second album — made entirely in SoundForge, a $60 audio editor, with no sequencer. The crackle and vinyl hiss are synthetic. Burial (William Bevan) remained anonymous for years, recording at night in his South London flat. The album sounds like London at 4 AM in the rain.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen for the ghost vocals — they're pitched-up R&B samples, chopped so the original song is unrecognizable. Burial recorded the rain sounds from his bedroom window. The drum patterns are deliberately off-grid — he drew them by hand in the audio editor, giving them a human stagger that no drum machine can replicate.

synopsis: Untrue (2007) is the album where Burial, the anonymous South London producer whose real identity, Will Bevan, was unknown when the record appeared, made a masterpiece of dark, haunted electronic music that completely reinvented UK garage and dubstep, and it is now regarded as one of the most important electronic albums of the 2000s. Burial made the album entirely in SoundForge, a cheap audio editor, using no sequencer, cutting and pasting audio by hand, and the result is music of astonishing atmosphere: slow, skeletal beats, layers of rain and street noise, and fragments of vocal samples, pitched and manipulated until they sound like ghostly memories of R&B songs. Tracks like 'Archangel', 'Ghost Hardware' and 'Etched Headplate' are among the most emotionally affecting electronic music ever made, full of loneliness and longing. The album won the Mercury Prize nomination and universal acclaim, and its influence on electronic music, from dubstep to ambient to pop, is enormous.

name: Waveform Transmission Vol. 3
teaser: Jeff Mills 1994 — the Detroit techno purist's most essential album. Recorded live to DAT tape with no overdubs. Mills, a former radio DJ known as The Wizard, built tracks from Roland TR-909 drum patterns and minimal synth lines, creating a sound so precise it felt like mathematics set to a 4/4 kick.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Bells' — the track is a single synth stab repeated for 5 minutes while the 909 kicks you in the chest. Mills famously plays 3-4 decks simultaneously in his DJ sets. Then 'Changes of Life' — the snare roll at 2:17 sounds like a machine gun made of hi-hats. Detroit techno's philosophy: less is more, but louder.

synopsis: Waveform Transmission Vol. 3 (1994) is the album where Jeff Mills, the Detroit techno pioneer who had spent years as one of the genre's most radical figures, made his most essential statement, a record of relentless, hypnotic techno that is now regarded as a masterpiece of the form. Mills, a former radio DJ and a founding member of the legendary Underground Resistance collective, recorded the album live to DAT tape with no overdubs, a display of technical mastery that few other producers could match, and the result is music of astonishing purity and power: stripped-down, propulsive tracks that build and release tension with machine-like precision. Tracks like 'The Bells', which became one of the most famous techno tracks ever recorded, 'The Dancer' and 'Jungle Wobble' show Mills at the peak of his powers, and the album's relentless energy made it a favorite of DJs and dancers around the world. It is now regarded as one of the defining documents of techno, the sound of the genre at its most pure and powerful.

name: Deep Space
teaser: Juan Atkins (as Model 500) 1995 — the godfather of techno's space-obsessed masterwork. Atkins coined the term 'techno' in the early 80s after reading Alvin Toffler's 'The Third Wave'. The album imagines Detroit not as a decaying industrial city but as a launching pad to the stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Flow' — the bassline is a single arpeggiated note from a Roland TB-303, the same synth that created acid house. Then 'Night Drive' — inspired by Atkins' actual drives through Detroit's empty 3 AM streets. The album's sci-fi aesthetic wasn't escapism; it was a Black American's vision of a future that included him.

synopsis: Deep Space (1995) is the album where Juan Atkins, the man who coined the term techno and is universally known as the godfather of the genre, made his most complete and ambitious statement under his Model 500 alias, a record of cosmic, otherworldly electronic music that lives up to its name. Atkins had been making music since the early 1980s, when he and his high school friends invented what would become techno in the suburbs of Detroit, and Deep Space gathers his explorations of the music's more experimental side: tracks built on the science fiction themes that had always obsessed him, full of sweeping synthesizers, hypnotic rhythms and a sense of vast, empty space. 'Starlight' and 'No UFO's' are among the best-known tracks, and the album's overall mood, somewhere between a journey through the cosmos and a night in a Detroit club, is entirely his own. Deep Space is now regarded as an essential document of techno's origins, the record where the genre's founding father showed just how far his vision could go.

name: Innovator
teaser: Derrick May 1997 — a compilation of the Detroit techno pioneer's most important tracks from 1987-1990. May called his music 'Hi-Tech Soul', believing that machines could express human emotion. His track 'Strings of Life' — a piano-driven techno anthem — was made in a single afternoon and accidentally became the most important dance track of the era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Strings of Life' — the piano was played by May's friend Michael James, who didn't know the tape was rolling. The string sample is from a 1970s Detroit Symphony recording. Then 'Nude Photo' — the track was produced in Juan Atkins' mother's basement. May, Atkins, and Kevin Saunderson went to the same high school in Belleville, Michigan.

tracks.title: Strings of the Strings of Life
Daymares, It Is What It Is
Feel Surrreal Ends the Feel Surreal
To Be or Not to Be

synopsis: Innovator (1997) is the essential collection of Derrick May, one of the three founding figures of Detroit techno, and it remains the best introduction to the music of the man who called his sound 'high-tech soul'. May, along with his high school friends Juan Atkins and Kevin Saunderson, invented techno in the suburbs of Detroit in the early 1980s, and Innovator gathers the tracks he made between 1987 and 1990 under his own name and as Rhythim Is Rhythim, including the monumental 'Strings of Life', a track of soaring, emotional beauty that is often called one of the greatest electronic records ever made. Also included are 'Nude Photo', 'The Dance' and 'Kaos', and the collection shows how May took the cold machinery of techno and filled it with human feeling. His music became the soundtrack of the first wave of techno in Europe, and Innovator remains a cornerstone of the genre, the sound of techno at its most romantic and its most futuristic.

name: More Songs About Food and Revolutionary Art
teaser: Carl Craig 1997 — the second-generation Detroit techno producer's masterpiece. Craig fused techno with jazz, ambient, and classical influences. The album title is a Talking Heads reference. Craig played nearly every instrument himself, layering Rhodes piano, synthesizers, and drum machines into a sound that was both futuristic and deeply human.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'At Les' — the track builds for 15 minutes from a single piano chord into a full orchestral-techno climax. Then 'Televised Green Smoke' — the drum programming is so intricate it sounds like a live jazz drummer, but it's entirely sequenced. Craig's secret: he programs drums at half-speed, then speeds them up.

tracks.title: Food and Art (In the Spirit of Revolution)

synopsis: More Songs About Food and Revolutionary Art (1997) is the album where Carl Craig, the most important producer of the second generation of Detroit techno, made his masterpiece, a record that fused the mechanical pulse of techno with jazz, ambient and classical music to create something entirely new. Craig had spent the early 1990s releasing a dazzling series of records under various aliases, and this album, released under his own name, gathered his most ambitious work into a single statement. 'At Les' is a gorgeous tribute to the jazz drummer, 'Darkness' is a brooding, hypnotic epic, 'The Climax' and 'Sandstorms' show his gift for building enormous, cinematic structures, and 'Bug in the Bassbin', with its live drums and horn samples, sounds like techno meeting a jazz band in a dark room. The album was hailed as a landmark of electronic music, and it established Craig as the most important figure in the music after the genre's founders, the producer who proved techno could contain multitudes.

name: Dubnobasswithmyheadman
teaser: Underworld 1994 — the album where a failed 80s pop band reinvented itself as techno poets. Karl Hyde's stream-of-consciousness vocals — collected from overheard conversations, late-night TV, and London street observations — floated over Rick Smith and Darren Emerson's propulsive beats. The album made techno feel like literature.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dark & Long' — the 7-minute opener evolves from a single bass pulse into a panorama. Then 'Cowgirl' — the lyric 'everything everything' was repeated so many times during recording that Hyde lost his voice. The album was recorded at night after the band's day jobs; they'd finish at 6 AM and watch the sunrise over the Thames.

synopsis: Dubnobasswithmyheadman (1994) is the album where Underworld, a band that had spent the 1980s as a failed synth-pop act, reinvented themselves as the most emotionally powerful act in electronic music, and it remains a landmark of the genre. Karl Hyde and Rick Smith had been making music together for years without finding their voice, and on this album, recorded with the addition of the DJ Darren Emerson, they finally cracked it: Hyde's stream-of-consciousness lyrics, half-sung, half-spoken, full of fractured images of travel, weather and urban life, floated over Smith's deep, hypnotic techno, creating music that was both danceable and strangely moving. 'Dark & Long' and 'Mmm... Skyscraper I Love You' became anthems of the emerging progressive house scene, and 'Cowgirl', 'Dirty Epic' and the closing 'River of Bass' showed the band's extraordinary range. The album was a huge influence on the electronic music that followed, and it remains the record where Underworld found the sound that would make them legends.

name: Orbital (Brown Album)
teaser: Orbital 1993 — the Hartnoll brothers' second album, named for its brown cover (they never title their albums). Recorded in a studio built into a converted water tower in Kent. The album took techno's rigid structures and made them bend — shifting time signatures, unexpected melodic turns, and a warmth that most electronic music lacked.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Halcyon + On + On' — the track is built around a sample of Opus III's 'It's a Fine Day' and Kirsty Hawkshaw's vocals, pitched and reversed. Then 'Impact (The Earth Is Burning)' — the track samples a BBC documentary about environmental collapse. The album was made entirely on hardware: no computers, just synthesizers and a 24-track tape machine.

synopsis: Orbital (1993), known as the Brown Album for its plain brown cover, is the album where the Hartnoll brothers, Phil and Paul, who never title their records, made their masterpiece, a record of techno that was as melodic and emotional as any pop music of its era. The brothers had broken through with their self-titled debut in 1991, and their second album found them expanding their sound: 'Halcyon', built around a sample of a Kirsty MacColl song, became one of the most beautiful and beloved electronic tracks ever recorded, a piece of music that has been used in films, television and countless compilations, while 'Lush' and 'Semi-Detached' showed their gift for building enormous, immersive structures. The album was recorded in the brothers' own studio and released on their label, and its blend of rave energy and genuine emotion made it a favorite of both DJs and home listeners. It is now regarded as one of the essential albums of the 1990s electronic boom.

name: Beyond the Mix
teaser: Frankie Knuckles 1991 — the godfather of house music's only proper studio album. Knuckles, who started DJing at Chicago's Warehouse club (which gave house music its name), brought in vocalists, string sections, and gospel influences. The album bridged underground dance music and the pop mainstream.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Whistle Song' — the synth-whistle melody was played on a Roland D-50. The track became a global hit despite having no verse, no chorus, and almost no words. Then 'Rain Falls' — Lisa Michaelis's vocal was recorded in a single take in Knuckles's apartment. The album's warmth comes from Knuckles mixing everything through vintage analog compressors.

synopsis: Beyond the Mix (1991) is the only proper studio album by Frankie Knuckles, the DJ who is universally known as the godfather of house music, and it stands as a testament to the man who invented the sound that conquered the world. Knuckles had started DJing at Chicago's Warehouse club in the late 1970s, and it was there that he developed the style, mixing disco records with drum machines and other electronic sounds, that became known as house music, named after the club itself. Beyond the Mix, recorded at the height of his fame, captures the warmth and sophistication of his sound: deep, gospel-tinged house with gorgeous vocals and a sense of joy that was entirely his own. Tracks like 'Tears' and 'Whistle Song' show his gift for building emotional peaks, and the album remains a beloved classic of the genre. Knuckles died in 2014, but his influence is everywhere in dance music, and Beyond the Mix preserves the sound of the man who started it all.

name: Another Side
teaser: Larry Heard (as Mr. Fingers) 1988 — the album that proved house music could be deeply emotional. Heard's track 'Can You Feel It' had already become an anthem; this album extended that vision into a full-length statement. Heard played all the instruments: Rhodes piano, Juno-106, TR-808, and his own voice.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Can You Feel It' — the spoken word intro ('In the beginning, there was Jack…') is a sermon about the origins of house music. Then 'Mystery of Love' — Heard's falsetto floats over a Rhodes chord progression that never resolves. Heard was a drummer before he was a producer; every track has a rhythmic sophistication that most house music lacks.

synopsis: Another Side (1988) is the album where Larry Heard, recording as Mr. Fingers, proved that house music could be as deep and emotional as any music ever made, and it remains one of the most influential records in the history of dance music. Heard, a Chicago musician who had been making house records since the mid-1980s, was one of the genre's most gifted producers, and this album, his debut, showed a side of house that went far beyond the dance floor: tracks of quiet, meditative beauty built on lush synthesizer chords and gentle rhythms, full of the melancholy and longing that would come to define the subgenre known as deep house. The album contains 'Can You Feel It', a track of such simple, profound beauty that it is often called the greatest deep house record ever made, and its influence on the generations of producers who followed, from Detroit to London to everywhere else, is immeasurable. Another Side is the sound of house music finding its soul.

name: Silentintroduction
teaser: Moodymann (Kenny Dixon Jr.) 1997 — the Detroit producer's debut, a collage of deep house, soul samples, and spoken-word interludes that feel like eavesdropping on a private conversation. Dixon's signature move — leaving vinyl crackle and tape hiss in the mix — made the music feel like it was coming from a dusty record collection, not a computer.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Can't Kick This Feeling When It Hits' — the track is built from a 4-bar Chic sample looped for 8 minutes, and it never gets boring. Then 'Dem Young Sconies' — the shouted vocal sample is Dixon's friends at a Detroit party. Dixon famously refuses to show his face in interviews, insisting the music speak for itself.

tracks.title: I Can't Kick This Feeling When It Hits

synopsis: Silentintroduction (1997) is the debut album of Moodymann, the Detroit producer born Kenny Dixon Jr., and it is now regarded as one of the most influential albums in the history of house music, a record that treated the genre as a medium for autobiography, collage and deep feeling. Moodymann made the album using cheap equipment and an obsessive record collection, building his tracks from layers of soul and funk samples, live instrumentation and spoken-word interludes that reveal fragments of his life and philosophy. The result is music of extraordinary warmth and depth, house tracks that feel less like club music and more like letters from a friend: 'I Can't Kick This Feelin When It Hits', 'Music 4 My People' and 'Sunday' have become classics of the genre, and the album's collage of voices, including snippets of sermons and phone messages, gives it an intimacy that few electronic records have ever matched. Moodymann became the most influential figure in the Detroit house scene of the late 90s and beyond, and Silentintroduction is where it all began.

name: Raw Footage
teaser: Ron Trent 1999 — the Chicago-born, New York-based producer's magnum opus. Trent started DJing at 14; by 16 he'd produced 'Altered States', a track that defined deep house. This album expands that sound into something cinematic: jazz fusion, African percussion, and spoken-word poetry over deep, patient grooves.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Sound' — the opening congas were recorded in a single session with a percussionist Trent met at a drum circle. Then 'Journey' — the track runs 12 minutes and passes through at least 4 distinct movements. Trent's production philosophy: 'let the track breathe.' Most of these songs were first takes.

tracks.title: Gangsta Rap Made Me Do It
Get Money, Spend Money, No Money

synopsis: Raw Footage (1999) is the magnum opus of Ron Trent, the Chicago-born producer who was one of the most gifted musicians of the deep house generation, a double album that stands as a complete statement of his vision. Trent was a child prodigy of house music, starting to DJ at fourteen and producing his first classic, 'Altered States', at sixteen, and by the time he recorded Raw Footage, in his early twenties, he had spent a decade absorbing the music of Chicago, New York and Detroit. The album draws all of those influences together: deep, hypnotic house, jazzy ambient textures, Afrocentric rhythms and the warm, organic sound that defined his best work. 'Morning', 'Devotion' and 'Raw Footage' are among the highlights, and the album's unhurried, meditative pace made it a favorite of DJs and dancers who wanted music with depth. It is now regarded as one of the essential deep house albums of the 1990s.

name: Timeless
teaser: Goldie 1995 — the first drum & bass album to cross over to the mainstream. Recorded over 2 years at a cost of £250,000 (unheard of for electronic music at the time). Goldie couldn't read music or play an instrument; he hummed ideas to session musicians. The 21-minute opening track 'Inner City Life' was originally 3 separate songs stitched together.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Inner City Life' — Diane Charlemagne's vocal was recorded in a single session after Goldie found her singing in a London jazz club. Then 'Angel' — the swirling strings were arranged by a classical composer who'd never heard drum & bass before. The album's ambition was so extreme that the label tried to cut it in half; Goldie refused.

tracks.title: Inner City Life (Rabbit's Short Attention Span edit)

synopsis: Timeless (1995) is the album that took drum and bass, the fast, breakbeat-driven music of the British rave underground, into the mainstream, and it remains the genre's most ambitious and celebrated record.
