Goldie, born Clifford Price, was a former breakdancer and graffiti artist who had become one of the most important figures in the jungle scene, and his debut album, recorded over two years at a reported cost of £250,000, was a staggering statement of intent: the title track alone is twenty-one minutes long, a suite that moves from soaring strings and angelic vocals into rolling breakbeats and back again, and the album as a whole showed that drum and bass could be as grand and emotional as any music ever made. 'Inner City Life', the album's centerpiece, became an anthem of the genre, and its combination of jungle rhythms with lush, cinematic production was unlike anything that had come before. Timeless made Goldie a star and proved that the music of the rave could be art, and its influence on electronic music is enormous.

name: New Forms
teaser: Roni Size / Reprazent 1997 — the album that won the Mercury Prize and proved drum & bass could be a live band, not just a DJ genre. Recorded in a Bristol basement with a rotating crew of musicians. Size's production blended jazz improvisation, dub basslines, and breakbeats into something wholly new.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Brown Paper Bag' — the bassline was played by a live double bassist, then sampled and looped. Then 'Heroes' — the track's orchestral swell was recorded with the Bristol Philharmonic in a single afternoon. Size built the album's beats from live drum recordings, not samples, giving it a human feel that most drum & bass lacked.

synopsis: New Forms (1997) is the album where Roni Size and his collective Reprazent proved that drum and bass could be played by a live band, and in doing so they made the most acclaimed record the genre has ever produced, winning the Mercury Prize in the process. Size had been a fixture of the Bristol music scene since the late 1980s, and New Forms, recorded with his collaborators including DJ Krust and the vocalist Onallee, treats drum and bass as a living, breathing music: double bass, piano, live drums and voices weave in and out of the fast, rolling breakbeats, creating a sound that was both danceable and deeply musical. 'Brown Paper Bag', with its iconic bass line, became the album's signature track, and 'Heroes', 'Share the Fall' and 'Hi-Potent' showed the collective's extraordinary range. The album won the Mercury Prize in 1997, beating Radiohead's OK Computer, and it is now regarded as a landmark, the record that proved drum and bass could be art music without losing its power to move people.

name: Logical Progression
teaser: LTJ Bukem 1996 — the album that defined 'intelligent' drum & bass (a term Bukem himself hated). Recorded at his Good Looking Records studio. Bukem's production was the antithesis of the aggressive jungle dominating the scene: lush pads, jazz-influenced chords, and breakbeats that rolled rather than attacked.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Horizons' — the track's string pads were played on a Korg M1, the same synthesizer that scored a thousand 90s house tracks. Then 'Music' — the vocal sample is a single phrase from an obscure 1970s soul record, pitched and stretched into a 7-minute meditation. Bukem's secret: he mixed the drums lower than the melody, which was heresy in drum & bass.

synopsis: Logical Progression (1996) is the album that defined the sound of intelligent drum and bass, the smoother, more atmospheric side of the genre, and it remains the signature work of LTJ Bukem, the producer and DJ who was its leading figure. Bukem, born Danny Williamson in London, had been making music since the early 1990s, and his label, Good Looking Records, became the home of a new sound: drum and bass built on warm, jazzy chords, lush pads and a sense of space that was a world away from the aggressive energy of the rave. This compilation gathers the key tracks of that sound, including the gorgeous 'Music' and 'Horizons', and it became the definitive statement of the movement, even though Bukem himself hated the term 'intelligent' that journalists attached to it, insisting that all drum and bass required intelligence to make and appreciate. The album introduced a generation to the more contemplative side of the genre, and it remains an essential document of drum and bass's golden age.

name: Diary of a Digital Soundboy
teaser: Shy FX 2005 — the jungle pioneer's debut album, recorded 13 years after his genre-defining track 'Original Nuttah'. The album spans jungle, reggae, dancehall, and liquid drum & bass, reflecting Shy FX's London upbringing where sound system culture and pirate radio were inseparable.

exploreAction.targetName: Diary of a Digital Soundboy (2005) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Feelings' — the vocal by Kele Le Roc was recorded at 4 AM after the studio had emptied. Then 'On the Run' — the track samples a 1960s Lee 'Scratch' Perry production and runs it through a digital delay so aggressive it almost breaks apart. The album title refers to Shy FX's belief that digital production tools had finally caught up with his imagination.

synopsis: Diary of a Digital Soundboy (2005) is the debut album of Shy FX, the jungle pioneer who had helped define the genre thirteen years earlier with 'Original Nuttah', and it shows the full range of a producer who had been at the heart of British dance music for over a decade. Shy FX, born Andre Williams, had made his name as a teenager with 'Original Nuttah', a track of such raw energy that it became one of the defining records of jungle, and Diary of a Digital Soundboy, recorded over years of evolution in the sound, moves between the fast breakbeats of his roots and the newer sounds of garage, grime and dancehall that had grown up around them. 'Shake It', a collaboration with the vocalist Di, became a massive hit, and tracks like 'Plastic Soul' and 'Feeling U' showed his range. The album is a document of one man's journey through the changing landscape of British dance music, and it confirmed Shy FX as one of the genre's most enduring figures.

name: Hard Normal Daddy
teaser: Squarepusher (Tom Jenkinson) 1997 — the album where a bass virtuoso applied jazz-fusion technique to drum & bass. Jenkinson played every instrument: bass guitar, drums, synthesizers. The bass solos — played on a 6-string bass through a distortion pedal at 180 BPM — sounded like a computer but were entirely human.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Beep Street' — the drum programming shifts time signatures every 4 bars while the bass plays a walking jazz line. Then 'Chin Hippy' — the track's central bass riff was recorded at half-speed and sped up, giving it an inhuman precision. Jenkinson's father was a jazz drummer; the album's complex rhythms are genetic.

synopsis: Hard Normal Daddy (1997) is the album where Squarepusher, the British producer and bass virtuoso Tom Jenkinson, proved that drum and bass could contain the technical brilliance of jazz fusion, and it remains one of the most astonishing displays of musicianship in electronic music. Jenkinson was a classically and jazz-trained bassist before he turned to electronic music, and Hard Normal Daddy is built on his extraordinary playing: live, upright bass solos weave in and out of the fastest, most complex breakbeats ever programmed, creating music that sounds like a virtuoso jazz trio being chased by a machine. Tracks like 'Cooper's World', 'Beep Street' and the title track are masterpieces of the form, full of warmth, humor and sheer technical audacity. The album was released on Warp Records, the home of the British electronic avant-garde, and it established Squarepusher as one of the most brilliant and unpredictable figures in the music, the record where drum and bass met jazz and produced something entirely new.

name: The Fat of the Land
teaser: The Prodigy 1997 — the album that took rave culture to #1 in 22 countries. Recorded in Liam Howlett's Essex home studio. The album fused breakbeats, punk energy, and arena-rock ambition. 'Firestarter' was the first electronic track to top the UK singles chart while simultaneously being banned from daytime radio.

exploreAction.targetName: The Fat of the Land (1997) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Smack My Bitch Up' — the track samples at least 6 different records including Ultramagnetic MCs and Rage Against the Machine. The video (banned by MTV) was shot from a first-person perspective of a night out. Then 'Breathe' — Keith Flint's sneering vocal was his attempt to channel the Sex Pistols. Flint was a dancer, not a singer; Howlett liked the amateur energy.

synopsis: The Fat of the Land (1997) is the album that took rave culture to the top of the charts in twenty-two countries and made The Prodigy, led by Liam Howlett, the biggest electronic act in the world. Howlett built the album in his home studio in Essex, layering the distorted, punk-tinged energy of the band's live shows with the hardest, most aggressive beats he could program, and the result was a record that sounded like nothing else on earth: rave, punk, hip-hop and metal all crushed together into music of pure adrenaline. 'Firestarter', with its menacing vocal and industrial beat, and 'Breathe' became massive global hits, 'Smack My Bitch Up', with its controversial lyrics and stunning video, showed the band's willingness to provoke, and 'Serial Thrilla' and 'Funky Shit' kept the energy at fever pitch. The album debuted at number one in the US and UK and sold millions, and it remains the most successful record of the rave generation, the sound of a subculture conquering the world.

name: Dig Your Own Hole
teaser: The Chemical Brothers 1997 — the album that made big beat the sound of the late 90s. Tom Rowlands and Ed Simons built tracks from psychedelic rock samples, hip-hop breakbeats, and acid house squelches. Noel Gallagher's guest vocal on 'Setting Sun' was recorded in a single afternoon after he'd been up all night.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Setting Sun' — the bassline is a slowed-down sample from a 1960s Indian classical record. Gallagher's vocal was recorded through a cheap microphone to make it sound distorted. Then 'Block Rockin' Beats' — the track won a Grammy for Best Rock Instrumental despite having no guitars. The Chemical Brothers' secret: they treated the sampler as a rock instrument.

tracks.title: Get Up on It Like This

synopsis: Dig Your Own Hole (1997) is the album where the Chemical Brothers, Tom Rowlands and Ed Simons, made big beat the defining sound of the late 1990s, a record of such swaggering, psychedelic confidence that it turned two British DJs into global stars. The duo had spent years building their reputation as the kings of the emerging big beat scene, and their second album, recorded in their London studio, delivered on every promise: 'Block Rockin' Beats', built on a pounding breakbeat and a sample of a funk bass line, became their biggest hit, 'Setting Sun', a collaboration with Noel Gallagher of Oasis, was a stunning fusion of rock and electronic music, and 'The Private Psychedelic Reel' and 'Where Do I Begin' showed their more experimental side. The album debuted at number one in Britain and made the duo the most successful electronic act of the era, and its influence on the music that followed, from dance rock to the sound of the 2000s, is enormous.

name: Rounds
teaser: Four Tet (Kieran Hebden) 2003 — an album made entirely on a desktop computer with found sounds: a squeaky door, a radio broadcast, an old folk record played at the wrong speed. Hebden stitched these fragments into something that felt organic, not digital. The album's warmth comes from its imperfections.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'My Angel Rocks Back and Forth' — the central melody is a music box sample slowed to half-speed. Then 'As Serious as Your Life' — the drum pattern was assembled from single hits Hebden recorded on a hand-held microphone in his kitchen. The album's title refers to the circular nature of Hebden's compositional method: ideas that loop back on themselves.

tracks.title: My Angel Rocks Back and Forth
And They All Look Broken Hearted

synopsis: Rounds (2003) is the album where Four Tet, the British producer Kieran Hebden, made his masterpiece, a record built almost entirely from found sounds and samples that sounds like nothing else in electronic music. Hebden made the album on a desktop computer in his flat in London, cutting up recordings of a squeaky door, a radio broadcast, a music box and countless other everyday sounds, along with samples of jazz and folk records, and weaving them into music of extraordinary warmth and delicacy: songs that feel less like electronic music and more like memories, full of the textures of real life. 'She Moves She' and 'Unspoken' are among the most beautiful tracks in his catalogue, 'Hands' and 'My Angel Rocks Back and Forth' show his gift for hypnotic repetition, and the album's overall mood, gentle, melancholic and strange, is entirely his own. Rounds was hailed as a masterpiece on release, and it remains one of the most beloved electronic albums of the 2000s, the record that proved electronic music could be made from the poetry of everyday sound.

name: Swim
teaser: Caribou (Dan Snaith) 2010 — an album about swimming through grief, built from liquid synthesizer arpeggios and submerged beats. Snaith has a PhD in mathematics; the album's complex polyrhythms were derived from mathematical models of water turbulence. Despite the academic origins, the album is deeply emotional.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Odessa' — the flute melody was played by Snaith's wife on a recorder purchased the day before. Then 'Sun' — the track builds for 6 minutes around a single chord before releasing into a chorus that feels like surfacing for air. Snaith recorded most of the album alone in a remote cabin during a Canadian winter.

synopsis: Swim (2010) is the album where Caribou, the Canadian producer Dan Snaith, made his most emotionally direct and acclaimed record, a collection of songs about swimming through grief that turned his signature blend of electronic and organic sound into something transcendent. Snaith wrote the album after the death of a close friend, and the record's submerged, liquid quality, all its synthesizer arpeggios and muffled drums, reflects the experience of being underwater, of moving through a world that feels distant and strange. 'Odessa' and 'Sun' are among his most beloved songs, built on gorgeous melodies and insistent rhythms, 'Kaili' and 'Bowls' show his gift for hypnotic repetition, and the album's combination of dancefloor energy and genuine melancholy made it his biggest commercial and critical success. Swim confirmed Snaith as one of the most gifted producers of his generation, and it remains the record where his emotional and musical ambitions finally met.

name: ISAM
teaser: Amon Tobin 2011 — an album built entirely from field recordings: a motorcycle engine, a wasp trapped in a jar, a creaking gate, human teeth chattering. No traditional instruments appear. Tobin, a Brazilian-born sound designer, spent 4 years collecting and processing sounds into an album that makes you question what music is.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Journeyman' — the percussion comes from recordings of falling bricks, a pneumatic drill, and a typewriter carriage return. Then 'Lost & Found' — the 'melody' is a violin sample that Tobin stretched until it became unrecognizable texture. The album was accompanied by a custom-designed 3D projection system for live shows.

synopsis: ISAM (2011) is the album where Amon Tobin, already one of the most technically brilliant producers in electronic music, pushed his craft to its absolute limit, building an entire record from field recordings that are almost impossible to recognize. Tobin, a Brazilian-born producer based in Montreal, recorded the album's sounds himself, capturing a motorcycle engine, a wasp trapped in a jar, a creaking gate, human voices and countless other sources, and then processed and sculpted them into music that sounds like it was made by machines from another planet. The result is an album of astonishing textures: rhythms that seem to move in impossible ways, melodies that emerge from the noise like signals from a distant civilization, and a sense of scale that few electronic records have ever matched. The album was accompanied by an extraordinary live show featuring a giant 3D cube, and it is now regarded as one of the most ambitious electronic albums of its era, the sound of a producer operating at the absolute frontier of what music can be.

name: Rossz Csillag Alatt Született
teaser: Venetian Snares (Aaron Funk) 2005 — an album of breakcore built around classical samples, named after a Hungarian phrase meaning 'born under a bad star'. Funk, a Canadian producer from Winnipeg, recorded the album after a trip to Hungary. The track titles are quotes from Hungarian poetry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hajnal' — the track opens with a solo violin from a 1930s Hungarian recording, then the drums explode at 120 BPM while the violin keeps playing, unaffected. Then 'Öngyilkos Vasárnap' — the title means 'Suicidal Sunday', a reference to the famous 'Gloomy Sunday' song. The album makes classical music and breakcore feel like they were always meant to be together.

synopsis: Rossz Csillag Alatt Született (2005) is the album where Venetian Snares, the Canadian producer Aaron Funk, made his most unlikely and most beautiful record, fusing the violent, chaotic rhythms of breakcore with the lush harmonies of classical music. The album's title is Hungarian for 'born under a bad star', and Funk made the record after visiting Budapest, where he fell in love with the city and its music; he built the album around samples of Hungarian classical recordings, including the music of Béla Bartók and other composers, and laid his trademark breakcore beats over them at terrifying speed. The result is music of astonishing contrast, at once brutal and beautiful: the strings soar and swoon while the drums batter and fragment, creating something that sounds like a classical orchestra being torn apart and reassembled in real time. 'Sikertelenség' and 'Öngyilkos Vasárnap' are the album's centerpieces, and it is now regarded as a landmark of experimental electronic music, the record where breakcore met high culture.

name: Tri Repetae
teaser: Autechre 1995 — the Sheffield duo's third album, where their sound shifted from melodic techno to something more abstract and machine-like. Sean Booth and Rob Brown built their own software to generate sounds no existing synthesizer could make. The album's title suggests 'three repetitions', but nothing on it repeats in any predictable way.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Clipper' — the track's rhythm is in 4/4 but every sound lands slightly off the grid, creating a sensation of constant unease. Then 'Eutow' — the central synth line seems to be made of melting metal. Autechre's music divides listeners: some hear noise, others hear structures too complex for the ear to decode on first listen.

synopsis: Tri Repetae (1995) is the album where Autechre, the Sheffield duo of Rob Brown and Sean Booth, made the leap from melodic techno to the cold, abstract machine music that would define their career, and it remains one of the most influential electronic albums of the 1990s. The duo's earlier records had been danceable, even warm, but Tri Repetae found them stripping their sound down to its mechanical essence: tracks built on hard, precise rhythms and dark, metallic textures, with melodies reduced to eerie fragments that seemed to be struggling to escape the machines that made them. 'Drane' and 'Clipper' are among the album's best-known tracks, 'Leterel' and 'E.P.' show the duo's gift for building hypnotic structures, and the album's overall mood, cold, alien and utterly compelling, was unlike anything else in electronic music. It is now regarded as a cornerstone of the intelligent techno movement, the record where two of the genre's most important figures found their true voice.

name: Kesto
teaser: Pan Sonic 2004 — the Finnish duo's 4-disc magnum opus of industrial minimalism. Mika Vainio and Ilpo Väisänen built their own electronic instruments from circuit boards and scrap metal. The album's 50 tracks range from 15-second bursts of pure noise to a single 67-minute drone piece that tests the limits of human patience.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the drone tracks at low volume. Pan Sonic's music is about texture, not structure: the way a frequency vibrates in your chest, the physical sensation of bass that's almost subsonic. Then try 'Havainto' — the entire track is a single tone that slowly changes timbre over 12 minutes. The album's title is Finnish for 'duration' or 'stamina'.

synopsis: Kesto (2004) is the four-disc magnum opus of Pan Sonic, the Finnish duo of Mika Vainio and Ilpo Väisänen, and it stands as one of the most ambitious and uncompromising documents in the history of electronic music. Pan Sonic had spent a decade building a reputation as the most extreme and rigorous practitioners of minimalist electronic music, constructing their own electronic instruments and using them to explore the raw physical properties of sound: pure sine waves, brutal bass frequencies, static, noise and silence, all arranged with the precision of sculptors. Kesto, whose title means 'duration', gathers four hours of their work, from austere minimalism to crushing noise to moments of strange, austere beauty, and it is music that demands total commitment from the listener. The album is not easy listening, but it is a profound meditation on the nature of sound itself, and it is now regarded as one of the essential documents of the experimental electronic underground.

name: OutRun
teaser: Kavinsky 2013 — the album that defined synthwave nostalgia. Named after the 1986 Sega arcade game, the album imagines a 1980s that never existed: neon grids, testarossas, and synthesized sunsets. Kavinsky's alter-ego is a teenager who died in a car crash in 1986 and returned as a zombie producer.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Nightcall' — the vocal is by Daft Punk's Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, processed through a vocoder. The track opened the film 'Drive'. Then 'ProtoVision' — the synth solo was played on a Roland Jupiter-8, the same synthesizer that scored every 80s action movie. The album's conceit — that it's the soundtrack to a film that doesn't exist — became the genre's defining idea.

synopsis: OutRun (2013) is the album that defined the sound of synthwave, a record of pure, loving nostalgia for a 1980s that never quite existed, and it made Kavinsky, the French producer born Vincent Belorgey, the genre's most famous figure. The album is named after the 1986 Sega arcade game, and its whole concept is built on that kind of retro-futurism: Kavinsky imagines himself as a character from a forgotten 80s movie, driving a Ferrari through a neon-lit night city, and his music, all pulsing synthesizers, booming drums and saxophone stabs, sounds exactly like that fantasy. 'Nightcall', which had already become famous through the film Drive, is the album's centerpiece, and 'Protovision', 'Odd Look' and the title track are pure, ecstatic synthwave. The album was a huge success and made Kavinsky an unlikely star, and it remains the definitive statement of a genre that has only grown more popular since, the sound of a decade remembered by people who were never there.

name: Dangerous Days
teaser: Perturbator (James Kent) 2014 — the darker, heavier side of synthwave. Kent, a French producer and metal guitarist, brought distorted guitars and horror-movie atmospherics to the genre. The album's cyberpunk dystopia feels less like nostalgia and more like a warning.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Humans Are Such Easy Prey' — the title is a reference to the Terminator franchise. Then 'She Is Young, She Is Beautiful, She Is Next' — the synth arpeggio at 2:30 was played on a Minimoog and run through a distortion pedal. Kent recorded the album in his Paris apartment at night, deliberately working in the dark to maintain the mood.

tracks.title: She Is Young, She Is Beautiful, She Is Next

synopsis: Dangerous Days (2014) is the album where Perturbator, the French producer and former metal guitarist James Kent, took synthwave into darker and heavier territory, and it remains the definitive statement of the genre's aggressive, cinematic side. Kent came to electronic music from playing guitar in metal bands, and his music brings that background to the retro-futurism of synthwave: the pulsing synthesizers and 80s nostalgia are still there, but they are wrapped in distorted, industrial textures and a menacing, dystopian atmosphere that owes as much to horror movies and cyberpunk as to the pop of the 1980s. 'Dangerous Days', 'Vengeance' and 'Future Club' are the album's standouts, and its blend of danceable energy and apocalyptic darkness made it a favorite of the growing synthwave scene. The album was a breakthrough for the genre, and it established Perturbator as one of its most important figures, the artist who showed that synthwave could be heavy, dark and genuinely frightening.

name: Galactic Melt
teaser: Com Truise (Seth Haley) 2011 — the album that perfected the 'slow-motion 80s' sound. Haley, a New Jersey graphic designer, built tracks from detuned analog synthesizers, gated reverb, and drum machines pitched down to the point of melting. The music sounds like a VHS tape of a corporate training video left in a hot car.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Brokendate' — the synth melody sounds like it's being played through a stretched cassette tape. Then 'VHS Sex' — the title says it all. Haley worked as an art director for a pharmaceutical company; the album's aesthetic was partly inspired by the cold, geometric graphics of 1980s drug advertisements.

synopsis: Galactic Melt (2011) is the album that perfected the sound of slow-motion 80s nostalgia, and it made Com Truise, the New Jersey producer Seth Haley, one of the most distinctive voices in electronic music. Haley, who worked as a graphic designer before turning to music, built his sound around a simple idea: what if the music of the early 1980s, the smooth synth pop and funk of the era, had been slowed down to a dreamlike crawl and played through damaged, dusty equipment? The result is music of extraordinary warmth and texture: chunky, off-kilter beats, lush analog synths and melodies that feel like half-remembered songs from an old television show. 'Flightwave', 'Terminal' and the title track are highlights, and the album's overall mood, nostalgic and strange, made it an instant favorite of the emerging chillwave and synthwave scenes. Galactic Melt is now regarded as a modern classic of electronic music, the record that made Com Truise the sound of memory itself.

name: Body Riddle
teaser: Clark (Chris Clark) 2006 — the Warp Records artist's breakthrough, an album of glitch-techno that sounds like a machine learning to feel. Clark played most of the acoustic instruments — strings, woodwinds, percussion — then processed them until the source was unrecognizable. The result is electronic music with something human trapped inside.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Herr Bar' — the track's central melody is a single piano note processed through six different effects chains simultaneously. Then 'Night Knuckles' — the rhythm sounds random but is actually a highly structured 11/8 pattern. Clark's secret: he records improvisations at 3 AM while half-asleep, then edits the most interesting moments.

synopsis: Body Riddle (2006) is the album where Clark, the British producer Chris Clark, made his breakthrough, a record of glitchy, intricate electronic music that sounds like a machine learning how to feel. Clark had released two albums of dense, difficult electronic music on Warp Records before Body Riddle, but this record found him letting melody and emotion into his sound for the first time: the beats are still fractured and hyper-detailed, but they now support soaring, almost pop-like melodies, played on everything from analog synthesizers to what sounds like music boxes and children's instruments. 'Ted', with its gorgeous, melancholic melody, and 'Vengeance Drools' and 'Rattlesnake' are among the highlights, and the album's blend of technical brilliance and genuine feeling made it his most accessible and acclaimed work. Body Riddle established Clark as one of the most gifted producers of his generation, the record where the machine finally learned to sing.

name: Room(s)
teaser: Machinedrum (Travis Stewart) 2011 — an album that fused footwork, jungle, and IDM into something new. Stewart, a North Carolina native, had been making music since age 10. The album's title refers to the different emotional spaces Stewart was navigating: grief, hope, anxiety, love.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'She Died There' — the track's vocal sample is a single phrase from an R&B record, pitched and glitched until it sounds like a skipping CD. Then 'U Don't Survive' — the 808 kick patterns are so fast they blur into a drone. Stewart produced the entire album on headphones in a Brooklyn apartment while his neighbors complained about the bass.

tracks.title: Now U Know tha Deal 4 Real

synopsis: Room(s) (2011) is the album where Machinedrum, the North Carolina producer Travis Stewart, fused the breakneck rhythms of Chicago footwork with jungle, UK garage and IDM to create something entirely new, and it remains his most celebrated record. Stewart had spent years making music on the fringes of the electronic underground, but Room(s) found him at the peak of his powers, building tracks of astonishing rhythmic complexity from the fastest, most intricate beat patterns imaginable: footwork's rapid-fire drums, jungle's rolling breaks and garage's swing all processed and arranged with the precision of a mathematician. 'She Died There' and 'Sacred Frequencies' are among the album's standouts, and its combination of intellectual rigor and dancefloor energy made it a favorite of critics and DJs alike. The album was hailed as one of the best electronic records of the year, and its influence on the wave of footwork and jungle-inspired music that followed is enormous.

name: Replica
teaser: Oneohtrix Point Never (Daniel Lopatin) 2011 — an album built almost entirely from samples of 1980s TV commercials. Lopatin processed the audio until the original content was unrecognizable, leaving only emotional residue. The result is an album that feels like watching Nick at Nite through a fever dream.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sleep Dealer' — the central sample is a single sustained note from a furniture commercial, stretched until it fills 3 minutes. Then 'Andro' — the 'melody' is a fragment of dialogue from an unknown 1980s soap opera. Lopatin described the album as 'music for a memory you're not sure you actually have.'

synopsis: Replica (2011) is the album where Oneohtrix Point Never, the American producer Daniel Lopatin, made his most radical and influential record, building almost the entire album from samples of 1980s television commercials. Lopatin, who had spent years making dreamy, nostalgic ambient music, discovered a collection of old commercial tapes and began sampling them, processing the jingles, voiceovers and sound effects until they became something entirely new: music that sounds like the ghost of consumer culture, full of uncanny, half-remembered fragments of advertising. 'Replica' and 'Sleep Dealer' are the album's centerpieces, and its blend of beauty and unease made it an instant classic of the experimental electronic scene. The album marked a turning point in Lopatin's career, moving him from cult ambient artist to one of the most important figures in contemporary electronic music, and its influence on the sample-heavy music of the following decade is incalculable.

name: Ravedeath, 1972
teaser: Tim Hecker 2011 — an album of digitally-abused pipe organ, recorded in a church in Reykjavik, then processed beyond recognition. Hecker and Ben Frost spent a day recording the church organ, then Hecker spent a year destroying the recordings — overdriving them, pitch-shifting them, burying them in static — until the sacred became profane.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'In the Fog I' — the pipe organ is audible but just barely, like hearing a church service from a block away. Then 'Studio Suicide, 1980' — a single sustained chord slowly dissolves into white noise over 9 minutes. The album's title refers not to a literal event but to the death of analog music in the digital age.

synopsis: Ravedeath, 1972 (2011) is the album where Tim Hecker, the Canadian producer who had spent years making some of the most beautiful ambient music in the world, turned to pure digital destruction, and the result is one of the most powerful and acclaimed records of his career. The album was recorded in a church in Reykjavik, where Hecker played a pipe organ, and the recordings were then processed and abused until the majestic instrument was transformed into something else entirely: a roaring, crumbling, beautiful wall of sound that seems to be collapsing in real time. 'The Piano Drop' and 'In the Air' are among the album's most striking tracks, and its blend of overwhelming noise and fragile beauty made it an instant classic of the ambient underground. The title refers to a photograph of a piano being dropped from a building in 1972, and the album has the same sense of destruction and release. It is now regarded as one of the most important ambient albums of the 21st century.

name: Lustmore
teaser: Lapalux (Stuart Howard) 2015 — a concept album about liminal states: the moment between sleep and waking, between sobriety and intoxication, between one relationship and the next. Howard, an Essex-born producer, built tracks from warped R&B samples, field recordings, and synthesizers so processed they sound liquid.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'U Never Know' — Andréya Triana's vocal was recorded at 1.5x speed, then slowed down to create an otherworldly timbre. Then 'Don't Mean a Thing' — the drum pattern was generated by a random algorithm Howard coded himself. The album's interlude tracks are recordings of Howard's friends describing their strangest dreams.

synopsis: Lustmore (2015) is the concept album where Lapalux, the British producer Stuart Howard, made his most ambitious and acclaimed record, a collection of songs about liminal states: the moment between sleep and waking, between intoxication and sobriety, between one world and another. The album's title comes from an archaic word for melancholy, and its music lives up to the name: dense, dreamy, half-submerged tracks built on layers of warped vocals, lush synths and intricate, off-kilter beats, all suffused with a sense of longing and dislocation. 'Displace' and 'The Third Person' are among the album's highlights, and its guest vocalists, including the singer Louisahhh, float through the mix like voices heard through a wall. The album was hailed as a landmark of the experimental R&B and beat scene, and it established Lapalux as one of the most gifted producers of his generation, the record where his dreamlike vision reached its fullest expression.

name: What's Going On
teaser: Marvin Gaye 1971 — Motown refused to release it. Berry Gordy called it uncommercial. Gaye threatened to leave the label he'd built his career on. It became the first political soul album, a song cycle about Vietnam, poverty, and environmental collapse, sung from the perspective of a returning veteran.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the vocal overdubs are layer upon layer. Notice how Gaye breathes 12 distinct times in the first 30 seconds; each breath is a punctuation mark. The album was recorded with members of the Detroit Symphony Orchestra who slipped out of rehearsals to play on the sessions.

tracks.title: Inner City Blues (Make Me Wanna Holler)

synopsis: What's Going On (1971) is Marvin Gaye's masterpiece, the album where the smoothest singer at Motown turned his back on the label's formula and made the most profound and influential record of his career, a concept album about the state of America that has never lost its power. Gaye had spent the late 1960s in a deep depression, mourning the death of his duet partner Tammi Terrell and questioning everything about his life and music, and he channeled that despair into this record: inspired by a song written by the Four Tops' Obie Benson about police brutality, Gaye wrote an album about war, poverty, racism, environmental destruction and faith, sung with a tenderness and desperation that made the politics feel deeply personal. Motown's Berry Gordy refused to release it, calling it uncommercial, but Gaye threatened to quit, and the album became his greatest success, producing the title track, 'Mercy Mercy Me (The Ecology)', 'Inner City Blues' and 'What's Happening Brother'. It is now universally regarded as one of the greatest albums ever made.

name: Innervisions
teaser: Stevie Wonder's 1973 album — recorded mostly alone, playing nearly every instrument himself. The album's opening is an arrhythmic assault; the closing track protests a food stamp cut. Three weeks after the album was released, Wonder was in a car accident that put him in a coma.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Higher Ground' — Stevie's clavinet entrance at 0:48 is a single note. The keyboard was lent to him by Clint Eastwood. Then 'Living for the City' — a 7-minute story of urban destitution with a spoken-word middle section featuring Stevie playing multiple characters. The police siren was an actual recording from outside the studio.

synopsis: Innervisions (1973) is the album where Stevie Wonder, already one of the most gifted musicians in popular music, made the record that is now regarded as his masterpiece, a stunning fusion of funk, soul, jazz and social commentary that set a new standard for what a pop album could be. Wonder wrote, produced and arranged the album, playing nearly every instrument himself, and its songs are a complete portrait of America in the early 1970s: 'Living for the City' is a devastating seven-minute epic about the journey of a young black man from the rural South to the violence of the city, 'Higher Ground' is a funk masterpiece about spiritual rebirth, 'Don't You Worry 'Bout a Thing' shows his joyful side, and 'Golden Lady' and 'All in Love Is Fair' are gorgeous ballads. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys and is now regarded as one of the greatest records ever made, the moment Wonder fully realized the extraordinary promise he had shown since childhood.

name: Songs in the Key of Life
teaser: Stevie Wonder's 1976 double album + bonus EP — released the day before his 26th birthday. He had threatened to quit music and move to Ghana; Motown gave him unprecedented creative control to keep him. The album took 3 years to make and used over 130 musicians.

exploreAction.targetName: Songs in the Key of Life (1976) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Wish' — one of the most-sampled songs in history. The backwards-mixed bassline in the first 8 bars was an accident. Then 'Pastime Paradise' — Coolio sampled it 20 years later for 'Gangsta's Paradise'. Then 'As' — Stevie recorded the vocal so loud it distorted the tape; they kept it.

tracks.title: Love's in Need of Love Today
Ngiculela – Es Una Historia – I Am Singing

synopsis: Songs in the Key of Life (1976) is the double album where Stevie Wonder, at the absolute peak of his powers, made the most ambitious and celebrated record of his career, a sprawling masterpiece that has never been out of print. Wonder had spent the early 1970s reinventing popular music with a series of stunning albums, and he announced that he was quitting music to focus on his spiritual life before returning with this record, released on the day before his 26th birthday. The album's twenty-one songs cover an astonishing range: 'Isn't She Lovely', written for his newborn daughter, 'Sir Duke', a tribute to Duke Ellington, 'Pastime Paradise', later sampled by Coolio for 'Gangsta's Paradise', 'As', 'Knocks Me Off My Feet' and the epic 'Village Ghetto Land'. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys and is now regarded as one of the greatest records of the 1970s, the moment Wonder's genius reached its fullest expression.

name: Blonde
teaser: Frank Ocean's 2016 second album — released without promotion in two physical editions, then never officially made available for streaming for months. Recorded across Abbey Road, Electric Lady, and a house in Japan. The album's most-quoted track 'Self Control' was co-written with Alex G.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Self Control' — the vocal and guitar are layered until they sound like a memory being assembled in real time. Then 'Nights' — the song is two halves: a contemplative 2-minute introduction, then at exactly the midpoint a beat switch so abrupt it feels like falling. Ocean sings the entire album from the perspective of someone looking back.

synopsis: Blonde (2016) is Frank Ocean's second album, and it is one of the most beloved and influential records of the 2010s, a stunningly intimate and experimental work that seemed to exist entirely on its own terms. Ocean released the album with almost no promotion, after years of delays and legal battles, and it appeared in two physical editions before being made available for streaming, an act of artistic defiance that became part of its legend. The album is built on sparse, gorgeous arrangements, with Ocean's voice, vulnerable and pitch-perfect, floating over guitars, pianos and strange electronic textures, and its songs deal with love, loss, sexuality, memory and faith with a rawness that few artists had ever brought to mainstream pop. 'Nikes', 'Ivy', 'Pink + White', 'Self Control' and the closing 'Godspeed' are among the most beautiful songs of the decade, and the album's influence on the R&B and pop that followed is enormous. Blonde is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 2010s.

name: Channel Orange
teaser: Frank Ocean's 2012 debut — released the same day he published an open Tumblr letter about his first love being a man. The album blends Prince, Stevie Wonder, and a stripped-down indie-R&B. It won a Grammy and changed the sound of pop music for the next decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Thinkin Bout You' — the most-quoted track, recorded in a single afternoon. Then 'Pyramids' — a 10-minute exercise in doubling: John Mayer plays guitar at 7:40 while Frank's opening vocal returns as a ghost at 0:01 of the second half. The song spans ancient Egypt and a modern strip club without losing coherence.

synopsis: Channel Orange (2012) is the debut album of Frank Ocean, and it announced one of the most singular talents in modern music, a record of stunning originality that redefined what R&B could be. Ocean had spent years as a songwriter for other artists before releasing his own music, and his debut arrived with extraordinary context: the same day the album appeared, Ocean published an open letter revealing that his first love had been a man, a confession that made him a pioneer of queer visibility in hip-hop and R&B. The album itself is a masterpiece of atmosphere and invention, its songs built on lush, cinematic production and Ocean's extraordinary voice, which could move from a whisper to a falsetto cry in a second. 'Thinkin Bout You', 'Pyramids', a stunning ten-minute epic, 'Bad Religion', 'Sweet Life' and 'Forrest Gump' are among the highlights, and the album's blend of personal confession and cinematic ambition made it an instant classic, nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys.

name: Sunday at the Village Vanguard
teaser: Bill Evans Trio 1961 — recorded live at the Village Vanguard on June 25, 1961, just 10 days before bassist Scott LaFaro died in a car accident at age 25. The trio's telepathic interplay, particularly between Evans and LaFaro, redefined the piano trio format from rhythm-section-plus-soloist to three equal voices.

exploreAction.targetName: Sunday at the Village Vanguard (1961) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Gloria's Step' — LaFaro's bass solo is the lead voice while Evans comps behind him. Then 'Alice in Wonderland' — Evans plays the melody so quietly you lean in to hear it. The album captures the last performance of one of jazz's greatest trios; LaFaro would be dead within two weeks.

synopsis: Sunday at the Village Vanguard (1961) is one of the most celebrated live jazz albums ever recorded, and its history gives it an almost unbearable poignancy: the music was recorded on June 25, 1961, just ten days before the trio's bassist, Scott LaFaro, was killed in a car accident at the age of 25. The Bill Evans Trio, with Evans on piano, LaFaro on bass and Paul Motian on drums, had spent two years developing a revolutionary approach to jazz, in which the three musicians interacted as equal partners rather than a soloist with accompaniment, and this album captures that telepathic communication at its peak. The interplay between Evans and LaFaro, in particular, is regarded as one of the highest achievements in jazz: 'Gloria's Step', 'Alice in Wonderland' and 'My Man's Gone Now' are among the most beautiful recordings the music has ever produced. The album was released after LaFaro's death, and it stands as a heartbreaking monument to one of the most gifted musicians jazz has ever known.

name: Brilliant Corners
teaser: Thelonious Monk 1957 — an album so difficult the title track had to be assembled from 25 separate takes because the band couldn't play it all the way through. Monk's compositions use dissonant chords and angular melodies that sound wrong until they suddenly sound inevitable. The album took 3 sessions to record, nearly unprecedented for jazz at the time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the tempo changes three times, and the saxophone solo by Sonny Rollins had to be spliced from multiple takes because the chord changes were so unusual. Then 'Pannonica' — a ballad named for Baroness Pannonica de Koenigswarter, Monk's patron and friend, played on the celeste.

tracks.title: (4) I Surrender, Dear (Harry Barris, Gordon Clifford)

synopsis: Brilliant Corners (1957) is the album where Thelonious Monk, the most idiosyncratic genius in jazz, made his most ambitious and enduring statement, a record so difficult that the title track had to be assembled from twenty-five separate takes because no single performance was clean enough. Monk's music had always been strange, full of jarring dissonances, unexpected pauses and rhythms that seemed to lurch and stumble, and Brilliant Corners pushed that strangeness to its limit: the title track, with its constantly shifting tempo and fiendishly difficult written melody, is one of the most demanding pieces in the jazz repertoire, while 'Ba-Lue Bolivar Ba-Lues-Are' and 'Pannonica', named for his patroness, show his more lyrical side. The album features a rotating cast of brilliant musicians, including Sonny Rollins, Max Roach and Clark Terry, and its recording sessions were legendary for their difficulty. It is now regarded as Monk's masterpiece, the record where his revolutionary vision reached its fullest expression.

name: Saxophone Colossus
teaser: Sonny Rollins 1956 — recorded in a single day at Rudy Van Gelder's studio. Rollins was 25 and already a master. The album's centerpiece 'Blue 7' is an 11-minute blues that jazz critics have analyzed bar-by-bar as an example of 'thematic improvisation' — Rollins develops a single motif across the entire solo.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'St. Thomas' — Rollins adapted a Caribbean folk melody his mother sang to him as a child. The calypso rhythm was radical for jazz in 1956. Then 'Blue 7' — track Rollins's opening 4-note motif as it transforms across 11 minutes. He plays the entire solo without ever repeating himself.

tracks.title: You Don't Know What Love Is

synopsis: Saxophone Colossus (1956) is the album that made Sonny Rollins, still only 25 years old, the most celebrated tenor saxophonist in jazz, and it remains one of the most important records in the history of the instrument. Rollins recorded the album in a single day at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in New Jersey with a quartet featuring Tommy Flanagan on piano, Doug Watkins on bass and Max Roach on drums, and the result was a masterpiece of hard bop: 'St. Thomas', based on a calypso melody Rollins had heard as a child in the Virgin Islands, became his signature tune, and 'Blue 7', 'You Don't Know What Love Is' and 'Strode Rode' showed his extraordinary command of the instrument. Rollins' sound was huge, warm and endlessly inventive, and his ability to develop a solo from a single idea made him the model for a generation of saxophonists. Saxophone Colossus is now regarded as one of the greatest jazz albums ever recorded.

name: Out to Lunch!
teaser: Eric Dolphy 1964 — his only album for Blue Note, recorded just months before he died of undiagnosed diabetes at 36. Dolphy's compositions use intervals so wide they sound like the melody is falling down stairs. The album features a teenage Tony Williams on drums and Freddie Hubbard on trumpet.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hat and Beard' — the title refers to Thelonious Monk. The rhythm section plays in 5/4 while Dolphy's bass clarinet solo floats free of any time signature. Then 'Something Sweet, Something Tender' — Dolphy plays the entire melody on bass clarinet in its highest register, making it sound like a completely different instrument.

synopsis: Out to Lunch! (1964) is the only album Eric Dolphy recorded for Blue Note, and it stands as one of the most original and influential jazz records of the 1960s, made by a musician who died just months after the session at the age of 36. Dolphy, a virtuoso of the alto saxophone, flute and bass clarinet, was one of the most adventurous musicians in jazz, and Out to Lunch! found him at the peak of his powers, leading a quintet that included Freddie Hubbard on trumpet, Bobby Hutcherson on vibraphone, Richard Davis on bass and Tony Williams on drums. The album's compositions, including 'Out to Lunch', 'Something Sweet, Something Tender' and 'Hat and Beard', named for Thelonious Monk, are full of Dolphy's signature angularity and wit, moving through shifting meters and unexpected harmonies with total freedom. Dolphy died of undiagnosed diabetes weeks after the session, and the album has taken on an almost mythic status, the final testament of one of jazz's most original voices.

name: The Shape of Jazz to Come
teaser: Ornette Coleman 1959 — the album that launched free jazz and divided the jazz world. Coleman abandoned chord changes entirely, playing melodies that followed their own logic. Miles Davis said Coleman was 'all screwed up inside'; others heard liberation. The album's title was a manifesto.

exploreAction.targetName: The Shape of Jazz to Come (1959) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Lonely Woman' — the opening is a single held drum cymbal and a bowed bass note while Coleman and Don Cherry play a melody that sounds like crying. Then 'Congeniality' — Coleman's plastic alto saxophone (he played a white plastic Grafton) produces a sound no metal saxophone can make. The album's rules are: there are no rules.

synopsis: The Shape of Jazz to Come (1959) is the album that launched free jazz and split the jazz world in two, a record so radical that it is still debated more than sixty years later. Ornette Coleman, an alto saxophonist from Texas, had developed a revolutionary approach to improvisation: instead of playing over the chord changes of a song, his band played freely, improvising together without a predetermined harmonic structure, a style he called 'harmolodics'. The album, recorded with Don Cherry on trumpet, Charlie Haden on bass and Billy Higgins on drums, outraged traditionalists who heard chaos, but it thrilled those who heard the future. 'Lonely Woman' is the album's most famous track, a haunting, blues-tinged lament that has become a jazz standard, and 'Eventually' and 'Peace' show the range of the band's approach. The album is now regarded as one of the most important in jazz history, the record that gave musicians permission to play whatever they heard.

name: Spiritual Unity
teaser: Albert Ayler 1965 — 29 minutes that sound like a saxophone being exorcised. Recorded in a single afternoon for $350. Ayler's sound — wide vibrato, upper-register screams, folk-like melodies buried in chaos — divided listeners violently. But his influence on later avant-garde and free jazz is incalculable.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Ghosts: First Variation' — the melody sounds like a nursery rhyme played through a megaphone at a funeral. Then 'Spirits' — Ayler's sound has been described as 'a saxophone trying to talk.' Gary Peacock's bass and Sunny Murray's drums don't keep time; they create texture. The album is 29 minutes; it feels like both more and less.

synopsis: Spiritual Unity (1965) is the album where Albert Ayler, the most radical saxophonist in the history of jazz, made his definitive statement, a record so raw and intense that it sounds like a saxophone being exorcised. Ayler had developed a style that abandoned conventional melody and harmony almost entirely, playing with a huge, shaking tone full of screams, honks and multiphonics, sounds that seemed to come from somewhere beyond music, and his trio, with bassist Gary Peacock and drummer Sunny Murray, created a sound that was part church service, part primal scream. The album's two extended pieces, 'Ghosts' and 'Spirits', were recorded in a single afternoon for a fee of $350, and they capture Ayler at his most transcendent: music that sounded like the end of the world and the beginning of a new one at the same time. Ayler drowned in 1970 under mysterious circumstances, and Spiritual Unity stands as the purest document of his extraordinary, terrifying genius.

name: Space Is the Place
teaser: Sun Ra 1973 — the Arkestra's afrofuturist manifesto, recorded in Chicago with a 20-piece big band playing free jazz, swing, funk, and chants about Saturn. Sun Ra claimed he was from outer space and used the album to outline his philosophy: Black people must leave Earth and colonize a new planet.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — it's 21 minutes, opening with a chant declaring that outer space is the only escape from earthly oppression. Then 'Images' — a composition for flute, bells, and voice that sounds like ancient Egyptian music beamed through a wormhole. Sun Ra's keyboard solo uses a Moog synthesizer in ways Bob Moog never intended.

synopsis: Space Is the Place (1973) is the album where Sun Ra, the visionary bandleader who claimed to be from Saturn, made his most complete musical statement, a record that fused free jazz, swing, funk and afrofuturist philosophy into something entirely his own. Sun Ra led the Arkestra, a rotating collective of musicians who lived together in a house in Philadelphia, rehearsing constantly and performing in wild, elaborate costumes, and his music was always in service of a larger vision: that black people would one day escape the oppression of Earth and find freedom in space. The album, recorded in Chicago with a twenty-piece big band, moves between the roaring free jazz of the title track and 'Discipline 27-II', the ecstatic funk of 'Sea of Sounds' and the swinging 'Rocket Number Nine Take Off for the Planet Venus', all of it sounding like a transmission from another world. Space Is the Place is now regarded as a masterpiece of afrofuturism, and its influence on everything from jazz to hip-hop to science fiction is enormous.

name: Moanin'
teaser: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers 1959 — the definitive hard bop album. Blakey's Jazz Messengers was a finishing school for jazz talent; alumni include Wayne Shorter, Lee Morgan, Freddie Hubbard, and Wynton Marsalis. The title track's call-and-response between piano and horns became a jazz standard.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Benny Golson wrote it specifically for Blakey's drumming style. The piano riff by Bobby Timmons is 8 bars of pure blues. Then 'Along Came Betty' — Golson's composition is a masterclass in arranging for a 5-piece band. Blakey's press rolls on the snare are so precise they sound like a single sustained note.

tracks.title: The Drum Thunder (Miniature) Suite" / "First Theme: Drum Thunder" / "Second Theme: Cry a Blue Tear" / "Third Theme: Harlem's Disciples
Warm-up and dialogue between Lee Morgan and Rudy Van Gelder

synopsis: Moanin' (1959) is the definitive hard bop album, the record where Art Blakey and his Jazz Messengers, the most important finishing school in jazz history, made their masterpiece. Blakey, a drummer of explosive power, had been leading the Jazz Messengers since the mid-1950s, and the band was a proving ground for the greatest young musicians in jazz, including, over the years, Horace Silver, Clifford Brown, Lee Morgan, Wayne Shorter and Wynton Marsalis. On Moanin', Blakey was joined by a classic lineup: Lee Morgan on trumpet, Benny Golson on tenor saxophone, Bobby Timmons on piano and Jymie Merritt on bass, and the album's title track, written by Timmons, with its famous gospel-tinged melody and call-and-response vocals, became one of the most beloved jazz tunes ever recorded. The album also contains Golson's 'Blues March' and 'Along Came Betty', and its blend of blues, gospel and bop made it the model for hard bop, the sound of jazz getting back to its roots and its joy.

name: Somethin' Else
teaser: Cannonball Adderley 1958 — the only Blue Note album where Miles Davis appears as a sideman. Davis chose the material and effectively led the session. The album's 10-minute version of 'Autumn Leaves' is studied by jazz students as the definitive small-group performance of a standard.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Autumn Leaves' — Miles Davis's muted trumpet solo is 2 choruses that say more with silence than notes. Then 'Love for Sale' — Adderley's alto sax solo quotes no less than 5 other standards in passing. The album's rhythm section — Hank Jones, Sam Jones, Art Blakey — recorded these tracks in a single afternoon.

synopsis: Somethin' Else (1958) is the only Blue Note album on which Miles Davis appears as a sideman, and that alone would make it historic, but the record is also one of the great jazz albums of its era, a masterclass in relaxed, bluesy sophistication. Cannonball Adderley, the brilliant alto saxophonist who was then a member of Davis's sextet, led the session, and Davis, returning the favor, played trumpet on it, along with Hank Jones on piano, Sam Jones on bass and Art Blakey on drums. Davis effectively chose the material and shaped the session, and the result has the relaxed, unhurried feel of his own best records: 'Autumn Leaves' became the definitive version of the standard, 'Love for Sale' swings with effortless cool, and 'One for Daddy-O' and the title track are originals that have become standards themselves. The album is now regarded as a masterpiece of hard bop, the record where two of jazz's greatest musicians made magic together.

name: Speak No Evil
teaser: Wayne Shorter 1966 — his third Blue Note album as leader, recorded with Herbie Hancock, Ron Carter, Elvin Jones, and Freddie Hubbard. Shorter's compositions blur the line between hard bop and the modal freedom that would define his work with Miles Davis. Every track has a mystery at its center.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the melody sounds like a question that never gets answered. Then 'Infant Eyes' — a ballad Shorter wrote for his daughter, played with such tenderness by Hubbard that it feels like a lullaby. Hancock's piano comping is so sparse he sometimes plays only one chord per bar.

synopsis: Speak No Evil (1966) is the album where Wayne Shorter, already the most important composer in jazz through his work with Art Blakey and Miles Davis, made his masterpiece as a leader, and it remains one of the greatest jazz records of the 1960s. Shorter recorded the album with a stunning lineup of his peers, Herbie Hancock on piano, Ron Carter on bass, Elvin Jones on drums and Freddie Hubbard on trumpet, and the music they made is full of the dark, mysterious beauty that defined Shorter's vision: compositions like 'Witch Hunt', 'Speak No Evil', 'Fee-Fi-Fo-Fum' and 'Infant Eyes' move through strange, shifting harmonies with a sense of drama and melancholy that no one else in jazz could match. Shorter's tenor saxophone playing is at its most expressive, and the interplay between the quintet is telepathic. The album is now regarded as a cornerstone of the Blue Note catalog and one of the essential jazz records of the decade.

name: Karma
teaser: Pharoah Sanders 1969 — a 32-minute track on side A called 'The Creator Has a Master Plan', the definitive spiritual jazz anthem. Sanders had been John Coltrane's protégé; after Coltrane's death, Sanders carried forward the spiritual dimension of his mentor's music. Leon Thomas's yodeling vocal was unlike anything in jazz.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Creator Has a Master Plan' — Sanders's tenor saxophone sounds like it's praying. Leon Thomas's yodel was learned from Central African pygmy singers he'd studied. The bassline by Reggie Workman repeats a two-note figure for the entire 32 minutes, becoming a meditation.

tracks.title: The Creator Has a Master Plan

synopsis: Karma (1969) is the album where Pharoah Sanders, the saxophonist who had carried the flame of John Coltrane's spiritual music after Coltrane's death, made his definitive statement, a record of transcendent, ecstatic jazz that is now regarded as the pinnacle of the spiritual jazz movement. The album's entire first side is taken up by 'The Creator Has a Master Plan', a thirty-two-minute suite that moves from a gentle, hypnotic melody through passages of explosive collective improvisation and back again, with Sanders' huge, keening tenor saxophone crying out over the rhythm section and Leon Thomas's extraordinary yodelling vocals, which sounded like a man speaking in tongues. The music builds to an almost unbearable intensity before resolving into peace, and its combination of African rhythms, Eastern philosophy and gospel fervor made it a touchstone for a generation of musicians. Karma is now regarded as one of the most important jazz albums of the 1960s, the sound of music as spiritual quest.

name: Getz/Gilberto
teaser: Stan Getz and João Gilberto 1964 — the album that launched bossa nova globally. Recorded in New York over two days. Astrud Gilberto had never sung professionally; she was at the session to translate for her husband João. When they needed an English vocal on 'The Girl from Ipanema', she volunteered. The take they used was her first public performance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Girl from Ipanema' — Astrud's untrained, breathy vocal was considered a weakness at the time; it became the defining bossa nova vocal sound. Then 'Corcovado' — João Gilberto's guitar playing uses a rhythm so subtle it's almost subliminal. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys, the first jazz album to do so.

synopsis: Getz/Gilberto (1964) is the album that introduced bossa nova to the world and made it a global phenomenon, a record of such gentle, effortless beauty that it remains one of the best-selling jazz albums of all time. The album brought together the American tenor saxophonist Stan Getz, whose warm, breathy sound was perfect for the music, and the Brazilian guitarist and singer João Gilberto, who had helped create bossa nova in the late 1950s, along with the composer Antônio Carlos Jobim on piano. Recorded in New York over two days, the album is anchored by 'The Girl from Ipanema', sung by João's wife Astrud Gilberto, whose shy, untrained voice became one of the most famous in music history, and it also contains 'Corcovado', 'Desafinado' and 'Doralice'. The album won the Grammy for Album of the Year and sold millions, and its blend of samba rhythm and cool jazz made it the soundtrack of an era, the sound of sophistication itself.

name: Wave
teaser: Antônio Carlos Jobim 1967 — the bossa nova composer's most fully realized solo album. Jobim wrote nearly every classic bossa nova standard; this album collects his instrumental versions, played with a restraint that makes the melodies feel inevitable. Claus Ogerman's string arrangements wrap the songs in late-60s sophistication.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Jobim's piano is so understated it barely exists. Then 'Triste' — the melody is 16 bars that feel like they've always existed. Jobim's genius was writing songs that sounded like they were discovered, not composed. The album was recorded in Rudy Van Gelder's studio with a full orchestra in a single day.

synopsis: Wave (1967) is the most fully realized solo album of Antônio Carlos Jobim, the Brazilian composer who wrote nearly every classic of bossa nova and who is regarded as one of the greatest songwriters of the 20th century. After the worldwide success of bossa nova, which Jobim had helped create with songs like 'The Girl from Ipanema' and 'Corcovado', he made this album with the arranger Claus Ogerman, who gave his music lush, orchestral settings that perfectly matched the sophistication of the compositions. The title track, with its unforgettable melody, became one of the most covered instrumental tunes in the world, and the album also contains 'Wave', 'Triste', 'Antigua' and Jobim's beautiful settings of his own songs. The record's blend of samba rhythm, jazz harmony and classical elegance made it an instant classic, and it is now regarded as one of the essential albums of Brazilian music and of the 1960s, the sound of a master at the peak of his powers.

name: Night Train
teaser: Oscar Peterson Trio 1963 — recorded in a single evening session. The album's laid-back, blues-inflected swing made it one of the best-selling jazz albums of the 60s. Peterson's technique — his right hand could play faster than most pianists could think — is on full display, but it's the tastefulness that impresses.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the bassline by Ray Brown walks with the authority of a freight train. Then 'C Jam Blues' — Peterson quotes no less than 8 other songs in his solo, a game of musical spot-the-reference. The album was recorded so fast that the band didn't realize they'd made a classic until they heard the playback.

tracks.title: Things Ain't What They Used to Be
I Got It Bad (and That Ain't Good)

synopsis: Night Train (1963) is one of the best-loved albums in the vast catalog of Oscar Peterson, the Canadian pianist whose dazzling technique made him one of the most celebrated musicians in jazz, and it is a masterclass in relaxed, bluesy swing. Peterson recorded the album with his trio, Ray Brown on bass and Ed Thigpen on drums, in a single evening session, and the album's title track, a blues associated with Jimmy Forrest, became one of the most recognizable melodies in jazz. The album is full of the effortless virtuosity that made Peterson legendary, from the swinging 'C-Jam Blues' and 'Georgia on My Mind' to the tender 'My Heart Stood Still', and its overall mood, laid-back and joyful, made it a favorite of both jazz connoisseurs and casual listeners. Night Train is now regarded as one of the essential piano trio albums, the record where Peterson's extraordinary gifts were captured at their most accessible and most sublime.

name: I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You
teaser: Aretha Franklin 1967 — her Atlantic Records debut and the album that crowned her the Queen of Soul. Recorded at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama with the legendary Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section. The first single 'I Never Loved a Man' was recorded at 3 AM after a fight between Aretha's husband and the studio owner shut down the session.

exploreAction.targetName: I Never Loved a Man (1967) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Respect' — the song was Otis Redding's, but Aretha's version (with her own added 'sock it to me' bridge and sister backing vocals) completely reclaimed it. Then 'Do Right Woman, Do Right Man' — Aretha plays piano herself, a fact often forgotten. The album was recorded in just 9 days.

tracks.title: I Never Loved a Man (The Way I Love You)
Don't Let Me Lose This Dream
Dr. Feelgood (Love Is a Serious Business)
Do Right Woman, Do Right Man

synopsis: I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You (1967) is the album that crowned Aretha Franklin the Queen of Soul, the record where the most gifted singer of her generation finally found the sound that would define her career. Franklin had spent years at Columbia Records, where her immense talent was never quite captured, and her move to Atlantic Records changed everything: recording at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, with the young producer Jerry Wexler and a band of brilliant Southern musicians, she finally made music that matched the power and passion of her voice. The album's title track became her first number one single, and 'Respect', her transformation of an Otis Redding song into a feminist and civil rights anthem, became one of the defining records of the decade. The album also contains 'Do Right Woman, Do Right Man' and 'Dr. Feelgood', and its blend of gospel fervor, Southern soul and Franklin's extraordinary piano playing made it an instant classic, the record that changed the course of American music.

name: Otis Blue: Otis Redding Sings Soul
teaser: Otis Redding 1965 — recorded in a 24-hour marathon session at Stax Studios in Memphis. Redding's voice — rough, pleading, erupting into screams that never lost the melody — defined Southern soul. The album covers Sam Cooke, the Temptations, and the Rolling Stones and makes each song feel like it was written for Otis.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I've Been Loving You Too Long' — recorded in a single take. Redding's vocal starts as a whisper and builds to a scream that sounds like it cost him something. Then 'Respect' — the original version, before Aretha transformed it. Stax's house band Booker T. & the M.G.'s played on every track; their groove is the album's secret weapon.

tracks.title: I've Been Loving You Too Long

synopsis: Otis Blue: Otis Redding Sings Soul (1965) is the album where Otis Redding, the most powerful and passionate singer in soul music, made his definitive statement, a record recorded in a single twenty-four-hour marathon session at Stax Studios in Memphis. Redding's voice, rough, pleading and capable of erupting into a scream of pure feeling, was one of the greatest instruments in popular music, and Otis Blue captures it at its peak: 'I've Been Loving You Too Long', his own composition, became a classic, and his versions of 'Respect', later made famous by Aretha Franklin, 'Satisfaction', 'My Girl' and 'A Change Is Gonna Come' showed his genius for making other people's songs his own. The album also contains the devastating ballad 'Pain in My Heart', and its blend of gospel, blues and Southern soul made it the template for the Stax sound. Redding died in a plane crash two years later, at 26, and Otis Blue stands as the definitive document of his extraordinary voice.

name: Call Me
teaser: Al Green 1973 — recorded at Royal Studios in Memphis with producer Willie Mitchell. Green's falsetto floats over Hi Records' signature sound: tight drums, warm organ, and the Memphis Horns. The album made Green a star while he was secretly struggling with his faith, eventually becoming an ordained pastor.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Call Me (Come Back Home)' — the bassline by Leroy Hodges is two notes for the entire song. Then 'Here I Am (Come and Take Me)' — Green's falsetto sounds effortless, but the yearning underneath is real. Mitchell's production secret: record everything quietly, then turn it up. The intimacy is in the headroom.

tracks.title: Have You Been Making Out O.K.
I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry
Your Love Is Like the Morning Sun
Here I Am (Come and Take Me)
You Ought to Be with Me

synopsis: Call Me (1973) is the album where Al Green, the most gifted soul singer of his generation, made the masterpiece of his classic period, a record of such tender, sensual beauty that it is now regarded as one of the greatest soul albums ever made. Green recorded the album at Royal Studios in Memphis with the producer Willie Mitchell, whose Hi Records sound, built on the deep, hypnotic grooves of the Hi Rhythm Section, was the perfect setting for Green's extraordinary voice, which could float into a featherlight falsetto or drop into a rasping cry of passion. 'Call Me (Come Back Home)', 'Here I Am (Come and Take Me)' and 'I'm Still in Love with You' are among the most beautiful love songs ever recorded, and the album's blend of sacred feeling and profane desire gives it a tension that few records have matched. Call Me was the peak of Green's commercial success, and it stands as the definitive statement of his genius, made just before he left secular music for the ministry.

name: Live at the Harlem Square Club, 1963
teaser: Sam Cooke 1963 — recorded at a sweaty Miami club before a mostly Black audience. RCA shelved it for 22 years because Cooke sounded too raw, too Black, too much like a gospel preacher instead of a pop crooner. Released posthumously in 1985, it's now recognized as one of the greatest live albums ever.

exploreAction.targetName: Live at the Harlem Square Club (1963)
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Chain Gang' — Cooke transforms a pop single into a call-and-response with the audience that builds for 5 minutes. Then 'Bring It On Home to Me' — the audience sings the chorus unprompted. Cooke's band, led by King Curtis on sax, plays with the energy of a gospel revival. The album was recorded on a single microphone suspended from the ceiling.

tracks.title: Medley: It's All Right/For Sentimental Reasons (Cooke/Deke Watson, William Best)
Bring It On Home to Me

synopsis: Live at the Harlem Square Club, 1963 (recorded 1963, released 1985) is one of the greatest live soul albums ever made, and its history is almost as remarkable as its music: RCA Records shelved the recording for twenty-two years because Sam Cooke sounded too raw, too Black, too unlike the smooth pop star they had created. The album captures Cooke performing at a sweaty club in Miami before an ecstatic, mostly Black audience, and it shows a completely different side of the singer who had conquered the pop charts with songs like 'You Send Me': here, his voice is gritty, gospel-soaked and utterly electrifying, driving the crowd into a frenzy with 'Bring It On Home to Me', 'Having a Party' and a stunning version of 'Twistin' the Night Away'. The recording was released in 1985, twenty-one years after Cooke was killed, and it immediately took its place as one of the essential documents of soul music, proof that the smooth pop star was also one of the greatest rhythm and blues singers who ever lived.

name: Baduizm
teaser: Erykah Badu 1997 — the album that launched neo-soul. Recorded in New York and Philadelphia over a year. Badu's voice — jazzy, conversational, floating between singing and speech — was unlike anything in 90s R&B. The album's organic sound, built on live instrumentation and Fender Rhodes, rejected the synth-heavy production dominating the era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'On & On' — Badu wrote it in 15 minutes while waiting for a bus. The lyrics are a stream of cosmic consciousness. Then 'Next Lifetime' — a love song told from the perspective of someone who believes in reincarnation. The album's production by the Roots' Questlove and others used vintage analog equipment to achieve its warm, timeless sound.

synopsis: Baduizm (1997) is the debut album of Erykah Badu, and it launched the neo-soul movement, a record of such confident originality that it felt like a new genre arriving fully formed. Badu, born Erica Wright in Dallas, brought together the warmth of 1970s soul, the intelligence of jazz, the politics of conscious hip-hop and her own fiercely individual vision, and the result was music that sounded both timeless and completely new. Her voice, jazzy, conversational and full of Southern warmth, was unlike anything on the radio, and her lyrics, full of Afrocentric pride, spiritual searching and unapologetic womanhood, made her an instant icon. 'On & On', 'Appletree' and 'Otherside of the Game' became classics, and the album's blend of live instrumentation and hip-hop beats, produced by the Roots' Questlove among others, set the template for the movement that followed. Baduizm debuted at number two and won a Grammy, and it remains one of the most influential R&B albums of the 1990s.

name: Voodoo
teaser: D'Angelo 2000 — recorded over 5 years at Electric Lady Studios, the same studio built for Jimi Hendrix. D'Angelo and his band (the Soulquarians — Questlove, J Dilla, Pino Palladino, Roy Hargrove) recorded hundreds of hours of jam sessions, then edited the best moments into songs. The album sounds like a séance captured on tape.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Untitled (How Does It Feel)' — the falsetto was inspired by Prince, but D'Angelo's vocal sounds like it's being pulled out of him against his will. Then 'The Root' — the bassline by Pino Palladino was played on a fretless bass and never repeats exactly. Questlove's drumming is intentionally behind the beat, creating a tension that never resolves.

synopsis: Voodoo (2000) is the masterpiece of D'Angelo, the album where the Virginia singer took the neo-soul movement he had helped launch and pushed it into new, darker, more mysterious territory, a record that is now regarded as one of the greatest R&B albums ever made. D'Angelo spent five years recording the album at Electric Lady Studios in New York, the studio built for Jimi Hendrix, working with a loose collective of musicians including the Roots' Questlove and the bassist Pino Palladino, and the result has the feel of a late-night jam session, full of deep, hypnotic grooves and dense, murky textures. 'Untitled (How Does It Feel)', with its unforgettable video and falsetto vocal, became his biggest hit, and 'Devil's Pie', 'Chicken Grease' and 'Africa' showed the album's extraordinary range, from politics to sensuality to spiritual searching. Voodoo was hailed as a masterpiece on release, and its influence on the R&B and hip-hop of the following decades is incalculable.

name: Maxwell's Urban Hang Suite
teaser: Maxwell 1996 — the album that defined the softer side of neo-soul. Recorded over 3 years with producer Stuart Matthewman (Sade's guitarist). Maxwell's falsetto and the album's concept — a single night of romance from flirtation to morning — made it both critically acclaimed and commercially successful.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Ascension (Don't Ever Wonder)' — the bassline by Matthewman was played on a fretless bass through a vintage tube preamp. Then 'Whenever Wherever Whatever' — Maxwell recorded the vocal in complete darkness. The album's narrative arc was inspired by Marvin Gaye's 'I Want You', a suite of songs about a single relationship.
