synopsis: Maxwell's Urban Hang Suite (1996) is the album that defined the softer, more romantic side of neo-soul, and it made the New York singer Maxwell, still in his early twenties, one of the most distinctive voices in R&B. Maxwell recorded the album over three years with the producer Stuart Matthewman, best known as Sade's guitarist, and the record's concept, a suite of songs tracing a relationship from first meeting through intimacy, gave it the feel of a single, continuous statement. Maxwell's voice, a high, delicate instrument that he often used in falsetto, floated over the album's smooth, understated grooves, and songs like 'Ascension (Don't Ever Wonder)', 'Sumthin' Sumthin'' and the gorgeous 'Whenever Wherever Whatever' became classics of the genre. The album was a commercial and critical success, nominated for a Grammy, and it established Maxwell as the most romantic figure of the neo-soul movement, the record where smooth R&B met the new sophistication of the 1990s.

name: Love Deluxe
teaser: Sade 1992 — recorded over two years at Studio Condulmer in Venice, Italy. The band's perfectionism was legendary: they'd spend weeks on a single snare sound. Sade Adu's voice — cool, controlled, impossibly elegant — delivers lyrics about heartbreak with the poise of someone who's already survived it.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'No Ordinary Love' — the bassline by Paul Denman was recorded in a concrete stairwell for natural reverb. Then 'Cherish the Day' — Sade's vocal was the first take. The band recorded everything to analog tape and refused to use digital effects. The album took 2 years to make; it sounds like it took 2 years.

synopsis: Love Deluxe (1992) is the fourth album by Sade, the band led by the Nigerian-born British singer Sade Adu, and it is the masterpiece of her elegant, melancholy style, a record of such sophisticated beauty that it made her one of the most successful and respected artists in the world. The band recorded the album over two years at a studio in Venice, Italy, and their legendary perfectionism is audible in every track: the music is built on slow, luxurious grooves, brushed drums, warm bass and Adu's extraordinary voice, which can convey more feeling in a whisper than most singers can in a scream. 'No Ordinary Love', with its unforgettable melody, and 'Kiss of Life' became hits, and the album also contains the gorgeous 'Cherish the Day' and 'Feel No Pain'. Love Deluxe is now regarded as one of the essential albums of the 1990s, the record where Sade's vision, at once cool and deeply emotional, reached its fullest expression.

name: Super Fly
teaser: Curtis Mayfield 1972 — the soundtrack to a blaxploitation film about a cocaine dealer trying to leave the game. Mayfield's lyrics, sung in his impossibly smooth falsetto, critique the very lifestyle the film glamorizes. The album outgrossed the movie and became a landmark of socially conscious funk.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Pusherman' — Mayfield's vocal makes a drug dealer sound like a tragic hero. Then 'Freddie's Dead' — the chorus is a funeral dirge set to a wah-wah guitar riff. Mayfield played nearly every instrument on the album himself. The album's message — that drugs destroy Black communities — was delivered with such beauty that the message slipped in unnoticed.

synopsis: Super Fly (1972) is the soundtrack to the blaxploitation film about a cocaine dealer trying to escape the game, and Curtis Mayfield's music for it became something far greater than a film score, a masterpiece of social commentary and a landmark of black music. Mayfield, who had been a star since his days with the Impressions, wrote the songs from the point of view of the film's protagonist but used them to condemn the drug trade and celebrate the struggle for liberation: 'Freddie's Dead' and 'Pusherman' are chilling portraits of the cost of the game, while the title track and 'Superfly' itself are stunning blends of funk, soul and Mayfield's falsetto, with his guitar playing, full of wah-wah and delicate filigree, setting the template for a decade of funk. The album sold millions, outselling the film itself, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest soundtracks ever made and one of the most important albums of the 1970s, the record where black pop music became political art.

name: Hot Buttered Soul
teaser: Isaac Hayes 1969 — the album that made Stax Records relevant again after losing their Atlantic catalog. Hayes took lounge-soul and stretched it to orchestral proportions: 4 songs, 45 minutes, with lengthy spoken introductions that predate rap. The album invented the 'Black Moses' persona that would define Hayes's career.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Walk On By' — Hayes transforms Burt Bacharach's 3-minute pop song into a 12-minute orchestral epic with a 4-minute spoken intro. Then 'By the Time I Get to Phoenix' — an 18-minute version where the spoken introduction is actually longer than the original song. Hayes's baritone was so deep it made the studio monitors vibrate.

tracks.title: By the Time I Get to Phoenix

synopsis: Hot Buttered Soul (1969) is the album where Isaac Hayes, already a legendary songwriter and producer at Stax Records, reinvented himself as a solo artist and changed the course of soul music, a record of such boldness and originality that it is now regarded as a cornerstone of the genre. Stax had lost its entire back catalog to Atlantic Records, and Hayes' album was part of the label's fight for survival; he responded by making music that broke every rule of the pop single: the album's four tracks are all extended workouts, with 'By the Time I Get to Phoenix' stretched to over eighteen minutes of spoken-word introduction and slow-burning soul, and 'Walk on By' reimagined as a twelve-minute epic. Hayes' deep, gravelly voice, his lush orchestral arrangements and his pioneering use of the wah-wah guitar and the Moog synthesizer made the album a sensation, and it is now regarded as the birth of the smooth, cinematic soul that dominated the next decade.

name: Maggot Brain
teaser: Funkadelic 1971 — the album that proved funk could be psychedelic, political, and transcendent. The 10-minute title track is a guitar solo by Eddie Hazel that George Clinton instructed him to play as if he'd just learned his mother had died. Hazel recorded it in one take, weeping through parts of the solo.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — close your eyes. Hazel's guitar sounds like it's mourning, raging, and praying simultaneously. The solo was recorded with no overdubs: one guitar, one amp, one take. Then 'Can You Get to That' — a gospel-influenced track about karma that the Rolling Stones would later cover. The album's eclecticism defined the P-Funk aesthetic.

tracks.title: You and Your Folks, Me and My Folks

synopsis: Maggot Brain (1971) is the album where Funkadelic, the psychedelic alter ego of George Clinton's P-Funk empire, made its masterpiece, a record that proved funk could be psychedelic, political and transcendent all at once. The album's centerpiece is its ten-minute title track, which began when Clinton, in the studio, told guitarist Eddie Hazel to play as if he had just learned that his mother was dead, and Hazel responded with one of the most extraordinary guitar solos ever recorded, a performance of such raw grief and beauty that it has become legendary. Around it, the album moves from the political funk of 'Super Stupid' and 'Hit It and Quit It' to the gospel-inflected 'Can You Get to That' and the eerie 'Wars of Armageddon', and its blend of Jimi Hendrix-inspired guitar, James Brown-inspired funk and Clinton's wild, cosmic vision made it unlike anything else in music. Maggot Brain is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 1970s, the record where funk became art.

name: Risqué
teaser: Chic 1979 — the peak of Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards's disco empire. Rodgers's 'chucking' guitar style — playing 16th-note rhythms on muted strings — became the rhythmic DNA of dance music for the next 40 years. The album's biggest hit 'Good Times' was directly sampled for 'Rapper's Delight', birthing hip-hop's first commercial success.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Good Times' — the bassline by Bernard Edwards is 2 bars long, repeated for 8 minutes, and never gets boring. Then 'My Feet Keep Dancing' — Rodgers's guitar part uses a chord voicing that music theorists call 'the Chic chord'. The album's production is so precise that every instrument occupies its own frequency space without ever crowding.

tracks.title: Will You Cry (When You Hear This Song)

synopsis: Risqué (1979) is the peak of Chic, the band that Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards built into the most sophisticated hit machine of the disco era, and it remains the definitive statement of their genius. Chic had already conquered the world with 'Le Freak' and 'Everybody Dance', but Risqué found them at the height of their powers, and the album is a masterclass in the sound they invented: Rodgers' 'chucking' guitar style, playing bright, syncopated sixteenth-note rhythms, Edwards' deep, melodic bass lines, Tony Thompson's powerful drums and the lush string and horn arrangements that gave the band their elegance. 'Good Times', the album's centerpiece, with its immortal bass line that would be sampled for the Sugarhill Gang's 'Rapper's Delight' and countless records after, became one of the defining songs of the disco era, and 'My Forbidden Lover' and 'A Warm Summer Night' completed a record of effortless sophistication. Risqué is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the disco era.

name: Street Songs
teaser: Rick James 1981 — the album that bridged funk and the emerging sound of 80s R&B. James's 'punk-funk' — raw, aggressive, built on synthesizers and drum machines — created the template that Prince would refine. The album's biggest hit 'Super Freak' was written in a single night and became one of the most-sampled songs in history.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Super Freak' — the bassline was played on a Minimoog synthesizer, not a bass guitar. Then 'Give It to Me Baby' — the song's groove was inspired by the punk bands James was listening to at the time. James produced the entire album himself, playing many of the instruments, and mixed it for maximum impact on car stereos.

tracks.title: Fire and Desire (Duet with Teena Marie)

synopsis: Street Songs (1981) is the album where Rick James, the most flamboyant figure in funk, made his masterpiece, a record that bridged the raw energy of 70s funk and the emerging sound of 80s R&B, and it remains one of the best-selling funk albums of all time. James, who called his music 'punk-funk', built the album on the aggressive, synth-driven grooves he had been perfecting for years, and its lyrics, delivered in his trademark shout, mixed celebration with social commentary: 'Super Freak', with its iconic bass line and chorus, became one of the most famous songs of the decade, later sampled by MC Hammer for 'U Can't Touch This', while 'Give It to Me Baby' and 'Ghetto Life' showed the album's range from pure party music to portraits of urban struggle. Street Songs was a massive commercial success, and it established James as one of the defining figures of the era, the record where funk got ready for the 1980s.

name: Sketches of Spain
teaser: Miles Davis and Gil Evans 1960 — Davis's third collaboration with arranger Gil Evans, recorded with a 16-piece orchestra. The album is built around Spanish folk melodies, particularly the 'Concierto de Aranjuez' by Joaquín Rodrigo. Davis's muted trumpet and Evans's impressionistic arrangements created a sound that was orchestral jazz at its most cinematic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the opening of 'Concierto de Aranjuez' — Davis enters 3 minutes in and plays only 12 notes in his first phrase. Then 'Saeta' — based on a Spanish religious procession, Davis's trumpet mimics a flamenco singer. Evans's arrangements use harp, bassoon, and French horn in combinations no jazz album had attempted.

synopsis: Sketches of Spain (1960) is the third collaboration between Miles Davis and the arranger Gil Evans, and it is one of the most beautiful and ambitious albums either man ever made, a record that blended jazz with the music of Spain to create something entirely new. Davis and Evans had already made history with Miles Ahead and Porgy and Bess, and Sketches of Spain pushed their vision even further: the album's centerpiece is 'Concierto de Aranjuez', a twenty-minute adaptation of Joaquín Rodrigo's guitar concerto, which Davis and Evans completely reimagined for trumpet and orchestra, and the album also contains 'Will o' the Wisp', based on Manuel de Falla's ballet, and the stunning 'Solea'. Davis's playing on the album is among his most expressive, soaring and weeping over Evans's lush, impressionistic arrangements. Sketches of Spain was a commercial success and is now regarded as a masterpiece, the record where Davis proved that jazz could absorb the classical tradition and make it something new.

name: Blue Train
teaser: John Coltrane 1958 — his only album as leader for Blue Note. Recorded after Coltrane had kicked heroin and was playing with Thelonious Monk. The band — Lee Morgan, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Drew, Paul Chambers, Philly Joe Jones — was a hard bop supergroup. The album's title track is a blues that Coltrane transforms into something transcendent.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Coltrane's solo starts with short, declarative phrases and builds to torrents of 16th notes without losing melodic coherence. Then 'Moment's Notice' — the chord changes move through three keys in the first 8 bars. Coltrane wrote all the material in a single week before the session.

synopsis: Blue Train (1958) is the only album John Coltrane recorded for Blue Note as a leader, and it is one of the cornerstones of his catalog, a record of hard bop perfection made at a turning point in his life. Coltrane recorded the album just after kicking his heroin addiction, during the period when he was playing with Thelonious Monk and beginning to develop the harmonic innovations that would make him famous, and the session, with Lee Morgan on trumpet, Curtis Fuller on trombone, Kenny Drew on piano, Paul Chambers on bass and Philly Joe Jones on drums, captures him on the verge of greatness. The title track, with its bluesy, loping melody, and the gorgeous ballad 'Lazy Bird' and 'Moment's Notice' show Coltrane's extraordinary command of his instrument and his rapidly evolving harmonic language. Blue Train is now regarded as one of the essential jazz albums of the 1950s, the record where one of the music's greatest figures began to show what he would become.

name: Maiden Voyage
teaser: Herbie Hancock 1965 — a concept album about the sea, recorded when Hancock was 25 and already a member of Miles Davis's Second Great Quintet. The band — Freddie Hubbard, George Coleman, Ron Carter, Tony Williams — plays with the telepathy of musicians who'd been touring together for years. Every track evokes water without a single wave sound effect.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the opening piano chords are so sparse you can hear the studio's air conditioning. Then 'Dolphin Dance' — Hancock's solo builds from single notes to cascading runs. The album's secret: Hancock restricts himself to a handful of chords per track, forcing himself to find infinite variation within narrow constraints.

synopsis: Maiden Voyage (1965) is the album where Herbie Hancock, still only 25 and already a member of Miles Davis's great quintet, made his masterpiece as a leader, a concept album about the sea that is now regarded as one of the finest jazz records of the 1960s. Hancock composed the album's five tracks as a suite evoking the ocean, from the title track, with its dark, mysterious melody that has become a jazz standard, to 'Dolphin Dance', 'Eye of the Hurricane' and the peaceful 'Survival of the Fittest', and he recorded it with a stunning band of his peers: Freddie Hubbard on trumpet, George Coleman on tenor saxophone, Ron Carter on bass and Tony Williams on drums. The music is at once adventurous and accessible, full of the modal harmonies and shifting structures that defined the era, and Hancock's piano playing is superb throughout. Maiden Voyage is now regarded as one of the essential Blue Note albums, the record where the great pianist fully arrived.

name: The Köln Concert
teaser: Keith Jarrett 1975 — an entirely improvised solo piano concert recorded at the Cologne Opera House. Jarrett had slept only a few hours, the wrong piano had been delivered (a rehearsal instrument with a broken sustain pedal), and he nearly cancelled. Instead, he played for 66 minutes and created the best-selling solo piano album in history.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Part I — Jarrett establishes a two-chord vamp in A minor that he sustains for 26 minutes without ever repeating himself. The broken piano forced him to play in the middle register and avoid the tinny high notes. The result sounds deliberate, not compromised. Jarrett's audible humming and foot-stomping are part of the recording.

synopsis: The Köln Concert (1975) is the most famous solo piano recording in the history of jazz, an entirely improvised concert that has sold millions of copies and introduced generations of listeners to the magic of Keith Jarrett. Jarrett had been performing his legendary solo improvisations for years, and the concert at the Cologne Opera House was nearly a disaster: Jarrett had slept badly, the piano provided was a small, inferior instrument that had to be tuned twice, and he nearly canceled. What emerged from that unpromising situation was one of the most sublime recordings in all of music: Jarrett, forced to work around the piano's limitations, created a performance of extraordinary beauty, full of gospel-tinged melodies, driving ostinatos and moments of transcendent lyricism, punctuated by his characteristic groans and moans. The concert has been hailed as a masterpiece of spontaneous creation, and it remains the definitive document of an artist who treated the piano as a gateway to something beyond words.

name: Journey in Satchidananda
teaser: Alice Coltrane 1971 — recorded after John Coltrane's death, this album represents Alice's turn toward Hindu spirituality. The title references her guru Swami Satchidananda. Pharoah Sanders plays soprano saxophone; Cecil McBee and Charlie Haden both play bass. The album sounds like a temple ceremony drifting through space.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Alice's harp enters 3 minutes in, and the effect is like sunlight breaking through water. Then 'Shiva-Loka' — the tambura drone was played by Tulsi, a monk from the Vedanta Center. Alice replaced John in his own band, then transformed it into something entirely her own.

synopsis: Journey in Satchidananda (1971) is the album where Alice Coltrane, the pianist and composer who had spent years in the shadow of her husband John Coltrane, emerged as one of the most original voices in spiritual jazz, a record of transcendent beauty that is now regarded as a masterpiece. After John Coltrane's death in 1967, Alice devoted herself to music and to the Hindu spirituality that had increasingly occupied her, and this album, her first with a group billed under her own name, reflects that journey: the title track is a seven-minute meditation built on her ecstatic harp playing, the tamboura drone of Indian classical music and Pharoah Sanders' keening saxophone, and the album as a whole moves between the piano meditations of 'Something About John Coltrane' and the cosmic jazz of 'Stop'. Alice Coltrane would eventually devote herself entirely to devotional music, and Journey in Satchidananda stands as the bridge between her jazz past and her spiritual future.

name: Brown Rice
teaser: Don Cherry 1975 — a fusion of free jazz, Indian raga, African rhythm, and funk that sounds like nothing else. Cherry plays trumpet through a wah-wah pedal and sings in a language of his own invention. The album was recorded in New York and Stockholm with musicians from four continents.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Cherry's trumpet is processed through a Mutron envelope filter, the same pedal that created the funk guitar sound. Then 'Malkauns' — based on an Indian raga, with Cherry playing pocket trumpet (a smaller, higher instrument) alongside tambura. The album was decades ahead of its time.

synopsis: Brown Rice (1975) is the album where Don Cherry, the trumpeter who had helped invent free jazz as a member of Ornette Coleman's revolutionary quartet, made his most accessible and visionary statement, a record that fused free jazz, Indian raga, African rhythm and funk into a sound that belonged entirely to him. Cherry had spent the years after his work with Coleman traveling the world, absorbing the music of India, Africa and the Middle East, and Brown Rice reflects those journeys: the title track is built on a deep, hypnotic groove with Cherry's trumpet floating above it, 'Malkauns' is a beautiful meditation on an Indian raga, and 'Chenrezig' and 'Degi-Degi' show the range of his vision. Cherry plays trumpet, piano and the doussn'gouni, a West African instrument, and the album's blend of spiritual searching and earthy funk made it a touchstone for the world music movement. Brown Rice is now regarded as one of the essential albums of the jazz avant-garde.

name: The Inner Mounting Flame
teaser: Mahavishnu Orchestra 1971 — John McLaughlin's jazz-rock fusion quintet turned volume, speed, and Eastern spirituality into a new genre. The band played complex compositions in odd time signatures at high volume. McLaughlin's double-neck guitar and Billy Cobham's drumming set new standards for instrumental virtuosity.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Meeting of the Spirits' — the opening guitar riff is in 18/8 time. Then 'The Dance of Maya' — the song shifts between 10/8, 20/8, and 4/4. Cobham's bass drum patterns are so fast they sound like a machine gun. McLaughlin played through a 100-watt Marshall stack, the same amplifier Jimi Hendrix used.

synopsis: The Inner Mounting Flame (1971) is the debut album of the Mahavishnu Orchestra, the band that John McLaughlin, the most technically brilliant guitarist in jazz, built to fuse the volume and speed of rock with the sophistication of jazz and the spirituality of the East, and it remains one of the most explosive albums ever recorded. McLaughlin had played with Miles Davis on Bitches Brew and had become a follower of the Indian spiritual teacher Sri Chinmoy, and the Mahavishnu Orchestra, featuring the violinist Jerry Goodman, keyboardist Jan Hammer, bassist Rick Laird and drummer Billy Cobham, was his attempt to create music of overwhelming power and intensity. The album's tracks, including 'Meeting of the Spirits', 'Dawn' and 'The Noonward Race', are built on ferocious unison lines, blazing solos and rhythms of astonishing complexity, and the band's live shows were legendary for their volume and virtuosity. The Inner Mounting Flame is now regarded as the founding document of jazz fusion, the record where jazz met rock at full volume.

name: Heavy Weather
teaser: Weather Report 1977 — the album that made jazz fusion commercially viable without compromising artistry. Joe Zawinul and Wayne Shorter, both Miles Davis alumni, led a band that included the 25-year-old Jaco Pastorius, whose fretless electric bass playing redefined the instrument. 'Birdland' became a jazz standard.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Birdland' — Zawinul wrote it on a plane and recorded the synthesizer parts himself. Then 'Teen Town' — Pastorius's bass is the lead instrument, playing a melody at high speed on a fretless bass. His technique — harmonics, rapid-fire 16th notes, percussive slaps — was unprecedented. Pastorius would be dead within a decade.

synopsis: Heavy Weather (1977) is the album where Weather Report, the greatest band of the jazz fusion movement, made its commercial breakthrough without compromising its artistry, and it remains the best-selling fusion album ever recorded. The band, led by keyboardist Joe Zawinul and saxophonist Wayne Shorter, both veterans of Miles Davis's electric bands, had spent years building a reputation as the most adventurous group in jazz, and Heavy Weather found them at the peak of their powers: 'Birdland', Zawinul's tribute to the legendary jazz club, with its irresistible melody and gospel-inflected power, became a worldwide hit, and the album also contains 'A Remark You Made', 'Teen Town', featuring the astonishing bass playing of Jaco Pastorius, and 'Havona'. The record's blend of intricate composition, virtuoso playing and irresistible grooves made it a favorite of both jazz purists and rock fans, and it is now regarded as the definitive statement of jazz fusion.

name: Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music
teaser: Ray Charles 1962 — the album where a Black rhythm-and-blues singer from Georgia covered white country songs with a full orchestra and a big band. The result was so radical that ABC-Paramount refused to release it at first. It became one of the best-selling albums of the 60s and redefined what American music could be.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Can't Stop Loving You' — Charles transforms Don Gibson's country ballad into a slow-burning soul anthem with a choir. Then 'You Don't Know Me' — the string arrangement by Marty Paich wraps Charles's voice in a velvet fog. The album proved that genre boundaries were imaginary.

tracks.title: I Love You So Much It Hurts
Just a Little Lovin' (Will Go a Long Way)

synopsis: Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music (1962) is the album where Ray Charles, the genius who had already fused gospel and blues to create soul music, broke every rule of American music by recording an album of white country songs, and it became one of the best-selling and most influential records of the decade. Charles had grown up listening to country music on the radio in the segregated South, and he insisted that the country songs he loved were as much his as anyone's; his record label resisted, fearing a backlash, but Charles went ahead, recording the album in New York with a full orchestra and arrangements that blended country melodies with his signature soul, jazz and gospel. 'I Can't Stop Loving You' became a massive hit, and the album also contains gorgeous versions of 'You Don't Know Me', 'Born to Lose' and 'Hey, Good Lookin''. The album was a phenomenon, and it is now regarded as a landmark, the record where a Black artist proved that American music had no color line.

name: At Last!
teaser: Etta James 1960 — her debut album for Chess Records, recorded in Chicago with a full string orchestra. James was 22 and had already been a professional singer for 8 years. The title track became her signature song, but the entire album showed a vocalist who could move from jazz to blues to R&B in a single phrase.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'At Last' — the string arrangement by Riley Hampton was recorded in a single afternoon. Then 'I Just Want to Make Love to You' — James transforms Willie Dixon's blues into a declaration of desire. Her voice has been described as 'church and juke joint in the same breath.' The album was recorded in just 4 days.

tracks.title: I Just Want to Make Love to You
All I Could Do Was Cry

synopsis: At Last! (1960) is the debut album of Etta James, and it introduced one of the most powerful and versatile voices in American music, a record that showed a 22-year-old singer who could do absolutely anything. James had been making waves in R&B since her teens, and her move to Chess Records, which had built its empire on blues, was a gamble: the label gave her a full string orchestra and let her loose on a mix of standards, blues and pop. The album's title track, 'At Last', a sweeping ballad that James made her own despite it being written years earlier, became one of the most famous love songs of all time, and the album also contains her versions of 'A Sunday Kind of Love', 'Trust in Me' and the blues growler 'All I Could Do Was Cry'. James's voice could be as smooth as silk or as rough as sandpaper, often in the same song, and At Last! announced the arrival of a singer who would spend the next five decades proving she was one of the greatest of all time.

name: Cloud Nine
teaser: The Temptations 1969 — the album where Motown's smoothest vocal group went psychedelic. Producer Norman Whitfield pushed the group into socially conscious lyrics and funky, wah-wah-guitar-driven production inspired by Sly Stone. David Ruffin had just been fired; Dennis Edwards replaced him and brought a grittier edge.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the opening guitar riff, played by Dennis Coffey through a wah-wah pedal, was Motown's first use of the effect. Then 'Run Away Child, Running Wild' — a 9-minute suite about a runaway, complete with sound effects. The album won Motown its first Grammy.

tracks.title: I Heard It Through the Grapevine
Why Did She Have to Leave Me (Why Did She Have to Go)
Don't Let Him Take Your Love From Me
I Gotta Find a Way (To Get You Back)
Gonna Keep on Tryin' till I Win Your Love

synopsis: Cloud Nine (1969) is the album where the Temptations, Motown's smoothest and most successful vocal group, went psychedelic, and in doing so they completely reinvented themselves and changed the sound of soul music. Producer Norman Whitfield, who had pushed the group away from their polished pop toward harder, more socially conscious material, brought in the emerging sound of psychedelic rock, complete with wah-wah guitars, fuzz bass and dense production, and the group, led by the extraordinary voices of Eddie Kendricks, David Ruffin and the young Dennis Edwards, responded with some of the most powerful music of their career. The title track, 'Cloud Nine', with its message about finding peace through music, won the group their first Grammy and became a hit, and the album also contains 'Runaway Child, Running Wild', 'Love Is a Hurtin' Thing' and the anti-drug anthem 'Don't Let the Joneses Get You Down'. Cloud Nine is now regarded as a landmark, the record where Motown proved it could evolve with the times.

name: Talking Book
teaser: Stevie Wonder 1972 — recorded mostly alone, playing nearly every instrument. The album opens with 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life' and closes with 'Superstition', both written within weeks of each other. The synthesizer work — using TONTO, a massive custom modular synth — was groundbreaking for R&B.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Superstition' — Stevie wrote it for Jeff Beck, but Motown insisted he release it himself. The clavinet riff was played through a Mu-Tron III envelope filter, creating the squelchy sound. Then 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life' — the vocal was a first take. Stevie recorded the album while also working on 'Innervisions'.

tracks.title: You Are the Sunshine of My Life
You and I (We Can Conquer the World)
I Believe (When I Fall in Love It Will Be Forever)

synopsis: Talking Book (1972) is the album where Stevie Wonder, freed from the constraints of Motown's hit-making machine by a new contract that gave him total creative control, made the first fully realized masterpiece of his golden age, a record of astonishing range and warmth. Wonder wrote, produced and arranged the album, playing nearly every instrument himself, and it opens with two of the most beloved songs in his catalog: 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life', a tender ballad that became a standard, and 'Superstition', with its iconic clavinet riff, one of the most imitated grooves in funk history. The album also contains 'Maybe Your Baby', 'You and I' and 'I Believe (When I Fall in Love It Will Be Forever)', and its blend of funk, soul, jazz and pop, all filtered through Wonder's extraordinary voice and his pioneering use of synthesizers, made it an instant classic. Talking Book won three Grammys and is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 1970s, the record where Wonder fully came into his own.

name: Just As I Am
teaser: Bill Withers 1971 — the 33-year-old former aircraft mechanic's debut album, recorded while he was still working at a factory making toilet seats. Withers showed up to the studio in his work boots. Booker T. Jones produced the album; Stephen Stills played guitar. The songs were so direct they felt less like compositions than conversations set to music.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Ain't No Sunshine' — Withers wrote it after watching the film 'Days of Wine and Roses'. The 'I know' section repeated 26 times was a placeholder that Withers intended to replace with lyrics. They kept it. Then 'Grandma's Hands' — a song about his grandmother's hands that is 2 minutes long and contains a novel's worth of detail.

synopsis: Just As I Am (1971) is the debut album of Bill Withers, and it remains one of the most remarkable first records in soul history, made by a 33-year-old former aircraft mechanic who wrote songs of such plainspoken beauty that they have never gone out of style. Withers recorded the album while still working at a factory, and its production, overseen by Booker T. Jones of Booker T. & the M.G.'s and featuring the guitarist Stephen Stills on several tracks, is warm and unhurried, perfectly matching the songs. 'Ain't No Sunshine', written in a flash of inspiration and recorded with its famous gap where Withers forgot to add lyrics, became one of the most beloved songs ever recorded, and the album also contains 'Grandma's Hands', 'Lean on Me' was still to come but 'Harlem', 'Let It Be' and the title track show Withers's gift for finding the profound in the everyday. Just As I Am is now regarded as a cornerstone of 70s soul, the record where one of music's most honest voices introduced himself.

name: Diana
teaser: Diana Ross 1980 — produced by Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards of Chic, the album that reinvented Ross for the 80s. Rodgers and Edwards wrote and produced every track, including 'I'm Coming Out' (built around a drum break inspired by a night out at a gay club) and 'Upside Down' (which Ross initially hated and tried to remix herself).

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I'm Coming Out' — the trombone riff was played by Meco Monardo and arranged in 10 minutes. Then 'Upside Down' — Ross remixed the song without Rodgers's permission after the first release. The version we know is a compromise between her mix and his. The album made Ross a disco icon and a pop star simultaneously.

synopsis: Diana (1980) is the album that reinvented Diana Ross for the 1980s, the record where the most famous woman in pop music handed her sound to Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards of Chic, and it became the biggest-selling album of her career. Rodgers and Edwards had built Chic into the most sophisticated act in disco, and Ross, desperate to update her image after a decade of solo hits, flew to New York to work with them; the sessions were famously tense, with Ross initially rejecting the duo's material before agreeing to record it. The album that emerged is a masterpiece of slick, sophisticated dance pop: 'Upside Down', with its irresistible groove, became a worldwide number one, and 'I'm Coming Out', written by Rodgers after seeing drag queens dressed as Diana Ross outside a New York club, became an anthem of liberation that has never gone away. The album also contains 'My Old Piano' and 'It's My Turn', and its blend of Chic's grooves and Ross's glamour made it a landmark of the disco-to-dance transition.

name: Off the Wall
teaser: Michael Jackson 1979 — his first adult album, produced by Quincy Jones. Jackson was 21 and determined to be taken seriously. The album bridged disco and pop with songs by Stevie Wonder, Paul McCartney, and Rod Temperton. It was the first solo album to generate four top-10 singles.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough' — Jackson wrote the entire song, including the string arrangement, which he sang note-for-note to the arranger. Then 'Rock with You' — the vocal was a single take. The album's production is so pristine that every instrument sounds like it's been polished. Jackson won his first Grammy for Best R&B Vocal Performance.

synopsis: Off the Wall (1979) is the album where Michael Jackson, at 21, finally escaped the shadow of his childhood with the Jackson 5 and established himself as a solo star of the first rank, a record of pure, joyful pop perfection. Jackson had decided to work with the producer Quincy Jones, and the partnership immediately paid off: the album is a seamless blend of disco, funk, soul and pop, built on Jackson's extraordinary voice, which had deepened into a supple, powerful instrument, and his already legendary dancing. 'Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough', written by Jackson himself, became his first solo number one, 'Rock with You' and 'Off the Wall' were massive hits, and his version of 'She's Out of My Life', which reduced him to tears in the studio, became a classic ballad. The album sold over twenty million copies, and its blend of sophistication and joy made it the template for everything that followed, including the record that would make Jackson the biggest star in the world.

name: Thriller
teaser: Michael Jackson 1982 — the best-selling album of all time (over 70 million copies). Recorded over 8 months with Quincy Jones. Jackson was obsessed with making an album where every track could be a single — nine tracks, seven became top-10 hits. The title track's video, directed by John Landis, changed what music videos could be.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Billie Jean' — Jackson recorded the vocal in a single take while singing into a cardboard tube for a specific sound. Then 'Beat It' — Eddie Van Halen's guitar solo was recorded for free as a favor; he did it in one take and thought no one would notice. The album spent 37 weeks at #1.

synopsis: Thriller (1982) is the best-selling album of all time, with over seventy million copies sold, and it turned Michael Jackson from a star into a global phenomenon the likes of which the world had never seen. Jackson reunited with producer Quincy Jones for the follow-up to Off the Wall, and this time they aimed even higher: the album's seven singles, from the menacing funk of 'Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'' and the rock edge of 'Beat It', with its legendary Eddie Van Halen guitar solo, to the duet with Paul McCartney 'The Girl Is Mine' and the ballad 'Human Nature', dominated the charts for over a year. The title track, with its horror-movie video directed by John Landis, changed the relationship between music and film forever, and 'Billie Jean', with its iconic bass line and the moonwalk Jackson unveiled on television, became one of the defining songs of the decade. Thriller won a record-breaking eight Grammys and remains the benchmark against which all pop albums are measured.

name: Sign o' the Times
teaser: Prince 1987 — a double album recorded almost entirely alone at his Paisley Park studio. Originally planned as a triple album, Warner Bros. forced him to cut it down. The album is a one-man tour through funk, rock, soul, gospel, and experimental pop. Prince played every instrument on most tracks.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — nothing but a drum machine, a synth bass, and Prince's voice reporting the news of 1987: AIDS, gang violence, drug addiction. Then 'If I Was Your Girlfriend' — Prince sings in a sped-up voice as his alter ego Camille, asking what intimacy would look like if he were female. The album is a complete universe.

tracks.title: I Could Never Take the Place of Your Man
It's Gonna Be a Beautiful Night

synopsis: Sign o' the Times (1987) is the album where Prince, already one of the most prolific and gifted musicians of his era, made his masterpiece, a sprawling double record that captured every side of his genius. Prince recorded most of the album alone at his Paisley Park studio, playing nearly every instrument, and the record was originally planned as a triple album before Warner Bros. insisted he trim it; even cut down, it is a stunning showcase of his range. 'Sign o' the Times', the title track, is a chilling account of the AIDS crisis, crack epidemic and Cold War anxiety of the mid-80s, 'If I Was Your Girlfriend' and 'I Could Never Take the Place of Your Man' show his gift for pop, 'Housequake' and 'Hot Thing' are pure funk, and 'Adore' is one of the greatest love songs ever recorded. The album is now universally regarded as Prince's greatest work and one of the essential records of the 1980s, a double album with not a wasted moment.

name: Janet Jackson's Rhythm Nation 1814
teaser: Janet Jackson 1989 — the album that proved Janet was not just Michael's sister. Produced by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis at Flyte Tyme Studios in Minneapolis. Every track uses the same drum sound: a Roland TR-808 programmed with a swing that became the template for 90s R&B. The album spawned seven top-5 singles, a record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the industrial clang-and-clatter production was inspired by Janet watching CNN and wanting to make music that sounded like the news. Then 'Love Will Never Do (Without You)' — the song was originally written for a duet but Janet sang both parts, pitched at different registers. The video launched Antonio Sabàto Jr.'s career.

tracks.title: Livin' in a World (They Didn't Make)

synopsis: Janet Jackson's Rhythm Nation 1814 (1989) is the album where Janet Jackson proved she was a superstar in her own right, not just Michael's sister, a record of such ambition and social consciousness that it remains one of the most important pop albums of its era. Jackson and her producers, Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, built the album around a concept, a vision of a world united through music, and its songs tackle racism ('Rhythm Nation'), illiteracy ('State of the World'), drug abuse and homelessness, all wrapped in some of the most innovative, hard-hitting production of the decade. 'Rhythm Nation', 'Miss You Much', 'Escapade' and 'Love Will Never Do (Without You)' were a string of number one hits unmatched by any artist of the era, and the album's choreography, unveiled in a series of groundbreaking videos, set a new standard for pop performance. Rhythm Nation was the first album to produce seven top-five singles, and it remains a landmark of socially conscious pop.

name: Songs in A Minor
teaser: Alicia Keys 2001 — her debut at age 20, recorded over 3 years. Keys wrote, arranged, and produced most of the album herself, playing piano on every track. The album won 5 Grammys, including Best New Artist and Song of the Year for 'Fallin'. It sold 12 million copies and redefined what a young Black female artist could do in the 2000s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Fallin' — Keys wrote it at 18. The song is built on a single descending chord progression she improvised in her Harlem apartment. Then 'A Woman's Worth' — the song samples Isaac Hayes but the lyric is entirely Keys's. She recorded the album while maintaining a 4.0 GPA at Columbia University.

tracks.title: How Come You Don't Call Me
Why Do I Feel So Sad

synopsis: Songs in A Minor (2001) is the debut album of Alicia Keys, and it announced the arrival of one of the most gifted musicians of her generation, a record that fused classical training, jazz, soul and hip-hop into something entirely her own. Keys, who had signed her first record deal at 15 and spent years being told to sound more commercial, made the album on her own terms, writing, arranging and producing most of it herself and playing piano throughout; her extraordinary musicianship, rare in the pop world, became her calling card. 'Fallin'', built on a classical piano figure, became one of the biggest hits of the year and won her multiple Grammys, 'A Woman's Worth' and 'How Come You Don't Call Me' showed her range, and the album's blend of old-school soul and contemporary R&B made it a phenomenon. Songs in A Minor sold over twelve million copies and made Keys, still in her early twenties, one of the most celebrated artists in music.

name: House of Balloons
teaser: The Weeknd (Abel Tesfaye) 2011 — released as a free download with no promotion and no artist photos. The album's haunted R&B — samples of Siouxsie and the Banshees, lyrics about drugs and empty sex, Tesfaye's voice floating through digital reverb — created a new subgenre. Nobody knew what The Weeknd looked like for a full year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'High for This' — the opening line ('you don't know what's in store') delivered in a near-whisper, sets the tone. Then 'House of Balloons / Glass Table Girls' — the beat switches from a Siouxsie sample to a trap drum pattern. Tesfaye recorded the vocals in a single night in a Toronto apartment, deliberately keeping the room cold.

tracks.title: House of Balloons / Glass Table Girls

synopsis: House of Balloons (2011) is the mixtape that introduced the Weeknd to the world, a record of such dark, haunted beauty that it completely reinvented R&B and made its anonymous creator, Abel Tesfaye, one of the most important artists of his generation. Released as a free download with no promotion, no artist photos and no interviews, the mixtape spread by word of mouth on the strength of its music alone: Tesfaye's extraordinary voice, a high, aching instrument that could move from a whisper to a cry, floated over production that mixed slow, skeletal beats with unexpected samples, including tracks from Siouxsie and the Banshees, Beach House and Aaliyah. The album's songs are about sex, drugs and the hollow glamour of the party life, told with a candor and melancholy that made them feel like confessions. 'Wicked Games', 'The Morning' and 'House of Balloons / Glass Table Girls' became underground anthems, and the mixtape was hailed as a masterpiece, the sound of R&B being torn down and rebuilt.

name: Back to Oakland
teaser: Tower of Power 1974 — the definitive album from the Oakland-based band that combined James Brown's funk with big-band horn arrangements. The five-piece horn section could shift from staccato punches to lush harmonies in a single bar. The album's 'What Is Hip?' became a question that defined the entire funk era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'What Is Hip?' — the bassline by Francis Rocco Prestia was played fingerstyle with such precision that bassists still study it. Then 'Don't Change Horses (In the Middle of a Stream)' — the horn arrangement by Greg Adams uses all five horns as a single instrument. The band recorded live in the studio with minimal overdubs.

tracks.title: Oakland Stroke... (Emilio Castillo, David Garibaldi, Stephen Kupka)
Don't Change Horses (In the Middle of a Stream) (Johnny "Guitar" Watson, Lenny Williams)
Just When We Start Makin' It (Castillo, Kupka, Lenny Williams)
Can't You See (You Doin' Me Wrong) (Castillo, Kupka, Williams)
Man from the Past (Castillo, Kupka, Williams)
Love's Been Gone So Long (Bruce Conte)
Below Us, All the City Lights (Castillo, Kupka)

synopsis: Back to Oakland (1974) is the definitive album of Tower of Power, the Oakland band that combined the raw energy of James Brown's funk with the precision and power of big-band horn arrangements, and it remains one of the greatest funk records ever made. The band's signature was its legendary horn section, five musicians who played with a tightness and power that no other group could match, and their leader, Emilio Castillo, had spent years building the group into a precision instrument. The album contains some of their most beloved tracks: 'Oakland Stroke', 'Don't Change Horses (In the Middle of a Stream)', 'Time Will Tell' and the instrumental showcase 'Squib Cakes', which became a favorite of musicians everywhere. The band's blend of funk, soul and jazz, powered by Lenny Pickett's extraordinary saxophone playing and the tightest rhythm section in the business, made them the most respected funk band of their era, and Back to Oakland is the album where they reached their peak.

name: Ship Ahoy
teaser: The O'Jays 1973 — the album that made Philly soul a national force. Produced by Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff at Philadelphia's Sigma Sound Studios with MFSB, the house band that defined the 'Philly sound': lush strings, tight drums, and a groove that never quits. The album's artwork was a fold-out depicting a slave ship.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'For the Love of Money' — the bassline was played by Anthony Jackson on a Fender Precision through a flanger pedal, creating the sinister, liquid sound that defined the track. Then 'Now That We Found Love' — the song rides a single chord for 4 minutes, powered entirely by the rhythm section. The album addressed race in America without ever sounding preachy.

tracks.title: This Air I Breathe (Gamble, Bunny Sigler)
You Got Your Hooks in Me (Sigler)
For the Love of Money (Gamble, Huff, Anthony Jackson)
People Keep Tellin' Me (John Whitehead, Gene McFadden, Victor Carstarphen)

synopsis: Ship Ahoy (1973) is the album that made Philadelphia soul a national force, the record where the O'Jays and the production team of Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff created the definitive statement of the sound that defined the early 70s. Gamble and Huff had built Philadelphia International Records into the most important soul label in America, and the O'Jays, veterans who had been singing together since the 1950s, were their greatest vehicle: Eddie Levert's soaring, gospel-trained voice and the group's harmonies were the perfect match for the duo's lush, orchestral productions. The album's centerpiece is the title track, 'Ship Ahoy', a stunningly ambitious account of the Middle Passage, the journey of enslaved Africans across the Atlantic, that remains one of the most powerful protest songs in soul music, and the album also contains 'For the Love of Money', later a theme song for The Apprentice, 'Put Your Hands Together' and 'Now That We Found Love'. Ship Ahoy is now regarded as a landmark of 70s soul.

name: Wild and Peaceful
teaser: Kool & the Gang 1973 — the Jersey City band's breakthrough, built on three anthems: 'Jungle Boogie', 'Hollywood Swinging', and 'Funky Stuff'. The horn section, led by Ronald Bell, played riffs so tight they sounded like one instrument. The album turned a struggling jazz-funk band into one of the biggest groups of the 70s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Jungle Boogie' — the opening 'get down, get down' vocal was improvised by a roadie they pulled into the booth. Then 'Hollywood Swinging' — the horn riff came to Bell in a dream. The band recorded the album in 3 days at a converted church in Jersey City. The studio's natural reverb gave the horns their cathedral-like sound.

tracks.title: This Is You, This Is Me
Life Is What You Make It

synopsis: Wild and Peaceful (1973) is the album that broke Kool & the Gang into the big time, a record built on three of the most enduring funk anthems ever written, and it remains the definitive statement of their early, instrumental-heavy sound. The band, a collective of musicians from Jersey City led by brothers Robert 'Kool' Bell and Ronald Bell, had spent years building a reputation as one of the tightest funk groups in the country, and Wild and Peaceful finally captured their live energy on record. 'Jungle Boogie', with its famous spoken refrain and growling horns, and 'Hollywood Swinging' became massive hits, and 'Funky Stuff' completed a trio of anthems that still fill dance floors fifty years later. The album's blend of James Brown-style funk, Latin percussion and the band's own sophisticated arranging made it a blueprint for the funk and disco that followed. Wild and Peaceful was a huge success, and it established Kool & the Gang as one of the most important funk bands in America.

name: Can't Get Enough
teaser: Barry White 1974 — the album that perfected the 'love man' persona. White's impossibly deep baritone, the Love Unlimited Orchestra's 40-piece string section, and arrangements that turned 3-minute songs into 7-minute suites made every track feel like a seduction. The album's centerpiece 'Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe' was written in 20 minutes.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the opening harp glissando announces the arrival of something serious. Then 'You're the First, the Last, My Everything' — White wrote it as a country song, then transformed it into disco-funk. The string section was the LA Philharmonic moonlighting for session pay. White conducted them himself despite having no formal training.

tracks.title: You're the First, the Last, My Everything
I Can't Believe You Love Me
Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe
Oh Love, Well We Finally Made It
I Love You More Than Anything (In This World Girl)

synopsis: Can't Get Enough (1974) is the album that perfected the love man persona of Barry White, and it remains the definitive statement of the most distinctive voice in soul music. White, a former arranger and producer, had invented his sound around his own impossibly deep baritone, which he used less as a singing instrument than as a seductive force of nature, speaking and crooning over the lush arrangements of his Love Unlimited Orchestra. The album's centerpiece is 'Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe', one of the most famous love songs of the decade, and it also contains 'You're the First, the Last, My Everything', which became his signature hit, and 'Oh What a Night for Dancing'. White's music was pure seduction, built on deep strings, warm bass and his whispered declarations of love, and it made him one of the best-selling artists of the 1970s. Can't Get Enough is now regarded as the essential Barry White album, the record where his vision reached its fullest expression.

name: Never Can Say Goodbye
teaser: Gloria Gaynor 1975 — the first album to present disco as a continuous mix, with three songs on side A joined by seamless transitions. Gaynor's church-trained voice brought gospel power to disco. The title track (a Clifton Davis cover) and 'Honey Bee' established the template for the disco diva.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the side A medley — the three tracks flow into each other with no breaks, creating a 19-minute dance suite. Then 'Honey Bee' — the instrumental break features a conga solo by Carlos Martin. The album's production by Tom Moulton, who essentially invented the 12-inch single, defined how disco albums would be structured for the next 5 years.

tracks.title: All I Need Is Your Sweet Lovin'

synopsis: Never Can Say Goodbye (1975) is the album that made Gloria Gaynor a star and changed the way disco albums were made, the first record to present its music as a continuous mix rather than a collection of separate songs. The producer Meco Monardo and his team had the radical idea of mixing the album's side A, three songs, into a single seamless track, with Gaynor's powerful voice soaring over the nonstop groove, and the effect was electrifying: the title track, a cover of a Jackson 5 song, became a massive hit, and the album's continuous mix made it a favorite of DJs and dancers. Gaynor's voice, big, soulful and full of gospel fire, was perfect for the emerging disco sound, and the album established her as one of the genre's first stars. She would surpass it two years later with 'I Will Survive', but Never Can Say Goodbye remains a landmark of early disco, the record that showed how the album format could serve the dance floor.

name: Carrie & Lowell
teaser: Sufjan Stevens' 2015 album about his mother's death. Carrie was bipolar and abandoned the family when Sufjan was a baby; Lowell was his stepfather who ran an Oregon folk music shop. The album was recorded in a single room with almost no production between you and the words.

exploreAction.instruction: Don't put it on as background. The lyrics do the work — give them your full attention on first listen. 'Fourth of July' is a conversation with his dying mother in a hospital bed. The production hides on purpose; Stevens recorded the vocals in a closet so the sound would feel enclosed and intimate.

tracks.title: All of Me Wants All of You
No Shade in the Shadow of the Cross

synopsis: Carrie & Lowell (2015) is the album where Sufjan Stevens, a songwriter known for elaborate, orchestral concept records, turned his attention to the most personal subject imaginable, the death of his mother, and made the most devastating and beautiful album of his career. Stevens's mother, Carrie, struggled with bipolar disorder and abandoned the family when he was young; she died in 2012, and Stevens, who had barely spoken to her in years, was left with a lifetime of complicated grief. The album, named for his mother and stepfather, Lowell, is a spare, acoustic record, a world away from the baroque arrangements of his earlier work, with Stevens's fragile voice and fingerpicked guitar carrying songs of haunting, almost unbearable honesty. 'Should Have Known Better', 'Fourth of July', 'The Only Thing' and 'John My Beloved' are among the most beautiful songs he has ever written, and the album was hailed as a masterpiece on release, the sound of grief made into art.

name: Blue
teaser: Joni Mitchell 1971 — recorded mostly with just her voice, a guitar, and a piano. She wrote the songs while traveling through Europe after breaking up with Graham Nash and beginning a relationship with James Taylor. Every song is an open wound dressed as a folk tune.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'A Case of You' — Mitchell plays a dulcimer she was given in Greece. The song references a breakup with Leonard Cohen, who she met at the Isle of Wight festival. Then 'River' — a Christmas song about wanting to escape, built around a Jingle Bells piano line that Mitchell subverts into a minor key.

tracks.title: The Last Time I Saw Richard

synopsis: Blue (1971) is the album where Joni Mitchell laid herself completely bare, and it is now universally regarded as one of the greatest records ever made, the sound of a songwriter at the absolute peak of her powers. Mitchell wrote the album's songs while traveling through Europe, heartbroken and searching, and she recorded them in California with mostly just her voice, her guitar and her piano, stripping away the orchestration of her earlier records until only the songs remained. The result is an album of almost unbearable intimacy: 'California', 'Carey', 'This Flight Tonight' and 'A Case of You' are portraits of love and longing, 'The Last Time I Saw Richard' is a devastating look at cynicism, and 'River' and 'Blue' are songs of such raw feeling that they still stop listeners in their tracks. Mitchell's voice, with its extraordinary range and its jazz-influenced phrasing, had never been more expressive, and Blue is now regarded as the definitive singer-songwriter album, the record that gave a generation permission to be honest.

name: Highway 61 Revisited
teaser: Bob Dylan 1965 — the album where he went electric and the folk world lost its mind. Recorded in 6 days with a band that included Al Kooper, a guitarist who had never played organ before but who improvised the iconic riff on 'Like a Rolling Stone'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Like a Rolling Stone' — the opening snare drum hit was described by Bruce Springsteen as sounding 'like somebody'd kicked open the door to your mind.' Then 'Desolation Row' — an 11-minute dreamscape with no chorus, recorded with session musicians who had no idea what the song was about.

tracks.title: It Takes a Lot to Laugh, It Takes a Train to Cry

synopsis: Highway 61 Revisited (1965) is the album where Bob Dylan went electric and changed the course of popular music, a record of such brilliance and defiance that it remains one of the most important albums ever made. Dylan had shocked the folk world at the Newport Folk Festival that summer by playing with an electric band, and his sixth album, recorded over six days in New York with a band that included Al Kooper and Mike Bloomfield, was a full declaration of war on the folk purists who wanted to keep him acoustic. 'Like a Rolling Stone', with its organ riff and its six-minute length, rewrote the rules of what a pop song could be, 'Desolation Row' is an eleven-minute surrealist epic, and 'Highway 61 Revisited', 'Tombstone Blues' and 'Ballad of a Thin Man' are full of the gallows humor and biblical imagery that defined his new sound. The album is now regarded as the moment rock and roll grew up, the record where Dylan's poetry met electricity and changed the world.

name: Pink Moon
teaser: Nick Drake's 1972 third album — recorded in two late-night sessions totaling about 4 hours. Just Drake's voice and guitar, almost no overdubs. He dropped the master tapes off at Island Records' reception desk without telling anyone. The album sold fewer than 5,000 copies in his lifetime.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen in complete darkness. The title track is 2 minutes long — a miniature that contains a lifetime. Drake was severely depressed during the sessions; you can hear his fingernails hitting the guitar strings. The producer John Wood later said he'd never seen anyone so withdrawn make something so complete.

synopsis: Pink Moon (1972) is the third and final album of Nick Drake, and it remains one of the most haunting and beloved records ever made, a document of extraordinary fragility made by an artist who was disappearing into himself. Drake recorded the album in two late-night sessions totaling about four hours, with just his voice and his guitar and almost no overdubs or accompaniment, and the result is music of devastating spareness: his intricate, jazz-influenced fingerpicking and his quiet, melancholy voice carrying songs of isolation and longing. The title track, 'Pink Moon', with its gentle, unsettling beauty, and 'Place to Be', 'Road' and 'Things Behind the Sun' are among the most beautiful songs ever recorded, and the album's atmosphere of solitude has never been matched. Drake, struggling with depression, retreated further into himself after the album's release and died in 1974 at the age of 26. Pink Moon, which sold almost nothing on release, has since become one of the most beloved cult records in music history.

name: For Emma, Forever Ago
teaser: Bon Iver 2007 — Justin Vernon retreated to his father's hunting cabin in Wisconsin after his band broke up and he got mononucleosis. He spent three winter months alone, recording on a single SM57 microphone and a laptop. The album was meant as a series of demos, never intended for release.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Skinny Love' — the guitar was tuned to an open chord Vernon invented. The cracking in his voice at the end of the first chorus is real; he was running a fever. Then 're: stacks' — the song builds an entire emotional world from three fingerpicked guitar notes and a falsetto that barely rises above a whisper.

synopsis: For Emma, Forever Ago (2007) is the album that made Bon Iver, born Justin Vernon, one of the most beloved voices in indie music, a record of such stark, wintry beauty that it seemed to come from another world. Vernon recorded the album alone at his father's hunting cabin in the woods of Wisconsin, where he had retreated after his band broke up and he came down with mononucleosis; over three months of isolation, chopping wood and surviving the winter, he wrote and recorded the songs that became the album, layering his extraordinary falsetto over fingerpicked guitars, distant drums and the sounds of the cabin itself. 'Skinny Love', 'For Emma', 'Re: Stacks' and 'Flume' are songs of heartbreak and solitude that sound like they are being sung from inside a snowstorm, and the album's blend of folk intimacy and atmospheric production made it an instant classic. For Emma, Forever Ago is now regarded as one of the essential indie albums of the 2000s, the record that proved solitude could be the most fertile ground for art.

name: Paranoid
teaser: Black Sabbath 1970 — the album that accidentally invented heavy metal. The title track was written and recorded in 25 minutes as filler because the album was too short. The band thought the real single would be 'War Pigs'. 'Paranoid' became their signature song.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the opening of 'War Pigs' — the air raid siren was a real siren Ozzy Osbourne found and plugged into the mixing desk. Then 'Iron Man' — the riff was improvised by Tony Iommi during a soundcheck. Iommi had lost the tips of two fingers in an industrial accident; he tuned his guitar down to C# to reduce string tension, creating Sabbath's signature low sound.

synopsis: Paranoid (1970) is the album where Black Sabbath, accidentally and almost by default, invented heavy metal, and it remains one of the most influential records ever made. The band had recorded their self-titled debut earlier that year, but it was Paranoid, recorded in just a few days to capitalize on their growing reputation, that codified the sound that would define metal for the next fifty years: Tony Iommi's crushing, downtuned riffs, Geezer Butler's rumbling bass, Bill Ward's pounding drums and Ozzy Osbourne's eerie, anguished vocals. The title track, written in twenty-five minutes as filler, became the band's signature song and one of the most famous riffs in rock, 'War Pigs' is an anti-war anthem of apocalyptic power, 'Iron Man' and 'Hand of Doom' are portraits of destruction and addiction, and 'Planet Caravan' shows the band's more psychedelic side. Paranoid went to number one in Britain and is now universally regarded as the founding document of heavy metal.

name: Master of Puppets
teaser: Metallica 1986 — recorded in Copenhagen over three months. Cliff Burton's final album; he died in a bus crash six months after its release while the band was on tour in Sweden. The album has no ballads and no radio-friendly singles, yet went 6x platinum without music videos.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the mid-section clean guitar interlude was Burton's idea, a moment of beauty in 8 minutes of fury. Then 'Orion' — an 8-minute instrumental written primarily by Burton, with a bass solo that quotes classical Bach-influenced counterpoint. The album's production (by Flemming Rasmussen) captures the sound of a band playing live in a room.

tracks.title: The Thing That Should Not Be

synopsis: Master of Puppets (1986) is the album where Metallica, already the most ferocious band in the emerging thrash metal scene, made the record that would define the genre and outlive nearly everything around it, and it remains one of the greatest metal albums of all time. The band recorded the album over three months in Copenhagen, and it found them expanding their sound beyond the raw aggression of their earlier records into something more ambitious: the eight-and-a-half-minute title track, with its intricate riffs and classical-tinged middle section, is regarded as one of the greatest metal songs ever written, and 'Battery', 'Damage, Inc.', 'Leper Messiah' and the anti-drug epic 'Master of Puppets' show the band's extraordinary musicality. The album was the last to feature the legendary bassist Cliff Burton, who died in a bus crash six months after its release, and his playing, melodic and powerful, is all over the record. Master of Puppets is now regarded as the definitive thrash metal album, the record where the genre reached its artistic peak.

name: Buena Vista Social Club
teaser: Ry Cooder's 1997 Cuban session album — most of the musicians were over 70, some over 90, and most had retired decades earlier. The recording sessions were supposed to feature Malian musicians, but their visas didn't arrive. Cooder pivoted and assembled elderly Cuban musicians who hadn't played together in 40 years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Chan Chan' — Compay Segundo's voice was 89 years old when he recorded it; the song was written in his sleep. Then 'Dos Gardenias' — a 1945 son-form bolero sung by Omara Portuondo at age 67. The album captures the last generation of pre-revolution Cuban musicians, most of whom died within 5 years of its release.

synopsis: Buena Vista Social Club (1997) is one of the most beloved albums in the history of world music, a record that brought the golden age of Cuban music back to life and made international stars of a group of musicians who had been forgotten for decades. The guitarist and producer Ry Cooder traveled to Havana in 1996 hoping to find the great Cuban musicians of the 1940s and 50s, and he found them: most of the musicians he recorded were over seventy, some over ninety, and nearly all had retired years earlier, their careers ended by the revolution and the decades of isolation that followed. The album that emerged is a stunning document of their genius: the guitarist Compay Segundo, the pianist Rubén González, the singer Ibrahim Ferrer, who had been shining shoes, and the singer Omara Portuondo all delivered performances of extraordinary warmth and vitality. The album won a Grammy and led to a documentary film and sold millions, and it remains the most successful world music album ever made.

name: Zombie
teaser: Fela Kuti 1976 — the album that attacked the Nigerian military directly. The title track compared soldiers to mindless zombies. In retaliation, the Nigerian army invaded Fela's compound, beat him, threw his elderly mother out a window (she later died), and burned his studio. Fela delivered her coffin to the army barracks.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — it's 12 minutes of polyrhythmic fury. The horn section plays the same riff for minutes at a time while Fela's keyboard and Tony Allen's drums build a groove that never resolves. Then notice how the call-and-response vocals are structured like a town hall meeting, not a concert.

synopsis: Zombie (1976) is the album where Fela Kuti, the Nigerian musician and activist who invented Afrobeat, made his most direct attack on the Nigerian government, and it remains one of the most politically powerful records ever made. Fela, whose music fused West African rhythms with funk, jazz and the influence of James Brown, had been using his Kalakuta Republic compound as a base for his political activism, and on Zombie he compared the Nigerian military to mindless zombies who follow orders without thinking, a direct insult that the government could not ignore. The title track, with its hypnotic groove and chanted vocals, became an anthem of resistance, but it came at a terrible cost: in 1977, soldiers attacked Kalakuta Republic, beating Fela and throwing his elderly mother from a window, and burning the compound to the ground. Zombie is now regarded as Fela's masterpiece, the record where his music and his politics became one, and its influence on everything from Afrobeat to hip-hop to protest music is incalculable.

name: Juju Music
teaser: King Sunny Adé 1982 — the album that brought Nigerian juju music to Western audiences. Adé led a band of 20 musicians with talking drums, pedal steel guitar, and layered percussion. Island Records signed him hoping he'd be 'the African Bob Marley'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Ja Funmi' — count the distinct percussion layers. There are at least seven: talking drums, congas, shakers, claves, bells, and two trap drum kits playing in different time signatures. Then notice the pedal steel guitar — Adé added it after hearing American country music on the radio in Lagos, and it became a permanent part of juju.

synopsis: Juju Music (1982) is the album that introduced Nigerian juju music to Western audiences, and it made King Sunny Adé, the genre's most celebrated star, an international phenomenon. Adé had spent nearly two decades building his reputation in Nigeria, where his live shows, featuring a band of up to twenty musicians with pedal steel guitars, talking drums and choruses of singers, were legendary, and Juju Music, his international debut, captured that sound for the world: gentle, hypnotic grooves built on interlocking guitar patterns, the talking drums of Yoruba culture, and Adé's warm, laid-back vocals. The album's most famous track, 'Ja Funmi', became an international hit, and the record's blend of traditional Yoruba music with modern electric instrumentation made it a revelation for Western listeners who had never heard anything like it. Juju Music sold over a million copies and earned Adé a reputation as the most important African musician of his generation, the record that brought the joy of juju to the world.

name: Mothership Connection
teaser: Parliament 1975 — George Clinton's P-Funk empire at its peak. The album invented the mythology of an alien funk mothership coming to liberate Earth through dance. The horn arrangements were written by Fred Wesley, James Brown's former bandleader, who had just joined Clinton's crew.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Give Up the Funk (Tear the Roof off the Sucker)' — the chorus was improvised during a rehearsal when Clinton shouted the phrase and the band kept playing. Then 'Mothership Connection (Star Child)' — the opening radio-dial narration was Clinton imitating a DJ he heard as a kid in Plainfield, New Jersey. The album was sampled extensively by Dr. Dre for The Chronic.

tracks.title: P. Funk (Wants to Get Funked Up)
Give Up the Funk (Tear the Roof off the Sucker)

synopsis: Mothership Connection (1975) is the album where George Clinton's P-Funk empire reached its peak, a record of such cosmic, larger-than-life invention that it remains one of the most influential funk albums ever made. Clinton had spent years building the Parliament and Funkadelic collective into a musical universe of its own, complete with mythology, characters and a vision of funk as a force for liberation, and Mothership Connection is where that vision fully came into focus: the album imagines a spaceship full of funky aliens arriving to rescue Earth through the power of the groove, and its music is as extravagant as its concept. 'Give Up the Funk (Tear the Roof off the Sucker)' and 'Mothership Connection (Star Child)' are among the greatest funk tracks ever recorded, and the album's horn arrangements, chanted choruses and Clinton's wild, theatrical vocals made it a blueprint for the funk, disco and hip-hop that followed. Mothership Connection is now regarded as one of the most important albums of the 1970s.

name: Live at the Apollo
teaser: James Brown 1963 — the most electrifying live album ever recorded. Brown financed the recording himself because his label, King Records, thought live albums didn't sell. The album cost $5,700 to record and grossed over a million dollars. It's still taught in music schools as a masterclass in showmanship.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the opening — the MC hypes the crowd for nearly 3 minutes before a note is played. Then Brown launches into 'I'll Go Crazy' and doesn't stop moving for the next 30 minutes. Notice how he controls the band's tempo from the stage with hand signals and body movements. Every scream from the audience was real — the Apollo's Tuesday amateur nights were legendary.

tracks.title: Introduction to James Brown and The Famous Flames

synopsis: Live at the Apollo (1963) is the most electrifying live album ever recorded, the record that captured James Brown, the hardest-working man in show business, at the absolute peak of his powers and changed the course of soul music. Brown was a legend in the Black community but had yet to break through to white audiences, and his label, King Records, refused to fund a live album; Brown financed the recording himself, and the result proved him right beyond his wildest dreams. The album captures a single performance at Harlem's Apollo Theater, and from the opening note it is a document of Brown's extraordinary command: his band, the Famous Flames, his screaming, sweating, collapsing performances, and the audience's ecstatic response, which is as much a part of the record as the music. The album sold over a million copies, an almost unheard-of feat for a live soul record, and it is now regarded as the definitive live album in soul history, the record where Brown's legend was sealed.

name: Bad Girls
teaser: Donna Summer 1979 — the double album that bridged disco and rock. Produced by Giorgio Moroder, who recorded Summer's vocals through a custom Eventide Harmonizer to create the layered, robotic sound that defined the era. The title track was inspired by a police officer mistaking Summer for a sex worker.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hot Stuff' — the guitar solo is by Jeff Baxter of Steely Dan, recorded in a single take at 2 AM. Then 'Bad Girls' — the 'toot-toot, beep-beep' hook was Summer mimicking car horns. The synth bassline was Moroder's Moog modular, programmed note by note because sequencers didn't exist yet.

tracks.title: Journey to the Center of Your Heart
Can't Get to Sleep at Night
There Will Always Be a You

synopsis: Bad Girls (1979) is the double album where Donna Summer, already the undisputed queen of disco, made her most ambitious and successful record, a stunning blend of disco, rock, R&B and new wave that sold millions and won her a Grammy. Summer recorded the album with the producers Giorgio Moroder and Pete Bellotte, who had helped invent the sound of Eurodisco with her earlier hits, and Bad Girls found them pushing disco in bold new directions: the title track, with its story of a streetwalker and its irresistible groove, and 'Hot Stuff', with its rock guitar, became two of the biggest hits of the decade, and the album also contains the gorgeous ballad 'Dim All the Lights' and the haunting 'Sunset People'. Summer's extraordinary voice, which could move from a whisper to a full-throated roar, was the perfect instrument for the album's range, and Bad Girls proved that disco could be as ambitious and varied as any music of its era.

name: At Folsom Prison
teaser: Johnny Cash's 1968 live album at Folsom State Prison. Cash had been playing prisons since the late 1950s, but this was the first time one was recorded. The inmates were told not to cheer because the warden feared a riot; you can hear them holding back until Cash baits them with the line 'I shot a man in Reno just to watch him die.'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen in order. The opening is the clack of a train — we never see the train. Then 'Folsom Prison Blues' — when Cash sings 'I shot a man in Reno', the inmates erupt; the warden had forbidden cheering, so their roar is one of defiance. The closing song 'Greystone Chapel' was written by inmate Glen Sherley; Cash got him a record deal, but Sherley died by suicide a decade later.

tracks.title: Flushed from the Bathroom of Your Heart

synopsis: At Folsom Prison (1968) is the album that saved Johnny Cash's career and became one of the most legendary live records in American music, a document of a man who had been to the edge finding his way back through music. Cash had been playing prison concerts since the late 1950s, but his career was in freefall by 1968: he was struggling with addiction, his records were failing, and his label was ready to drop him.
