He recorded this album live at Folsom State Prison in California, in front of an audience of inmates, and the chemistry between Cash and his audience, who whooped and cheered his songs about crime, punishment and redemption, is electric: 'Folsom Prison Blues', with its immortal line about shooting a man in Reno, became his biggest hit in years, and the album also contains 'Cocaine Blues', '25 Minutes to Go' and 'Give My Love to Rose'. The album went to number one and relaunched Cash's career, and it remains the definitive prison album and one of the greatest live records ever made.

name: King of the Delta Blues Singers
teaser: Robert Johnson's 1961 compilation — 16 songs recorded in two sessions in 1936-37, in a San Antonio hotel room and a Dallas warehouse. Johnson played with his back to the wall so no one could see his fingerings. The myth that he sold his soul at the crossroads came from these recordings.

exploreAction.targetName: King of the Delta Blues Singers (1961 compilation)
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Cross Road Blues' — Johnson plays slide guitar with a pocketknife and sings in a voice that sounds decades older than his 25 years. Then 'Hellhound on My Trail' — the guitar part contains a walking bassline, rhythm chords, and a lead melody, all played simultaneously. Eric Clapton said the first time he heard this album, he had to pull his car over.

tracks.title: If I Had Possession Over Judgement Day
When You Got a Good Friend

synopsis: King of the Delta Blues Singers (1961) is the compilation that introduced Robert Johnson, the most legendary figure in blues history, to the world, sixteen songs recorded in two sessions in 1936 and 1937 that became the foundation of rock and roll. Johnson recorded all of his known music in two bursts, in a hotel room in San Antonio and a warehouse in Dallas, over a period of less than a year, and then died at 27 in 1938 under mysterious circumstances, poisoned, according to legend, by a jealous husband. His music, built on his extraordinary guitar playing, which combined boogie bass lines, slide guitar and intricate fingerpicking with a voice full of pain and menace, became the template for everything that followed: 'Cross Road Blues', with its legend of Johnson selling his soul to the devil, 'Sweet Home Chicago', 'Come On in My Kitchen' and 'Hellhound on My Trail' are among the most influential songs ever recorded. This compilation, released decades after his death, introduced Johnson to the rock generation, and every guitarist from Eric Clapton to Keith Richards to Jimi Hendrix has acknowledged their debt to him.

name: Talking Timbuktu
teaser: Ali Farka Touré and Ry Cooder 1994 — the album that introduced Malian blues to the world. Touré, a farmer and guitarist from northern Mali, played a style so close to American Delta blues that musicologists debated whether the blues traveled from Africa to America or back. The answer is both, and this album is the proof.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Diaraby' — Touré's guitar mimics the kora, a West African harp. Then 'Ai Du' — Cooder's slide guitar and Touré's fingerpicking interlock as if they'd played together for decades (they'd met 3 days before). The album won a Grammy and was recorded in a makeshift studio in a Bamako hotel room.

synopsis: Talking Timbuktu (1994) is the album where Ali Farka Touré, the Malian guitarist known as the African John Lee Hooker, joined forces with the American guitarist Ry Cooder, and together they created one of the most celebrated world music albums ever recorded, a record that proved the deep connection between the blues and the music of West Africa. Touré was a farmer and musician from the north of Mali, and his guitar playing, built on the traditional music of the Songhai people, sounded uncannily like the Mississippi blues that had evolved an ocean away; the album, recorded mostly live in the studio with a small band, explores that connection with extraordinary warmth and skill. 'Ai Du', 'Soukora' and the title track are among the highlights, and Touré's voice and guitar, rooted in centuries of Malian tradition, blend seamlessly with Cooder's American blues sensibility. The album won a Grammy and introduced Touré to the world, and it remains one of the essential documents of the bond between African and American music.

name: Pata Pata
teaser: Miriam Makeba 1967 — the South African singer's global breakthrough, recorded while in exile from apartheid. The title track, based on a Johannesburg township dance, became a worldwide hit. Makeba's voice carried the weight of exile — she wouldn't return to South Africa for 30 years. She testified against apartheid at the UN; her music was banned in her homeland.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Pata Pata' — the click consonants of Xhosa create a percussive texture no other language can produce. Then 'Malayisha' — the groove is based on marabi, the township jazz that evolved under apartheid. Makeba testified at the UN in 1963; South Africa revoked her citizenship. She returned only after Mandela's release.

synopsis: Pata Pata (1967) is the album that made Miriam Makeba, the South African singer known as Mama Africa, a global star, and it remains the most famous record of her extraordinary career. Makeba had been exiled from South Africa in 1960 because of her opposition to apartheid, and she spent the 1960s introducing the world to the music of her homeland, becoming the first African artist to achieve international fame; this album, her biggest commercial success, was recorded while she was living in exile in America. The title track, 'Pata Pata', based on a South African dance, became a worldwide hit and remains one of the most recognizable songs in African music, and the album also contains 'The Click Song', sung partly in Xhosa with its famous click consonants, and 'Malaika', a haunting Swahili love song. Makeba's warm, luminous voice and her political courage made her a symbol of African liberation, and Pata Pata is the record where her music reached the whole world.

name: Egypt
teaser: Youssou N'Dour 2004 — the Senegalese singer's Grammy-winning tribute to Islam, recorded with an Egyptian orchestra. N'Dour's voice sings devotional lyrics in Wolof over Arabic orchestration. The album was initially controversial among Senegalese Muslims for blending sacred texts with secular music.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Allah' — N'Dour's voice rises from a whisper to a full-throated call over oud and strings. Then 'Touba — Daru Salaam' — the track references the holy city of the Mouride brotherhood, N'Dour's Sufi order. The album bridged West African mbalax with Egyptian classical music.

synopsis: Egypt (2004) is the album where Youssou N'Dour, the Senegalese singer who had spent decades as the most famous voice in African music, made his most personal and acclaimed record, a tribute to his Muslim faith that won him a Grammy and silenced the critics who had dismissed him as a pop star. N'Dour, whose mbalax music had made him a legend in West Africa and whose collaborations with Peter Gabriel had introduced him to the West, shocked many of his fans by announcing that he was turning to religious music, but Egypt, recorded with an Egyptian orchestra in Cairo, was a revelation: N'Dour's extraordinary voice, one of the most beautiful in any music, soared over arrangements that fused the griot traditions of Senegal with the classical music of the Arab world. The album's songs, including 'Tijaniyya' and 'Ba Toup' and the gorgeous 'Redemption', are meditations on faith, love and peace, and the record was hailed as a masterpiece, the sound of one of Africa's greatest voices making music for the soul.

name: Transa
teaser: Caetano Veloso 1972 — recorded in London while exiled from Brazil's military dictatorship. The album mixes bossa nova, samba, folk, and psychedelic rock, all sung in Portuguese with the urgency of separation from home. Veloso and Gilberto Gil were arrested, imprisoned, and exiled by the junta for 'subversive' music.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'You Don't Know Me' — Veloso sings in English for the first time, to hosts who couldn't understand what he'd lost. Then 'Nostalgia (That's What Rock'n Roll Is)' — homesickness disguised as a rock song. Veloso's exile lasted 3 years; Gil later became Brazil's Minister of Culture.

tracks.title: Nostalgia (That's What Rock'n Roll Is All About)

synopsis: Transa (1972) is the album where Caetano Veloso, the Brazilian singer and songwriter who had been exiled by the military dictatorship that ruled Brazil, made the masterpiece of his exile years, a record of such restless invention that it remains one of the essential albums of Brazilian music. Veloso had been arrested and forced into exile in 1969 for his role in the tropicalia movement, which had challenged the dictatorship with its fusion of Brazilian music and international pop, and he spent his exile in London, where he recorded Transa with a group of musicians including the guitarist Jards Macalé. The album moves through bossa nova, samba, folk rock and experimental sound with breathtaking freedom: 'Tropicalia', 'You Don't Know Me', 'Nine Out of Ten' and the title track, which mixes English and Portuguese, are full of longing for Brazil and determination to keep creating. Transa is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of Veloso's career, the record where exile became art.

name: Live at the Monterey International Pop Festival
teaser: Ravi Shankar 1967 — the performance that introduced Indian classical music to the Western counterculture. Shankar played a 20-minute raga to thousands of hippies who'd never heard a sitar. He gently taught the audience when to clap, treating the festival as a teaching moment. Alla Rakha's tabla playing is a masterclass.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dhun' — Shankar closes his eyes and doesn't open them for 20 minutes. The audience doesn't clap between movements because Shankar asked them not to. His influence runs through The Beatles, Coltrane, and Philip Glass.

synopsis: Live at the Monterey International Pop Festival (1967) is the performance that introduced Indian classical music to the Western counterculture, and it made Ravi Shankar, already a master of the sitar, a beloved figure to a generation of rock fans. Shankar was invited to the Monterey Pop Festival by the organizers, who wanted to expose the audience of hippies and rock fans to the breadth of world music, and his afternoon set, which he later said he was nervous about playing to such an audience, was a revelation: his twenty-minute raga, building slowly from meditative exploration to breathtaking virtuosity, held the crowd of thousands completely spellbound. The recording captures Shankar at the peak of his powers, and the album introduced the sound of the sitar to the West at exactly the moment when musicians like the Beatles and the Byrds were beginning to experiment with Indian instruments. It remains one of the most important live recordings of the 1960s, the record where Indian classical music and Western rock first truly met.

name: Éthiopiques Vol. 4: Ethio Jazz
teaser: Mulatu Astatke 1969-1974 (compiled 1998) — the godfather of Ethio-jazz, fusing traditional Ethiopian scales with American jazz and Latin rhythms. Astatke studied at Berklee. The music was nearly lost during the Derg regime; master tapes were hidden by a radio station archivist and rescued decades later.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Yèkèrmo Sèw' — the vibraphone melody is based on a 5-note Ethiopian scale. Then 'Yègellé Tezeta' — the horns could be from a 1940s Harlem ballroom. The Éthiopiques series introduced Ethiopian music to the world.

synopsis: Éthiopiques Vol. 4: Ethio Jazz (compiled 1998, music from 1969-1974) is the essential document of Mulatu Astatke, the father of Ethio-jazz, and it is the record that introduced one of the most unique sounds in music history to the world. Astatke, an Ethiopian who studied music in London, New York and Boston, spent the 1960s developing a music that fused the five-note pentatonic scales and rhythms of traditional Ethiopian music with American jazz, Latin percussion and funk, and the result sounded like nothing else on earth. This compilation gathers his finest work from the golden age of Ethiopian music, including 'Yèkèrmo Sèw', 'Mètché Dérshè' and 'Mulatu', and its blend of swinging jazz horns, vibraphone, organ and hypnotic Ethiopian melodies is utterly intoxicating. The album was compiled decades after the music was recorded, and it became the gateway through which the world discovered Ethiopian music, later gaining new fame through its use in Jim Jarmusch's film Broken Flowers. It remains an essential, magical record.

name: Miss Perfumado
teaser: Cesária Évora 1992 — the Cape Verdean singer's international debut at age 51. She sang barefoot on stage in a style called morna — songs of longing, separation, and the sea. Her voice carried decades of singing in bars for drinks. The album made her a star across Europe and Africa.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sodade' — the word means deep, existential longing for something lost, and Évora's voice makes you feel it. Then 'Angola' — about Cape Verdean men who emigrated for work. Évora was 51 when this album made her a star.

synopsis: Miss Perfumado (1992) is the album that made Cesária Évora, the Cape Verdean singer known as the barefoot diva, an international star at the age of 51, and it remains the most beloved record of her extraordinary career. Évora had been singing for decades in the bars of Mindelo, the port city of the Cape Verde islands, but it was not until a French record producer discovered her in her late forties that her voice reached the world; her international debut, recorded in Paris with a group of musicians from her homeland, introduced the world to the morna, the melancholy, blues-tinged song form of Cape Verde, and to her extraordinary voice, warm, sorrowful and full of the saudade, the longing for home and lost love, that defines the music. The title track, 'Miss Perfumado', and the haunting 'Sodade', a song about the Cape Verdeans who left home to work abroad, became classics, and the album sold millions. Évora, who famously performed barefoot in solidarity with the poor women of her islands, became a symbol of her country, and Miss Perfumado is the record where her genius reached the world.

name: Mustt Mustt
teaser: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan 1990 — the Pakistani qawwali master's crossover album, produced by Michael Brook at Peter Gabriel's Real World Studios. Khan's voice could hold a single note for over a minute while improvising elaborate variations. He could sing for 10 hours without stopping; his marathon shrine performances attracted hundreds of thousands.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Khan's voice rises from a rumble to an ecstatic wail over a harmonium drone. Then 'Nothing Without You' — subtle electronic production added to traditional qawwali. Khan's collaboration with Western artists introduced Sufi devotional music to new audiences.

tracks.title: Mustt Mustt (Lost in His Work) (Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan)

synopsis: Mustt Mustt (1990) is the album where Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, the Pakistani master of qawwali, the ecstatic devotional music of Sufi Islam, made his crossover album, and it introduced the most powerful voice in world music to Western audiences. Khan had spent two decades perfecting the art of qawwali, a music of hypnotic rhythms, call-and-response and extraordinary vocal improvisation designed to induce spiritual ecstasy, and his voice, which could soar for minutes on a single breath, was regarded as one of the greatest instruments in any music. For this album, produced by the Canadian guitarist Michael Brook and released on Peter Gabriel's Real World label, Khan was joined by Western musicians, including a rock drummer and the members of the band Massive Attack in later sessions, and the result was a stunning fusion of tradition and modernity. The title track, a soaring, ecstatic song of love for God, became a favorite of the world music audience, and the album remains the essential introduction to the genius of the man often called the voice of God.

name: Reign in Blood
teaser: Slayer 1986 — 28 minutes of relentless thrash metal, produced by Rick Rubin. The album's 10 tracks average under 3 minutes. 'Angel of Death', about Nazi doctor Josef Mengele, was so controversial that Columbia refused to distribute it. Drummer Dave Lombardo's double-bass patterns hit 240 BPM without triggers.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Raining Blood' — the opening thunderstorm leads into one of metal's most famous riffs. Then 'Angel of Death' — the tempo shifts are so abrupt they sound like tape skipping. Rubin's production is dry and close, making the band sound like they're in the room with you.

synopsis: Reign in Blood (1986) is the album that took thrash metal to its absolute extreme, a record of such speed, brutality and precision that it remains one of the most influential metal albums ever made. Slayer had spent the early 1980s building a reputation as the most aggressive band in the emerging thrash scene, and Reign in Blood, produced by Rick Rubin, who gave the band's attack a clean, crushing sound, was their breakthrough: ten songs in under twenty-nine minutes, an unrelenting barrage of blast beats, razor-sharp riffs and Tom Araya's shouted, snarled vocals. 'Angel of Death', which opens the album, is a harrowing account of the Nazi doctor Josef Mengele's experiments at Auschwitz, and its subject matter, like the rest of the album's fascination with death and violence, caused controversy, but the music's technical brilliance silenced most critics. 'Raining Blood', the closing track, became the band's signature song. Reign in Blood is now universally regarded as a masterpiece of extreme metal, the record that set the standard for everything that followed.

name: Symbolic
teaser: Death 1995 — Chuck Schuldiner's masterpiece of technical death metal. Schuldiner had evolved from primitive death metal into progressive territory while losing none of the intensity. The lyrics addressed philosophy and human nature. He died of brain cancer at 34, leaving behind a legacy as the father of death metal.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the opening riff shifts time signatures every 4 bars. Then 'Crystal Mountain' — closer to progressive rock than metal, with a guitar solo quoting classical themes. Schuldiner was 28 when he recorded this.

synopsis: Symbolic (1995) is the album where Death, the band of Chuck Schuldiner, who is universally regarded as the father of death metal, reached the peak of its evolution, a record of stunning technical mastery and surprising musicality. Schuldiner had invented death metal in the mid-1980s with albums of primitive, savage extremity, but he was never content to repeat himself: over the course of his career, his music grew steadily more complex and sophisticated, and Symbolic, recorded with a brilliant young band including the guitarist Shannon Hamm and drummer Gene Hoglan, found him writing music of extraordinary ambition. The album's songs, including 'Symbolic', 'Zero Tolerance', 'Crystal Mountain' and the epic '1,000 Eyes', move effortlessly between crushing heaviness and soaring, almost melodic passages, with Schuldiner's riffs and solos displaying a command of the instrument that few metal guitarists have matched. Schuldiner died of brain cancer in 2001 at the age of 34, and Symbolic stands as the crowning achievement of his remarkable career, the record where death metal became art.

name: Filosofem
teaser: Burzum 1996 — Varg Vikernes's fourth album, recorded in prison while serving a sentence for murder. The only instrument he was allowed was a synthesizer. The lo-fi production — a headset microphone through a cheap amplifier — became the defining sound of atmospheric black metal.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dunkelheit' — the synth drone lasts 2 minutes before the guitars enter, and the distortion turns riffs into texture. Then 'Rundgang' — a 25-minute ambient track from a single repeating melody. Vikernes recorded the guitar through his prison roommate's stereo.

tracks.title: Beholding the Daughters of the Firmament
Rundtgåing av den transcendentale egenhetens støtte

synopsis: Filosofem (1996) is the fourth album of Burzum, the project of the Norwegian musician Varg Vikernes, and it is one of the most influential and controversial records in the history of black metal, an album of extraordinary bleakness recorded while its creator was in prison for murder. Vikernes had been a central figure in the Norwegian black metal scene of the early 1990s, which was notorious for its church burnings and violence, and in 1994 he was convicted of the murder of his former friend, the guitarist Euronymous of Mayhem; he recorded Filosofem while serving his sentence, with the prison authorities allowing him only a guitar and a keyboard, and the album's music, which he had composed earlier, reflects his extreme isolation. The album's four long tracks, including the fifteen-minute 'Dunkelheit' and the ambient piece 'Rundtgåing av den Transcendentale Identitetens Støtte', are built on a single, hypnotic, heavily distorted guitar riff repeated to the point of trance, with Vikernes's shrieking vocals buried deep in the mix. Filosofem is now regarded as a landmark of the genre, the sound of black metal at its most pure and most desolate.

name: In the Nightside Eclipse
teaser: Emperor 1994 — recorded in Norway's Grieg Hall, home of the Bergen Philharmonic. Ihsahn's compositions layered distorted guitars, blast-beat drums, and keyboards into a sound both beautiful and terrifying. The album defined symphonic black metal.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Am the Black Wizards' — the keyboard melody sounds like a corrupted church organ. Then 'Inno a Satana' — the title is Italian for 'Hymn to Satan'. Emperor's members were teenagers. The production is deliberately murky, keyboards mixed high to overwhelm the guitars.

tracks.title: Cosmic Keys to My Creations & Times
The Majesty of the Night Sky

synopsis: In the Nightside Eclipse (1994) is the debut album of Emperor, and it remains one of the most important and influential records in the history of black metal, the album that took the genre's raw aggression and elevated it into something symphonic and majestic. Emperor, led by the guitarist and vocalist Ihsahn and guitarist Samoth, were teenagers when they recorded the album in Norway's Grieg Hall, the concert hall of the Bergen Philharmonic, and the building's grand acoustics shaped the record's sound: the band layered their distorted, tremolo-picked guitars with sweeping keyboard melodies, creating a sound that was both ferocious and operatic. 'I Am the Black Wizards', 'Into the Infinity of Thoughts' and 'Cosmic Keys to My Creations and Times' are among the album's highlights, and its blend of satanic fury, fantasy imagery and classical ambition made it a template for the symphonic black metal that followed. In the Nightside Eclipse is now regarded as one of the essential albums of the genre, the record where black metal's second wave reached its artistic peak.

name: Destroy Erase Improve
teaser: Meshuggah 1995 — invented the 'djent' sound a decade before the term existed. Guitarists used detuned 8-string guitars and polymetric riffs — guitars in one time signature, drums in another. The title is a manifesto: destroy conventions, erase boundaries, improve the form.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Future Breed Machine' — the opening riff cycles through a pattern of 17 before repeating, while drums stay in 4/4. Then 'Soul Burn' — a guitar solo played through a breath controller, normally used by saxophonists. Meshuggah rewired how metal thinks about rhythm.

synopsis: Destroy Erase Improve (1995) is the album where Meshuggah, the Swedish band that would become the most influential force in extreme metal of the next two decades, invented the sound that would later be called djent, a full decade before the term existed. The band's core innovation was rhythmic: their guitarist Fredrik Thordendal and Mårten Hagström played in detuned 8-string guitars, creating a crushing, percussive sound, and their music was built on polyrhythms and polymeters that pitted different rhythmic patterns against each other with mathematical precision. Destroy Erase Improve was their second album, and it found them fully developing this approach: 'Future Breed Machine', 'Soul Burn' and 'New Millennium Cyanide Christ' are relentless assaults of technical fury, while the eleven-minute 'Inside What's Within Behind' showed their more experimental side. The album was ahead of its time, and it is now regarded as a landmark, the record where the rhythmic complexity of progressive metal and the brutality of death metal were fused into something entirely new.

name: Blackwater Park
teaser: Opeth 2001 — produced by Steven Wilson of Porcupine Tree. Mikael Åkerfeldt's songwriting combined death metal aggression with 70s progressive dynamics, shifting from guttural growls to clean falsetto within a song. The 10-minute title track is a masterclass in dynamics.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the acoustic interlude at 4:30 arrives like sunlight through a storm. Then 'The Drapery Falls' — a fingerpicked acoustic pattern returns as a distorted riff 5 minutes later. Wilson's production gave the album clarity that made the heavy sections heavier.

synopsis: Blackwater Park (2001) is the album where Opeth, the Swedish band led by Mikael Åkerfeldt, made their masterpiece, a record that fused the brutality of death metal with the beauty of 1970s progressive rock in a way no band had managed before. Åkerfeldt, who had spent the 1990s building Opeth into one of the most respected bands in extreme metal, was a devoted fan of the progressive rock of the 1970s, and Blackwater Park, produced by Steven Wilson of Porcupine Tree, found him finally bringing those two loves together: the album moves seamlessly from crushing, guttural death metal passages to passages of gorgeous, melancholic acoustic beauty, often within the same song. 'The Leper Affinity', 'Blackwater Park', 'The Drapery Falls' and the epic 'Deliverance' are among the album's highlights, and Åkerfeldt's voice, which could switch from a demonic growl to a fragile croon, is one of the most versatile in metal. Blackwater Park is now regarded as one of the greatest metal albums of the 2000s, the record that proved extreme metal could be beautiful.

name: Leviathan
teaser: Mastodon 2004 — a concept album about Moby-Dick. The band's three vocalists trade off like characters in a play. Drummer Brann Dailor, influenced by jazz as much as metal, propels songs that shift time signatures like whales changing depth.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Blood and Thunder' — the opening riff sounds like a ship being dragged under. Then 'Hearts Alive' — a 13-minute epic following the Pequod's final pursuit. The band read Moby-Dick together before writing. The lyrics use direct Melville quotes.

synopsis: Leviathan (2004) is the album where Mastodon, the Atlanta quartet who had spent their early years making ferocious sludge metal, announced themselves as one of the most ambitious and gifted bands of their generation, a concept album based on Herman Melville's Moby-Dick. The album retells the story of Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for the white whale through music of crushing heaviness and surprising sophistication: the band's three vocalists, Troy Sanders, Brent Hinds and Brann Dailor, trade off like characters in a play, and their riffs and rhythms, powered by Dailor's extraordinary drumming, are among the most inventive in modern metal. 'Blood and Thunder' opens the album with a statement of intent, 'I Am Ahab' and 'Seabeast' are crushing epics, 'Hearts Alive', the album's thirteen-minute centerpiece, is a stunning account of the final confrontation with the whale, and 'Joseph Merrick' closes the record with unexpected tenderness. Leviathan made Mastodon the leaders of the new wave of American heavy metal, and it remains their most beloved album.

name: Mama Tried
teaser: Merle Haggard 1968 — an ex-convict's apology to his mother for a life of crime. Haggard had spent 3 years in San Quentin (where he saw Johnny Cash perform). His Bakersfield sound — raw, Telecaster-driven, stripped of Nashville strings — was a rebuke to country-pop crossover.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Haggard's vocal carries the weight of someone who'd actually done time. Then 'I'm a Lonesome Fugitive' — a song about life on the run that Haggard understood firsthand. The album was recorded in Bakersfield with his touring band, not Nashville session players.

tracks.title: In the Good Old Days (When Times Were Bad)
The Sunny Side of My Life
Too Many Bridges to Cross Over

synopsis: Mama Tried (1968) is the album where Merle Haggard, the most gifted and complex figure in country music, made his most personal statement, a record built around an ex-convict's apology to his mother for a life of crime. Haggard had spent his youth in and out of trouble, eventually serving three years in San Quentin prison, where he saw Johnny Cash perform and decided to change his life; the title track, 'Mama Tried', written from the point of view of a man who knows his mother did everything she could to keep him from crime, became one of the most famous songs in country music history. The album, recorded with his band the Strangers, is full of the hard-edged, honest honky tonk that made Haggard the most important country artist of his era: 'The Day the Rains Came', 'I'll Always Know' and his version of the prison song 'Green, Green Grass of Home' complete a record that is both deeply personal and utterly universal. Mama Tried is now regarded as one of the essential albums of country music.

name: Red Headed Stranger
teaser: Willie Nelson 1975 — a concept album about a preacher on the run after killing his wife. Columbia thought it was an unfinished demo and refused to release it. Nelson recorded it with just his guitar, his sister Bobbie on piano, and minimal accompaniment. It became the cornerstone of outlaw country.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain' — Nelson's vocal is so sparse the silence between phrases carries as much weight as the words. Then the title track — the album's narrative unfolds across 15 tracks with Nelson's guitar as narrator. Recorded in 5 days for $4,000. Nelson refused to add strings.

tracks.title: I Couldn't Believe It Was True
Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain
Can I Sleep in Your Arms
Remember Me (When the Candle Lights Are Gleaming)

synopsis: Red Headed Stranger (1975) is the album where Willie Nelson, already one of the most respected songwriters in country music, made the record that defined the outlaw country movement and saved his career, a spare, haunting concept album that remains one of the most beloved records in American music. Nelson recorded the album in just a few days with almost no instrumentation, just his guitar, his voice and a small group of musicians, and its story, about a preacher who kills his wife and her lover and flees across the West, was told so subtly that Columbia Records executives thought it was an unfinished demo and refused to release it. Nelson fought for the album, and he was right: 'Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain', the album's biggest hit, became his first number one single in over a decade, and the record's stripped-down sound, a direct rebuke to the overproduced country pop of the era, made it a landmark. Red Headed Stranger is now regarded as one of the greatest concept albums ever made.

name: Jolene
teaser: Dolly Parton 1974 — the title track, written in a single afternoon, is a plea to another woman not to take her man. It became the most-covered country song by non-country artists. The album proved Parton was more than a country singer — she was one of America's great songwriters.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the fingerpicking by guitarist Chip Young was improvised in the studio. Then 'I Will Always Love You' — Parton wrote it as a farewell to mentor Porter Wagoner. Whitney Houston's version sold 20 million, but Parton's original, with just voice and guitar, is definitive.

synopsis: Jolene (1974) is the album that features the most famous song Dolly Parton ever wrote, and it captures the singer at the moment she was becoming one of the most beloved and important figures in American music. The title track, 'Jolene', written in a single afternoon after a young girl asked Parton for her autograph and told her she had the most beautiful name, is a plea from a woman to another woman not to take her man, and its haunting melody, built on a minor key and Parton's crystalline voice, made it an instant classic that has been covered by hundreds of artists. The album also contains 'I Will Always Love You', a farewell song Parton wrote for her mentor Porter Wagoner, which would later become Whitney Houston's biggest hit, and 'Please Don't Stop Loving Me'. Parton's songwriting, which combined the honesty of country with the craft of the best pop writers, was at its peak, and Jolene remains one of the essential albums of her extraordinary career.

name: 40 Greatest Hits
teaser: Hank Williams 1978 compilation — the essential collection from country music's first mythic figure. Williams recorded all his hits between 1947 and 1952; he died at 29 from heart failure caused by alcohol and morphine. His songs established the emotional vocabulary of country music.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry' — the line 'the moon just went behind a cloud to hide its face and cry' is one of the most perfect couplets in American song. Then 'Your Cheatin' Heart' — written in the back of a car, dictated to his future wife. Williams never used headphones; he sang to the musicians in the room.

tracks.title: A Mansion on the Hill (Fred Rose/Hank Williams)
Wedding Bells (Arthur Q. Smith) sold to Claude Boone
You're Gonna Change (Or I'm Gonna Leave)
My Bucket's Got a Hole in It (Clarence Williams)
I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry
I Just Don't Like This Kind of Living
My Son Calls Another Man Daddy (Hank Williams/Jewell House)
Why Don't You Love Me (Like You Used to Do)
They'll Never Take Her Love from Me (Leon Payne)
I Can't Help It (If I'm Still in Love with You)
(I Heard That) Lonesome Whistle (Jimmie Davis/Hank Williams)
I'm Sorry for You, My Friend
Settin' the Woods on Fire (Ed G. Nelson/Fred Rose)
I'll Never Get Out of This World Alive (Hank Williams/Fred Rose)
Take These Chains from My Heart (Fred Rose/Hy Heath)
I Won't Be Home No More

synopsis: 40 Greatest Hits (1978) is the essential collection from Hank Williams, the man who more than anyone else created modern country music and who remains its most mythic figure. Williams recorded all of his greatest songs in a period of just five years, between 1947 and his death at the age of 29 in 1953, and this double album gathers the best of them: 'Your Cheatin' Heart', 'I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry', 'Hey, Good Lookin'', 'Jambalaya (On the Bayou)', 'Cold, Cold Heart', 'I Saw the Light' and forty more. Williams wrote with a simplicity and emotional directness that has never been surpassed, and his voice, which could convey heartbreak, humor and gospel fervor in a single song, was one of the most expressive in American music. He died in the back of his Cadillac on New Year's Day 1953, at the height of his fame, and his music became the foundation on which country music, and much of rock and roll, was built. This collection remains the definitive introduction to his genius.

name: Songs of Leonard Cohen
teaser: Leonard Cohen 1967 — the 33-year-old Canadian poet's debut, after 4 books of poetry and 2 novels. Cohen couldn't really sing, but his songs — 'Suzanne', 'So Long, Marianne' — needed a poet, not a vocalist. The production is so sparse you can hear his fingers sliding on the guitar strings.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Suzanne' — the song began as a poem about dancer Suzanne Verdal. Then 'So Long, Marianne' — written for Marianne Ihlen on the Greek island of Hydra. Cohen described his voice as 'a basso profundo born without a larynx.'

tracks.title: Hey, That's No Way to Say Goodbye
One of Us Cannot Be Wrong

synopsis: Songs of Leonard Cohen (1967) is the debut album of Leonard Cohen, the Canadian poet who came to music late and ended up changing it forever, a record of such quiet, literary power that it remains one of the most influential debuts in popular music. Cohen was 33 when the album was released, an established poet and novelist who had published four books of poetry and two novels, and he had come to music almost by accident, discovering that he could not live on poetry alone; he taught himself to sing and play guitar, and his songs, full of the religious imagery, erotic longing and dark wit of his poetry, were unlike anything else in the folk scene he entered. 'Suzanne', a haunting song about a woman he met in Montreal, became a standard, and the album also contains 'Sisters of Mercy', 'So Long, Marianne' and 'Hey, That's No Way to Say Goodbye'. Cohen's voice, low and grave, was not conventionally beautiful, but it was utterly compelling, and Songs of Leonard Cohen announced one of the greatest songwriters of the century.

name: Tea for the Tillerman
teaser: Cat Stevens 1970 — recorded after near-death from tuberculosis. The songs — about fathers and sons, spiritual searching, finding peace — were written on a single acoustic guitar while Stevens recovered in a London hospital. He converted to Islam in 1977 and wouldn't release secular music for 28 years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Father and Son' — Stevens sings both roles: the father in a low register, the son higher. Then 'Wild World' — a farewell written for Patti D'Arbanville. The album's warmth comes from producer Paul Samwell-Smith's restraint: nothing is added that doesn't need to be there.

tracks.title: On the Road to Find Out

synopsis: Tea for the Tillerman (1970) is the album where Cat Stevens, a pop star who had nearly died of tuberculosis two years earlier, found his true voice, and it remains one of the most beloved singer-songwriter albums of its era. Stevens had been a teen idol in the mid-1960s, but a serious bout of tuberculosis forced him to stop performing and rethink his life; when he returned to music, his songs were deeper, more spiritual and more personal, and Tea for the Tillerman, his fourth album, is full of that new maturity. 'Wild World', his biggest hit, is a bittersweet farewell song, 'Father and Son' is a heartbreaking dialogue between a father and his son about following your own path, 'Tea for the Tillerman' and 'Longer Boats' show his growing interest in spirituality, and 'Where Do the Children Play?' questions the cost of progress. Stevens's warm voice and his gift for simple, profound melodies made the album a worldwide hit, and it remains the definitive statement of his classic period.

name: Vespertine
teaser: Björk's 2001 chamber-electronic album, mostly recorded alone in her Reykjavík home. She used micro-beats built from everyday sounds: shuffling cards, footsteps in snow, ice cracking. The beats sit closer to your chest than your head — that's intentional.

exploreAction.instruction: Notice how the beats hit your chest vs your head — that's intentional. The album mixes orchestral and beat programming in a way most artists avoid. It rewards headphones and speakers differently. The harp parts were played by Zeena Parkins, a classical harpist who had to learn to play against electronic beats.

synopsis: Vespertine (2001) is the album where Björk, the Icelandic artist who had spent a decade reinventing pop music, made her most intimate and delicate record, a work of chamber-electronic beauty that is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 2000s. Björk recorded most of the album alone in her home in Reykjavik, and its sound is built on micro-beats, tiny fragments of everyday sound, footsteps, shuffling cards, ice cracking, that she recorded herself and arranged with the producers Thomas Knak and Matthew Herbert, alongside lush string arrangements and music-box melodies. The album's subject is the private world of a new love, its tenderness, its secrecy and its ecstasy, and songs like 'Hidden Place', 'Pagan Poetry', 'It's Not Up to You' and the extraordinary 'Unison' are among the most beautiful of her career. Björk's voice, which had never sounded more fragile or more powerful, floats over the delicate textures like a creature from another world. Vespertine was hailed as a masterpiece on release, and it remains Björk's most cherished album.

name: Homogenic
teaser: Björk 1997 — recorded in Spain after a stalker mailed her a letter bomb and then killed himself on camera. She channeled the trauma into an album that sounds like Iceland itself: volcanoes, glaciers, and strings that sweep like the northern lights. The cover was shot by Alexander McQueen.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Jóga' — the strings were arranged by Eumir Deodato and recorded in a single session in London. The rhythmic beat underneath is a distorted sample of volcanic rock hitting water. Then 'Bachelorette' — the lyrics are a short story about a tree that grows a city, written by Sjón, an Icelandic poet and novelist.

synopsis: Homogenic (1997) is the album where Björk, who had spent the first half of the 1990s exploring the boundaries of electronic pop, turned her attention to the raw power of emotion, and it remains one of the most important albums of her career. Björk recorded the album after a traumatic period in her life, during which a stalker sent her a letter bomb and then killed himself on camera, and the record's title reflects her determination to channel that fear and anger into something controlled and beautiful: Homogenic fuses the warm, organic sound of Icelandic strings with beats of crushing, almost industrial power, creating music of extraordinary tension and release. 'Jóga', written for her friend and later her country, 'Bachelorette', 'Hunter' and the stunning 'All Is Full of Love', which closes the album with one of the most beautiful songs she has ever recorded, are among her finest work. Homogenic was hailed as a masterpiece, and it remains the record where Björk fully synthesized her experimental impulses into something transcendent.

name: Exodus
teaser: Bob Marley and the Wailers 1977 — recorded in London after Marley survived an assassination attempt in Jamaica. Gunmen broke into his house and shot him in the chest and arm two days before a peace concert. Marley played the concert anyway, then flew to London to record this album in exile.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Jamming' — the bassline by Aston 'Family Man' Barrett walks a single note for two minutes before changing. Then 'Three Little Birds' — the 'every little thing is gonna be alright' chorus was improvised during a studio jam. The album was Time magazine's Album of the Century.

synopsis: Exodus (1977) is the album where Bob Marley, already the most famous musician in the developing world, made the record that would introduce reggae to the entire planet, and it remains the greatest album of his career. Marley and the Wailers recorded the album in London, where Marley had fled after surviving an assassination attempt in Jamaica, when gunmen broke into his home and shot him and his wife; the album's title refers to the biblical story of exile and return, and its songs are full of the determination of a man who had looked death in the face and kept moving. 'Exodus', 'Waiting in Vain', 'Jamming', 'Three Little Birds' and the stunning 'One Love/People Get Ready', which became a global anthem of unity, are among the most beloved songs ever recorded, and Marley's music, rooted in reggae and Rastafari but open to the whole world, reached its fullest expression on this record. Exodus is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 20th century.

name: Super Ape
teaser: Lee 'Scratch' Perry 1976 — recorded at his legendary Black Ark studio, a converted backyard shed in Kingston. Perry produced the entire album alone, playing many instruments himself and bouncing tracks between two 4-track tape machines. The album includes recordings of cows mooing and Perry blowing bubbles into a microphone.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen on quality headphones. Perry mixed the album in mono because he believed stereo was a gimmick. The bass frequencies sit so low they're almost subsonic — Perry would crank the bass EQ until the mixing board meters pinned. The album was meant to be played loud enough to feel through your feet.

synopsis: Super Ape (1976) is the masterpiece of Lee 'Scratch' Perry, the Jamaican producer who was one of the most visionary and eccentric figures in the history of popular music, a record of pure, uncategorizable genius that remains one of the essential documents of dub reggae. Perry had built his legendary Black Ark studio in a converted backyard shed in Kingston, and it was there that he developed the art of dub, taking reggae rhythms and deconstructing them with echo, reverb and all manner of studio effects until they became something entirely new, music that seemed to be coming from a haunted, psychedelic otherworld. Super Ape, made with the group the Upsetters, is the purest expression of his vision: 'Zion's Blood', 'Croaking Lizard' and the title track are built on deep bass, ghostly horns and Perry's strange, chattering vocal fragments, all drenched in the echo that made his studio legendary. The album is now regarded as one of the greatest dub records ever made, the sound of a mad genius at the height of his powers.

name: Goldberg Variations (1955 Recording)
teaser: Glenn Gould's 1955 debut recording — he was 22 and unknown. Columbia Records thought he was insane to debut with Bach's Goldberg Variations, a piece considered academic and unmarketable. Gould hummed audibly throughout the recording; the engineers couldn't stop him. The album became a bestseller and redefined how Bach was played.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen for Gould's humming — it's audible in nearly every track. He believed the voice and fingers were one instrument. Then compare the Aria at the start and the Aria da Capo at the end — the same notes at the same tempo, but Gould plays them completely differently. The 1981 re-recording is slower by nearly 13 minutes and is a different universe.

synopsis: Goldberg Variations (1955 Recording) is the debut album of Glenn Gould, and it is one of the most famous and influential classical recordings ever made, the record that made a 22-year-old Canadian pianist a legend overnight. Gould chose to make his debut with Bach's Goldberg Variations, a monumental work consisting of an aria and thirty variations, a choice that Columbia Records executives thought was insane for an unknown pianist, but Gould's performance was so extraordinary that it silenced all doubt: his playing was fast, precise and revelatory, bringing a clarity and rhythmic drive to Bach's music that had never been heard before. The recording made Gould a star, and his interpretation of the Goldberg Variations became the benchmark against which all others were measured. Gould, famously eccentric, withdrew from live performance eight years later at the age of 31, devoting himself entirely to recordings, and he returned to the Goldberg Variations in 1981 with a slower, more profound interpretation that became his final testament. The 1955 recording remains a landmark of classical music.

name: Music for 18 Musicians
teaser: Steve Reich 1978 — a 56-minute pulse piece for violin, cello, clarinets, pianos, marimbas, xylophones, and metallophone, plus four female voices. The entire piece is built from 11 chords played in cycle. Musicians have described performing it as a form of meditation.

exploreAction.instruction: Focus on the pulse — it never stops for 56 minutes. Then shift your attention to the marimbas. Then to the voices. Each listening layer reveals a different piece. The work has no conductor; musicians cue each other by breathing audibly, which Reich scored into the piece.

synopsis: Music for 18 Musicians (1978) is the masterpiece of Steve Reich, one of the most important composers of the 20th century, and it remains one of the most beloved works in the history of minimalist music, a piece of hypnotic, radiant beauty that changed the course of contemporary composition. The piece, which runs for about an hour, is built on a single pulse, established at the beginning by the pianos and mallet instruments, and from that pulse Reich builds a series of sections that explore a constantly shifting pattern of harmonies and rhythms, with the eleven chords of the opening slowly cycling through the piece as the ensemble, including strings, clarinets, pianos and four female voices, weaves around them. The result is music of extraordinary clarity and emotional power, at once cerebral and deeply moving, and the work's influence, from classical music to rock to electronic music to film scores, is immeasurable. Music for 18 Musicians is now regarded as one of the essential works of the 20th century, the record where minimalism reached its peak.

name: Be the Cowboy
teaser: Mitski's 2018 album of tightly drawn vignettes, each under three minutes. She wrote the songs in bursts — some in 15 minutes, some over months. The album title came from her realization that women in music are expected to be vulnerable; she wanted to project the swagger of a cowboy instead.

exploreAction.instruction: Pick one track that doesn't grab you on first listen. Play it three times back-to-back. Mitski writes songs that read flat on the surface — give them room to flip. 'Nobody' sounds like a disco banger until you realize it's about the terror of being alone. The whole album fits in the time it takes to commute across a city.

synopsis: Be the Cowboy (2018) is the album where Mitski, already one of the most gifted songwriters of her generation, made her most fully realized record, a collection of tightly drawn vignettes that cemented her reputation as one of the most important voices in indie rock. Mitski wrote the album's fourteen songs, most of them under three minutes, in bursts of creativity, and each one is a complete world: songs about loneliness, desire, performance and the impossible demands of being a woman in the world, delivered with her extraordinary voice, which can move from a whisper to a primal scream in a second. 'Nobody', the album's breakout hit, is a devastatingly catchy song about the longing for connection, 'Geyser' and 'A Pearl' are gorgeous, anguished rock songs, 'Me and My Husband' is a wry look at domesticity, and 'Two Slow Dancers' is a heartbreaking ballad about growing old. Be the Cowboy was hailed as a masterpiece, and it established Mitski, still in her twenties, as one of the defining artists of her era.

name: Hounds of Love
teaser: Kate Bush 1985 — recorded in her own 48-track studio built in a converted barn behind her house. Side A is pop singles; Side B is 'The Ninth Wave', a 7-song suite about a woman drifting alone at sea, hallucinating her past. The album used a Fairlight CMI sampler when almost no one had one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Side B ('The Ninth Wave') as a single piece. It's a complete narrative cycle: a woman falls through ice, drifts in freezing water, and experiences visions while waiting to be rescued — or not. Bush sampled her own voice and played it back at different speeds to create the ghosts. The helicopter at the end is an actual RAF rescue helicopter she recorded from her garden.

tracks.title: Running Up That Hill (A Deal with God)

synopsis: Hounds of Love (1985) is the album where Kate Bush, one of the most original and influential artists in the history of popular music, made her masterpiece, a record that is now universally regarded as one of the greatest albums of the 1980s. Bush recorded the album in her own studio, a 48-track facility she had built in a converted barn behind her house, giving her total creative freedom for the first time, and the record is divided into two halves: the first side is a set of brilliant pop songs, including the title track, 'Cloudbusting', based on the memoir of Wilhelm Reich's son, and 'Running Up That Hill', her most famous song, while the second side, 'The Ninth Wave', is a seven-song suite about a woman lost at sea, a stunning piece of avant-garde storytelling. Bush's extraordinary voice, her theatrical imagination and her pioneering use of the Fairlight synthesizer made her unique, and Hounds of Love, which took her from cult figure to global star, remains her greatest achievement.

name: Purple Rain
teaser: Prince 1984 — the soundtrack to a film that made $70 million on a $7 million budget. Prince recorded the title track live at a benefit concert; the 8-minute version is the first take, with no overdubs except strings. The label thought the album was too long and too strange to sell.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Prince's guitar solo at the end was recorded live at First Avenue in Minneapolis, with the crowd audible. The song builds for nearly 4 minutes before the solo arrives, and when it does, it doesn't end — it keeps climbing for another 4 minutes. Then 'When Doves Cry' — a song with no bassline, because Prince removed it at the last minute and dared anyone to notice.

synopsis: Purple Rain (1984) is the album where Prince, already one of the most gifted musicians of his generation, became the biggest star in the world, and it remains one of the greatest albums ever recorded, the soundtrack to the film that made him a legend. The film, which Prince largely financed himself, was a semi-autobiographical story of a young musician, and its soundtrack, recorded with his band the Revolution, contains some of the most beloved songs of the decade: 'When Doves Cry', with its revolutionary absence of a bass line, became his first number one single, 'Let's Go Crazy', 'I Would Die 4 U', 'Baby I'm a Star' and the eleven-minute title track, a stunning epic that Prince recorded live at a benefit concert, are all classics. The album's blend of rock, funk, pop and gospel, held together by Prince's extraordinary voice and his revolutionary use of the synthesizer, made it a phenomenon, selling over twenty million copies and winning an Oscar for Best Original Song Score. Purple Rain is the definitive Prince album.

name: Melodrama
teaser: Lorde 2017 — recorded over four years with Jack Antonoff, mostly in his Brooklyn apartment. The album structures a house party as the arc of a breakup: arrival, exhilaration, the first crack, the fight, the lonely Uber home. The piano on the cover is the actual piano Lorde wrote the album on.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Green Light' — the piano chords change on unexpected beats, creating a sense of forward motion that never settles. Then 'Liability' — recorded in a single take at 2 AM with Lorde at Antonoff's piano. The entire album is a 41-minute arc structured like a single party from entrance to exit.

synopsis: Melodrama (2017) is the second album of Lorde, the New Zealand singer who had taken the world by storm as a teenager, and it is the record where she proved she was one of the most gifted songwriters of her generation, a stunning concept album about the end of youth. Lorde spent four years writing the album with the producer Jack Antonoff, recording mostly in his Brooklyn apartment, and she structured it around a single house party, tracing the arc of a night from anticipation to ecstasy to heartbreak to the lonely morning after. 'Green Light', the album's lead single, is a euphoric song about moving on, 'Liability' is a devastating ballad about being too much for people, 'The Louvre' and 'Supercut' are gorgeous meditations on memory, and 'Perfect Places' closes the album with a question about whether any of it was worth it. Lorde's lyrics, full of precise, original observations about youth, love and loneliness, were hailed as the work of a major talent, and Melodrama was nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys.

name: folklore
teaser: Taylor Swift 2020 — written and recorded in isolation during the pandemic with Aaron Dessner of The National and Jack Antonoff. Swift abandoned pop structures for indie folk storytelling. The album was announced 16 hours before release with no singles or promotion.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'exile' — Bon Iver's Justin Vernon wrote his verse in character as a ghost. Then 'august' — the bridge was recorded in a single take with Swift's voice cracking at the end; they kept it because the imperfection was the point. The album is a triptych of fictional love triangles told from different perspectives.

synopsis: folklore (2020) is the album where Taylor Swift, the biggest pop star of her generation, completely reinvented herself during a global pandemic, and it remains the most acclaimed record of her career, winning Album of the Year at the Grammys. Stuck in isolation at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic, Swift began collaborating remotely with Aaron Dessner of the National and her longtime producer Jack Antonoff, and the songs they made were a radical departure from the glossy pop of her recent albums: instead of confessional pop anthems, folklore is a quiet, literary record full of characters, stories and escape, built on acoustic guitars, pianos and Dessner's atmospheric production. 'Cardigan', 'Exile', a duet with Bon Iver, 'The 1', 'August' and the devastating 'My Tears Ricochet' are among her finest songs, and the album's mature, understated sound, a world away from the maximalist pop she had perfected, took everyone by surprise. folklore was hailed as a masterpiece and made Swift, at 30, the first woman to win Album of the Year three times.

name: Like a Prayer
teaser: Madonna 1989 — recorded with Patrick Leonard and Stephen Bray while Madonna's marriage to Sean Penn was collapsing. Prince played guitar on three tracks uncredited. The title track used a gospel choir and Catholic imagery that got the Vatican to issue a condemnation. Pepsi cancelled a $5M endorsement deal over the music video.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Like a Prayer' — the opening guitar riff was played by Prince, who walked into the studio, recorded his parts, and left without saying goodbye. Then 'Promise to Try' — Madonna's tribute to her mother who died when Madonna was 5. The song has almost no percussion; the entire rhythm is carried by the piano.

synopsis: Like a Prayer (1989) is the album where Madonna, already the biggest female star in the world, made her most personal and ambitious record, and it remains one of the greatest pop albums ever made, the record that proved she was far more than a dance-pop star. Madonna recorded the album with Patrick Leonard and Stephen Bray while her marriage to Sean Penn was collapsing, and the songs reflect her turmoil: 'Like a Prayer', with its gospel choir and its controversial video, became one of the defining songs of the decade, 'Express Yourself' is a feminist anthem, 'Cherish', 'Till Death Do Us Part', written about her failing marriage, and the devastating 'Oh Father' show her new emotional range. Prince played guitar on 'Act of Contrition', and the album's blend of dance pop, gospel, rock and soul, all filtered through Madonna's growing ambition, made it her most critically acclaimed record. Like a Prayer sold millions and is now regarded as a landmark of pop music, the record where the Material Girl became an artist.

name: Lemonade
teaser: Beyoncé 2016 — a visual album exploring Black womanhood, infidelity, and Southern heritage. Features from Jack White, Kendrick Lamar, the Weeknd, and James Blake. The album samples everything from Led Zeppelin to Animal Collective to Malcolm X speeches. It was released exclusively on Tidal, with each song getting a film chapter on HBO.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Don't Hurt Yourself' — Jack White's distorted vocal sample under Beyoncé's scream was recorded at his Third Man Records studio in Nashville. Then 'Freedom' — Kendrick Lamar's verse was written in 30 minutes while Beyoncé watched from the control room. The album's structure mimics the Kübler-Ross stages of grief.

synopsis: Lemonade (2016) is the album where Beyoncé, already the most important figure in popular music, made her most ambitious and personal statement, a visual album that explored black womanhood, infidelity and Southern heritage with a raw honesty she had never shown before. The album, released as a film on HBO, tells the story of a woman confronting her husband's infidelity, and its songs trace an arc from rage to forgiveness: 'Formation', a celebration of black Southern identity that became an anthem, 'Sorry', 'Hold Up', 'Don't Hurt Yourself', a rock song featuring Jack White, 'Freedom', featuring Kendrick Lamar, and the devastating ballad 'Sandcastles' are among her finest work. The album's blend of R&B, rock, country, gospel and rap, with contributions from the Yeah Yeah Yeahs' Karen O, the Weeknd and James Blake, was stunningly ambitious, and its celebration of black culture, from the imagery of New Orleans to the poetry of Warsan Shire, made it a cultural landmark. Lemonade was hailed as a masterpiece and is now regarded as one of the greatest albums of the decade.

name: ANTI
teaser: Rihanna 2016 — recorded over 18 months in 4 countries after Rihanna fired her previous management and took full creative control. The album's sound — sparse, paranoid, hypnotic — was influenced by Tame Impala and vintage dub. The opening track 'Consideration' features SZA, who Rihanna discovered on SoundCloud.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Work' — the patois-heavy verses were written by Drake and Rihanna in a Toronto studio at 3 AM, trading lines back and forth. Then 'Love on the Brain' — the doo-wop throwback was recorded with a live band in a single 4-hour session. Rihanna's vocal cracks in the final chorus were left in because they proved it was live.

synopsis: ANTI (2016) is the album where Rihanna, who had spent a decade as the most consistent hit machine in pop, finally made the album she wanted to make, and it remains her most personal and acclaimed record. Rihanna took full creative control of the album after firing her management, and the result, recorded over eighteen months in four countries, was a radical departure from the glossy dance pop that had made her famous: ANTI is a sprawling, eclectic record that draws on R&B, soul, rock, dancehall and even country, with songs that are darker, stranger and more intimate than anything she had released before. 'Work', a dancehall track with Drake, became her fourteenth number one single, 'Needed Me' and 'Kiss It Better' are stunning R&B songs, 'Love on the Brain' is a sweeping ballad that shows off her voice, and 'Same Ol' Mistakes', a cover of a Tame Impala song, showed her adventurous side. ANTI was hailed as Rihanna's best album, and it remains the record where one of pop's biggest stars finally showed the world who she really was.

name: After Hours
teaser: The Weeknd 2020 — a concept album about a single night in Las Vegas that spirals from hedonism to self-destruction. Abel Tesfaye wrote the script before writing the songs. The album cover shows him bloodied and bandaged, a character he maintained for the entire promotional cycle including his SNL performance and the Super Bowl halftime show.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Blinding Lights' — the synth riff was inspired by A-ha's 'Take On Me' and was recorded on a vintage Roland Juno-60. Then 'Faith' — the song transitions from a synth-pop verse to a gospel breakdown at 2:30 without warning. The album's narrative arc is mapped on the back cover: each song is a time-stamp on a clock counting down to dawn.

synopsis: After Hours (2020) is the album where the Weeknd, born Abel Tesfaye, made his masterpiece, a concept record about a single night in Las Vegas that spirals from hedonism to self-destruction, and it remains one of the defining albums of the decade. Tesfaye had spent the 2010s building a sound that fused R&B, pop and electronic music, and After Hours, made with his longtime collaborators and the producers Max Martin and Oneohtrix Point Never, found him at the peak of his powers: the album's glossy, cinematic production, full of 80s synthesizers and dark, pulsing grooves, provided the setting for his most ambitious storytelling. 'Blinding Lights', which became one of the biggest songs in chart history, 'Heartless', 'Save Your Tears', the devastating 'After Hours' and the closing 'Until I Bleed Out' trace a night of excess and regret with stunning coherence. The album's visual identity, with Tesfaye in a bloodied, bandaged red suit, added to its legend, and After Hours made the Weeknd the biggest star in pop, the record where his dark vision fully came into focus.

name: CTRL
teaser: SZA 2017 — the debut that took 4 years to finish because SZA kept re-recording it. She tried to delete the entire album in 2016; her label refused. The album's title refers to the illusion of having control over your life. Features from Travis Scott, Kendrick Lamar, and Isaiah Rashad feel secondary to SZA's confessional songwriting.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Drew Barrymore' — named after the actress because SZA felt the song's vulnerability matched Barrymore's on-screen persona. Then 'The Weekend' — written in 15 minutes after SZA found out her boyfriend had another girlfriend. The album's interludes are voicemails from SZA's grandmother, recorded without her grandmother knowing.

synopsis: CTRL (2017) is the debut album of SZA, and it announced one of the most distinctive and influential voices in modern R&B, a record of such intimate, self-lacerating honesty that it redefined what the genre could be. SZA, born Solána Rowe in St. Louis and raised in New Jersey, had spent years building a following with her unclassifiable music, and CTRL, which took four years to finish because she kept re-recording it, nearly got deleted entirely when she became overwhelmed by the process. The album that emerged is a masterpiece of modern R&B: its songs, about insecurity, love, self-doubt and the pressure of being a young woman, are delivered in SZA's extraordinary voice, which floats between singing, rapping and speaking with total freedom. 'Love Galore' and 'The Weekend' became hits, 'Drew Barrymore', 'Broken Clocks' and the stunning '20 Something', which closes the album, are among the most honest songs of the decade. CTRL was nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys and is now regarded as a landmark of 2010s R&B.

name: A Seat at the Table
teaser: Solange 2016 — a meditation on Black identity, exhaustion, and resilience. Recorded over 4 years in Louisiana, New Iberia, and New Orleans. Features from Lil Wayne, Q-Tip, Kelly Rowland, and Master P. The album's interludes are interviews with Solange's parents about their experiences of racism in 1960s Texas.

exploreAction.targetName: A Seat at the Table (2016) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Cranes in the Sky' — the strings were arranged by Raphael Saadiq and recorded at Abbey Road. Solange wrote the song in 2008 but waited 8 years because she didn't feel ready to sing it. Then 'Don't Touch My Hair' — the Sampha feature was recorded at 6 AM after an all-night session. Solange's pitch rises as her anger builds.

tracks.title: Interlude: The Glory Is in You
Interlude: I Got So Much Magic, You Can Have It

synopsis: A Seat at the Table (2016) is the album where Solange, who had spent years in the shadow of her older sister Beyoncé, made a masterpiece entirely her own, a stunning meditation on black identity, exhaustion and resilience that won her a Grammy and universal acclaim. Solange recorded the album over four years in Louisiana and New York, drawing on her own experiences and those of her family, and the result is a record of extraordinary grace and power: its songs, delivered in her delicate, assured voice, address the everyday toll of racism, the importance of black joy, and the exhaustion of constantly having to prove your worth. 'Cranes in the Sky', which became her signature song, is a gorgeous meditation on sadness, 'Don't Touch My Hair' is a defiant celebration of black beauty, 'Almeda' and 'F.U.B.U.' are proud declarations of black culture, and the album's spoken interludes, featuring her mother Tina Knowles and the scholar Ta-Nehisi Coates, add context and depth. A Seat at the Table is now regarded as one of the essential albums of the decade.

name: The ArchAndroid
teaser: Janelle Monáe 2010 — a sci-fi concept album about an android messiah in the city of Metropolis. Recorded with a 22-piece orchestra and a horn section from Outkast's touring band. Monáe wrote a 28-page manifesto explaining the narrative. Big Boi executive-produced it after hearing Monáe sing at an Atlanta open mic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Tightrope' — Big Boi's verse was recorded in a separate session and spliced in. The James Brown-style horn arrangement was played by the Wondaland ArchOrchestra, a group of Berklee students Monáe recruited. Then 'Cold War' — the music video is a single continuous take of Monáe crying while lip-syncing. She didn't plan to cry.

tracks.title: Come Alive (The War of the Roses)

synopsis: The ArchAndroid (2010) is the album where Janelle Monáe, one of the most gifted and original artists of her generation, made her extraordinary debut, a science-fiction concept album that fused R&B, funk, rock, soul and classical music into something entirely her own. The album continues the story Monáe had begun on her debut EP, telling the tale of an android messiah named Cindi Mayweather who falls in love with a human and is hunted by the authorities of the city of Metropolis; its two 'suites' of songs, recorded with a 22-piece orchestra, move from the funk of 'Tightrope' and 'Cold War' to the orchestral grandeur of 'BaBopByeYa' and the psychedelic soul of '57821', with guest appearances from the rapper Big Boi and the band of Montreal. Monáe's extraordinary voice, her theatrical vision and her celebration of black creativity and individuality made The ArchAndroid a landmark, and it announced the arrival of one of the most distinctive artists of the 21st century.

name: WHEN WE ALL FALL ASLEEP, WHERE DO WE GO?
teaser: Billie Eilish 2019 — recorded in her brother Finneas's bedroom in Highland Park, LA, with a laptop, a $80 microphone, and a mattress against the wall for soundproofing. Finneas, 21, produced and co-wrote every track. The album made Billie, at 17, the youngest artist ever to sweep the four major Grammy categories.

exploreAction.targetName: WHEN WE ALL FALL ASLEEP (2019) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'bad guy' — the bassline is a distorted sample of an Australian pedestrian crossing signal recorded on Billie's phone. The 'duh' was a mistake; Billie said it while the mic was hot and Finneas kept it. Then 'bury a friend' — the dental drill sound was recorded at Billie's actual dentist appointment. She asked the dentist to let her record it.

tracks.title: You Should See Me in a Crown
All the Good Girls Go to Hell

synopsis: Recorded in the bedroom of her brother Finneas O'Connell in Highland Park, Los Angeles, this debut turned whisper-close vocals and laptop production into the biggest pop record of 2019. Billie Eilish was 17 when it came out, and the songs deal in the fears and irritations of teenage life: sleep paralysis, body image, intrusive thoughts, a crush that curdles. Finneas produced the whole thing at home, with no studio polish, which is exactly what made tracks like 'bad guy' and 'bury a friend' sound like nothing else on the radio. It won Album of the Year at the Grammys, making Eilish the youngest solo artist to take the prize, and its success proved that a huge pop career no longer needed a big label studio behind it.

teaser: Adele 2011 — named after her age when she wrote it, following a devastating breakup. Recorded in London and Malibu with Rick Rubin, Paul Epworth, and Ryan Tedder. The album sold 31 million copies and won 6 Grammys. Adele recorded the vocals for 'Rolling in the Deep' in one take, then went home because she had a cold.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Someone Like You' — co-written with Dan Wilson of Semisonic in one afternoon at his piano. Adele's vocal was recorded as a demo; Wilson told her it was perfect and refused to let her re-record it. Then 'Rumour Has It' — the stomps in the intro are Adele and the band stamping on the floor of the tracking room because they couldn't find a kick drum sound they liked.

synopsis: Adele wrote this follow-up to 19 while she was 21, and it is an album of a specific, still-raw heartbreak: the end of the relationship that had inspired her debut. The songs move from fury ('Rolling in the Deep') to despair ('Someone Like You') to the quieter ache of 'Turning Tables', and she recorded them with a who's who of producers including Rick Rubin, Paul Epworth and Ryan Tedder. The record is built on gospel chords and classic soul arrangements that make the hurt feel bigger than life. It sold more than 30 million copies, won Album of the Year at the Grammys, and turned a breakup into one of the best-selling albums in history. 'Someone Like You', recorded in a single take with just piano, became her first number one in Britain.

name: Back to Black
teaser: Amy Winehouse 2006 — recorded mostly in Mark Ronson's New York studio with the Dap-Kings, a Brooklyn soul band. Winehouse wrote the lyrics in 3 hours after a breakup. The album's 1960s girl-group sound was Ronson's idea to give Winehouse's confessional lyrics a vintage frame. Winehouse never intended to make a retro album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Rehab' — Ronson built the beat from a sample of a 1968 soul record. Winehouse wrote the lyric about her actual refusal to go to rehab, which her management had suggested. Then 'Back to Black' — the song's descending chord progression was inspired by Shangri-Las records. Winehouse recorded the vocal at 2 AM, chain-smoking between takes.

synopsis: After the bare bones of Frank, Amy Winehouse teamed up with producer Mark Ronson and New York's Dap-Kings to make a record that sounds like 1963 while singing about 2006. The songs are mostly about her on-off relationship with Blake Fielder-Civil, told with a bluntness that made tabloids uncomfortable: 'Rehab' is her refusal of a treatment center, 'You Know I'm No Good' an admission of cheating, 'Back to Black' the fallout when the affair blew up. Winehouse wrote nearly everything herself, and her voice, all dusky quaver and swinging phrasing, gave the retro soul a modern ache. She took five Grammys at the 2008 ceremony, including Record and Song of the Year, and the album made her a global star, though the fame and the man at the center of the songs unraveled her soon after.

name: Pure Heroine
teaser: Lorde 2013 — recorded in 2 months in a small Auckland studio while Lorde was 16 and still in high school. Produced by Joel Little, who had never made a pop album before. The album's lyrics catalog adolescence with anthropological detachment: parties, small towns, and the boredom of growing up in the internet age.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Royals' — Lorde wrote the lyrics in 30 minutes after seeing a photo of a baseball player signing an endorsement deal. She'd never been to the kinds of parties she's describing. Then 'Ribs' — the song captures the exact moment of realizing you're growing up and can't stop it. The synth swell at 2:45 was played on a $100 keyboard.

synopsis: Lorde wrote or co-wrote every song here while still in high school in Auckland, working with producer Joel Little in a small studio over the space of a couple of months. The album is a teenager's report on her own world rather than a fantasy of adulthood: 'Royals' pushes back at luxury-brand rap, 'Tennis Court' is about the boredom that follows small-town success, 'Ribs' about the terror of growing up. Her lyrics are precise and a little chilling for someone her age, and the production is minimal, built on sparse beats and deep bass rather than the bombast of early 2010s pop. It sold in the millions, and its lead single 'Royals' made Lorde the youngest solo artist in 26 years to top the US singles chart, resetting what a teen pop star could sound like.

name: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
teaser: Aphex Twin 1994 — a double album of beatless ambient music inspired by lucid dreaming. Richard D. James composed much of it by manipulating sounds while half-asleep. None of the 24 tracks have proper names — just photographs in the liner notes. James said some of the sounds 'actually hurt to listen to' and apologized in advance.

exploreAction.targetName: Selected Ambient Works Vol II (1994) — at least first 10 tracks
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to track 3 ('Rhubarb') — a 7-minute piece built from three overlapping synth pads. James recorded it in one take while watching snow fall outside his window in Cornwall. Then track 20 ('Lichen') — the melody was generated by feeding random sine waves through a reverb unit. James later admitted he doesn't remember recording half the album.

synopsis: Aphex Twin's second proper album strips his sound down to almost nothing: two hours of beatless ambient textures, most tracks little more than a chord or a melody drifting through heavy reverb. The titles, printed as tiny thumbnail images of the places that inspired each piece, are as obscure as the music. Richard D. James said he made much of it while lucid dreaming, trying to capture the sound inside his head, and the results range from the eerie choir-like pulse of the famous 'Stone in Focus' to harsher, unsettling drones. It is ambient music with no new age comfort in it, closer to the inside of a dream or a flooded building than to a relaxation tape. It became the defining document of 1990s ambient and still sounds like nothing else recorded since.

name: Cosmogramma
teaser: Flying Lotus 2010 — an album that sounds like jazz, hip-hop, and electronic music melting into each other. Recorded at his aunt Alice Coltrane's house in Los Angeles, using her harp and mixing board. Thom Yorke and Thundercat appear on multiple tracks. The album is named after a Carl Sagan-inspired synthesis of cosmic order.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Zodiac Shit' — the beat was built from a sample FlyLo found on an obscure 1970s library record. The drum programming shifts time signatures 4 times. Then 'Computer Face // Pure Being' — the arpeggiated synth line was played on Alice Coltrane's actual synthesizer. FlyLo said recording at his aunt's house felt like channeling her spirit.

synopsis: Steven Ellison, the great-nephew of jazz pianist Alice Coltrane, spent years building this dense, fast-moving record that welds hip-hop beat science to jazz and orchestral textures. Guest players include saxophonist Kamasi Washington and harpist Rebekah Raff, and tracks like 'Zodiac Shit' and 'Do the Astral Plane' race through changes with a jazz improviser's freedom over bass-heavy electronic drums.
