It is regarded as one of the greatest dub albums ever made, and its influence on electronic music of all kinds is immeasurable.

name: Legalize It
teaser: Peter Tosh 1976 — the former Wailer's solo debut, released after he left Bob Marley's shadow. The title track was banned in Jamaica for advocating cannabis legalization. Tosh was a militant Rastafarian who taught himself guitar by watching a neighbor's hands through a window. He was murdered in his home in 1987 during a robbery.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the chorus is just the phrase 'legalize it' repeated, but Tosh's voice makes it a demand, not a request. Then 'Equal Rights' — a song that directly addresses apartheid in South Africa. Tosh later performed it at a concert where he criticized the Jamaican Prime Minister from the stage and was beaten by police afterward.

tracks.title: Why Must I Cry (Tosh, Bob Marley)
Till Your Well Runs Dry (Tosh, Livingston)

synopsis: Peter Tosh had spent over a decade as one third of the Wailers, the group that made Bob Marley a star, but he left in 1974, resentful at playing second fiddle, and this debut solo album announced him as a force of his own. The title track, a wry argument for the legalization of marijuana, became an international anthem, and the rest of the record mixes militant demands for liberation with roots reggae of uncommon warmth, sung in Tosh's rough, commanding voice. Released at the height of the reggae boom, it made Tosh a star in his own right and established the persona that would define the rest of his life: the uncompromising, ganja-smoking warrior of reggae, who would be murdered in his home in 1987.

name: Red
teaser: Black Uhuru 1981 — the first reggae album to win a Grammy. Produced by Sly and Robbie, the rhythm section that defined modern reggae. Michael Rose's voice is a weapon: part street chant, part wail, part gospel testimony. The album was recorded at Channel One in Kingston and mixed at Compass Point in the Bahamas.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sponji Reggae' — Sly Dunbar's drum pattern is a digital one-drop programmed on a drum machine, one of the first uses of electronic drums in reggae. Then 'Youth of Eglington' — a song about the gang violence in Kingston's Eglinton district. Rose's vocal was recorded in one take while looking at a photograph of the neighborhood.

synopsis: Black Uhuru, led by the gruff-voiced Michael Rose with harmonies from Duckie Simpson and Puma Jones, had been struggling for years when producers Sly Dunbar and Robbie Shakespeare took them into the studio. The result was this album, the first reggae record to win a Grammy, and it is the definitive statement of the dancehall-era roots sound. Sly and Robbie's rhythms are crisp and modern, built on electronic drums and bass lines that seemed to come from the future, while Rose's keening tenor and the group's harmonies carry songs of love, war and liberation. The title track, a brooding meditation on the color red, became a classic. It is the sound of reggae leaving the 70s behind and entering the 80s with confidence.

name: East of the River Nile
teaser: Augustus Pablo 1977 — an instrumental dub album where the melody is carried entirely by Pablo's melodica, a child's keyboard instrument that he turned into a mystical voice. Recorded at Randy's Studio in Kingston with session musicians who had never worked with a melodica player before. The album sounds like a prayer from a future that never arrived.

exploreAction.targetName: East of the River Nile (1977) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Pablo's melodica floats over a one-drop rhythm that sounds like it's being played underwater. Then 'Chant to King Selassie I' — the bassline descends chromatically while the melodica plays a single note for 4 bars. Pablo learned melodica by practicing with one hand while steering his delivery truck with the other.

tracks.title: Chant to King Selassie I (with Ja-Malla Band)
Memories of the Ghetto (with the Upsetters)

synopsis: Augustus Pablo had invented a new sound in reggae when he began playing the melodica, a toy-like keyboard instrument that he blew into like a harmonica, and this 1977 album is the fullest expression of his vision. Working with the great session band the Revolutionaries and producer King Tubby, Pablo built an album of instrumental and dub tracks in which his melodica, sounding like a ghostly, keening voice, carries the melodies over cavernous rhythms. The title track's rolling groove and the album's overall atmosphere of space and echo made it a favorite of reggae fans and DJs alike. It is regarded as one of the finest instrumental reggae albums ever made, a record where an unlikely instrument became a voice of pure feeling.

name: 007 (Shanty Town)
teaser: Desmond Dekker 1967 — the first Jamaican artist to have a UK #1 hit with 'Israelites.' His voice was a desperate falsetto that made songs about poverty and rude boys sound like they were floating. The album introduced ska and rocksteady to British mods and skinheads. Dekker was an orphan who learned to sing in church.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to '007 (Shanty Town)' — the song is about the Kingston neighborhood of Trenchtown, where the 'rude boys' (young gangsters) controlled the streets. Then 'Israelites' — Dekker wrote it after hearing an argument between a Jamaican couple about money. The 'Israelites' are the Jamaican working poor. The accent was so thick that British fans published lyric guides.

synopsis: Desmond Dekker had been one of the first stars of Jamaican ska, and by the late 60s he had evolved with the music into rocksteady, the slower, more soulful sound that preceded reggae. This album, whose title track about life in the shanty town of Kingston became his biggest Jamaican hit, collects the best of that period, including the international smash 'Israelites', the first Jamaican record to top the British charts and the first to make a real dent in America. Dekker's voice, high and plaintive, singing about poverty, work and faith over the Wailers' rhythms, gave the music a universal reach. It made him the first Jamaican artist to conquer the world, paving the way for everything that followed.

name: Satta Massagana
teaser: The Abyssinians 1976 — the holiest of Rastafarian harmony trios, named after the ancient name for Ethiopia. The title track is sung partly in Amharic, the language of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. The album was rejected by every major Jamaican label for being 'too religious' and the band released it themselves.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the harmony on 'Satta Massagana' is three men singing in a language none of them spoke fluently, learned phonetically from a Rastafarian elder. Then 'Yim Mas Gan' — the Amharic version of the same song, recorded with a single microphone in a concrete room. The reverb is the room itself.

tracks.title: Satta A Masagana (B. Collins, D. Manning, L. Manning)

synopsis: The Abyssinians took their name from the ancient name for Ethiopia, the promised land of Rastafari, and this debut album is the purest expression of the group's spiritual vision. The trio, led by Bernard Collins and the Manning brothers, sang in harmonies that echoed the old Jamaican gospel quartets, over roots rhythms produced by Carlton Lee, and their songs were almost entirely devoted to the Rastafarian faith: repatriation to Africa, the divinity of Haile Selassie, the rejection of Babylon. The title track, whose slow, chanting melody became one of the most covered songs in reggae history, is a high point of the genre. The album is regarded as one of the holiest documents of roots reggae, music that sounds like prayer.

name: ABBA Gold: Greatest Hits
teaser: ABBA 1992 — the compilation that turned a divorced Swedish quartet into one of the best-selling acts of all time. Recorded between 1973 and 1981, these songs are engineering marvels: Benny Andersson and Björn Ulvaeus layered so many keyboard and vocal tracks that some songs use 60 separate parts. The two couples divorced during the band's tenure but kept recording together.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dancing Queen' — the opening glissando was played on a grand piano miked from 20 feet away. The song was recorded in a summer cottage on an island near Stockholm. Then 'The Winner Takes It All' — Agnetha sang it while going through her divorce from Björn, who wrote the lyrics. The line 'I don't want to talk' was directed at him.

tracks.title: Lay All Your Love on Me
Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! (A Man After Midnight)

synopsis: ABBA had split in 1982, and for a decade their music seemed to belong to the past, dismissed by critics and relegated to nostalgic radio. This compilation, released to mark their comeback on stage in the musical Mamma Mia!, changed all that, selling over 30 million copies and turning the four Swedes into one of the best-selling acts in history. The track list is a parade of immaculate pop songs, from 'Dancing Queen' and 'Mamma Mia' to 'The Winner Takes It All' and 'Take a Chance on Me', each one a masterclass in melody, harmony and production. The album's success proved that the quartet's music, once sneered at, was among the most durable pop ever recorded, and it remains one of the best-selling albums in the world.

name: Revolver
teaser: The Beatles 1966 — the album where they stopped being a touring band and became a studio band. Recorded over 3 months at Abbey Road with producer George Martin and engineer Geoff Emerick, who invented new recording techniques daily. The album opens with a tax protest, closes with a Tibetan-inspired meditation on death, and contains the first use of tape loops in pop music.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Tomorrow Never Knows' — John Lennon told Martin he wanted to sound like 'a thousand Tibetan monks chanting from a mountaintop.' Emerick put Lennon's voice through a Leslie speaker (normally used for organs) to create the swirling effect. Then 'Eleanor Rigby' — no Beatles play instruments on this track, just a double string quartet scored by Martin.

tracks.title: Got to Get You into My Life

synopsis: The Beatles' seventh album was recorded in the middle of 1966, at the end of their final tour, when the screaming crowds and the pressure of live performance had pushed them to the brink of quitting. The solution was to stop touring and become a studio band, and Revolver is the first full flowering of that freedom. George Martin's production, the group's experiments with tape loops and Indian instruments, and a set of songs that range from the acid-tinged 'Tomorrow Never Knows' to the chamber pop of 'Eleanor Rigby' and the rocking 'Taxman', made it the most adventurous pop record yet made. It is the album where the Beatles stopped being a pop group and became the most influential artists of their era.

name: Goodbye Yellow Brick Road
teaser: Elton John 1973 — a double album recorded in 2 weeks at the Château d'Hérouville in France, a 16th-century castle turned recording studio. Bernie Taupin wrote all the lyrics in 2.5 weeks, sitting in a field behind the château. Elton wrote the music in 3 days. The album contains 'Candle in the Wind,' 'Bennie and the Jets,' and the title track.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Elton said the melody came to him fully formed while he was driving to the studio. Then 'Funeral for a Friend/Love Lies Bleeding' — the 11-minute opener where Elton's keyboardist David Hentschel created a synthesized storm on an ARP 2600 synthesizer. The opening sound is wind, recorded by opening a window in a hurricane.

tracks.title: Funeral for a Friend/Love Lies Bleeding
Your Sister Can't Twist (but She Can Rock 'n Roll)

synopsis: Elton John was at the absolute peak of his commercial power in 1973, coming off a string of hit albums, and for this one he rented a chateau in France and recorded with his band in a burst of creativity, cutting the whole double album in about two weeks. The record is a sprawling tour of his talents, from the glam-rock stomp of the title track and 'Bennie and the Jets' to the epic 'Funeral for a Friend/Love Lies Bleeding' and the country-tinged 'Candle in the Wind', with lyrics by his longtime partner Bernie Taupin ranging from movie-star elegies to the crusading 'The Ballad of Danny Bailey'. It became his best-selling studio album, and its confidence and range made it the definitive statement of the singer whose piano ballads and outsized spectacles defined 70s pop.

name: Blackstar
teaser: David Bowie 2016 — released on his 69th birthday, two days before his death from liver cancer. Bowie knew he was dying when he recorded it; only his closest collaborators knew. The album is a farewell letter: the title track is 10 minutes of jazz-inflected meditation on mortality, and 'Lazarus' opens with the line 'Look up here, I'm in heaven.'.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the band (a New York jazz quartet) played without knowing the songs were about death. The saxophone solo by Donny McCaslin was recorded in one take and sounds like a soul leaving a body. Then 'Lazarus' — the video was shot with Bowie in a hospital bed. The wardrobe cabinet in the video is the same one from 1976.

tracks.title: 'Tis a Pity She Was a Whore
Sue (Or in a Season of Crime)

synopsis: David Bowie recorded Blackstar in secret while dying of liver cancer, and he released it on his 69th birthday, two days before his death, a fact that the album's music seems to have known all along. Working with a jazz quartet led by saxophonist Donny McCaslin, Bowie made music that is eerie, searching and full of a strange serenity, from the ten-minute title track to the final song, 'I Can't Give Everything Away'. The lyrics are full of images of endings and partings, and the video for 'Lazarus', with its images of a man in a hospital bed, now reads as a farewell. It was hailed as a masterpiece on release, and its power only grew when listeners understood what they had been hearing.

name: BRAT
teaser: Charli XCX 2024 — an album that makes being a mess sound aspirational. Recorded over two years primarily with producer A. G. Cook in London and LA. The album's aggressive hyperpop production (distorted bass, clipped vocals, relentless tempo) is matched by lyrics about jealousy, insecurity, and not knowing if you're a good person. The album cover — simple green with blurry text — became a cultural phenomenon.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to '360' — the beat sounds like a ringtone played through a broken speaker, but the hook is undeniable. Then 'So I' — a song about Sophie, Charli's late collaborator, that addresses grief without ever becoming a slow ballad. Charli has said the album's thesis is that being 'brat' — messy, difficult, emotional — is not something to apologize for.

tracks.title: I Think About It All the Time

synopsis: Charli XCX had spent a decade as a cult favorite of the pop underground, but this album, her sixth, turned her into a global star on her own terms. Made in a burst of energy with producer A.G. Cook and others, the record is a celebration of messiness, insecurity and the chaotic joy of being young, set to music that fuses her hyperpop instincts with the biggest, dumbest, most fun pop hooks she had ever written. The single 'Von dutch' and the Billie Eilish duet 'Guess' became hits, and the album's neon green aesthetic and party energy spawned a whole cultural moment. It was named one of the best albums of the year by critics everywhere and made Charli the unlikely queen of the summer of 2024.

name: E•MO•TION
teaser: Carly Rae Jepsen 2015 — the 'Call Me Maybe' singer's pivot to critically adored synth-pop, recorded with a cast of indie producers including Dev Hynes, Rostam Batmanglij, and Ariel Rechtshaid. The album's saxophone solos, 80s drum machines, and unapologetically earnest lyrics about crushes turned a one-hit wonder into a cult icon.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Run Away with Me' — the opening saxophone blast was played by a session musician who'd worked on early Whitney Houston records. Then 'Your Type' — Jepsen sings about being in love with someone who only sees her as a friend, over a beat that sounds like it was ripped from a John Hughes movie. The album's B-sides were good enough to be their own album.

tracks.title: Making the Most of the Night

synopsis: Carly Rae Jepsen had become a global pop star in 2012 with the inescapable 'Call Me Maybe', but she responded to that success not by chasing it but by disappearing into the studio for three years to make the album she actually wanted to make. The result, produced with a team including Max Martin and Rostam Batmanglij, is a pure shot of 80s-influenced synth pop, full of enormous choruses and heartbroken lyrics. 'Run Away with Me', with its blazing saxophone intro, became a fan favorite, and 'I Really Like You' returned her to the charts. The album sold modestly but was greeted with rapture by critics, who hailed it as one of the great pop records of the decade, and its reputation has only grown since.

name: Body Talk
teaser: Robyn 2010 — released as three EPs and compiled into one album. After being dropped by her major label, the Swedish singer started her own label and made the album she wanted: sad songs you can dance to. The production (by Robyn and Klas Åhlund) is clinical synth-pop, but Robyn's voice cracks with real emotion. The album redefined what pop could sound like in the 2010s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dancing on My Own' — Robyn sings about watching her ex with someone new at a club, over a beat that makes you want to dance. The contradiction is the point. Then 'Call Your Girlfriend' — the song is advice to a man on how to break up with his current girlfriend because he's leaving her for Robyn. The synth bassline is one note.

tracks.title: Don't Fucking Tell Me What to Do

synopsis: Robyn had been a teen pop star in Sweden in the 90s, but after being dropped by her American label she took control of her career and began working with producers who shared her love of electronic music. This album was released as three EPs over the course of 2010 and then compiled into a single record, and the whole is greater than its parts. The music is sleek, futuristic and emotionally direct, from the electroclash of 'Dancing On My Own', which became an anthem of lonely heartbreak, to the euphoric 'Call Your Girlfriend'. The album made Robyn the most respected pop artist in the world among critics and fellow musicians, and its influence on the pop of the following decade is everywhere.

name: Tusk
teaser: Fleetwood Mac 1979 — the most expensive album ever made at the time ($1 million). After the perfect pop of Rumours, Lindsey Buckingham insisted on making the follow-up deliberately strange. The album's horns and marching band (the USC Trojan Marching Band on the title track) were recorded at Dodger Stadium. The band nearly broke up. Critics called it a mess. It's now considered a masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — the drum part was recorded in Buckingham's bathroom, then the USC marching band was overdubbed in a stadium. Then 'Sara' — Stevie Nicks wrote a 16-minute version and the band cut it to 6. She said the song was about her unborn child (she had an abortion during the Rumours tour). The editing is audible in the song's strange pauses.

tracks.title: What Makes You Think You're the One

synopsis: After the enormous success of Rumours, Fleetwood Mac could have made the same album again, but instead they gave singer and keyboardist Christine McVie's husband's bandmate Lindsey Buckingham the freedom to experiment, and he ran with it, recording for a year in a studio they built in their house. The result, a sprawling double album that cost over a million dollars, then a record sum, confused the label and divided the fans. But time has been kind to Tusk, whose strange, homemade textures and songs like the title track and 'Sara' now sound like the band's most adventurous work. It is the sound of a huge band at the height of its fame refusing to play it safe.

name: Parallel Lines
teaser: Blondie 1978 — the New York punk band's pivot to pop, produced by Mike Chapman (a bubblegum pop producer who'd never worked with a rock band). Chapman made them re-record songs dozens of times until every note was perfect. Debbie Harry's voice is both cool and vulnerable. The album spawned 4 hit singles and bridged punk, disco, and new wave.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Heart of Glass' — the disco beat was the band's idea, but Chapman made them layer it with a Roland drum machine. The song's first iteration was a slow reggae number called 'The Disco Song.' Then 'Hanging on the Telephone' — a cover of a song by an obscure LA band The Nerves. Harry recorded her vocal while just waking up.

tracks.title: I Know but I Don't Know

synopsis: Blondie had spent the late 70s as the most commercial band to come out of the New York punk scene, and this album, produced by the English hitmaker Mike Chapman, completed their transformation into pop superstars. The record is a stunning tour of styles, from the new wave disco of 'Heart of Glass', which became their first number one in America, to the reggae-flavored 'The Tide Is High' and the rap-inflected 'Rapture', one of the first pop songs to feature rapping. Debbie Harry's cool, knowing vocals made her the most iconic frontwoman of her era, and the album's effortless genre-hopping showed that punk's energy could power the top of the charts. It remains the definitive statement of the new wave pop moment.

name: Graceland
teaser: Paul Simon 1986 — an album that went from bankruptcy court to the Grammys. Simon's previous album flopped, his marriage to Carrie Fisher was collapsing, and he was nearly broke. After discovering a tape of South African township music, he flew to Johannesburg and recorded with Black South African musicians despite the UN cultural boycott against apartheid. The album won Album of the Year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Simon sings about a road trip to Elvis's Graceland mansion with his young son. Then 'Diamonds on the Soles of Her Shoes' — recorded with Ladysmith Black Mambazo, a South African a cappella group. Simon heard them on a cassette in a London taxi and tracked them down. The song begins with a Zulu a cappella section before any Western instruments enter.

tracks.title: Diamonds on the Soles of Her Shoes
All Around the World or the Myth of Fingerprints

synopsis: Paul Simon's solo career had stalled badly by the mid-80s; his last album had flopped and his marriage was ending, and he was in a creative slump. Looking for a new sound, he smuggled a bootleg tape of South African township music out of the country and built an album around it, traveling to Johannesburg to record with local musicians despite the cultural boycott against apartheid. The record was a smash, winning the Grammy for Album of the Year, and its fusion of Simon's songwriting with the mbaqanga and choral music of South Africa introduced a whole continent's pop to the world. It also drew criticism for breaking the boycott, a debate that has never quite been settled. The music, from 'Graceland' to 'You Can Call Me Al', remains irresistible.

name: Neu! 75
teaser: Michael Rother and Klaus Dinger 1975 — the third album from the band that invented the 'motorik' beat (a relentless 4/4 pulse that sounds like driving on an infinite highway). The album splits between two sides: Rother's ambient, melodic first side and Dinger's proto-punk second side. The two had stopped speaking to each other and recorded separately.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Isi' — the opening track floats between ambient and krautrock, with Rother's guitar buried in reverb. Then 'Hero' — Dinger's proto-punk anthem, with his voice sounding like Johnny Rotten 2 years before the Sex Pistols existed. The album's title refers to the year 1975 and also the band itself: 'neu' means 'new' in German.

synopsis: Neu! had spent the early 70s inventing a motorik sound, a steady, hypnotic beat that guitarist Michael Rother and drummer Klaus Dinger laid under minimalist riffs, and this third album refined it to perfection. The record opens with the eleven-minute 'Isi', a trance-like epic built on a single pulsing groove, and its second side is even stranger, with the ambient drift of 'Leb' Wohl' giving way to the ecstatic rock of the closer. The band had begun to fall apart during the sessions, and this was their last album together, but the friction produced some of their best music. It is regarded as one of the key documents of German experimental rock, and its influence on punk, post-punk and electronic music is vast.

name: Tago Mago
teaser: Can 1971 — a double album recorded in a converted castle outside Cologne, with Japanese busker Damo Suzuki as vocalist. Suzuki's lyrics were improvised in a mixture of Japanese, English, and made-up words. The band recorded hours of jams and edited the best 73 minutes. The album is the sound of rock music being reinvented as a single continuous trance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Halleluhwah' — 18 minutes of the same drum beat and bassline while Suzuki chants and the guitars melt. Then 'Aumgn' — a 17-minute track that sounds like a séance recorded in a cave. The album's original vinyl pressing was on 2 LPs because the band refused to cut any tracks. The cover is a single photograph of a world map, partially obscured.

synopsis: Can recorded this double album in a converted castle outside Cologne in 1971, and the setting seems to have seeped into the music, which is as strange and sprawling as the building itself. The band, led by the Japanese vocalist Damo Suzuki and the keyboardist Irmin Schmidt, plays long, improvised pieces that move between hypnotic grooves and free-form noise, from the eleven-minute funk of 'Paperhouse' to the terrifying drone of 'Mushroom' and the side-long title track, built on a single chord and Suzuki's wordless chanting. The album is the definitive statement of the experimental German scene that critics would later label krautrock, and its fearless approach to improvisation influenced everyone from David Bowie to Public Image Ltd.

name: The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady
teaser: Charles Mingus 1963 — a ballet scored for an 11-piece band, written as a single continuous suite in 6 movements. Mingus composed it on piano with his therapist present, using music as psychoanalysis. The album's liner notes were written by Mingus's own therapist. The music shifts between gorgeous melody and explosive chaos without warning.

exploreAction.targetName: The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady (1963) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Track A — Solo Dancer' — the composition starts as a Spanish-tinged ballad and becomes a cacophony of competing horn lines. Then 'Track C — Group Dancers' — the band plays as if in a dream, with instruments seeming to ignore each other and then suddenly synchronize. Mingus overdubbed himself on piano, playing different parts of the same composition.

tracks.title: Mode D - Trio and Group Dancers" / "Mode E - Single Solos and Group Dance" / "Mode F - Group and Solo Dance

synopsis: Charles Mingus was the great bassist and bandleader of postwar jazz, a man whose music was as political and mercurial as his temper, and this album, recorded in 1963, is his masterpiece. Written as a ballet for an eleven-piece band and played continuously across its four movements, the record is a suite of moods that Mingus called 'a solo dance', full of shifting tempos, screaming brass, lush passages and sudden violence, all anchored by his own ferocious bass. The music has a program: it depicts a man and a woman, their love affair and its destruction, and the liner notes describe it in Mingus's own poetic, wounded language. It is regarded as one of the greatest achievements in the history of jazz composition.

name: Big Science
teaser: Laurie Anderson 1982 — the debut album from the performance artist who used a violin with a tape head instead of strings, a vocoder pitched to sound male, and spoken-word narratives about technology, alienation, and America. 'O Superman' became a surprise #2 hit in the UK. The album was recorded in a New York loft with equipment borrowed from art grants.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'O Superman' — 8 minutes of a single looped 'ha' syllable, with Anderson's vocoder-distorted voice reciting a letter to an absent mother-figure who might be Mom, America, or technology. Then 'From the Air' — an airline pilot calmly announces the plane is going to crash. Anderson plays the 'tape-bow violin': a violin bow strung with magnetic tape.

synopsis: Laurie Anderson had spent the 1970s as one of the most talked-about figures in the New York avant-garde, a performance artist who told stories and played violin through electronic effects, and this debut album brought her work to a mass audience. The record is built around 'O Superman', an eight-minute meditation on technology, communication and power, built on a repeated vocal phrase and a pulsing synthesizer, which became a surprise hit in Britain. The rest of the album is full of her deadpan monologues and witty observations about modern life, delivered in a voice that is cool, detached and strangely warm. It made her a star and remains one of the most influential albums to come out of the downtown art scene.

name: Closer
teaser: Joy Division 1980 — released two months after Ian Curtis's suicide at 23. The album was already recorded, and the cover art (a photograph of a tomb in Genoa's Staglieno Cemetery) was chosen before Curtis died. Martin Hannett's production is cavernous and claustrophobic. The album is a ghost of an album: every song sounds like it's already mourning its singer.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Atrocity Exhibition' — named after the J.G. Ballard novel, the opening track features Stephen Morris's drums sounding like gunshots echoing in an empty warehouse. Then 'Decades' — the closing song where Curtis sings 'Here are the young men / The weight on their shoulders' over a synthesizer line that never resolves. After recording this vocal, Curtis went home and hanged himself.

synopsis: Joy Division recorded Closer in the first months of 1980, while singer Ian Curtis's epilepsy, depression and failing marriage were spiraling out of control, and the music sounds like a man saying goodbye. The band's sound had deepened since their debut, with Peter Hook's melodic bass, Bernard Sumner's sparse guitar and Stephen Morris's cold, precise drums framing songs of despair and dissolution. Curtis's baritone, already one of the most distinctive voices in rock, delivers lyrics full of hospitals, isolation and extinction. He killed himself in May 1980, two months before the album's release. It stands as one of the most harrowing and influential records ever made, the sound of a brilliant band at the end of its road.

name: Surf's Up
teaser: The Beach Boys 1971 — released after years of Brian Wilson retreating from the band. The title track was written in 1966 for the abandoned SMiLE album, and its resurrection became the album's centerpiece. Carl Wilson stepped in as producer and lead vocalist while Brian was bedridden with depression. The album is a funeral for the 1960s disguised as a Beach Boys record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — Brian Wilson wrote it in a sandbox he'd installed in his living room to overcome writer's block. The song's imagery is by Van Dyke Parks, who wrote the lyrics as a surreal meditation on the death of innocence. Then ''Til I Die' — Brian's existential despair set to music: 'I'm a cork on the ocean, floating over the raging sea.'

tracks.title: Take a Load Off Your Feet
A Day in the Life of a Tree

synopsis: The Beach Boys spent the late 60s struggling to follow up Pet Sounds, with Brian Wilson's mental health collapsing and the rest of the band taking over the creative direction. Surf's Up, their first album of the new decade, was a compromise between the group's pop instincts and their ambitions, and its second side contains some of their greatest music: the title track, a fragment of Wilson's unfinished Smile project, and the extraordinary 'Till I Die', one of Wilson's most personal songs. The album also includes the Top 10 hit 'Student Demonstration Time' and the lovely 'Disney Girls'. It sold poorly and the band nearly broke up, but it has since been recognized as one of the high points of their later period.

name: Yankee Hotel Foxtrot
teaser: Wilco 2002 — the album their label refused to release, calling it 'career suicide.' Wilco bought back the masters for $50,000 and streamed it for free; 200,000 people listened before it was officially released. Nonesuch Records (a Warner subsidiary) then signed them and released the same album. The cover is a photograph of Marina City in Chicago.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Am Trying to Break Your Heart' — the song dissolves into noise for a full minute before the verse begins. Jeff Tweedy sang the lyric looking at a photograph of his wife. Then 'Jesus, Etc.' — the string arrangement was written by a friend who'd never arranged strings before. The album title is a phrase repeated on a numbers station that the band heard on a shortwave radio.

tracks.title: I Am Trying to Break Your Heart
I'm the Man Who Loves You

synopsis: Wilco spent two years making this album, their fourth, and when they delivered it to their label Reprise, the label refused to release it, calling it a career-killer. The band bought the rights back and released it themselves, and it became one of the most acclaimed albums of the decade. The music is a strange, beautiful hybrid, with Jeff Tweedy's ragged country-rock songs buried under layers of studio noise, tape hiss and electronic experiments by multi-instrumentalist Jim O'Rourke. Songs like 'Jesus, Etc.' and 'I Am Trying to Break Your Heart' are both fragile and tough. The label's fears proved exactly wrong: the album was a hit, and its story made Wilco symbols of artistic independence.

name: A Brief Inquiry Into Online Relationships
teaser: The 1975 2018 — the album that made them critics' darlings, tackling the internet, addiction and modern loneliness. Every song is a different genre, and the closer is a four-minute instrumental that ends with a choir.

exploreAction.targetName: A Brief Inquiry Into Online Relationships (2018) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Love It If We Made It' — a literal list of 2018 news headlines set to a euphoric chorus. Then 'The Man Who Married a Robot / Love Theme' — a spoken-word song narrated by Siri about a man who marries his phone. The album's title is a joke about the internet.

tracks.title: Love It If We Made It
I Like America & America Likes Me
The Man Who Married a Robot / Love Theme
It's Not Living (If It's Not with You)
I Couldn't Be More in Love

synopsis: The 1975 had spent years building a following with a sound that mixed emo, funk and 80s pop, but this, their third album, found them broadening their scope to take on the whole of modern life. The record's songs are about the internet, anxiety, addiction, love and the way technology has rewired all of it, and the music jumps between genres with a confidence that earned them comparisons to the great pop maximalists. The single 'Love It If We Made It' became an anthem of the late 2010s with its list of horrors and memes, and the album won the Mercury Prize. It established frontman Matty Healy as one of the most provocative and interesting voices in rock.

name: I Like It When You Sleep, for You Are So Beautiful yet So Unaware of It
teaser: The 1975 2016 — the 74-minute double album that made them stars, a maximalist sprawl of 17 songs that jumps from Motown pastiche to ambient soundscapes. It debuted at #1 in the UK, and its title is the longest ever to top the chart.

exploreAction.targetName: I Like It When You Sleep, for You Are So Beautiful yet So Unaware of It (2016) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Love Me' — the funk opener satirizes celebrity before the band had really hit fame. Then 'Somebody Else' — the heartbreak anthem whose chorus is a single repeated line. Skip nothing: the album deliberately refuses to stay in one genre, and the sequencing is the joke.

tracks.title: The Ballad of Me and My Brain
I Like It When You Sleep, for You Are So Beautiful yet So Unaware of It

synopsis: The 1975's second album was recorded at the peak of their ambition, and it shows: the double album runs over seventy minutes and touches on everything from driving rock to R&B ballads to spoken word interludes, all held together by the band's melodic gifts and frontman Matty Healy's confessional wit. The record made them stars, with 'The Sound' and 'Somebody Else' becoming anthems for a generation raised on the internet, and its title, borrowed from a Facebook status, set the tone for its self-aware, affectionate embrace of millennial angst. Critics praised its willingness to be both silly and sincere, often in the same song. It is the album where the band fulfilled the promise they had been building toward for years.

name: Short n' Sweet
teaser: Sabrina Carpenter 2024 — the 36-minute album that turned a Disney actress into the biggest pop star of the year. Recorded in just a few months, it's a country-tinged, innuendo-loaded pop record that spent weeks at #1.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Espresso' — the song has no real chorus, just a hook on a loop, and the 'screaming' backing vocals are pitched-down scream takes. Then 'Taste' — the opener, a breakup anthem with a horror-comedy video. The whole album is 12 songs in 36 minutes: no filler.

synopsis: Sabrina Carpenter had spent nearly a decade as a Disney Channel actress and a competent pop singer when she decided to remake herself as a sharp, funny, openly sexual pop star, and this album made the transformation complete. The record is short, tight and full of clever, cutting songs about love and its discontents, led by the inescapable 'Espresso' and the revenge fantasy 'Taste'. Carpenter's voice, precise and playful, delivers lyrics that are funnier and more specific than most pop songs dare to be, over production that mixes 70s soft rock with modern pop. The album turned her into one of the biggest pop stars in the world and was one of the defining records of 2024.

name: Harry's House
teaser: Harry Styles 2022 — his third solo album, named after a Joni Mitchell lyric, designed to sound like walking through the rooms of a home. It won Album of the Year at the Grammys, and 'As It Was' became his first #1 single.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'As It Was' — the lyrics are about loneliness at a party, the music is pure pop joy, and the music video was shot in the real Harry's House. Then 'Cinema' — the title track's subtitle references the Joni Mitchell lyric the album is named for. Each song is a room.

synopsis: Harry Styles had spent his first two solo albums establishing himself as a credible artist after leaving One Direction, but this third record, named for the Joni Mitchell lyric about having your own house, found him at ease with himself. The album is a warm, eclectic collection that touches on the 70s soft rock of his heroes, funk, folk and even a little bossa nova, with Styles' easy charm and the crack band he assembled carrying songs like 'As It Was', which became one of the biggest singles of the decade. The record won Album of the Year at the Grammys, and its relaxed confidence made Styles the most successful male pop star of his generation.

name: Planet Her
teaser: Doja Cat 2021 — a concept album about a fictional planet where women rule, and the record that made her a global star. It spawned three top-10 hits and mixes pop, R&B, Afrobeats and rap. The album's sci-fi aesthetic runs through every video.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Kiss Me More' — the SZA duet whose chorus samples an old Olivia Newton-John song, and which won a Grammy. Then 'Woman' — the opener, an ode to women's power built on an African vocal sample. The album is Planet Her; the interludes are her radio broadcasts.

synopsis: Doja Cat had established herself as a master of viral pop with her genre-hopping singles, but this album gave her music a fictional home: Planet Her, a world where women rule and the music is a mix of pop, R&B, reggaeton and rap. The record is a showcase for her astonishing versatility, from the disco-funk of 'Kiss Me More' with SZA to the Afrobeats of 'Woman' to the strange, funny 'Need to Know', and her delivery shifts effortlessly between singing, rapping and everything in between. It was a global hit, spending months in the charts and turning Doja Cat into one of the defining pop stars of the early 2020s, an artist who seemed to be able to do anything.

name: Montero
teaser: Lil Nas X 2021 — the debut album that turned a meme rapper into a pop visionary. Its title track, named for his birth name, became the first song to hit #1 with an openly queer message and a video that sparked global outrage. The album is a coming-of-age story in 15 tracks.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'MONTERO (Call Me by Your Name)' — a letter to his younger self, with a video where he gives the devil a lap dance. Then 'Sun Goes Down' — about the bullying he endured as a closeted teen. The album ends with a Miley Cyrus duet.

synopsis: Lil Nas X had conquered the world in 2019 with 'Old Town Road', a country-rap joke that became the longest-running number one in history, and the question was whether he could do anything else. This debut album answered with a vengeance, establishing him as a pop visionary who used his platform to tell his story as a young Black gay man with humor, pain and total confidence. The record is built around 'Montero (Call Me by Your Name)', a defiant anthem about forbidden love that he performed at the Grammys in a version that made headlines, and it also includes the vulnerable 'Sun Goes Down' and the swaggering 'Industry Baby'. It made him one of the most talked-about artists in the world.

name: Think Later
teaser: Tate McRae 2023 — the debut album from the Canadian dancer-singer, a 14-song pop record whose title is her motto for impulsive decisions. It debuted at #3 in the US and made 'Greedy' her first global hit.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Greedy' — built on a two-note bass loop, with a hook she wrote in one take. Then 'Exes' — the sequel to 'Greedy', with a bridge that drops to just her voice and a kick drum. She choreographed every video; watch her hands in 'Greedy'.

synopsis: Tate McRae had been a viral sensation since her teens, first as a dancer on television competitions and then as a songwriter whose early ballads racked up billions of streams, but this debut album found her sound. The record is a collection of sharp, propulsive pop songs about young love and its messes, led by the global smash 'Greedy' and its follow-up 'Exes', and her background as a dancer is audible in the way she attacks the rhythms. The album's fourteen songs are remarkably consistent, and its success, with over a billion streams within months, made McRae one of the leading new pop stars of the mid-2020s.

name: The Secret of Us
teaser: Gracie Abrams 2024 — her second album, written after a year of touring, a diary of friendship and self-destruction. It features a duet with Taylor Swift recorded live in one take, and 'I Love You, I'm Sorry' became a global hit.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Love You, I'm Sorry' — the title is the whole apology and the song never says it in the chorus. Then 'us.' — the Taylor Swift duet, recorded in one take, both in the same room. The album's secret: every song is about a real person she's never named.

tracks.title: I Knew It, I Know You
Gave You I Gave You I

synopsis: Gracie Abrams wrote most of this, her second album, while on the road supporting her debut, and the touring life pours into the songs, which are full of rented rooms, missed calls and the strange loneliness of being surrounded by people every night. She recorded with producer Aaron Dessner of the National, who helped her build on the intimate, diaristic style that had made her a streaming star, and the album's centerpiece, 'Close to You', became her breakout hit. Abrams has a gift for turning small, specific moments into songs that feel universal, and this record, her first to top the charts, proved she was more than a famous father's daughter.

name: Stick Season
teaser: Noah Kahan 2022 — a Vermont folk-pop album named for the bleak weeks between autumn and snow, written during lockdown in his hometown. It became one of the biggest folk records of the decade after TikTok rediscovered it, spawning an entire 'Stick Season' cover phenomenon.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Stick Season' — the title track about leaving a small town and the guilt of staying. Then 'Northern Attitude' — the fiddle-and-banjo opener. The album's genius is how specific it is: his Vermont references became anthems for everyone who left home.

synopsis: Noah Kahan grew up in a small town in Vermont, and this album, his third, is named for the bleak stretch between the end of fall and the first real snow, when the landscape is bare and everyone is stuck inside. The songs are full of that place and that feeling, mixing the storytelling of folk with the anthemic choruses of pop, and 'Stick Season' itself became one of the biggest songs of the decade after it blew up on social media. The album's follow-up version, with extra tracks and duets with artists like Post Malone and Kacey Musgraves, only extended its reach. It turned Kahan from a cult folk act into one of the most streamed artists in the world, singing about home, mental health and the people who never left.

name: American Heartbreak
teaser: Zach Bryan 2022 — a 34-song double album recorded in 12 days with a live band in a cabin, released with almost no promotion. It became the biggest country record of the year, and turned the Navy veteran into a folk-country superstar.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Something in the Orange' — the viral demo version exists and is worth hearing too; the studio version is the song about a sunset he watched while a relationship faded. Then 'Burn, Burn, Burn' — the closer, recorded live in the room. 34 songs, no skips.

synopsis: Zach Bryan had been building a following one raw, self-recorded song at a time, and this sprawling double album, thirty-four songs recorded in just twelve days with a live band, was his declaration that he had arrived. The record is all over the map in the best way, from the screaming rock of 'Something in the Orange' to the tender country ballads and the spoken-word opener, and his voice, huge and grainy, carries every bit of it. Written in the aftermath of his mother's death, the album is full of grief, faith and the hard work of moving on. It debuted at number one and made Bryan, still in his twenties, the biggest new voice in country music, a genre he stretched to fit his own wounds.

name: I've Tried Everything but Therapy (Part 1)
teaser: Teddy Swims 2023 — a debut EP from a YouTube cover singer whose gospel-and-soul voice made 'Lose Control' his first #1. The title is a joke about his therapy-themed album rollout; Part 2 came later. Eight songs that show off a voice that shouldn't fit in any one genre.

exploreAction.targetName: I've Tried Everything but Therapy (Part 1) (2023) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Lose Control' — the chorus scream is a note he'd never hit until the final take, and the raw vocal was kept. Then 'The Door' — a soul-pop breakup song whose falsetto bridge was recorded in a closet. He's a cover artist by origin; these are the originals.

synopsis: Teddy Swims had spent years posting cover songs on YouTube, where his huge, soulful voice turned pop songs into gospel testimonials, before he finally released his own music. This EP, his debut, shows what all those covers were building toward: a mix of pop, R&B and country that exists mainly as a vehicle for his extraordinary voice, which can go from a whisper to a full-throated roar in a single line. The ballad 'Lose Control' became a slow-burning global smash, climbing the charts for months and turning the former cover singer into one of the most streamed artists in the world. The record's title is a joke about his journey through therapy, and its songs are full of that self-aware, hard-won warmth.

name: Fireworks & Rollerblades
teaser: Benson Boone 2024 — a debut album from the singer who quit American Idol mid-season. It's a rock-leaning pop record anchored by 'Beautiful Things', one of the biggest songs of 2024, which he nearly didn't include.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Beautiful Things' — the quiet-verse-to-screaming-chorus structure is the whole trick; the fear-of-loss lyrics are real. Then 'Slow It Down' — the piano intro was written the night his grandmother died. He quit a TV show to gamble on his own sound; it paid off.

synopsis: Benson Boone's path to pop stardom was unusual: he made it onto American Idol, then quit the show mid-season to pursue his own music, a gamble that this debut album proved right. The record is a set of big, earnest pop rock songs built for arenas, led by 'Beautiful Things', a soaring anthem about gratitude and fear that became one of the biggest hits of 2024. Boone's voice, a high, emotive tenor, carries songs about love, faith and the terror of losing what you have, and his songwriting, co-written with a team of Nashville and LA pros, is polished without losing its heart. The album made him one of the most successful new pop stars of the decade.

name: Take Me Back to Eden
teaser: Sleep Token 2023 — the third album from the anonymous masked band, a 63-minute epic that refuses to stay in one genre: metal, pop, R&B and gospel all appear. It's the conclusion of a trilogy about the singer's relationship with the deity Sleep.

exploreAction.targetName: Take Me Back to Eden (2023) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Summoning' — the song that made them famous when its second half turned from metal into a funk groove into gospel. Then 'Chokehold' — the opener, soft-loud-soft personified. The lore matters: the whole album is a letter to a god.

synopsis: Sleep Token built their whole world around anonymity, with members performing in masks and led by a figure known only as Vessel, singing about a mysterious deity called Sleep, and this, their third album, brought that strange vision to the mainstream. The music is a dizzying fusion of metal, pop, R&B and gospel, with Vessel's silky croon sliding into screamed choruses over djent riffs and huge synth swells, and the record's centerpiece, 'The Summoning', became a viral sensation with its shocking mid-song groove shift. It is a demanding, theatrical album that somehow became a commercial hit, debuting in the top five and turning the anonymous band into one of the most talked-about acts in rock.

name: Unreal Unearth
teaser: Hozier 2023 — his third album, structured around Dante's nine circles of Hell, one song per circle. Recorded with a folk ensemble and a string section, it became his first #1 album in the US, and 'Eat Your Young' a viral hit.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Eat Your Young' — the church-organ opener hides a trap beat, and the title is a Greek myth reference. Then 'Francesca' — the second circle of Hell, where the damned lovers say even damnation was worth it. The whole album is a descent; start at the top and go down.

tracks.title: To Someone from a Warm Climate (Uiscefhuaraithe)

synopsis: Hozier spent years working on this, his third album, and he structured it around a bold idea: each of its sixteen songs corresponds to one of the nine circles of hell in Dante's Inferno, with the record tracing a journey from sin and punishment toward something like redemption. The music matches the ambition, drawing on Irish folk, blues, gospel and art rock, with Hozier's enormous voice carrying songs about desire, faith, history and the climate crisis. The single 'Eat Your Young' and the aching 'First Light' became favorites, and the album was hailed as his best work, a record that uses an ancient poem to make sense of the present moment without ever feeling academic.

name: Norman Fucking Rockwell!
teaser: Lana Del Rey 2019 — the album critics called the best of the decade, a 67-minute piano-and-guitar epic produced by Jack Antonoff. The title is a joke about American culture, and the closing track 'Hope Is a Dangerous Thing for a Woman Like Me to Have' is a one-woman requiem.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Venice Bitch' — a 9-minute song that spends its last four minutes as a psychedelic guitar jam. Then 'The Greatest' — the line 'the culture is lit, and I had a ball' is a farewell to a dying California. The album is a love letter to a country she's already mourning.

tracks.title: Hope Is a Dangerous Thing for a Woman Like Me to Have – but I Have It

synopsis: Lana Del Rey had spent a decade being underestimated, written off as a sad girl making pastiche, but this album, her fifth, silenced every critic. Produced with Jack Antonoff, the record is a wry, gorgeous meditation on America, fame and love, full of her best songwriting and sung with a new confidence, and it opens with the devastating one-two of 'Norman Fucking Rockwell' and 'Mariners Apartment Complex'. Rolling Stone named it the greatest album of the 2010s, and its reputation has only grown. It is the record where Del Rey stopped being a persona and became, in the eyes of nearly everyone, one of the essential songwriters of her generation.

name: Utopia
teaser: Travis Scott 2023 — his fourth album, a 73-minute odyssey built around the concept of a utopia he couldn't reach. Recorded with a rotating cast of 20+ producers, it debuted at #1 and its desert-set rollout included a live album premiere at the Pyramids of Giza.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'FE!N' — no hook, just a chant, over a single distorted synth. Then 'MELTDOWN' — the Drake feature that dissects their feud. The album is sequenced like a journey through a desert; notice how the second half turns psychedelic.

synopsis: Travis Scott spent five years building this, his fourth album, and it arrives with the weight of everything that happened in between, including the Astroworld tragedy that nearly ended his career. The record is a seventy-three minute odyssey through Scott's psychedelic trap universe, full of cavernous beats, Auto-Tuned wails and guest verses from a who's who of rap, and its songs bleed into one another like a film score. The production, led by Scott himself with help from Metro Boomin and others, is the real star, with beats that sound like they are being played in a cathedral. It debuted at number one and reminded everyone why Scott had been the biggest rapper of his generation before the fall.

name: I Never Liked You
teaser: Future 2022 — his ninth studio album, a 16-track set that debuted at #1 and featured Tems, Gunna and Young Thug. Its lead single 'Wait for U' won a Grammy. The title is a direct diss to the industry that doubted him.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Wait for U' — the Tems-sampled song that won a Grammy, with Drake trading verses. Then 'PUFFIN ON ZOOTIEZ' — the album's centerpiece, named for his ad-lib. Future's genius is melodic repetition: every hook is built on a phrase you can't stop humming.

synopsis: Future had spent the previous two years releasing a flood of music, including a pair of albums with his on-off collaborator Drake, but this record, his ninth studio album, showed he had lost none of his power. The sixteen songs are classic Future: dark, druggy, luxurious and brutally honest about his own self-destruction, with the centerpiece 'Wait for U', a collaboration with Tems and Drake built on a sample of a South African song, becoming one of the biggest hits of his career. The album debuted at number one, his eighth chart-topper, and its title, aimed at his critics and exes alike, captured the defiant mood of a rapper who had outlasted everyone. It is pure, uncompromising Future.

name: Savage Mode II
teaser: 21 Savage & Metro Boomin 2020 — the sequel to their 2016 breakout, a 15-track horror-movie of a trap album. It debuted at #1 and 'Runnin' and 'Mr. Right Now' became anthems. Metro's beats are the star: cinematic, string-laden, menacing.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Runnin' — the beat switches from a warped vocal sample into a soul loop mid-song. Then 'Mr. Right Now' — the Drake feature recorded over FaceTime during lockdown. The album's horror-movie interludes are the thread: it's a trap slasher film.

synopsis: 21 Savage and Metro Boomin had made one of the defining mixtapes of the 2010s with their first collaboration, and this sequel, arriving four years later, picks up exactly where they left off. Metro's production is darker and more cinematic than before, full of creeping melodies and bass that hits like a freight train, and 21 Savage's deadpan delivery, cold and precise, floats over it with total control. The album features the smash 'Runnin' and the eerie 'Mr. Right Now' with Drake, and its fifteen tracks move with the confidence of two artists at the peak of their powers. It debuted at number one and confirmed that the duo had become one of the great partnerships in rap.

name: Whole Lotta Red
teaser: Playboi Carti 2020 — a 24-song, 62-minute album of chaos that fans waited four years for. It's the sound of a rapper abandoning melody for pure rhythm and texture, and it became a template for the next decade of underground rap.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sky' — the synth loop never changes while Carti's voice morphs from deep to baby-high. Then 'New Tank' — notice the verses are made of sounds, not words. The album is deliberately exhausting; it's named for the luxury store that banned him.

synopsis: Playboi Carti had fans waiting four years for this album, his second, and what he gave them was chaos: twenty-four songs, most of them under three minutes, built on screaming, distorted vocals and beats that sound like they are falling apart. The record is an assault, with Carti abandoning the playful melodies of his debut for a harsh, ecstatic style he called his 'vampire' era, and its unrelenting energy made it an instant cult classic. It debuted at number one despite the fact that Carti did almost no promotion, and its influence on the sound of rap in the following years has been enormous. It is difficult, confrontational music that rewards total surrender.

name: Eternal Atake
teaser: Lil Uzi Vert 2020 — the long-delayed third album, named after a UFO-cult philosophy Uzi made up. It debuted at #1 and its first three songs all hit the top 10. The album's sci-fi aesthetic — including a fake religion — is the point.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Baby Pluto' — the song that reveals the album's fiction: Pluto is Uzi's alien alter ego. Then 'Silly Watch' — the deadpan flex anthem. The album opens with a fake church sermon and ends with a 2-minute piano ballad; the range is the joke.

synopsis: Lil Uzi Vert announced this album, his third, years before it came out, and its title, a reference to a UFO cult, only added to the mystery as release dates came and went. When it finally arrived in 2020 it was worth the wait: eighteen songs that bounce between the melodic rap that made Uzi a star and harder, weirder experiments, with the record's centerpiece 'XO Tour Llif3' already a classic from its earlier release. The album debuted at number one and broke streaming records, and its long-delayed arrival became one of the strangest and most successful rollouts in recent rap history. It is the sound of an artist who built his own mythology and then delivered on it.

name: So Much Fun
teaser: Young Thug 2019 — his first album, and his first #1, after a decade of mixtapes. It's a 16-track showcase of the most imitated voice in modern rap, with features from Travis Scott, Lil Baby and Future.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hot' — a single piano loop under Thug's pure-melody verse; the song is 3 minutes of him singing in tongues. Then 'The London' — the Travis Scott and J. Cole feature, recorded after a chance meeting in London. Try counting how many distinct voices he uses in one song.

synopsis: Young Thug had spent a decade as the most influential rapper of his generation without ever releasing a proper album, building his legend on a mountain of mixtapes, and this record, his first official studio album, finally gave the world a single statement of his genius. The nineteen songs are a showcase for his uncanny voice, which can go from a squeak to a growl to a gorgeous melody in the space of a bar, and his collaborators, including Travis Scott, J. Cole and Lil Baby, all seem to be trying to keep up. The album debuted at number one, confirming what his fans had always known, and its loose, joyful weirdness is the sound of an artist who had nothing left to prove.

name: Melt My Eyez See Your Future
teaser: Denzel Curry 2022 — a jazz-rap meditation on mortality and growth, recorded after his grandmother's death and a life-threatening health scare. It features Thundercat, Robert Glasper and T-Pain, and it's his most mature, most collaborative album.

exploreAction.targetName: Melt My Eyez See Your Future (2022) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Walkin' — the song that changes genre mid-track as it shifts from rage to hope. Then 'Troubles' — the T-Pain duet about therapy. The album's title is a mantra: look at your mortality, and use it to grow. The jazz is real — Glasper plays keys throughout.

synopsis: Denzel Curry had spent his career as one of rap's most ferocious technicians, and this album, his fifth, found him slowing down and looking inward. Made with producer Kenny Beats and a crew of live jazz musicians, the record is a meditation on mortality, therapy and growth, with Curry rapping over warm, soulful beats instead of the punishing trap he was known for. 'Walkin' became a hit with its triumphant horn line, and the album's title, a reference to the idea of seeing yourself clearly, is the key to its mood: this is a hard man learning to be soft. It was hailed as the best work of his career and proved that rap's most intense voice could also be its most reflective.

name: Veteran
teaser: JPEGMAFIA 2018 — the album that made Peggy the king of glitch-rap, a 44-minute collage of broken beats, alarm bells, and pure confrontation. It was recorded in a year where he also produced for others and toured constantly.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to '1539 N. Calvert' — the song named after a Baltimore address, built on a broken drum machine. Then 'Baby I'm Bleeding' — the stalker voicemail sample is real. The album is designed to be uncomfortable: turn it up and notice the audio clipping is intentional.

tracks.title: I Cannot Fucking Wait Til Morrissey Dies
Does This Ski Mask Make Me Look Fat?
This Song Is a Safe Space

synopsis: JPEGMAFIA, known to his fans as Peggy, had spent years making music that sounded like the internet having a breakdown, and this album, his second, is where the method clicked. The record is a collage of distorted beats, strange samples and verses that lurch between fury and hilarity, with Peggy rapping about race, politics and the music industry over production that sounds like it was assembled from broken electronics. It is confrontational and alienating by design, but underneath the noise is a sharp, funny and deeply political artist. The album made Peggy the king of the underground, and its influence on experimental rap in the years since has been massive.

name: The Forever Story
teaser: JID 2022 — his second album, named for his late grandmother, a 15-track epic that moves from boom-bap to trap to soul. It's considered one of the best rap albums of the 2020s, and its production credits read like a who's-who of the genre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Surround Sound' — the chopped soul sample and the title's metaphor: his family's voices surrounding him as a kid. Then 'Kody Blu 31' — named for his grandmother's birthday, a sung hook that breaks the rap flow. The whole album is a family tree in song form.

synopsis: JID had spent years as the most technically gifted rapper in his crew, and this album, his second, named for his late grandmother, is where he turned that skill into a complete statement. The record is an epic, fifteen tracks of rapid-fire rapping, soulful singing and production that draws on boom bap, trap and gospel, with JID's voice moving through flows with dizzying speed. The centerpiece is the posse cut '2007', and the album features guest spots from Lil Wayne, 21 Savage and others, all of them overshadowed by the host. It debuted to near-universal acclaim and established JID, long hyped as the future of rap, as the present.

name: Sometimes I Might Be Introvert
teaser: Little Simz 2021 — the acronym album (SIMBI) that won the Mercury Prize, a 19-track epic mixing orchestral hip-hop with soul and funk. It's a portrait of an introvert navigating fame, and it made Simz the voice of British rap.

exploreAction.targetName: Sometimes I Might Be Introvert (2021) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Introvert' — the 5-minute opener with no hook, just an orchestral declaration. Then 'Woman' — the video features over 100 real British women. The album's drama is its point: it swings from full orchestra to bare boom-bap, mirroring an introvert's social battery.

tracks.title: I Love You, I Hate You
The Rapper that Came to Tea (Interlude)

synopsis: Little Simz had spent a decade building a reputation as one of Britain's most uncompromising rappers, and this album, whose acronym spells out her nickname SIMBI, is her masterpiece. The record is a lush, cinematic epic, produced largely by Inflo, with strings, choirs and soul samples framing Simz's extraordinary rapping, which moves between autobiography, social commentary and pure poetry. Songs like 'Woman' and 'Introvert' show her range, and the album won the Mercury Prize, Britain's most prestigious music award. It established Little Simz as one of the greatest rappers of her generation, an artist with the ambition of a filmmaker and the precision of a surgeon.

name: Orquídeas
teaser: Kali Uchis 2024 — her first all-Spanish album, named for the orchid, Colombia's national flower. It debuted at #2 in the US, the highest chart position ever for an all-Spanish album by a woman, and mixes reggaetón, cumbia and bolero.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Igual Que un Ángel' — the Peso Pluma duet that sets corrido vocals over dream-pop. Then 'Muñekita' — reggaetón meets cumbia, the album's strangest and best track. The album is 12 songs in 32 minutes, and every one is in Spanish; she wrote them with her own lyrics book.

synopsis: Kali Uchis had spent a decade moving between English and Spanish, between pop, R&B and reggaeton, and this album, her first recorded entirely in Spanish, is a homecoming. Named for the orchid, a flower that blooms in harsh conditions, the record is a lush, psychedelic take on Latin pop, with Uchis's honeyed voice floating over boleros, cumbias and reggaeton beats. The collaborations, including Peso Pluma on 'Igual Que Un Ángel' and El Alfa on the raucous 'Muñekita', show her range, and the album won a Grammy for best Latin pop record. It is the sound of an artist fully in control of her identity, singing in the language of her family and making it feel like the whole world's music.

name: Vice Versa
teaser: Rauw Alejandro 2021 — the album that broke reggaetón's mold, mixing the genre with synth-pop, disco and even house. 'Todo de Ti' was the biggest Latin song of the year, and the album's title reflects its dualities: sweet and dark, old and new.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Todo de Ti' — the 80s funk bassline and the total absence of reggaetón rhythm; that's why it stood out. Then '2:00 AM' — the Rosalía duet, recorded during lockdown, a late-night ballad. The album flips between two moods — vice, versa — as its title promises.

synopsis: Rauw Alejandro had been one of the biggest stars in reggaeton, but with this album he decided to break the genre's rules. The record mixes reggaeton with funk, disco, R&B and even hints of rock, all wrapped in a sleek, futuristic production that made it feel like Latin pop had entered a new era. The single 'Todo de Ti', a slice of pure disco-funk, became a global smash, and the album debuted at number one in the United States, a first for a Spanish-language album by a solo male artist. Rauw's voice, smooth and versatile, carries the whole experiment, and the record proved that the biggest stars of Latin music could take risks and still rule the charts.

name: Mor, No Le Temas a la Oscuridad
teaser: Feid 2023 — the album that turned 'Ferxxo' into a Latin superstar, a reggaetón record full of emo heartbreak anthems. Its title means 'Love, Don't Fear the Darkness', and its green-eyed emo aesthetic took over Latin pop.

exploreAction.targetName: Mor, No Le Temas a la Oscuridad (2023) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Normal' — the TikTok phenomenon about realizing a breakup is just normal. Then 'Luna' — the nursery-rhyme-simple chorus that became a stadium singalong. The album is 14 songs of heartbreak; Feid's whole persona — Ferxxo — is the emo kid who grew up to rule the club.

synopsis: Feid, known to his fans as Ferxxo, had spent years as one of reggaeton's most reliable hitmakers before this album turned him into a superstar. The record is a love letter to his native Medellín, full of the paisas sounds of his childhood, and its songs, mostly about love and heartbreak, are delivered with a sweetness that set him apart from the genre's harder edges. Tracks like 'Ferxxo 151' and 'Normal' became anthems, and the album's title, which means 'don't fear the darkness', captured its mood of romantic vulnerability. It made Feid one of the biggest Latin artists in the world and confirmed that reggaeton's future was in Medellín.

name: Génesis
teaser: Peso Pluma 2023 — the album that took corridos tumbados global, a 15-track record of narcocorridos with trap beats and traditional sierreño guitars. 'Ella Baila Sola' became the first Mexican song to crack Spotify's global top 10.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Ella Baila Sola' — the Eslabon Armado duet that made history; the guitar is pure sierreño over a trap groove. Then 'Lagunas' — the accordion solo is the emotional peak. The album is a genesis story: the corrido tradition reborn with a nasal, deadpan new voice.

synopsis: Peso Pluma had been part of the corridos tumbados movement, a Mexican take on the narcocorrido that mixed traditional storytelling with trap beats, but this album, his fourth, is what made the genre a global phenomenon. The record's fifteen songs, with their brassy, accordion-driven corridos and Pluma's high, airy voice, topped charts around the world and made him the first Mexican artist to reach the top of the global Spotify chart. The single 'Ella Baila Sola', a collaboration with Eslabon Armado, became the highest-charting Mexican song in Billboard history. Pluma's sudden, enormous success turned corridos tumbados from a regional style into one of the defining sounds of the decade.

name: Born in the Wild
teaser: Tems 2024 — the long-awaited debut from Nigeria's most in-demand voice, a 16-track album that moves between Afrobeats, R&B and alternative soul. It features Asake and J. Cole, and was recorded over four years between tours.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Free Mind' — the anxiety-born anthem that spent years climbing charts before it peaked. Then 'Burning' — the opener she wrote to process her mother's death. Tems's voice is the album's instrument: it floats above every beat, never forcing anything.

synopsis: Tems had spent years as the most in-demand voice in African music, singing hooks for Drake, Future and Beyoncé, before she finally released her own debut album. The wait was worth it: the record is a stunning showcase for her voice, a warm, weightless instrument that floats over sparse, atmospheric production, and its songs move between R&B, Afrobeats and something entirely her own. 'Burning' and 'Free Fall' show her range, and the album debuted to acclaim that confirmed what everyone in the industry already knew. It is the sound of an artist who had been shaping other people's music for so long that her own vision was fully formed.

name: The Year I Turned 21
teaser: Ayra Starr 2024 — her second album, recorded between sold-out tours, a 17-track record that captures the chaos of being 21 and famous. It debuted at #3 on the Billboard World Albums chart and confirmed her as the new face of Afrobeats.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Commas' — the opener, a statement of arrival with a beat that hits like a victory lap. Then 'Control' — the album's most personal track, about the cost of fame. She was 21 while making it, and the album sounds like that: restless, hungry, unapologetic.

synopsis: Ayra Starr had become a star as a teenager, and this album, her second, was made between sold-out tours and festival headline sets, which only sharpened its energy. The record is a confident statement from one of the brightest young voices in Afrobeats, mixing the genre's rhythms with R&B and pop, and its songs are about growing up in public, taking control and having fun. The single 'Commas' became a global hit, and the album's seventeen tracks show a young woman who has learned to command a room. It confirmed Ayra Starr as the leader of the new generation of Nigerian pop.

name: My 21st Century Blues
teaser: Raye 2023 — the debut album from the songwriter who spent six years writing for other people, released independently after her label refused to put it out. It won the Brit Award for Album of the Year, and its 15 tracks are a therapy session set to music.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Escapism' — spoken-word verses over a jazz-swing hook that became her first #1. Then 'Ice Cream Man' — the devastating account of assault in the industry. She funded it herself after leaving a major label; it's her revenge and confession.

synopsis: Raye had spent six years writing songs for other people, including some of the biggest hits in British pop, while her own record label refused to release her music, a battle she fought publicly and finally won by going independent. This debut album is the sound of that fight, a sprawling, genre-defying record that moves from gospel to jazz to house to pop, all anchored by her extraordinary voice and her fury at the industry that tried to silence her. The single 'Escapism', a rap-inflected song about self-destruction, became a global hit, and the album won the Mercury Prize. It is one of the great revenge records in pop, made by an artist who refused to be anyone's ghostwriter.

name: Magdalene
teaser: FKA twigs 2019 — her second album, named after Mary Magdalene, a 39-minute art-pop epic about womanhood, faith and heartbreak. Co-produced with Nicolas Jaar and Daniel Lopatin, it's built on her signature mix of operatic vocals and brutalist beats.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Cellophane' — about being treated like glass, with a pole-dancing video that's a fall-and-rise metaphor. Then 'Mirrored Heart' — giving everything to someone who reflects nothing back. The album reframes Magdalene as every woman who's been written off.

synopsis: FKA twigs had spent years as one of the most adventurous artists in pop, and this album, her second, is her most personal and ambitious work. Named after Mary Magdalene, the record uses the biblical figure as a lens for exploring femininity, desire, betrayal and faith, and its music, produced with Nicolas Jaar and others, is a strange, beautiful fusion of art pop, R&B and electronic music. The centerpiece, 'Cellophane', a piano ballad about a love that turned cruel, became her most famous song. The album was made while twigs was recovering from surgery and a very public heartbreak, and its pain is worn openly. It is a difficult, rewarding record that rewards deep listening.

name: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You
teaser: Caroline Polachek 2023 — her third solo album, a maximalist pop record with bagpipes, opera, and a 6-minute guitar solo. It was named album of the year by several major critics, and it sounds like nothing else released that year.

exploreAction.targetName: Desire, I Want to Turn Into You (2023) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Welcome to My Island' — bagpipe-like synth and a real guitar solo, about wanting to be consumed. Then 'Bunny Is a Rider' — the hit whose title is nonsense she invented. Her whistle register appears mid-song without warning.

tracks.title: Spring Is Coming With a Strawberry in the Mouth

synopsis: Caroline Polachek had spent two decades making inventive pop, first in the band Chairlift and then as a solo artist, but this album, her third, is where she let all her ideas loose at once. The record is a maximalist wonder, full of flamenco guitars, bagpipes, operatic vocals and the biggest melodies she had ever written, all anchored by her extraordinary voice, which can leap from a whisper to a soaring wail in a heartbeat. 'Welcome to My Island' and 'Blood and Butter' became instant classics, and the album was hailed as one of the best of the year. It is pop music as high art, made by an artist with no interest in playing it safe.

name: Beatopia
teaser: Beabadoobee 2022 — her second album, named after the imaginary world she invented as a 7-year-old to escape school bullying. It's a bedroom-pop record that stretches into shoegaze, bossa nova and folk, with the 90s sound she's famous for.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'the perfect pair' — the song about a relationship too perfect to last. Then '10:36' — named for the timestamp when she wrote the hook. The album's title is a real place she drew as a kid; the music is what that place sounds like grown up.

tracks.title: The Adults Are Talking (Antidote Live Session)

synopsis: Beabadoobee, born Beatrice Laus, named this album after the imaginary world she invented as a child to escape from her strict Catholic upbringing, and the record is an attempt to return to that place as an adult. It is a dreamy, warm collection of songs that mix the 90s alt-rock and shoegaze she grew up loving with her own gentle voice and gift for melody, and its songs about love, nostalgia and finding your own world made her one of the most beloved voices of her generation. The single 'Talk' became a hit, and the album's title track captures its mood of soft defiance. It is music for the dreamers, made by an artist who never stopped believing in her own.

name: If I Could Make It Go Quiet
teaser: Girl in red 2021 — the debut album from the Norwegian bedroom-pop artist, a 10-song record about anxiety, heartbreak and queer joy. It made her a global star and an icon for a generation of queer listeners.

exploreAction.targetName: If I Could Make It Go Quiet (2021) end-to-end
