exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Serotonin' — the song about intrusive thoughts that literally glitches and distorts when the thoughts win. Then 'we fell in love in october' — the gentle anthem that became a queer coming-out soundtrack. The album is 27 minutes: short, and every second counts.

synopsis: Girl in red, the project of Norwegian artist Marie Ulven, had built a devoted following with songs about queer love and mental health recorded in her bedroom, and this debut album brought that world into sharper focus. The record is full of the anxieties and ecstasies of being young, with Ulven's intimate voice and guitar-driven sound, and its songs about depression, desire and self-acceptance made her a hero to a generation that saw themselves in her. 'Serotonin', with its frank lyrics about intrusive thoughts, and the aching 'You Stupid Bitch' became anthems. It is a brave, tender record that turned a bedroom project into one of the most important voices in modern pop.

name: Superache
teaser: Conan Gray 2022 — his second album, a 12-track pop record about grief, friendship and growing up in a small Texas town. The title means 'super-pain', and the album's heartbreak anthems made him one of the defining voices of sad-pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Memories' — the song about losing a friend who's still alive. Then 'The Exit' — the album's thesis, about a relationship that ended before it started. He wrote the album in his childhood bedroom; the small-town loneliness is the thread running through every song.

synopsis: Conan Gray had built his following as a teenager making painfully honest songs about growing up in Texas, and this album, his second, found him turning those confessions into bigger, more polished pop. The record is about grief, friendship and the messy end of youth, and its twelve songs are built on enormous choruses and Gray's clear, emotive voice. 'Heather', a devastating song about unrequited love that had become a viral hit in its earlier version, appears in a new form, and the album's title, a word he invented for the feeling of hurting so much you cannot speak, captures its mood. It made Gray one of the leading voices of the sad pop generation.

name: Gemini Rights
teaser: Steve Lacy 2022 — his second solo album, 10 songs made largely on his iPhone and laptop. It won a Grammy for Best Progressive R&B Album, and 'Bad Habit' became the biggest song of the year — a song recorded on a phone.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Bad Habit' — the GarageBand-made hit; listen for the phone-quality textures in the drums. Then 'Mercury' — the bassline is the hook. The album's title is a joke about astrology; the songs are a post-breakup rebound set to neo-soul.

synopsis: Steve Lacy had spent his career as a teenage guitar prodigy, first in the band the Internet and then as a solo artist, and this album, his second, was made mostly on his iPhone and laptop, a fact that became part of its legend. The record's ten songs are short, loose and full of joy, mixing funk, R&B, rock and pop into something that sounds effortless, and Lacy's voice, warm and sly, floats over guitar lines he recorded in his bedroom. The single 'Bad Habit' became one of the biggest songs of 2022, a year after its release, and the album won a Grammy. It is the sound of a young genius making music for the pure pleasure of it.

name: Dreamland
teaser: Glass Animals 2020 — their third album, a memory-palace of frontman Dave Bayley's childhood, made during his sister's illness and after the band's drummer nearly died. It features 'Heat Waves', the slowest-burning #1 hit in chart history, and 'Tokyo Drifting' with Denzel Curry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Heat Waves' — the flooded-world video and the lyrics about missing someone until it feels like drowning. Then 'Space Ghost Coast to Coast' — the song about a friendship ended by conspiracy theories. The album's interludes are real audio from Bayley's childhood tapes.

tracks.title: I Don't Wanna Talk (I Just Wanna Dance)

synopsis: Glass Animals had spent years making intricate, electronic-tinged indie rock, but this album, their third, was shaped by tragedy: frontman Dave Bayley's best friend and collaborator was hit by a car and left with a severe brain injury, and the record is an attempt to process that loss. Bayley described the album as a memory palace, full of images from his childhood and his friend's recovery, and the music, made with a new pop clarity, carries those memories into the light. 'Heat Waves' became one of the biggest songs of the decade, a global smash that spent months at number one. It is a heartbreaking record that somehow became the soundtrack to millions of people's summers.

name: Rat Saw God
teaser: Wednesday 2023 — the Asheville band's fourth album, a 47-minute collision of shoegaze and country that made them the most talked-about indie band of the year. Frontwoman Karly Hartzman screams over pedal steel; it shouldn't work, and it does.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Bull Believer' — the 8-minute closer that builds to a wordless scream of catharsis. Then 'Chosen to Deserve' — the pedal steel cutting through distortion. The album is named after a tattoo Hartzman saw on a stranger; the title is a promise: no mercy for the mediocre.

synopsis: Wednesday, a band from Asheville, North Carolina, had been making noisy, strange music for years when this album, their fourth, brought them to a wider audience. The record is a collision of everything the band loves, with guitarist MJ Lenderman's sprawling, psychedelic solos crashing into frontwoman Karly Hartzman's songs, which mix country twang with screams and stories of the American south. 'Bull Believer', the album's eight-minute centerpiece, became a cult sensation with its howled climax. The record's title, a reference to a plaque the band saw on the back of a bathroom stall, captures its mood of resigned, hilarious despair. It made Wednesday the most exciting band in American rock.

name: Any Shape You Take
teaser: Indigo De Souza 2021 — her breakthrough second album, a 13-song set of raw, confessional indie rock recorded in Asheville. 'Kill Me' became an anthem for the heartbroken, and the album made her a hero of the new American sad-rock scene.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Kill Me' — the country-tinged diary entry that builds into a scream; the title is a joke about a breakup. Then 'Real Pain' — the song about a friend's car accident, written years later. Her voice cracks on purpose; the imperfection is the performance.

synopsis: Indigo De Souza had been making raw, home-recorded music in North Carolina for years when this album, her second, broke her out of the underground. The record's thirteen songs are built on her extraordinary voice, which can go from a whisper to a full-throated scream in the same song, and her lyrics, about family, love and the mess of being alive, are painfully specific. 'Kill Me' and 'Real Pain' show her range, and the album's production, warmer and fuller than her earlier work, lets the songs breathe. It was hailed as a breakthrough and established De Souza as one of the most exciting young songwriters in American indie rock.

name: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
teaser: Big Thief 2022 — a 20-song double album recorded in five locations over five months, from a cabin to a rock club. It's a sprawling American folk record that deliberately refuses a single style, and it won Album of the Year at the 2023 Libera Awards.

exploreAction.targetName: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You (2022) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Simulation Swarm' — the 6-minute song with four guitar solos, recorded live in one take. Then 'Not' — the song that dissolves into noise at the end. The album is 80 minutes; treat it like a long conversation, not a single record.

tracks.title: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You

synopsis: Big Thief had been making acclaimed, restless music for years when their singer and guitarist Adrianne Lenker proposed the idea that became this album: instead of picking songs for a single record, they would record everything, traveling to five different places over five months and making music wherever they landed. The result is a double album of twenty songs that wander through folk, rock, country and free improvisation, full of the band's trademark intimacy and strange beauty. Songs like 'Spud Infinity' and 'Simulation Swarm' became instant favorites, and the record was hailed as their masterpiece. It is the sound of a great band at the peak of its powers, unafraid to follow every idea.

name: Kick I
teaser: Arca 2020 — the first of four albums she released in a year, a 40-minute set that reimagines reggaetón as avant-garde art. With guests Rosalía, Björk, Shygirl and SOPHIE, it's the sound of a producer at the peak of her powers refusing every genre rule.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'KLK' — the Rosalía collab that sets flamenco-adjacent vocals over a brutalist reggaetón beat. Then 'Mequetrefe' — a Spanish insult turned into an anthem. The album's four 'Kick' siblings exist because she had too much material; this one is the statement of intent.

synopsis: Arca, born Alejandra Ghersi, had spent years as the most sought-after producer in experimental pop, working with Kanye West, Björk and FKA twigs, before she turned fully to her own music. Kick I, the first of four albums she released in a year, is her boldest statement yet, a record that welds the harsh, deconstructed club sounds of her early work to something closer to pop, with her own voice, often pitched and twisted, singing in Spanish and English over beats that lurch between beauty and violence. Songs like 'Nonbinary' and the Björk duet 'Afterwards' show her range, and the album confirmed her as one of the most singular artists of her generation, making music that sounds like the future arriving early.

name: uknowhatimsayin¿
teaser: Danny Brown 2019 — his fifth album, produced entirely by Q-Tip of A Tribe Called Quest, a 32-minute set of surrealist, funky rap. It's the most accessible Danny Brown album and one of the strangest; both are true at once.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to '3 Tearz' — the Run-DMC-style posse cut produced by Q-Tip, whose hand is all over the album's clean funk. Then 'Negro Spiritual' — the jazz sample and the album's emotional core. Q-Tip made Danny keep his weirdest instincts; the title is his shrug.

synopsis: Danny Brown had spent a decade as rap's strangest and most beloved voice, a Detroit rapper with a voice like a cartoon character and a gift for making pain funny, and for this album he handed the controls to Q-Tip, the legendary leader of A Tribe Called Quest. The result is a record that smooths out Brown's chaos without taming it, with Q-Tip's warm, jazzy production framing some of the most personal raps of Brown's career. Songs like '3 Tearz' and 'Dirty Laundry' show the alchemy, and the album is full of the humor and heartbreak that made Brown a cult hero. It is the sound of two generations of rap geniuses finding common ground.

name: Some Rap Songs
teaser: Earl Sweatshirt 2018 — his third album, 24 minutes of grief made after his father's death. The beats are warped, the raps are whispers, and it's one of the most devastating albums in hip-hop. It's best listened to as a single poem.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Nowhere2go' — the warped soul sample and the barely-there verse, a whisper of grief. Then 'December 24' — named for his father's death date, the closing elegy. The album is 24 minutes and 15 songs; listen to it straight through, once.

synopsis: Earl Sweatshirt had been a teenage prodigy, part of the Odd Future collective, and he spent years retreating from the spotlight after the death of his father, the South African poet Keorapetse Kgositsile. This album, his third, is only twenty-four minutes long, but it is packed with more feeling than most records twice its length. The production is murky and abstract, built on strange samples and off-kilter drums, and Earl's raps, delivered in a weary mumble, are dense with grief and wordplay. It is a difficult record that rewards patience, and it was hailed as the sound of a young artist processing loss on his own terms, refusing to perform his sadness for anyone.

name: Michael
teaser: Killer Mike 2023 — his first solo album in 11 years, named for his birth name, a 40-minute soul-rap record about the Black men who raised him. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album, and its features include André 3000 and CeeLo Green.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Scientists & Engineers' — the André 3000 feature that's his first rap verse in years, a prayer-like meditation on Black excellence. Then 'Motherless' — the title track's emotional core, about his mother's death. The album is a eulogy that's also a celebration.

synopsis: Killer Mike had spent over a decade as one of rap's most forceful voices, first as a solo artist and then as half of Run the Jewels, and this album, his first solo record in eleven years, is named for his birth name, Michael Render. It is a deeply personal and political record, made with producer No I.D., that tells the story of his life in Atlanta, from his childhood to his grandmother's death to his work in the community, and it features an all-star cast including André 3000, Future and Eryn Allen Kane. Songs like 'Motherless' and 'Run' are among the most powerful of his career. It won the Grammy for best rap album and stands as a towering statement from a rapper at the peak of his powers.

name: Testing
teaser: A$AP Rocky 2018 — his third album, an experimental record whose title is literal: he's testing new sounds. From gospel choir samples to grime beats, it's Rocky's most adventurous album, and 'Praise the Lord' with Skepta became a global hit.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Praise the Lord (Da Shine)' — the Skepta collab made from a beat a stranger sent as a joke. Then 'A$AP Forever' — the choir sample and the video featuring his late friend A$AP Yams. The album's genre-hopping is the test; nothing repeats.

synopsis: A$AP Rocky had spent his career as rap's most stylish figure, but with this album he decided to make things strange. The record's title is a promise of experimentation, and its seventeen tracks live up to it, with Rocky pushing his sound into new territory, from the Frank Ocean collaboration 'Purity' to the Kid Cudi team-up 'Kids Turned Out Fine' and the wild 'A$AP Forever'. The production, led by Rocky himself with help from Skepta and others, is restless and unpredictable, and his laid-back voice floats over it all with total cool. It was not the commercial blockbuster his fans expected, but it showed an artist willing to risk his formula, and its reputation has grown since.

name: Wunna
teaser: Gunna 2020 — his second studio album, a 50-minute masterclass in melodic trap. The title is 'winner' in his family's dialect, and the album's warm, syrupy production became the sound of Atlanta's next generation.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Skybox' — the opener that sounds like a stadium filling up. Then 'Dollaz on My Head' — the Young Thug collab that shows his lineage. Gunna's verses are more melody than rap; count how many words he actually raps in a verse, then how many melodies he hums.

synopsis: Gunna had spent years as the smoothest voice in Atlanta trap, first as a guest on other people's songs and then as a star in his own right, and this album, his second, is a masterclass in his style. The record's title means 'winner' in his vocabulary, and its songs are full of the luxurious, melodic trap he helped perfect, with his voice, soft and Auto-Tuned, gliding over beats by Wheezy and Turbo. There are no hard edges here, just an hour of immaculately produced, effortlessly cool music, and its songs like 'Drip Too Hard' and 'Skybox' became anthems. It debuted at number one and confirmed Gunna as the leading voice of the new Atlanta school.

name: Currents
teaser: Tame Impala 2015 — the album that turned Kevin Parker's bedroom recordings into a global phenomenon, a psych-pop masterpiece about change and growth. 'The Less I Know the Better' and 'Let It Happen' made it the defining indie album of the mid-2010s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Let It Happen' — the 8-minute opener that glitches and stutters in the middle, a metaphor for letting go. Then 'The Less I Know the Better' — the disco-funk hit. Parker plays every instrument on the album himself; it's a one-man band's diary of a breakup.

tracks.title: The Less I Know the Better

synopsis: Kevin Parker had spent years making music alone in his bedroom in Perth, Australia, building a whole world of sound with just his voice and his instruments, and this album, his third under the name Tame Impala, was the one that brought that world to everyone. The record is a psychedelic pop masterpiece, full of warm synthesizers, honeyed harmonies and songs about love and self-doubt that feel both cosmic and intimate. 'The Less I Know the Better' and 'Let It Happen' became global hits, and the album topped charts around the world, turning the bedroom producer into one of the biggest acts in music. It is the sound of loneliness transformed into pure joy.

name: Nurture
teaser: Porter Robinson 2021 — the long-awaited second album from the EDM prodigy, made over five years while he recovered from depression. It samples his own voice as an instrument, uses real rain and birdsong, and turns grief into a euphoric, hopeful pop record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Something Comforting' — the song about finding comfort in art while depressed. Then 'Look at the Sky' — the turning point where the album finds hope. He recorded field sounds and his own voice as textures; the album is a garden grown out of a dark room.

synopsis: Porter Robinson had become an EDM prodigy as a teenager, playing the biggest festivals in the world with his hands on the decks, but he spent years trying to escape that persona. This album, his long-delayed second, is the result: a gentle, human record full of pianos, guitars and Robinson's own voice, singing about depression, recovery and the simple joy of making music. It is deeply influenced by the Japanese pop and video game soundtracks he grew up with, and its songs build from intimate beginnings into euphoric climaxes. The record divided his fans, who wanted bangers, but it was hailed by critics as a brave and beautiful statement of an artist finding himself.

name: Kid A
teaser: Radiohead's 2000 reinvention — they abandoned guitars for synthesisers, sequencers, and a glassy panic, and the world's most anticipated album became a pulse of pure unease that somehow topped the charts.

exploreAction.targetName: Kid A (2000) — 'Everything in Its Right Place' and 'How to Disappear Completely'
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to how the album opens mid-thought — Thom Yorke's voice cut into fragments over a pulsing organ. Then 'How to Disappear Completely', the song he wrote from advice Michael Stipe gave him for coping on stage. Notice how the strings smear the melody rather than support it.

synopsis: Radiohead had spent the 90s as the biggest rock band in the world, but in 1999 they were exhausted by their own success and terrified of repeating themselves. Their solution was to abandon guitars almost entirely, and Kid A, recorded in a Paris studio with the band playing synthesizers and computers instead of instruments, sounded like nothing they had made before. The album has almost no conventional songs, instead unfolding as a series of electronic soundscapes, from the krautrock pulse of the title track to the ambient drift of 'Treefingers' and the glitchy 'Idioteque'. It debuted at number one in America, a shock for such an experimental record, and it has been hailed ever since as the sound of a band blowing up its own formula.

name: Grace
teaser: Jeff Buckley's only completed album — a 1994 record that vaults between his father's folk legacy, Led Zeppelin power, and a falsetto that bends gender, ending with a 7-minute cover of Leonard Cohen's 'Hallelujah' that became the definitive version.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arc across the album: the garage-punk 'Eternal Life', the Spanish-sung 'Lilac Wine', the build of 'Hallelujah' from whispered to full-voice. Buckley drowned in 1997 at 30, and Grace became the great what-if of rock.

synopsis: Jeff Buckley was a cult figure when he recorded this, his only completed album, in 1994, and its release made him a legend. The record vaults between styles with dizzying confidence, from the devastating cover of Leonard Cohen's 'Hallelujah' to the Led Zeppelin rock of 'Last Goodbye' to the jazz-tinged 'Lilac Wine', and his voice, an astonishing four-octave instrument that could go from a whisper to a full-throated wail, carries all of it. He died in a drowning accident in 1997, at 30, before he could make a follow-up, which turned the album into an elegy for what might have been. It is one of the great debut albums in rock history, the sound of a once-in-a-generation voice.

name: Wish You Were Here
teaser: Pink Floyd's 1975 album about absence — a five-song suite that mourns their lost leader Syd Barrett, from the nine-minute 'Shine On You Crazy Diamond' to the title track that has made every stadium sing along for fifty years.

exploreAction.targetName: Wish You Were Here (1975) — 'Shine On You Crazy Diamond' parts 1-5
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the four-note opening theme as it returns in different forms across the song — it's Syd Barrett's goodbye. The band recorded it while Barrett, bald and changed, wandered into the studio unrecognized. The album is built around that ghost.

synopsis: Pink Floyd had spent the years after Dark Side of the Moon dealing with the fallout of success, including the departure of their founding member Syd Barrett, whose mental collapse had haunted the band for a decade. This album, their follow-up to the biggest-selling record of its era, is about absence, and its centerpiece, the two-part 'Shine On You Crazy Diamond', is a long, mournful elegy for Barrett, written around a four-note theme that builds into one of the most beautiful passages in their catalog. The record also includes the band's famous critique of the music industry, 'Have a Cigar', and the epic 'Welcome to the Machine'. It is a quiet, strange masterpiece about loss, made by a band at the height of its powers.

name: Siamese Dream
teaser: The Smashing Pumpkins' 1993 album of layered, shoegaze-dense guitars — Billy Corgan reportedly played most of the guitar parts himself, tracking layer after layer until the songs sounded like a dream you couldn't wake from.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar layers — 'Cherub Rock' opens with a solo buried under its own feedback, and 'Mayonaise' floats on a guitar that sounds like it's melting. The album was recorded in a studio with a broken drum kit and a band falling apart; the lushness is armor.

synopsis: The Smashing Pumpkins had been building toward something big with their first two albums, but nothing prepared the world for this, their third, a record of layered, shoegaze-dense guitars that sounded like a symphony played by a rock band. Billy Corgan, the band's mercurial leader, recorded hundreds of guitar tracks for each song, building walls of sound that his thin, keening voice floated over, and the album's songs, from the arena-sized 'Today' to the devastating ballad 'Disarm', were his most personal yet. The making of the record nearly destroyed the band, with producer Butch Vig pushing them through endless takes, but the result was worth it. It made the Pumpkins one of the biggest bands in the world.

name: Aja
teaser: 1977 Steely Dan's sixth album took jazz-rock to studio perfection: every track a small orchestra, every lyric a riddle. 'Deacon Blues' and 'Peg' were recorded with dozens of takes and the finest session players of the era. The band was mocked for its perfectionism; the album has outlasted the mockery.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the drum sound — Bernard Purdie and Steve Gadd anchor the grooves. The sax and guitar solos were cut from dozens of takes, and it shows.

synopsis: Steely Dan, the duo of Donald Fagen and Walter Becker, had spent the 70s perfecting a sound of immaculate studio jazz-rock, and this album, their sixth, is the ultimate expression of it. Every song is a miniature masterpiece of production, with the pair hiring the finest session musicians in the world and then pushing them through dozens of takes to get each part exactly right, and the record's seven tracks took over a year and cost a fortune to make. The music moves from the Brazilian-tinged title track to the jazz-funk of 'Peg' to the strange, sprawling 'Aja' itself, and the lyrics are full of the pair's trademark wit and misanthropy. It is the definitive document of studio perfectionism, a record that sounds better every time you hear it.

name: Murmur
teaser: 1983 R.E.M.'s debut made college rock a movement with jangling guitars and Michael Stipe's opaque lyrics. 'Radio Free Europe' and 'Talk About the Passions' sounded like nothing else on the radio. The album launched the alternative wave that dominated the next decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the vocals are buried low, adding to the mystery. The band recorded it in five weeks with producer Mitch Easter.

synopsis: R.E.M. had spent the early 80s as the leaders of the American underground, a band from Athens, Georgia, whose jangling guitars and mumbled lyrics made them the darlings of college radio. This debut album, produced by Mitch Easter and Don Dixon, distilled their sound into ten perfect songs, from the propulsive 'Radio Free Europe' to the mysterious 'Perfect Circle', and Michael Stipe's lyrics, delivered in his trademark mumble, were cryptic and beautiful. The record sold slowly but never stopped selling, and its success turned R.E.M. into the most important American band of the decade, the proof that a band could be both underground and beloved. It is the album that made college rock a movement.

name: Ágætis byrjun
teaser: 1999 Sigur Rós made a new language for music: bowed guitar, falsetto vocals, and arrangements that swell like glaciers. 'Svefn-g-englar' and 'Starálfur' are ambient post-rock at its most cinematic. The album made Icelandic music a global genre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the bowed guitar — Jon Birgisson plays it with a cello bow, creating the album's signature drone. The album rewards headphones and patience.

synopsis: Sigur Rós had spent their first album finding their sound, but this, their second, is where they perfected it, and its title, which means 'a good beginning' in Icelandic, is fitting. The record is built on singer Jónsi's extraordinary falsetto, which floats over bowed guitar, horns and strings in a language that is mostly invented, and its songs build from hushed whispers into vast, orchestral crescendos that sound like glaciers calving. The opener, 'Svefn-g-englar', became an underground anthem, and the album's closing masterpiece, 'Viðrar vel til loftárása', is one of the most beautiful pieces of music ever recorded. It made Sigur Rós the most beloved band in the world of atmospheric rock, music that sounds like a dream of Iceland.

name: Electric Ladyland
teaser: 1968 Jimi Hendrix's double album showed his full range: the blues of 'Voodoo Chile', the pop of 'All Along the Watchtower', and the noise symphony of the title track. He played, produced, and overdubbed endlessly, pushing the studio to its limits. It was his only number-one album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar tones — Hendrix's use of feedback and studio effects was unprecedented. His version of 'All Along the Watchtower' was praised by Bob Dylan himself.

tracks.title: Have You Ever Been (To Electric Ladyland)
1983....(A Merman I Should Turn to Be)
Moon, Turn the Tides....Gently Gently Away
1983... (A Merman I Should Turn to Be)

synopsis: Jimi Hendrix had already changed the sound of the electric guitar with his first two albums, but this double album, his third, showed the full range of his genius. The record is a sprawling tour of his talents, from the pure blues of 'Voodoo Chile' to the psychedelic pop of 'Crosstown Traffic' to the fourteen-minute space jam '1983... (A Merman I Should Turn to Be)', and it includes his extraordinary version of Bob Dylan's 'All Along the Watchtower', which Dylan himself called the definitive take. Hendrix played almost everything on the record, layering guitars and singing with a freedom that his band could not always match. It was his last studio album released in his lifetime, and it stands as the fullest statement of his vision.

name: The Downward Spiral
teaser: 1994 Nine Inch Nails' concept album traces a man's self-destruction through industrial noise and pop hooks. 'Closer' and 'Hurt' are among the decade's most provocative songs. Trent Reznor recorded it alone in the house where Sharon Tate was murdered, adding to the album's darkness.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album moves from quiet electronic passages to full-band assaults. Johnny Cash's cover of 'Hurt' was later praised by Reznor as a song no longer his.

synopsis: Nine Inch Nails was essentially one man, Trent Reznor, who wrote, performed and produced everything himself, and this album, his second, is a concept record about self-destruction. The music traces the downfall of a man through industrial rock songs that grow more desperate as they go, from the numb opening to the violence of 'Closer' to the exhausted calm of the closing 'Hurt', which would later be covered by Johnny Cash. Reznor built the album's sound from layers of distorted synthesizers, pounding drums and his own tormented vocals, and its unflinching portrait of addiction and despair made it one of the most influential records of the decade. It is a harrowing listen and a masterpiece of confession.

name: Arular
teaser: 2005 M.I.A.'s debut fused Tamil politics, dancehall, and grime into a sound that felt like the future. 'Galang' and 'Sunshowers' were built from cheap beats and radical ideas. The album made global pop political again.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the density — samples and percussion pile up in every track. The political references reward attention to the lyrics.

synopsis: M.I.A., born Mathangi Arulpragasam, had grown up in Sri Lanka during its civil war before moving to London, and this debut album, named after her father's guerrilla name, is the sound of those two worlds colliding. The record fuses Tamil politics with dancehall, grime and hip-hop into something entirely new, with M.I.A.'s shouted, singsong vocals riding over beats by herself, Diplo and Switch. 'Galang' and 'Sunshowers' became underground anthems, and the album's cover, made from her brother's paintings of Sri Lankan struggle, matched the music's political charge. It is one of the most original debut albums of the decade, the sound of a refugee making music that belonged to no country but spoke to all of them.

name: Hejira
teaser: 1976 Joni Mitchell recorded with jazz bassist Jaco Pastorius and filled the album with travel songs about escape and identity. 'Coyote' and 'Amelia' are the sound of someone driving across America alone. The album is her most jazz-influenced and most haunting.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Pastorius's bass — his melodic lines carry the songs. Mitchell's lyrics here are her most literary.

synopsis: Joni Mitchell had spent the early 70s as the most confessional songwriter in folk, but by the middle of the decade she had grown restless with her own style. This album, her eighth, was recorded with a group of jazz musicians including bassist Jaco Pastorius, whose melodic, singing bass lines became the record's secret weapon, and the music is looser and more mysterious than anything she had made. The songs, mostly written on a cross-country drive, are full of highways, motels and the ache of travel, and her lyrics are among the most literate in popular music. 'Coyote', 'Amelia' and the title track are perfect songs. It is the album where Mitchell left folk behind and became something stranger and greater.

name: A Ghost Is Born
teaser: 2004 Wilco's fifth album moved from alt-country toward noise and improvisation. 'Jesus, Etc.' and 'Hummingbird' balance fragility with feedback. The album's centerpiece 'Spiders (Kidsmoke)' is a 10-minute drone epic. It won a Grammy for best alternative album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jeff Tweedy recorded with guitarist Nels Cline, whose solos cut through the calm. The album's final track fades into silence before returning.

tracks.title: At Least That's What You Said

synopsis: Wilco had spent their first four albums moving from alt-country toward the experimental rock of Yankee Hotel Foxtrot, and this follow-up continued the journey. The record is full of long, searching songs that drift into noise and improvisation, with frontman Jeff Tweedy writing some of his most personal lyrics in the aftermath of his struggles with addiction and depression. The opening 'At Least That's What You Said' builds from a gentle piano ballad into a screaming guitar solo, and the record's title refers to both the noise that haunted Tweedy and the possibility of renewal. It won a Grammy for best alternative album and stands as one of the great records of the decade.

name: Blue Lines
teaser: 1991 Massive Attack's debut invented trip-hop: hip-hop beats slowed down, soul vocals, and dub bass. 'Unfinished Sympathy' and 'Safe from Harm' are cinematic and melancholic. The album defined the Bristol sound that shaped a decade of electronic music.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Unfinished Sympathy' — the orchestral strings were recorded in one take over the beat. The album's mood is the point: dark, smooth, and patient.

tracks.title: Be Thankful for What You've Got

synopsis: Massive Attack had been part of the Bristol music scene that also produced Portishead and Tricky, and this debut album, recorded over several years with a shifting cast of collaborators, invented a whole new genre. The record slows hip-hop beats down to a crawl, layers them with soul samples, dub bass and the voices of a rotating group of singers, and calls it trip-hop, and its centerpiece, 'Unfinished Sympathy', with its soaring string arrangement and Shara Nelson's vocal, became one of the defining singles of the decade. The rest of the album, from the eerie 'Blue Lines' to the menacing 'Safe from Harm', is nearly as strong. It is the sound of a new genre being born.

name: Ys
teaser: 2006 Joanna Newsom's second album told ancient-feeling stories over harp and full orchestral arrangements. 'Emily' and 'Only Skin' are songs that run ten and sixteen minutes. The album's language is archaic and its ambition total — folk music as epic poetry.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lyrics — every line is packed with imagery and wordplay. The orchestration by Van Dyke Parks adds cinematic scale to the harp.

synopsis: Joanna Newsom had made her name with her debut album, a collection of strange, wonderful songs for harp and voice, but this follow-up is a leap into another dimension. The record consists of just five long songs, each one a dense, novelistic epic full of archaic language, fairy tale imagery and musical settings that move from medieval folk to jazz to avant-garde orchestration, and her voice, high and childlike but utterly controlled, tells stories of love, loss and transformation. The centerpiece, 'Only Skin', runs nearly seventeen minutes. It is a demanding, astonishing record that rewards total attention, and it established Newsom as one of the most original composers in popular music.

name: Odelay
teaser: 1996 Beck mixed hip-hop, folk, funk, and noise into a collage of American pop. 'Where It's At' and 'Devils Haircut' were produced by the Dust Brothers with hundreds of samples. The album turned Beck from novelty into one of the decade's most inventive artists.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the album layers obscure records, sound effects, and vocal snippets. 'Where It's At' quotes an instructional record about turntables.

synopsis: Beck had been a cult figure in the early 90s, a one-man collage artist who mixed folk, hip-hop and noise, and this album, his fifth, is where the collage cohered into something brilliant. Produced with the Dust Brothers, the team behind the Beastie Boys' Paul's Boutique, the record is a dizzying tour of American music, sampling and recombining folk, funk, blues and rock into songs like 'Where It's At', 'Devils Haircut' and the ballad 'Jack-Ass'. Beck's deadpan wit and gift for found sound made the album feel like a mixtape from an alternate universe. It won Grammys and turned the oddball from the underground into a star, and its influence is still everywhere.

name: Blonde on Blonde
teaser: 1966 Bob Dylan's double album was recorded in Nashville with studio aces and a harmonica that never stops. 'Visions of Johanna' and 'Sad-Eyed Lady of the Lowlands' are surreal and sprawling. The album is often called the first great double record and the peak of Dylan's electric period.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the Nashville musicians — they play country licks underneath Dylan's electric band. The album rewards attention to the lyrics, which are among his most enigmatic.

tracks.title: One of Us Must Know (Sooner or Later)
Stuck Inside of Mobile with the Memphis Blues Again
Most Likely You Go Your Way and I'll Go Mine
Sad Eyed Lady of the Lowlands

synopsis: Bob Dylan had shocked his folk fans by going electric in 1965, and by the following year he had become the most important songwriter in rock, a position this double album only confirmed. Recorded in Nashville with a crew of studio musicians including Al Kooper and Robbie Robertson, the record is full of his most literate and hilarious songs, from the eleven-minute surrealist epic 'Sad-Eyed Lady of the Lowlands' to the rollicking 'Rainy Day Women #12 & 35' and the bitter masterpiece 'Just Like a Woman'. Dylan's voice, ragged and nasal, was never more expressive, and the record's blend of country, blues and rock defined the sound of the era. It is the summit of his mid-60s genius.

name: Low
teaser: 1977 David Bowie's Berlin trilogy began with this collaboration with Brian Eno: side one is fractured art-rock, side two is ambient instrumentals. 'Sound and Vision' and 'Warszawa' are the sound of isolation made beautiful. The album proved pop stars could go experimental and still matter.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the shift — the first half is song-based, the second half is ambient. 'Warszawa' builds from a single keyboard note into a wordless choir.

tracks.title: Always Crashing in the Same Car
A New Career in a New Town

synopsis: David Bowie had fled Los Angeles, where his drug use and paranoia had spiraled out of control, and moved to Berlin, where he began working with producer Brian Eno and guitarist Robert Fripp on a trilogy of albums that reinvented him. This first of those records is the strangest and most influential, an album of cold, European art rock built on synthesizers, treated drums and Bowie's most detached vocals. 'Sound and Vision', the record's most accessible song, became a hit, but it is the instrumental tracks, full of Fripp's eerie guitar and Eno's ambient textures, that pointed the way forward. It is the sound of an artist rebuilding himself from the rubble, and it influenced everything that came after.

name: The Soft Bulletin
teaser: 1999 The Flaming Lips turned heartbreak and philosophy into psychedelic pop: 'Race for the Prize' and 'Waitin' for a Superman' are songs about scientists and sadness. The album's orchestral arrangements and electronic textures made it a critical breakthrough after a decade of noise.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mix of orchestra and electronics — producer Dave Fridmann layered hundreds of tracks. The album's emotional arc rewards a full listen.

synopsis: The Flaming Lips had spent the 80s and early 90s as one of the strangest bands in American rock, making noisy, confrontational music, but this album, their eighth, found them turning toward beauty. Made in the aftermath of a tragedy, when their longtime guitarist had a breakdown and nearly burned down their studio, the record is full of songs about mortality, love and the small consolations of being alive, wrapped in lush orchestration that sounds like a psychedelic symphony. 'Race for the Prize', 'Waitin' for a Superman' and the devastating 'Feeling Yourself Disintegrate' became instant classics. It is a heartbreaking, uplifting record that made the Lips one of the most beloved bands of their era.

name: The Money Store
teaser: 2012 Death Grips exploded onto the internet with hyper-aggressive rap and industrial noise. 'Hacker' and 'I've Seen Footage' are frantic, confrontational, and unforgettable. The album became a touchstone for a generation that found rap's edges too smooth.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — producer Andy Morin and MC Ride built the album from cheap beats and maximalist samples. The energy is relentless from the first track.

synopsis: Death Grips arrived in 2011 with no warning, releasing an album of hyper-aggressive rap over industrial beats that sounded like a computer having a seizure, and this follow-up, released a year later, cemented their legend. The record is built on the furious rapping of MC Ride, whose screamed, stream-of-consciousness verses are among the most intense in music, and the production, by Zach Hill and Andy Morin, lurches between brutal noise and strange, catchy hooks. Songs like 'I've Seen Footage' and 'The Cage' became underground anthems, and the band's refusal to play by any rules, including the ones of their own label, made them cult heroes. It is the sound of the internet made flesh.

name: Rid of Me
teaser: 1993 PJ Harvey's second album is a howl: distorted guitars, brutal dynamics, and lyrics about desire and control. 'Rid of Me' and '50ft Queenie' are raw and confrontational. Steve Albini's production made it the definitive statement of 1990s rock fury.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album swings between near-silence and full-volume distortion. Albini recorded the band live, capturing the ferocity in the room.

synopsis: PJ Harvey had announced herself with her debut album, but this follow-up, produced by Steve Albini, is where she became a force of nature. The record is a howl, with Harvey's voice, all grit and fury, battling distorted guitars on songs of desire, revenge and rage, and its dynamics are brutal, lurching from near-silence to full assault. The title track, a twisted love song, became her signature, and the album's unflinching intensity made it one of the most talked-about records of the year. It is the sound of a young woman refusing to be anyone's muse, and it established Harvey as the most fearless voice in British rock.

name: Dookie
teaser: 1994 Green Day's major-label debut turned punk into pop radio: 'Basket Case', 'When I Come Around', and 'Longview' are three-minute anthems about boredom and anxiety. The album sold 20 million copies and made 1990s punk mainstream.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the craftsmanship — the songs are tight and hooky despite the punk attitude. 'Longview' was written while bassist Mike Dirnt was high, which explains its weird structure.

synopsis: Green Day had spent years as the biggest band in the Bay Area punk scene, and this album, their major label debut, was their attempt to bring punk to the mainstream. Recorded in three weeks with producer Rob Cavallo, the record is a burst of three-minute songs full of teenage frustration, humor and irresistible melodies, and its singles, 'Basket Case', 'When I Come Around' and 'Longview', became anthems for a generation. The album sold over ten million copies and turned punk from an underground movement into the sound of pop radio, opening the door for the entire pop punk explosion of the mid-90s. It is one of the most influential albums of the decade, the sound of a revolution made fun.

name: Blood Sugar Sex Magik
teaser: 1991 Red Hot Chili Peppers fused funk, punk, and melody into their breakthrough: 'Under the Bridge', 'Give It Away', and 'Breaking the Girl' made them rock stars. The band recorded in a haunted mansion with producer Rick Rubin. The album defined alternative rock's funk side.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk bass — Flea's playing drives the album. 'Under the Bridge' was written about singer Anthony Kiedis's loneliness and addiction, a quiet center in a loud record.

synopsis: Red Hot Chili Peppers had spent a decade as one of the wildest bands in funk rock, but tragedy and turmoil had nearly ended them, and this album, their fifth, was a last chance. Recorded in a rented mansion in Laurel Canyon with producer Rick Rubin, the band stripped down and focused, and the result was their masterpiece: a record that fused funk, punk and melody into something entirely their own. 'Under the Bridge', a lonely ballad about frontman Anthony Kiedis's struggles with addiction, became their biggest hit, and 'Give It Away' and 'Suck My Kiss' showed the funk side. The album sold over ten million copies and made the Chili Peppers one of the biggest bands in the world.

name: The Idler Wheel...
teaser: 2012 Fiona Apple's fourth album pairs her confessional piano with percussive rhythms and scat-like vocals. 'Every Single Night' and 'Werewolf' are raw and restless. Apple recorded it with producer Charley Drayton, playing drums herself. The album earned her a Grammy nomination and her reputation as a singular artist.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the percussion — Apple and Drayton play kitchen utensils and drums together. Her voice cracks and strains in ways that make the emotion visceral.

synopsis: Fiona Apple had been a star since she was a teenager, but she had spent years fighting with her label and struggling with her own demons, and this album, her fourth, was made after a long silence. The record is a stunning return, pairing her confessional piano playing with percussive, jazzy arrangements and some of the most extraordinary lyrics of her career, full of fury, tenderness and hard-won wisdom. 'Every Single Night', the lead single, is a surreal pop gem, and the album's full title, which runs over a hundred words, is a poem in itself. It was hailed as her best work, a record made entirely on her own terms by an artist who had earned every note.

name: The Velvet Underground
teaser: 1969 Lou Reed stopped the noise and wrote songs: 'Sweet Jane', 'Pale Blue Eyes', and 'Candy Says' are gentle, literate, and heartbreaking. The album is the calm after the storm of their debut. It quietly influenced every songwriter who heard it.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the band plays softly and the songs breathe. 'Sweet Jane' opens with a riff that punk bands would steal for decades.

synopsis: The Velvet Underground had spent their first two albums making some of the most confrontational music ever recorded, but by their third album, Lou Reed had decided to show his tender side. The record is full of the simple, beautiful songs he had been writing for years, from the streetwise romance of 'Sweet Jane' to the gorgeous 'Pale Blue Eyes' to the country-tinged 'Jesus', and the band, now including the bassist Doug Yule, plays with a warmth that their earlier records never allowed. It sold almost nothing on release, but its influence has been incalculable, with its blend of literary lyrics and simple rock and roll shaping everything from glam to punk to indie. It is the Velvet Underground's most human record.

name: The Stooges
teaser: 1969 The Stooges' debut invented punk a decade early: 'I Wanna Be Your Dog', '1969', and 'No Fun' are raw, minimal, and furious. Iggy Pop writhed and screamed while the band bashed out two chords. The album sold almost nothing at the time; it became the blueprint for punk.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rawness — the album was recorded in two days with producer John Cale. Iggy's lyrics are simple, repeated mantras that hit like punches.

synopsis: The Stooges had been formed in Ann Arbor, Michigan, by Iggy Pop, a frontman who seemed to have crawled out of a different species, and this debut album invented punk rock a decade before anyone had a name for it. Recorded with John Cale, fresh from the Velvet Underground, the record is built on the simplest possible riffs, played with a menace that made them sound like weapons, and Iggy's vocals, part howl and part taunt, are the sound of a man losing control in the best way. 'I Wanna Be Your Dog' and 'No Fun' became the template for everything that followed. It sold almost nothing at the time, but it is now recognized as one of the most influential records ever made.

name: The Suburbs
teaser: 2010 Arcade Fire's third album about growing up in the sprawl won Album of the Year: 'The Suburbs', 'Ready to Start', and 'Sprawl II' are anthems about memory and place. The band's chamber-rock arrangements made them the biggest indie band of their era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album follows the arc of childhood to adulthood across its sixteen tracks. 'Sprawl II' is a disco song about losing the suburbs.

synopsis: Arcade Fire had become the most beloved band in indie rock with their first two albums, but this third record found them turning their attention to the places where they grew up. The album is about the suburbs, the sprawling American communities that singer Win Butler called home, and its songs are full of the boredom, beauty and longing of that landscape, from the anthemic 'The Suburbs' to the elegiac 'Sprawl II (Mountains Beyond Mountains)'. The record won the Grammy for Album of the Year, a shock for such an ambitious, melancholy work, and its portrait of growing up in a world of identical houses and endless roads made it a generational touchstone. It is the sound of home, in all its comfort and confinement.

name: The Bends
teaser: 1995 Radiohead's second album stripped away the grunge of their debut for a more textured sound: 'High and Dry', 'Fake Plastic Trees', and 'Street Spirit' are brooding and beautiful. The album was recorded in four different studios with four producers. It made them critics' darlings.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — from the grunge of 'The Bends' to the quiet 'Fake Plastic Trees'. The album set the stage for OK Computer's experiments.

tracks.title: Bullet Proof... I Wish I Was

synopsis: Radiohead had become the biggest band in the world with their breakthrough album OK Computer, and the pressure of following it nearly broke them. This follow-up, made with producer John Leckie and recorded in a rented mansion, found them stripping away the electronic experiments of their later work for a more human sound, and the result was their most accessible record since their debut. The album is full of the anxious, beautiful rock songs they had perfected, from the soaring 'High and Dry' to the desperate 'Fake Plastic Trees' to the epic closer 'Street Spirit (Fade Out)', and Thom Yorke's voice, aching and precise, had never sounded better. It made them stars in America and set the stage for the reinvention of Kid A.

name: The Velvet Rope
teaser: 1997 Janet Jackson's sixth album is her most personal: 'Together Again', 'Got 'Til It's Done', and 'I Get Lonely' explore grief, sexuality, and healing. The album sold 10 million copies and influenced a generation of R&B stars. It remains her most introspective work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis built the album's smooth, dark sound. The spoken interludes frame the album as a journey of self-discovery.

synopsis: Janet Jackson had spent the early 90s as the biggest pop star in the world, but behind the success she was struggling with depression and the fallout of a controlling marriage, and this album, her sixth, is the first time she let that show. The record is her most personal, full of songs about love, pain, sexuality and self-acceptance, from the elegy 'Together Again', written for a friend who died of AIDS, to the explicit 'Rope Burn' and the anthemic 'Got Till It's Gone'. It is also her most adventurous musically, with production that draws on trip-hop, funk and world music. It was hailed as her masterpiece, a record that turned her private struggles into public art.

name: Post
teaser: 1995 Björk's second album is a collage of house beats, trip-hop, and orchestral pop: 'Army of Me', 'Hyperballad', and 'It's Oh So Quiet' are playful and ferocious. The album made her an international star and defined 1990s art-pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the genre jumps — from the industrial beat of 'Army of Me' to the big-band cover 'It's Oh So Quiet'. The production by Tricky and Howie B adds grit.

synopsis: Björk had spent her first solo album establishing herself as the strangest star in pop, and this follow-up is where she became a force of nature. The record is a collage of house beats, trip-hop, strings and her own extraordinary voice, which can leap from a whisper to a scream in a heartbeat, and its songs are about the aftermath of a breakup, full of fury, tenderness and surreal imagery. 'Army of Me' became an anthem of defiance, and 'It's Oh So Quiet', a cover of a 50s jazz song, showed her playful side. The album made her a global star and remains the purest statement of her vision: pop music as avant-garde art.

name: Woodstock: Music from the Original Soundtrack
teaser: 1970 The Woodstock soundtrack captured the defining festival of the 1960s: Jimi Hendrix's 'The Star-Spangled Banner', Joe Cocker's 'With a Little Help from My Friends', and performances by Santana, Sly and the Family Stone, and The Who. The triple album is a time capsule of the counterculture at its peak.

exploreAction.targetName: Woodstock: Music from the Original Soundtrack (1970) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Hendrix's national anthem — the feedback and distortion turned the song into a protest. The live recordings capture the festival's chaos and communion.

synopsis: The Woodstock festival in August 1969 was supposed to be a small concert for a few thousand people, but half a million showed up, and the three days of music became the defining moment of the 1960s counterculture. This double album, the first of several soundtrack releases, captured the festival's greatest performances, from Jimi Hendrix's shattering version of 'The Star-Spangled Banner' to Sly and the Family Stone's ecstatic set and Joe Cocker's howling 'With a Little Help from My Friends'. The record was a massive seller and brought the festival's music, and its ideals, to millions who had not been there. It is a document of a moment when a generation believed it could change the world.

name: Low End Theory
teaser: 1991 A Tribe Called Quest made jazz the backbone of hip-hop: upright bass, laid-back drums, and Q-Tip and Phife Dawg's traded verses. 'Scenario' and 'Check the Rhime' defined the Native Tongues sound. The album proved hip-hop could be both intellectual and funky.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to how the basslines carry every track — jazz bassist Ron Carter played on 'Verses from the Abstract'. The chemistry between Q-Tip and Phife is the album's engine.

synopsis: A Tribe Called Quest had made their debut with a record full of playful, positive rhymes, and this follow-up, their second, found them deepening their sound. The album is built on jazz, with producer Q-Tip constructing beats from upright bass lines, vibraphones and horn samples, and his raps, along with those of Phife Dawg, are more socially conscious than before. 'Check the Rhime' and 'Jazz (We've Got)' became anthems, and the album's centerpiece, 'Scenario', with its legendary posse cut finale, is one of the greatest moments in hip-hop history. It is the album that made jazz the backbone of hip-hop, and its influence on the next decade of rap is immeasurable.

name: Astral Weeks
teaser: 1968 Van Morrison's second album is a suite of stream-of-consciousness songs: 'Madame George', 'Cyprus Avenue', and the title track are jazz-folk meditations on Belfast and memory. Recorded in two sessions with jazz musicians, the album has no chord changes to speak of — just modal grooves. It is the most spiritual rock album of its era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the flow — the songs drift like memories, with bass and guitar circling the same themes. 'Madame George' builds to a climax of pure emotion.

synopsis: Van Morrison had been a star in his native Belfast as the singer of Them, but by 1968 he was a struggling solo artist living in Boston, and his label was ready to drop him. This album, his second, was recorded in two days with a group of jazz musicians, and it is unlike anything else in rock: a suite of stream-of-consciousness songs, full of mystical imagery and a searching, keening vocal performance, that sound like they were improvised in a single breath. 'Madame George' and 'Cyprus Avenue' are among the most beautiful songs ever written, and the record's title song, 'Astral Weeks', is a prayer for escape. It sold almost nothing on release, but it is now recognized as one of the greatest albums ever made.

name: Speaking in Tongues
teaser: 1983 Talking Heads' fifth album is their funkiest: 'Burning Down the House' and 'This Must Be the Place' are built on locked grooves and singable hooks. The tour was filmed for the concert movie Stop Making Sense. The album proved new wave could be a party.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rhythm section — bassist Tina Weymouth and drummer Chris Frantz lock into grooves that make the songs irresistible. The album rewards dancing as much as listening.

tracks.title: This Must Be the Place (Naive Melody)

synopsis: Talking Heads had spent their first four albums moving from art punk toward something more rhythmic, and this fifth record, their first with the enlarged lineup that included Bernie Worrell and other funk players, completed the transformation. The album is their funkiest, full of interlocking grooves that frontman David Byrne's nervy, ecstatic vocals float over, and its centerpiece, 'Burning Down the House', became their biggest hit. The record also includes the gorgeous ballad 'This Must Be the Place (Naive Melody)', a love song built on a simple, hypnotic guitar pattern. It is the sound of a band that had stopped being a rock group and become a rhythm machine.

name: The White Album
teaser: 1968 The Beatles' double album is a sprawling document of a band pulling apart: 'Back in the U.S.S.R.', 'While My Guitar Gently Weeps', and 'Helter Skelter' show four solo careers in one record. The band recorded 30 songs in five months. The album is messy, brilliant, and endless.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — from the music-hall 'Honey Pie' to the metal of 'Helter Skelter'. Each member contributed songs written alone, making it a compilation of four voices.

tracks.title: The Continuing Story of Bungalow Bill
Why Don't We Do It in the Road?
Everybody's Got Something to Hide Except Me and My Monkey

synopsis: The Beatles recorded this double album in 1968, during the most turbulent year of their career, and it is a sprawling document of a band pulling apart. The record's thirty songs range from the white-hot rock of 'Back in the U.S.S.R.' and 'Helter Skelter' to the tenderness of 'Blackbird' and 'Julia' to the strange experiments of 'Revolution 9', and they were mostly recorded separately, with each Beatle bringing in his own songs and the others drifting in and out of the sessions. Ringo Starr briefly quit the band during the making of it. It is messy, inconsistent and endlessly fascinating, the sound of four geniuses who had stopped being a band and become a collection of solo artists sharing a name.

name: The Great Twenty-Eight
teaser: 1982 Sun Records' compilation of Chuck Berry's first hits — 'Johnny B. Goode', 'Roll Over Beethoven', and 'Maybellene' — is the founding document of rock and roll. The songs are built on Berry's guitar riff and storytelling lyrics. Every rock band since has learned from them.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — Berry's signature riff opens nearly every song. The lyrics tell stories of cars, school, and teenage life with wit and rhythm.

tracks.title: I Want to Be Your Driver

synopsis: Chuck Berry had been the poet laureate of rock and roll since the mid-50s, the guitarist and songwriter whose songs about cars, girls and school defined the music's language, and this compilation, released by Chess Records in 1982, gathers the essential documents of his genius. 'Johnny B. Goode', 'Roll Over Beethoven', 'Maybellene', 'Sweet Little Sixteen' and the rest of the twenty-eight tracks here are the bedrock of rock music, songs that every guitarist since has had to learn. Berry's guitar playing, with its double stops and ringing clarity, and his lyrics, full of wit and teenage longing, created the template for everything that followed. It is the most important rock and roll compilation ever released.

name: Piano Man
teaser: 1973 Billy Joel's breakthrough album introduced his storytelling: 'Piano Man', 'Captain Jack', and 'The Entertainer' are songs about bars, dreams, and the music business. The title track is based on his own time playing piano in a Los Angeles bar. The album made him a star and defined his sound.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lyrics — 'Piano Man' paints a bar full of characters, each with a verse. The accordion and harmonica give the album its saloon feel.

tracks.title: The Ballad of Billy the Kid
If I Only Had the Words (To Tell You)

synopsis: Billy Joel had spent years as a struggling songwriter and piano bar player, a story he told in his breakthrough single 'Piano Man', and this album, his second, was built around that song's success. The record is full of the storytelling that would define his career, from the title track's portrait of the regulars in a bar to 'New York State of Mind', a love letter to his hometown that became a standard, and it shows a songwriter finding his voice. The album was a slow burner that eventually went platinum, and it established Joel as one of the most commercially successful singer-songwriters of the decade. It is the record where the Piano Man found his audience.

name: The Wall
teaser: 1979 Pink Floyd's rock opera about isolation and madness: 'Another Brick in the Wall', 'Comfortably Numb', and 'Run Like Hell' tell the story of a rock star building a wall around himself. The album spent 15 weeks at number one and sold 30 million copies. It is the most theatrical album in rock history.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album is a continuous story with recurring themes. 'Comfortably Numb' features one of the greatest guitar solos ever recorded.

tracks.title: Another Brick in the Wall, Part 1
The Happiest Days of Our Lives
Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2
Another Brick in the Wall, Part 3

synopsis: Pink Floyd had spent the late 70s becoming the biggest band in the world, but their leader Roger Waters was consumed by the alienation of fame, and he channeled that obsession into this, their most ambitious work. The Wall is a rock opera about a rock star named Pink who builds a wall around himself to keep the world out, and its double album traces his breakdown, from the childhood trauma of 'Another Brick in the Wall' to the fascist fantasy of 'In the Flesh' to the final, ambiguous collapse of 'The Trial'. It was a massive hit, spawned one of the most famous music videos ever made, and was turned into a film. It is a harrowing, brilliant and deeply personal record, the sound of a man building his own prison.

name: 3 Feet High and Rising
teaser: 1989 De La Soul's debut rebelled against rap's hardcore image with playful, eclectic sampling: 'Me Myself and I', 'The Magic Number', and 'Eye Know' sample everything from Steely Dan to schoolhouse records. The album's 'D.A.I.S.Y. Age' vibe made hip-hop whimsical for the first time. It remains a landmark of the Native Tongues movement.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the album was the first to use the phrase 'sampling' in its credits. The skits between songs frame it as a game show.

tracks.title: This Is a Recording 4 Living in a Fulltime Era (L.I.F.E.)

synopsis: De La Soul had arrived in 1989 with a debut album that rebelled against rap's hardcore image, and its title, a reference to a song by the 1910 Fruitgum Company, set the tone for its playful, psychedelic worldview. The record is built on dense layers of samples from old soul and funk records, and its rhymes, delivered by Posdnuos, Dave and Maseo, are full of wordplay, humor and a gentle, humanist politics. 'Me Myself and I' became a hit, and the album's famous skits, in which the group appears on a game show, were unlike anything in hip-hop. It is the founding document of alternative rap, a record that proved hip-hop could be weird, warm and wonderful.

name: Paul's Boutique
teaser: 1989 The Beastie Boys' second album is a dense collage of hundreds of samples — from Beatles to public-domain recordings. 'Hey Ladies' and 'Shake Your Rump' are endlessly layered. The album flopped at release but became the template for sample-based hip-hop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the Dust Brothers built the album from obscure records and sound effects. Each listen reveals new layers.

tracks.title: Looking Down the Barrel of a Gun

synopsis: The Beastie Boys had been dismissed as a joke after their debut album, a frat boy rap record that the group themselves came to hate, and this follow-up, made after they fled to Los Angeles and studied with the producers the Dust Brothers, was their revenge. The record is a dense collage of hundreds of samples, stitched together into a seamless flow of beats and rhymes, and its lyrics, delivered by all three members with a new wit and confidence, are full of pop culture references and self-deprecating humor. It sold slowly at first, but its reputation has grown into legend, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest hip-hop records ever made, a masterpiece of sample-based production.

name: DAMN.
teaser: 2017 Kendrick Lamar's fourth album is a meditation on faith, sin, and fame: 'HUMBLE.', 'DNA.', and 'LOVE.' alternate between boasts and confessions. The album won the Pulitzer Prize for music — the first rap album to do so — and became the most-streamed rap album of its year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the sequencing — the album is designed to be played both forward and backward, with each track leading into the next. The production by Mike WiLL Made-It and others is sharp and minimal.

synopsis: Kendrick Lamar had spent his career as the most acclaimed rapper of his generation, and this album, his fourth, found him turning inward. The record is a meditation on faith, sin and fame, structured as a series of confrontations between Lamar and his own doubts, and its songs move from the fury of 'DNA.' to the tenderness of 'LOVE.' to the shocking violence of 'ELEMENT.'. The album debuted at number one and won the Pulitzer Prize for music, the first time the award had gone to a hip-hop record, and its themes of grace and guilt made it his most personal work. It is the sound of the greatest rapper alive wrestling with his own soul.

name: Hunky Dory
teaser: 1971 David Bowie's fourth album is a songbook of characters and styles: 'Changes', 'Life on Mars?', and 'Oh! You Pretty Things' are glam-folk songs about change and identity. The album came a year before Ziggy Stardust and paved its way. It is Bowie at his most melodic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — Rick Wakeman plays on the album, adding a music-hall grandeur. 'Life on Mars?' was inspired by a Frank Sinatra song's failure.

synopsis: David Bowie had spent the late 60s as a struggling singer-songwriter, and this album, his fourth, was his attempt to break through by any means necessary. The result is a songbook of characters and styles, from the glam rock of 'Changes' and 'Life on Mars?' to the folk of 'Quicksand' and the vaudeville of 'Fill Your Heart', all sung by a singer who seemed to have invented a dozen personas overnight. The record also contains 'Oh! You Pretty Things' and the apocalyptic 'The Bewlay Brothers', and its title, which means 'the right course' in Japanese, captured its sense of a man finding his path. It is the album where Bowie became Bowie, and it set the stage for the stardom of Ziggy Stardust.

name: Jagged Little Pill
teaser: 1995 Alanis Morissette's third album sold 33 million copies and made angry female voices mainstream: 'You Oughta Know', 'Ironic', and 'Hand in My Pocket' are raw and cathartic. The album won five Grammys including Album of the Year. It defined 1990s confessional pop-rock.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album swings from whispered verses to full-throated choruses. 'You Oughta Know' was reportedly about a famous ex, adding to its edge.

tracks.title: You Oughta Know (Jimmy the Saint Blend) / Your House (a cappella)

synopsis: Alanis Morissette had spent her teenage years as a Canadian pop star, making records she later disowned, before she moved to Los Angeles and began writing with the producer Glen Ballard. This album, her third, recorded when she was 21, is the sound of all that frustration being released, and its raw, confessional songs about love, betrayal and anger struck a nerve around the world. 'You Oughta Know', with its furious opening, became an anthem, and the album sold over 30 million copies, making it one of the best-selling records of all time. It made angry young women a commercial force in music and turned Morissette into the voice of a generation that had been waiting to be heard.

name: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not
teaser: 2006 Arctic Monkeys' debut was recorded after the band became famous through leaked demos on the internet: 'I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor', 'Fake Tales of San Francisco', and 'Mardy Bum' are sharp and funny. The album sold 360,000 copies in its first week, a UK record. It is the fastest-selling debut in British history.

exploreAction.targetName: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not (2006) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lyrics — Alex Turner writes about nights out with wry detail. The album's punk-funk sound was recorded live in the studio.

tracks.title: I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor
You Probably Couldn't See for the Lights but You Were Staring Straight at Me
Red Light Indicates Doors Are Secured
Perhaps Vampires Is a Bit Strong But...
From the Ritz to the Rubble

synopsis: Arctic Monkeys had become the biggest band in Britain through word of mouth alone, giving away demo tapes at their shows in Sheffield and building a following on the internet before they had even released a record. This debut album, recorded in a matter of days, captures that moment, and its songs, written by the teenage Alex Turner, are full of sharp observations about nightlife, love and the boredom of northern England. 'I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor' and 'When the Sun Goes Down' became instant classics, and the album sold faster than any debut in British history. It is the sound of a generation finding its voice, delivered with wit, fury and immaculate style.

name: Achtung Baby
teaser: 1991 U2 reinvented themselves with industrial rhythms and ironic imagery: 'One', 'Mysterious Ways', and 'The Fly' are their most adventurous songs. The band recorded in Berlin's Hansa Studios, where Bowie made Low. The album sold 18 million copies and rescued the band from self-parody.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the textures — the Edge's guitar effects and the band's new electronic instruments. 'One' was written when the band nearly broke up; its lyrics are about reconciliation.

tracks.title: Even Better Than the Real Thing
Until the End of the World
Who's Gonna Ride Your Wild Horses
Tryin' to Throw Your Arms Around the World

synopsis: U2 had spent the 80s becoming the biggest band in the world, but by the end of the decade they were exhausted, stuck in a formula and on the verge of breaking up. This album, their seventh, recorded in Berlin as the Wall was coming down, was their reinvention, and it saved them. Working with producers Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois, the band stripped away their anthemic sound and rebuilt it around industrial rhythms, ironic imagery and new sonic textures, and the result was their best record. 'One' became one of the greatest songs of the decade, and 'Mysterious Ways' and 'The Fly' showed the new U2. It is the sound of a band that had everything to lose and risked it all.

name: The Nightfly
teaser: 1982 Donald Fagen's solo debut after Steely Dan is a concept album about growing up in the 1950s: 'I.G.Y.', 'New Frontier', and 'Maxine' are meticulous, warm, and literate. The album's production is among the best ever recorded. It remains a favorite of audiophiles.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded digitally with the finest musicians and equipment of the era. Every detail rewards headphones.

synopsis: Donald Fagen had spent the 70s as the co-leader of Steely Dan, the most meticulous band in rock, and after they split he spent years on this solo debut, a concept album about growing up in the late 50s and early 60s. The record is full of the sounds of that era, from the doo wop of 'Ruby Baby' to the cool jazz of the title track, all rendered with Fagen's trademark studio perfection, and its songs are narrated by a young man dreaming of escape from suburban New Jersey. The album's production, full of pristine detail, made it a favorite of audiophiles, and its nostalgic, wistful mood has only deepened with time. It is a perfect record, made by a perfectionist at the height of his powers.

name: Amnesiac
teaser: 2001 Radiohead recorded Amnesiac in the same sessions as Kid A, but the songs are more song-like: 'Pyramid Song', 'You and Whose Army?', and 'Knives Out' are jazz, blues, and folk refracted through the band's anxiety. The album rewards the patient listener.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — 'Pyramid Song' is built on a haunting figure inspired by jazz and classical music. The album's moods shift constantly.

tracks.title: Packt Like Sardines in a Crushd Tin Box

synopsis: Radiohead recorded enough music in their 1999 sessions to fill two albums, and if Kid A was the experimental half, this companion record is the more song-based half, though 'song-based' is relative. The album opens with the eerie 'Packt Like Sardines in a Crushd Tin Box' and moves through the jazzy 'Pyramid Song', the claustrophobic 'Knives Out' and the devastating 'How to Disappear Completely', one of the most beautiful songs in their catalog. Thom Yorke's lyrics are full of paranoia and dislocation, and the music, built on odd time signatures and electronic textures, is unsettling and gorgeous in equal measure. It is the quieter, stranger sibling of Kid A, and in some ways the better record.

name: White Blood Cells
teaser: 2001 The White Stripes' third album stripped rock to drums, guitar, and a singer: 'Fell in Love with a Girl', 'Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground', and 'Hotel Yorba' are raw and catchy. Recorded in four days, the album made the duo stars and kickstarted the garage rock revival.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the minimalism — Meg White's drumming and Jack White's guitar carry everything. The album's brevity and power made it a template for 2000s rock.

tracks.title: Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground
I'm Finding It Harder to Be a Gentleman
Fell in Love with a Girl
The Same Boy You've Always Known
I Think I Smell a Rat

synopsis: The White Stripes had spent their first two albums establishing a sound built on the simplest possible materials, and this third record stripped it down even further. Jack White's guitar, Meg White's drums and the two of them trading vocals, with no bass and no other instruments, was the whole formula, and on this album it reached its peak. 'Fell in Love with a Girl', a two-minute blast of garage rock, became an unlikely hit, and 'Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground' and 'Hotel Yorba' showed the band's range. The record made the duo the most important band in the garage rock revival, and its raw, immediate sound influenced everything that came after. It is rock and roll reduced to its essentials.

name: Life After Death
teaser: 1997 The Notorious B.I.G.'s double album was released two weeks after his murder: 'Hypnotize', 'Mo Money Mo Problems', and 'Sky's the Limit' are confident, funny, and dark. The album topped the charts for a month and sold 10 million copies. It is the definitive East Coast rap record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the flow — Biggie's delivery is unhurried and precise. The album's skits and interludes frame it as a movie.

tracks.title: I Got a Story to Tell

synopsis: The Notorious B.I.G. had become the biggest rapper in the world with his debut album, and this double album, his second, was the most anticipated record in hip-hop history, arriving two weeks after he was murdered in Los Angeles in March 1997. The record is a sprawling monument to his genius, full of the storytelling, humor and effortless flow that made him the greatest rapper of his era, from the menacing 'Hypnotize' to the elegiac 'I'll Be Missing You' to the epic 'Notorious Thugz'. It sold over ten million copies and debuted at number one, and its posthumous triumph only deepened the tragedy of his loss. It is the sound of a giant at his peak, silenced just as he reached it.

name: The Blueprint 3
teaser: 2009 Jay-Z's eleventh album returned him to the top of rap: 'Empire State of Mind', 'Run This Town', and 'On to the Next One' are anthems of success. Alicia Keys sang the chorus of the lead single, which became his first number-one in a decade. The album proved the veteran could still dominate.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Kanye West and Timbaland contribute beats. 'Empire State of Mind' is the album's triumphant centerpiece.

synopsis: Jay-Z had spent the late 2000s as rap's elder statesman, a businessman and mogul who seemed to have lost the hunger that made him great, and this album, his eleventh, was his answer to the doubters. The record is a return to form, full of the slick, confident rapping that made him a star, and its centerpiece, 'Empire State of Mind', a duet with Alicia Keys that became an anthem for New York, was his biggest hit in years. The album also features the Kanye West productions 'Run This Town' and 'On to the Next One', and it won three Grammys. It is the sound of a legend reminding everyone why he was a legend.

name: Wonderwall
teaser: 1995 Oasis's second album (What's the Story) Morning Glory? made them the biggest band in Britain: 'Wonderwall', 'Don't Look Back in Anger', and 'Champagne Supernova' are singalong anthems. The album sold 22 million copies and defined Britpop. It also contains the most famous feud in rock: the Gallagher brothers.
