exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the choruses — every song builds to a singalong moment. 'Wonderwall' was written by Noel Gallagher about his then-girlfriend.

tracks.title: I Am the Walrus (Live Glasgow Cathouse June 1994)

synopsis: Oasis had spent 1994 conquering Britain with their debut album, but this follow-up, recorded in a blur of drugs, fights and inspiration, made them the biggest band in the world. The album's centerpiece is the immortal 'Wonderwall', a song so ubiquitous it became a noun, and it is surrounded by 'Don't Look Back in Anger', 'Champagne Supernova' and 'Some Might Say', an unbroken run of anthems that made the Gallagher brothers the most famous siblings in rock. The record sold over 20 million copies and turned Britpop into a global phenomenon, and its blend of Beatlesque melodies and punk attitude defined the sound of the mid-90s. It is one of the greatest rock albums of the decade.

name: Voodoo People
teaser: 1994 The Prodigy's second album, Music for the Jilted Generation, fused rave, punk, and breakbeat: 'Voodoo People', 'No Good (Start the Dance)', and 'One Love' are aggressive and euphoric. The album sold 2 million copies and made rave music mainstream.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the beats — the album mixes breakbeats, hardcore rave, and punk guitars. The energy never lets up.

synopsis: The Prodigy had spent their early years as the wild men of the rave scene, and this album, their second, was the record that fused the dance floor and the mosh pit into a single, explosive sound. The record's title, a reference to the generation that had grown up in the shadow of the poll tax and the criminal justice bill, captured its fury, and its tracks, from the pounding 'Voodoo People' to the breakbeat assault of 'Their Law', were built to destroy clubs. The album made The Prodigy the biggest electronic act in the world and turned rave culture from a dance floor movement into a rock and roll force. It is the sound of a revolution, captured at full volume.

name: Axis: Bold as Love
teaser: 1967 Jimi Hendrix's second album is the psychedelic peak of his craft: 'Little Wing', 'Spanish Castle Magic', and 'If 6 Was 9' are built on his most inventive guitar playing. The title track's stereo panning was a studio landmark. The album is a bridge from the debut to his masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — 'Little Wing' is a masterclass in chord melody. The album's mix was recreated from mono tapes after the stereo master was lost.

synopsis: Jimi Hendrix had spent his debut album establishing himself as the most exciting guitarist in rock, and this follow-up, recorded in a rush to capitalize on his success, found him perfecting his art. The record's centerpiece is 'Little Wing', a delicate, impossibly beautiful song that became a standard, and it also includes the psychedelic 'Spanish Castle Magic', the blues of 'If 6 Was 9' and the fiery 'Bold as Love'. Hendrix's playing is more assured and more inventive than on his debut, full of the whammy bar acrobatics and studio tricks that made him a legend, and his songwriting had grown to match his guitar. It is the psychedelic peak of his craft.

name: Let It Bleed
teaser: 1969 The Rolling Stones' response to Altamont and the end of the sixties: 'Gimme Shelter', 'You Can't Always Get What You Want', and the title track are dark, loose, and prophetic. Brian Jones's last session appears on two tracks. The album closes the sixties with a shrug.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dread in 'Gimme Shelter' — Merry Clayton's wailing vocal was recorded in one take and nearly destroyed her voice. The album rewards loud speakers.

tracks.title: You Can't Always Get What You Want

synopsis: The Rolling Stones had spent the 60s as the bad boys of rock, but this album, their eighth, was recorded in the shadow of the decade's violent end, including the Altamont festival where a fan was killed by Hell's Angels during their set. The record's songs are full of that darkness, from the apocalyptic 'Gimme Shelter' to the murder ballad 'Midnight Rambler' to the weary 'You Can't Always Get What You Want', and they are some of the greatest songs the band ever wrote. It also contains the country classic 'Country Honk' and the raucous 'Live with Me'. It is the sound of the sixties dying, and the Stones were the band that lived to tell the tale.

name: Physical Graffiti
teaser: 1975 Led Zeppelin's double album is their most eclectic: 'Kashmir', 'Trampled Under Foot', and 'In My Time of Dying' move from heavy rock to funk to blues. The band recorded it over two years with leftover sessions. The album is the peak of their ambition.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Kashmir' — the orchestra and guitar create a sound unlike anything else in their catalog. The album rewards a full, loud listen.

synopsis: Led Zeppelin had spent the early 70s as the biggest band in the world, and this double album, their sixth, was recorded in a house they rented in London, with the band free to experiment in a way their studio schedule had never allowed. The result is their most eclectic record, ranging from the Eastern-tinged epic 'Kashmir', one of the greatest songs in rock history, to the acoustic folk of 'The Rover' to the funk of 'Trampled Under Foot' and the country of 'Down by the Seaside'. The record also includes the legendary 'In My Time of Dying' and 'Ten Years Gone'. It is the sound of a band at the absolute height of its powers, with nothing left to prove and everything to play for.

name: Loaded
teaser: 1970 The Velvet Underground's fourth album, named to satisfy a commercial push, is their most accessible: 'Sweet Jane', 'Rock & Roll', and 'Who Loves the Sun' are pop songs with an edge. Lou Reed wrote them to be hits; they became the band's most covered songs.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the pop craft — 'Sweet Jane' has the band's most singable riff. The album proves the Velvets could write hooks when they wanted.

synopsis: The Velvet Underground had spent their first three albums making the most influential music of the 60s, but they had never sold a record, and this fourth album was a last attempt to reach a commercial audience. Its title was chosen to please their label, and its sound was deliberately more accessible, full of the pop songs that Lou Reed had been writing for years, from the gorgeous 'Sweet Jane' to the elegiac 'Rock and Roll' to the country-tinged 'I'm Sticking with You'. The album was produced to sound polished, and the band, now led by Reed and Doug Yule, plays with a warmth that their earlier records lacked. It sold better than anything they had made, but it was still a commercial failure, and the band broke up shortly after.

name: Transformer
teaser: 1972 Lou Reed's second solo album, produced by David Bowie and Mick Ronson, turned his street poetry into glam rock: 'Walk on the Wild Side', 'Perfect Day', and 'Satellite of Love' are literate and catchy. The album made Reed a star without softening him.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Ronson's arrangements — the strings and piano give the album its elegance. 'Walk on the Wild Side' became his signature due to its bassline and chorus.

synopsis: Lou Reed had spent his first solo album making dense, difficult music, but for this follow-up he turned to David Bowie and guitarist Mick Ronson, who produced and arranged a set of his most accessible songs. The result is a record that balances Reed's streetwise poetry with glam rock's theatricality, from the immortal 'Walk on the Wild Side', with its bassline and salacious tales of Warhol's New York, to the tender 'Perfect Day' and the rocking 'Vicious'. Ronson's arrangements, full of strings and piano, gave the songs a warmth that Reed's earlier work lacked, and the album made him a star. It is the most beloved record in his catalog, and one of the greatest albums of the 70s.

name: Berlin
teaser: 1973 Lou Reed's third solo album is a harrowing concept record about addiction and abuse: 'Caroline Says', 'The Bed', and 'Oh, Jim' are brutal and beautiful. Producer Bob Ezrin built a cinematic wall of sound. The album flopped at release; it is now regarded as Reed's most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album tells a continuous story from start to finish. The orchestral arrangements contrast with the bleakness of the lyrics.

tracks.title: How Do You Think It Feels

synopsis: Lou Reed had followed the commercial success of Transformer with a record that seemed designed to alienate every fan he had just made. Berlin is a harrowing concept album about a couple, Caroline and Jim, whose love affair ends in addiction, abuse and suicide, and its songs are among the darkest ever recorded, full of violence, despair and moments of terrifying beauty. Reed sings them in a flat, weary voice over lush arrangements that make the misery feel almost elegant, and the album's centerpiece, 'The Bed', is one of the most disturbing songs in rock. It was savaged by critics on release and Reed disowned it, but it has since been recognized as a masterpiece of unflinching honesty.

name: Songs from the Big Chair
teaser: 1985 Tears for Fears' second album made synth-pop stadium-sized: 'Everybody Wants to Rule the World', 'Shout', and 'Head over Heels' are anthems about psychology and power. The album sold 10 million copies and defined mid-80s pop. The band's therapy-inspired lyrics gave the music depth.

exploreAction.targetName: Songs from the Big Chair (1985) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album layers synthesizers, guitars, and a full band into a massive sound. 'Shout' was written about primal therapy.

tracks.title: Everybody Wants to Rule the World

synopsis: Tears for Fears had spent their early career as one of the leading bands of the new wave, and this album, their second, was the record that made them stadium-sized. The band, built around the songwriting duo of Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith, had been studying the pop psychology of Arthur Janov, and the album's songs, full of confession and catharsis, reflect that, from the anthemic 'Shout' to the devastating 'Everybody Wants to Rule the World' and the gothic 'The Working Hour'. The record topped charts around the world, and its blend of synthesizers, guitars and huge choruses defined the sound of mid-80s pop. It is the album that turned a cult band into one of the biggest acts on earth.

name: Brothers in Arms
teaser: 1985 Dire Straits' fifth album was the first million-selling CD: 'Money for Nothing', 'Walk of Life', and 'Brothers in Arms' are polished and melancholy. Mark Knopfler's guitar and the album's digital recording made it a showcase for the new format. It sold 30 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar tones — the album was one of the first recorded digitally, and the sound is pristine. 'Money for Nothing' was written in a store watching MTV.

synopsis: Dire Straits had spent their career as one of the most successful bands of the new wave era, but this album, their fifth, was the one that made them superstars, and it did so partly by accident: it was the first album to sell a million copies on CD, the new format that was just taking off. The record's centerpiece is 'Money for Nothing', with its legendary guitar riff and its mocking portrait of MTV, and it also includes the epic anti-war song 'Brothers in Arms' and the haunting 'Ride Across the River'. Mark Knopfler's fingerpicked guitar and husky voice were never better, and the album's clean, detailed production made it the perfect showcase for the CD format.

name: So
teaser: 1986 Peter Gabriel's fifth album is his pop breakthrough: 'Sledgehammer', 'In Your Eyes', and 'Don't Give Up' with Kate Bush are cinematic and warm. The album's video for 'Sledgehammer' won nine MTV awards. It sold 5 million copies and made Gabriel a star.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Daniel Lanois gave the album its airy, spacious sound. 'In Your Eyes' became a wedding staple after being featured in a famous film scene.

synopsis: Peter Gabriel had spent the early 80s as one of the most respected figures in art rock, but he had never had a hit, and this album, his fifth, was the record that changed everything. Its lead single, 'Sledgehammer', with its groundbreaking stop-motion video, became one of the biggest hits of the decade, and the album's fusion of world music, pop and his own theatrical sensibility made it an instant classic. 'Big Time', 'In Your Eyes' and 'Mercy Street' showed the full range of his gifts, and the record topped charts around the world. It is the sound of a genius finally connecting with the mainstream, and its influence on the pop of the following decade is everywhere.

name: The Immaculate Collection
teaser: 1990 Madonna's greatest-hits compilation is a decade of reinvention in one disc: 'Vogue', 'Like a Prayer', and 'Material Girl' trace her transformation from dance-pop to icon. The album sold 30 million copies. It remains the best-selling compilation by a solo artist.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the remixes — several tracks were re-recorded or remixed for the collection. 'Vogue' introduced house music to the mainstream.

synopsis: Madonna had spent the 1980s reinventing herself with every album, and this compilation, released in 1990, is a document of that constant transformation. The record's seventeen songs trace her evolution from the dance pop of 'Holiday' and 'Like a Virgin' through the bold statements of 'Like a Prayer' and 'Express Yourself' to the sleek new tracks 'Vogue' and 'Justify My Love', and each one is a perfect pop single. It is a greatest hits record that tells a story, the story of the most important pop star of her generation, and its success confirmed her status as the defining artist of the decade. It remains one of the best-selling compilations of all time.

name: Faith
teaser: 1987 George Michael's solo debut mixed pop, soul, and gospel: 'Faith', 'Father Figure', and 'One More Try' are confident and intimate. The album sold 25 million copies and won Album of the Year at the Grammys. It made him one of the decade's biggest stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded in his home studio with multiple instruments played by Michael himself. The title track's stomp is iconic.

synopsis: George Michael had spent his career as half of Wham!, one of the most successful pop duos of the 80s, and this solo debut was his declaration that he was more than a teen idol. The record is a confident blend of pop, soul and gospel, and its title track, a horn-driven stomp, and 'Father Figure' and 'One More Try' showed a singer and songwriter of real ambition. The album was a massive hit, selling over 25 million copies, and it established Michael as one of the most successful artists of the decade, a pop star who could sing like a soul man. It is the record where the boy from Wham! grew up, and it remains the high point of his solo career.

name: Appetite for Destruction
teaser: 1987 Guns N' Roses' debut sold 30 million copies and defined late-80s hard rock: 'Welcome to the Jungle', 'Paradise City', and 'Sweet Child o' Mine' are sleazy, dangerous, and catchy. The band's chemistry made them the biggest rock act of the decade's end.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the interplay between Slash's guitar and Axl Rose's vocals — the album is a masterclass in rock dynamics. The cover art caused controversy on release.

synopsis: Guns N' Roses had spent years tearing up the Los Angeles club scene, a band of addicts and outcasts who seemed to live every lyric they wrote, and this debut album, recorded in 1987, captured their chaos with total fidelity. The record is a wall of sound, built on Slash's bluesy guitar, Izzy Stradlin's rhythm playing and the raw power of Axl Rose's voice, which could go from a keening wail to a menacing growl in a single verse. 'Welcome to the Jungle', 'Paradise City' and 'Sweet Child o' Mine' became anthems, and the album sold over 30 million copies, making it the best-selling debut in rock history. It defined late-80s hard rock and made the band the last great rock and roll outlaws.

name: And Justice for All
teaser: 1988 Metallica's fourth album is their most complex: 'One', 'Blackened', and the title track are technical and relentless. The production famously buried the bass, a source of fan debate for decades. The album is a bridge from thrash to mainstream metal.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the riffs — the album is built on intricate, changing time signatures. 'One' was inspired by the anti-war film Johnny Got His Gun.

synopsis: Metallica had spent the 80s as the most brutal band in thrash metal, and this album, their fourth, found them pushing their sound to its most complex and political. The record was made in the aftermath of the death of their bassist Cliff Burton, and the new bassist Jason Newsted's parts were mixed so low that he was nearly inaudible, a controversy that has followed the album ever since. But the music is extraordinary, from the nine-minute 'One', with its harrowing depiction of a soldier trapped in his own body, to the apocalyptic 'Blackened' and the epic title track. It was their commercial breakthrough and remains a high-water mark of progressive thrash.

name: Metallica
teaser: 1991 Metallica's self-titled 'Black Album' made heavy metal stadium-sized: 'Enter Sandman', 'Nothing Else Matters', and 'Sad but True' are slower, heavier, and more melodic. Produced by Bob Rock, the album sold 30 million copies. It is the best-selling metal album of all time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Bob Rock pushed the band to simplify and tighten their songs. The album's sound is bigger and cleaner than anything before it.

synopsis: Metallica had spent a decade as the kings of thrash metal, but this album, their fifth, was a deliberate attempt to reach a wider audience, and it worked beyond their wildest dreams. Produced by Bob Rock, who pushed the band to simplify their songs and tighten their sound, the record trades the speed and complexity of their earlier work for crushing, mid-tempo riffs and huge, singable choruses. 'Enter Sandman', 'The Unforgiven' and 'Nothing Else Matters' became global anthems, and the album sold over 30 million copies, making it one of the best-selling records of all time. It turned Metallica from an underground force into the biggest metal band on earth, and it divided their fans then and now.

name: Chronicle
teaser: 1976 Creedence Clearwater Revival's greatest hits compile their run of 1960s and early-70s classics: 'Fortunate Son', 'Proud Mary', and 'Bad Moon Rising' are protest songs and swamp rock. The compilation sold 8 million copies. It is the definitive CCR document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — John Fogerty wrote and produced nearly everything. 'Fortunate Son' remains the definitive anti-war protest song of its era.

tracks.title: I Put a Spell on You
Long As I Can See the Light
I Heard It Through the Grapevine
Have You Ever Seen the Rain?

synopsis: Creedence Clearwater Revival had one of the most extraordinary runs in rock history, releasing seven albums in four years, and this compilation gathers the best of that output, from the swamp rock of 'Proud Mary' and 'Bad Moon Rising' to the protest of 'Fortunate Son' and the weary beauty of 'Have You Ever Seen the Rain?'. Frontman John Fogerty wrote nearly everything, sang nearly everything and produced nearly everything, and his songs about the American south, Vietnam and the working class made the band the sound of the late 60s. It is one of the greatest greatest-hits records ever made, a single disc that captures a band at the peak of its powers.

name: Hot Rats
teaser: 1969 Frank Zappa's second solo album is a jazz-rock instrumental masterpiece: 'Peaches en Regalia', 'Willie the Pimp', and 'The Gumbo Variations' showcase his guitar and composition. The album features Captain Beefheart's only vocals. It is Zappa's most accessible work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arrangements — the album is a fusion of jazz, rock, and classical forms. 'Peaches en Regalia' became Zappa's signature tune.

synopsis: Frank Zappa had spent the 60s leading the Mothers of Invention, a band that mixed avant-garde composition with rock and roll, and this solo album, his second, was a declaration of independence. The record is almost entirely instrumental, built on the extraordinary playing of a band that included violinist Jean-Luc Ponty, drummer Ian Underwood and a young Lowell George on guitar, and its centerpiece, the nineteen-minute 'Peaches en Regalia' suite, is one of the greatest jazz-rock compositions ever recorded. Zappa's guitar playing, full of wit and fire, is all over the record, and his compositions move between funk, jazz and classical with dizzying ease. It is the album where Zappa found his mature voice.

name: Over-Nite Sensation
teaser: 1973 Frank Zappa's breakthrough album blends jazz fusion with comedic lyrics: 'Dinah-Moe Humm', 'Camarillo Brillo', and 'I'm the Slime' are tight, dirty, and virtuosic. The album made Zappa a star with the mainstream. Its production is among his cleanest.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album's lineup includes future stars like Jean-Luc Ponty and Ruth Underwood. The horn and percussion arrangements are flawless.

synopsis: Frank Zappa had spent his career as a cult figure, beloved by musicians but ignored by the public, and this album, his breakthrough, changed all that. The record blends the jazz fusion of his recent work with his most accessible songs to date, full of the comedic lyrics about sex, food and absurdity that would define his reputation, from the infamous 'Dinah-Moe Humm' to the doo-wop pastiche 'Fifty-Fifty'. Zappa's band, including Ruth Underwood on percussion and George Duke on keyboards, plays with dazzling precision, and his guitar solos are among his best. The album made him a star, and its blend of high musicianship and low comedy was unlike anything else in rock.

name: Apostrophe
teaser: 1974 Frank Zappa's highest-charting album: 'Don't Eat the Yellow Snow', 'Cosmik Debris', and the title track are surreal, funky, and funny. The album's concept follows a boy's adventures in the snow. It reached number 10 on the Billboard chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the bass — Jack Bruce of Cream plays on the title track. The album's humor is inseparable from its musical sophistication.

synopsis: Frank Zappa followed his commercial breakthrough with an album that consolidated his success, and this record, his highest-charting, is among his most beloved. The record's first side is a suite of connected songs built around the tale of Nanook, an Eskimo who refuses to eat the yellow snow, and its blend of comedy and virtuoso playing made it an instant classic. 'Cosmik Debris', a send-up of mysticism, and 'Stink-Foot', a funk workout, are highlights, and Zappa's guitar solos, including the legendary one on the title track, are among the best he ever recorded. It is the most accessible of his mid-70s masterpieces, a record that shows every side of his genius.

name: Joe's Garage
teaser: 1979 Frank Zappa's rock opera about the dangers of music: 'Joe's Garage', 'Watermelon in Easter Hay', and 'Central Scrutinizer' tell the story of a musician in a world where music is illegal. The three-act structure is his most ambitious narrative. The guitar solos are among his best.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the story — the album follows Joe from garage rocker to prisoner. The guitar solo in 'Watermelon in Easter Hay' is Zappa's most emotional.

tracks.title: Why Does It Hurt When I Pee?
Lucille Has Messed My Mind Up
He Used to Cut the Grass

synopsis: Frank Zappa had spent the 70s as one of the most prolific and unpredictable figures in rock, and this three-act rock opera, released in 1979, is one of his most ambitious works. The story follows a young man named Joe who forms a garage band, falls afoul of the authorities and ends up in a totalitarian society where music itself has been outlawed, and its songs range from the blues-rock title track to the doo-wop of 'Catholic Girls' to the extraordinary guitar solos of 'Watermelon in Easter Hay'. The record is Zappa's most sustained piece of social commentary, a warning about the dangers of censorship delivered with his trademark humor. It is regarded as one of the great concept albums in rock.

name: In the Court of the Crimson King
teaser: 1969 King Crimson's debut invented progressive rock: '21st Century Schizoid Man', 'Epitaph', and the title track are dark, symphonic, and apocalyptic. The album's Mellotron and jazz-influenced drums defined the genre. It is one of the most influential rock debuts ever.

exploreAction.targetName: In the Court of the Crimson King (1969) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the Mellotron — the keyboard's choir and string sounds give the album its eerie grandeur. '21st Century Schizoid Man' is proto-metal.

tracks.title: The Court of the Crimson King

synopsis: King Crimson had been formed by guitarist Robert Fripp and lyricist Pete Sinfield, and this debut album, recorded in 1969, invented progressive rock in a single stroke. The record's opening track, '21st Century Schizoid Man', with its distorted, howling vocals and crushing riffs, was heavier than almost anything being made at the time, and the rest of the album ranges from the delicate 'I Talk to the Wind' to the terrifying 'The Court of the Crimson King', a song that sounded like the end of the world set to Mellotron. It was a massive hit and made the band stars, and its influence on everything from heavy metal to art rock is incalculable. It is the album that started a genre.

name: Close to the Edge
teaser: 1972 Yes's fifth album is progressive rock at its most ambitious: the 18-minute title track, 'And You and I', and 'Siberian Khatru' are intricate and majestic. The band's virtuosity and Jon Anderson's ethereal vocals define the genre. It is the definitive prog album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the structure — the title track is one continuous piece with recurring themes. The album rewards focused listening.

tracks.title: And You and I / I. "Cord of Life (3:46) / II. "Eclipse (2:30) / III. "The Preacher, the Teacher (3:10) / IV. "The Apocalypse

synopsis: Yes had spent their first four albums building a following in Britain, but this fifth record, their first with the guitarist Steve Howe and the keyboardist Rick Wakeman, was where they reached the top of their game. The album consists of just three tracks, the centerpiece being the eighteen-minute title epic, a suite of constantly shifting sections that is regarded as one of the greatest achievements of progressive rock. The band's virtuosity is on full display, with Jon Anderson's soaring vocals, Chris Squire's melodic bass and Bill Bruford's complex drumming all working in perfect synchronization. It is the album that defined what progressive rock could be, a record of almost impossible ambition and precision.

name: Fragile
teaser: 1971 Yes's fourth album features each member's solo piece alongside the band's epics: 'Roundabout', 'South Side of the Sky', and 'Heart of the Sunrise' are virtuosic and melodic. Rick Wakeman's keyboards added a new dimension. The album was their international breakthrough.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Roundabout' — its opening bass and guitar riff is one of the most recognizable in prog. The album rewards headphones for its intricate layering.

synopsis: Yes had been moving toward progressive rock for years, and this fourth album, their first to crack the American top ten, was the record that completed the transformation. The album is built on two long suites, the ecstatic 'Roundabout' and the epic 'Heart of the Sunrise', and it also includes a set of solo pieces, one by each member, that show off the individual talents that made the band work. Rick Wakeman, newly recruited from the Strawbs, added his classical keyboard flourishes, and the band's harmonies and instrumental interplay reached a new level. It is a record of extraordinary virtuosity that somehow never loses its sense of joy.

name: The Yes Album
teaser: 1971 Yes's third album marked their turn to progressive rock: 'Yours Is No Disgrace', 'Starship Trooper', and 'I've Seen All Good People' are long, intricate, and melodic. Steve Howe's guitar became the band's signature voice. The album is their first masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arrangements — the band moves between folk, jazz, and rock within single songs. 'Starship Trooper' has one of Howe's best guitar solos.

tracks.title: Starship Trooper" / a. "Life Seeker (Anderson) (3:16) / b. "Disillusion (Squire) (2:21) / c. "Würm
I've Seen All Good People / a. "Your Move (Anderson) (3:32) / b. "All Good People

synopsis: Yes had spent their first two albums as a psychedelic pop band, and this third record, made after the addition of guitarist Steve Howe, marked their turn toward the progressive rock that would define them. The album opens with 'Yours Is No Disgrace', a twelve-minute epic that announced the new direction, and it also includes the delicate 'I've Seen All Good People', a two-part suite that became a staple of progressive rock radio. The band's playing, anchored by Chris Squire's melodic bass and Jon Anderson's soaring vocals, had reached a new level of confidence. It is the record where Yes stopped being a pop band and became one of the greatest acts in progressive rock.

name: Moving Pictures
teaser: 1981 Rush's eighth album is their commercial peak: 'Tom Sawyer', 'Limelight', and 'YYZ' are tight, virtuosic, and catchy. The band's prog-metal sound reached its most accessible form. The album is a gateway into Rush's massive catalog.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the interplay — Geddy Lee's bass, Alex Lifeson's guitar, and Neil Peart's drums lock into intricate grooves. 'YYZ' is named after Toronto's airport code.

synopsis: Rush had spent the 70s building a devoted following with their sci-fi epics and virtuoso playing, and this album, their eighth, was the record that finally brought them mainstream success. The album tightens their sound, with shorter songs and a new emphasis on melody, but it loses none of their ambition, from the anthemic 'Tom Sawyer' to the reflective 'Limelight' and the epic 'YYZ', an instrumental tribute to Toronto's airport. Geddy Lee's high, keening voice and intricate bass, Alex Lifeson's guitar and Neil Peart's legendary drumming were never better integrated. It is the album that made Rush stars, and it remains the favorite of many of their fans.

teaser: 1976 Rush's fourth album's side-long title track tells the story of a future where music is forbidden: 'Overture', 'The Temples of Syrinx', and 'Grand Finale' are sci-fi rock theater. Side two's shorter songs balanced the epic. The album saved the band's career.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the story — the title suite is a complete narrative inspired by Ayn Rand's ideas. The band fought their label to release it as the A-side.

synopsis: Rush had spent their first three albums searching for a sound, and this fourth record found it, anchored by the side-long title track that gave the album its name. '2112' tells the story of a future society ruled by the priests of the Temples of Syrinx, where music has been outlawed, and its seven movements, from the opening 'Overture' to the triumphant finale, became the definitive statement of the band's sci-fi vision. The second side contains 'A Passage to Bangkok' and the tender 'Tears', showing the band's range. The album made Rush stars in America, and its title track remains one of the great epics of progressive rock.

name: Hemispheres
teaser: 1978 Rush's sixth album continued their sci-fi saga: 'Cygnus X-1 Book II' and 'La Villa Strangiato' are long, complex, and epic. The band's virtuosity is on full display. The album is the climax of their prog period.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'La Villa Strangiato' — an instrumental that moves through multiple moods and styles. The band considered it their most difficult piece to play.

synopsis: Rush had ended their previous album with a cliffhanger, and this sixth record resolves it: 'Cygnus X-1 Book II' completes the story of the astronaut who was swallowed by a black hole, and its side-long suite is among the most ambitious music the band ever made. The record also contains 'The Trees', a fable about conflict, and 'La Villa Strangiato', an instrumental tour de force that the band called an exercise in self-indulgence. The album was the last to feature the band's classic power trio lineup before they added synthesizers, and its blend of sci-fi storytelling and virtuoso playing is unmatched. It is progressive rock at its most ambitious.

name: Permanent Waves
teaser: 1980 Rush's seventh album trimmed their epics into tighter songs: 'The Spirit of Radio', 'Freewill', and 'Jacob's Ladder' are progressive but accessible. The album marked the band's shift toward shorter, hookier material. It reached number four on the Billboard chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'The Spirit of Radio' — its reggae section and jazz outro show the band's range. The album is a bridge between their prog and synth eras.

synopsis: Rush had spent the late 70s making increasingly long and complex records, and this seventh album found them trimming their epics into tighter, more focused songs. The record's centerpiece, 'The Spirit of Radio', is a love letter to the medium that had made them stars, and it is surrounded by 'Freewill', a meditation on fate, and 'Jacob's Ladder', a suite that builds to a majestic climax. The band's new interest in synthesizers, which would define their next decade, is beginning to show, and the playing is as precise as ever. It is the album where Rush learned to say more with less, and it remains a favorite of their fans.

name: A Farewell to Kings
teaser: 1977 Rush's fifth album blended their prog epics with the emerging new wave: 'Closer to the Heart', 'Xanadu', and the title track are grand and melodic. The band recorded it in Wales with a classical guitarist on loan. The album expands their sonic palette.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the acoustic textures — classical guitar appears throughout the album. 'Xanadu' is one of their most ambitious epics.

tracks.title: Cygnus X-1 Book I: The Voyage :"Prologue (5:01) :"1 (0:44) :"2 (1:30) :"3

synopsis: Rush had spent the mid-70s as one of the most ambitious bands in progressive rock, and this fifth album found them adapting to the changing musical landscape. The record blends the epic suites of their earlier work with the emerging new wave sound, and its title track, a meditation on power and its costs, showed the band engaging with the real world for the first time. 'Closer to the Heart', a gentle, melodic song about the search for meaning, became one of their most beloved tracks, and the album's second side includes 'Xanadu', a twelve-minute epic inspired by Coleridge. It is a transitional record that pointed toward the stadium rock that would make them stars.

name: Gaucho
teaser: 1980 Steely Dan's seventh album took five years and cost over a million dollars: 'Hey Nineteen', 'Time Out of Mind', and the title track are sleek, sardonic, and immaculate. The band broke up after its release, exhausted by perfectionism. It is their most polished work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album's sound is a benchmark of studio craft. 'Time Out of Mind' features a sax solo by Mark Knopfler.

synopsis: Steely Dan had spent the 70s as the most meticulous band in rock, and this seventh album, their last for seven years, took their perfectionism to its logical extreme. The record took over two years to make and cost more than a million dollars, and its seven songs were recorded with dozens of musicians, many of whom were paid for sessions that never made the final cut. The music is polished to a mirror shine, from the jazz-funk of 'Babylon Sisters' to the elegant ballad 'Hey Nineteen' to the title track's portrait of decadence. Donald Fagen and Walter Becker had become so exacting that they stopped touring and eventually stopped recording together. It is a masterpiece of studio craft, the sound of a band achieving its vision at any cost.

name: Pretzel Logic
teaser: 1974 Steely Dan's third album is their most varied: 'Rikki Don't Lose That Number', 'Any Major Dude Will Tell You', and the title track mix jazz, rock, and pop. The band's writing duo, Becker and Fagen, were moving away from live performance toward studio perfection. The album reached number eight.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songcraft — every track is immaculate. 'Rikki Don't Lose That Number' was inspired by a Horace Silver jazz lick.

tracks.title: Any Major Dude Will Tell You

synopsis: Steely Dan had spent their first two albums establishing a sound of literate, jazz-tinged rock, and this third record is their most varied. The album ranges from the bossa nova of 'Rikki Don't Lose That Number', their biggest hit, to the jazzy instrumental 'Parker's Band' and the blues of 'With a Gun', and its lyrics are full of the cryptic, sardonic observations that made the band's reputation. The record also includes 'Night by Night' and the intricate 'Any Major Dude Will Tell You'. It is the album where Steely Dan perfected their formula of immaculate production and inscrutable wit.

name: Can't Buy a Thrill
teaser: 1972 Steely Dan's debut introduced their literate jazz-rock: 'Do It Again', 'Reelin' in the Years', and 'Dirty Work' are sly, polished, and catchy. The band's anonymous studio approach set the template for their career. The album made them stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar — 'Reelin' in the Years' features one of the most famous solos in rock. The album's debut was under a band name that was also a pseudonym.

tracks.title: Only a Fool Would Say That

synopsis: Steely Dan's debut album introduced one of the most distinctive sounds in 70s rock, a blend of jazz harmonies, pop melodies and the cryptic, literate lyrics of Donald Fagen and Walter Becker. The record's centerpiece is 'Do It Again', a hypnotic song built on a repeated keyboard riff that became their first hit, and it also includes the sardonic 'Reelin' In the Years' and the latin-tinged 'Dirty Work'. The band's playing is loose and confident, and the production, by Gary Katz, gives the music a warmth that their later, more polished records would lack. It announced a band that would become one of the most respected in rock.

name: Countdown to Ecstasy
teaser: 1973 Steely Dan's second album is darker and more complex than the debut: 'My Old School', 'Bodhisattva', and 'Show Biz Kids' are sardonic and funky. The band's growing perfectionism shows in every arrangement. It is a bridge to their masterpiece era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — 'Bodhisattva' is the band's most driving track. The lyrics are among Becker and Fagen's most oblique.

synopsis: Steely Dan had spent their debut album establishing their sound, and this second record deepened it, with darker, more complex music and lyrics that were even more cryptic. The album's centerpiece is 'My Old School', a song about Fagen and Becker's alma mater that became a staple of their live shows, and it also includes 'Bodhisattva', a propulsive rocker, and the elegiac 'Pearl of the Quarter'. The band, now including guitarist Jeff Baxter, plays with new confidence, and the production is more polished than on their debut. It is the record where Steely Dan became the band they would be for the rest of the decade.

name: The Royal Scam
teaser: 1976 Steely Dan's fifth album is their most guitar-driven: 'Kid Charlemagne', 'The Caves of Altamira', and 'Haitian Divorce' are funky, cinematic, and sardonic. Larry Carlton's solos are among the best on any Dan record. The album is a high point of their 70s run.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar solos — Larry Carlton played many of them in single takes. 'Kid Charlemagne' was written about a fictional LSD chemist.

synopsis: Steely Dan's fifth album is their most guitar-driven record, built around the extraordinary playing of Larry Carlton, whose solos on 'Kid Charlemagne' and 'The Royal Scam' are among the greatest ever recorded. The album's songs are darker and more cynical than their earlier work, full of hustlers, criminals and losers, from the title track's portrait of a con man to the noir of 'Don't Take Me Alive' and the funky 'Haitian Divorce'. Fagen and Becker's songwriting had never been sharper, and the production, immaculate as always, gives the music a sinister glow. It is one of the great albums of the mid-70s, the sound of a band at the height of its powers.

name: Bad
teaser: 1987 Michael Jackson's follow-up to Thriller was a worldwide smash: 'Bad', 'The Way You Make Me Feel', and 'Smooth Criminal' are sleek and confident. The album produced five number-one singles, a record. Its title track's music video with Martin Scorsese was a landmark.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Quincy Jones and Jackson crafted a harder, more aggressive sound. 'Smooth Criminal' features one of Jackson's most iconic dance routines.

tracks.title: The Way You Make Me Feel
I Just Can't Stop Loving You

synopsis: Michael Jackson had spent the four years since Thriller trying to top the biggest-selling album in history, and this follow-up, recorded with producer Quincy Jones over several years, was the result. The record sold over 30 million copies, a staggering number even if it fell short of Thriller, and its title track, with its horn-driven stomp and the famous duet with Siedah Garrett, became a global smash. 'The Way You Make Me Feel', 'Man in the Mirror' and 'Smooth Criminal' showed the full range of Jackson's talents, and the album's videos, including the epic short film for the title track, were events in themselves. It is the sound of the biggest star on earth at the peak of his fame.

name: Dangerous
teaser: 1991 Michael Jackson's eighth album blended new jack swing, funk, and rock: 'Black or White', 'Remember the Time', and 'Jam' are political and danceable. The album's 13-minute 'Black or White' video premiered worldwide. It sold 30 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Teddy Riley's new jack swing gave the album a modern edge. The album's social themes were a shift from his earlier work.

tracks.title: Why You Wanna Trip on Me

synopsis: Michael Jackson had spent the 80s as the biggest star in the world, and this album, his eighth, found him trying to reinvent himself for the new decade. Working with producer Teddy Riley, the pioneer of new jack swing, Jackson blended that sound with funk, rock and his own pop instincts, and the record's title track and 'Remember the Time' were among the most innovative pop songs of the era. The album also contains the anthemic 'Black or White', with its famous morphing video, and the charity single 'Heal the World'. It was a massive hit, though its darker, more paranoid lyrics hinted at the troubles to come. It is the last great album of Jackson's imperial period.

name: Ray of Light
teaser: 1998 Madonna's seventh album turned her toward electronic and spiritual themes: 'Frozen', 'Ray of Light', and 'The Power of Good-Bye' are ambient and danceable. Produced with William Orbit, the album won four Grammys. It is her most acclaimed work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Orbit's electronic textures give the album its otherworldly atmosphere. 'Ray of Light' was a reinvention that kept her at pop's forefront.

tracks.title: To Have and Not to Hold

synopsis: Madonna had spent the 90s reinventing herself, but nothing prepared her fans for this, her seventh album, a radical departure made after her daughter's birth and her embrace of Kabbalah and yoga. Working with producer William Orbit, Madonna built a record of electronic, ambient music that was also her most personal, from the dance anthem 'Ray of Light' to the meditative 'Frozen' to the confessional 'Mer Girl'. Her voice, thinner and more fragile than before, suited the new sound, and the album won four Grammys. It is the record where the queen of pop grew up, and it remains one of the most acclaimed albums of her career.

name: True Blue
teaser: 1986 Madonna's third album is a pop landmark: 'Live to Tell', 'Papa Don't Preach', and 'Open Your Heart' are confident and catchy. The album sold 25 million copies and produced four number-one singles. It is the peak of her 80s pop era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hooks — every track is built for the radio. 'Papa Don't Preach' sparked controversy for its topic of teen pregnancy.

tracks.title: Love Makes the World Go Round

synopsis: Madonna had spent her first two albums establishing herself as the queen of dance pop, and this third record was the one that made her a superstar. The album's run of singles, from the ballad 'Live to Tell' to the anthemic 'Papa Don't Preach' to the joyful 'True Blue' and the tribute 'La Isla Bonita', was unprecedented, and each one showed a different side of her talent. The record topped charts around the world and sold over 20 million copies, and its title track, a love letter to her husband Sean Penn, became her signature. It is the album that turned the pop star into a cultural force.

name: American Life
teaser: 2003 Madonna's ninth album is her most political and divisive: 'American Life', 'Hollywood', and 'Die Another Day' critique American culture with electronic folk. The album's title track video was pulled after controversy. It is her most underrated record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the lyrics — the album is a critique of celebrity and consumer culture. The acoustic guitars mixed with electronic beats were ahead of their time.

synopsis: Madonna had spent the 90s as the most famous woman in pop, and this ninth album found her turning political. Released in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks, the record is full of anti-war, anti-capitalist sentiments, from the title track, a critique of American consumerism that caused a scandal when she performed it during the invasion of Iraq, to the folk-tinged 'Hollywood' and the elegiac 'X-Static Process'. The album was her most divisive, with many critics and fans rejecting its preachiness, but time has been kinder to it, and its willingness to risk her popularity for her beliefs is admirable. It is the sound of a superstar refusing to stay in her lane.

name: Music
teaser: 2000 Madonna's eighth album embraced European dance music: 'Music', 'Don't Tell Me', and 'What It Feels Like for a Girl' are sleek and futuristic. Produced with Mirwais, the album gave her a new electronic sound. It sold 11 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Mirwais's filtered beats and glitch effects were cutting-edge. 'Music' became a global dance anthem.

tracks.title: What It Feels Like for a Girl

synopsis: Madonna had spent the 90s reinventing herself with every album, and this eighth record found her embracing the electronic dance music that was dominating Europe. Working with producers including Mirwais Ahmadzaï and William Orbit, Madonna built a record of sleek, futuristic pop, and its title track and 'What It Feels Like for a Girl' became global hits. The album's centerpiece is 'Don't Tell Me', a country-tinged electronic song that became one of her most beloved singles. The record was a massive hit, selling over 15 million copies, and it showed that Madonna, now in her forties, could still define the sound of the moment. It is one of the most confident records of her career.

teaser: 2011 Beyoncé's fourth album stripped her sound back to soul and funk: 'Run the World (Girls)', 'Love on Top', and 'Countdown' are confident and playful. The album's vocal runs and horns reference 80s R&B. It is a fan favorite in her catalog.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album mixes live instrumentation with electronic beats. 'Countdown' samples Boyz II Men and was inspired by reggae.

synopsis: Beyoncé had spent her career as the leader of Destiny's Child, one of the most successful girl groups in history, and this fourth solo album was her attempt to step away from the pop machinery and make music on her own terms. Working with a small group of producers, Beyoncé stripped her sound back to soul, funk and hip-hop, and the record's centerpiece, 'Run the World (Girls)', became an anthem of female empowerment. 'Countdown', 'Love on Top' and the tender 'I Was Here' showed her range, and the album's live performances, especially her legendary Glastonbury set, became the stuff of legend. It is the record where the pop star became an artist.

name: Dangerously in Love
teaser: 2003 Beyoncé's solo debut established her as a superstar apart from Destiny's Child: 'Crazy in Love', 'Baby Boy', and 'Me, Myself and I' are confident and catchy. The album sold 11 million copies and won five Grammys. 'Crazy in Love' remains her signature.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Crazy in Love' — its horn sample and drum break made it an instant classic. The album blends R&B, pop, and reggae.

tracks.title: The Closer I Get to You

synopsis: Beyoncé had spent her entire career as part of Destiny's Child, and this solo debut was her declaration that she could stand alone. The record was a massive hit, debuting at number one and selling over 11 million copies, and its lead single, 'Crazy in Love', with its iconic horn riff and a verse from Jay-Z, became one of the defining songs of the decade. 'Baby Boy', 'Me, Myself and I' and the ballad 'Dangerously in Love' showed the full range of her talents, and her voice, already one of the greatest in pop, was on full display. It won five Grammys and established Beyoncé as the most important female star of her generation.

name: Tidal
teaser: 1996 Fiona Apple's debut won a Grammy for Best Rock Vocal: 'Shadowboxer', 'Criminal', and 'Sleep to Dream' are dark, jazzy, and precociously mature. The album's confessional lyrics and piano-driven sound made her a star at 19. It sold 2 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — Apple's playing is percussive and jazz-influenced. The video for 'Criminal' sparked controversy and fame.

synopsis: Fiona Apple had been discovered at 18, when a friend gave her demo tape to a music executive, and this debut album, recorded when she was still a teenager, made her a star overnight. The record is a stunning display of her gifts, with her piano playing and her raw, confessional lyrics about love, anger and desire, and its first single, 'Shadowboxer', and the harrowing 'Sleep to Dream' announced a major new voice. She was nominated for a Grammy and won for best rock vocal, and her video for 'Criminal' made her a cultural phenomenon. It is one of the most assured debut albums ever made, the sound of a young woman who knew exactly who she was.

name: Butterfly
teaser: 1997 Mariah Carey's sixth album blended hip-hop with her signature ballads: 'Honey', 'Butterfly', and 'My All' are sleek and personal. The album marked her artistic reinvention after her divorce. It is her most critically acclaimed work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album features collaborations with hip-hop producers like Puff Daddy. 'Honey' introduced a more urban sound to her catalog.

synopsis: Mariah Carey had spent her career as the queen of the ballad, but by the mid-90s she was determined to prove she could do more, and this sixth album found her embracing hip-hop. The record's centerpiece, 'Honey', with its R&B groove and her famous whistle register, became her biggest hit, and 'Butterfly' and 'My All' showed she had lost none of her ballad power. The album also features collaborations with rappers like Mase and the track 'Breakdown' with Bone Thugs-n-Harmony, and its fusion of pop, R&B and hip-hop was groundbreaking. It is regarded as her most personal and artistically ambitious record, made as her marriage to Tommy Mottola was ending.

name: The Emancipation of Mimi
teaser: 2005 Mariah Carey's comeback album re-established her as a chart force: 'We Belong Together', 'Shake It Off', and 'Don't Forget About Us' are sleek R&B anthems. The album sold 10 million copies and produced two number-one singles. It is her best-selling album of the 2000s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends hip-hop beats with her vocal gymnastics. 'We Belong Together' was the decade's biggest R&B hit.

tracks.title: Makin' It Last All Night (What It Do)
So Lonely (One and Only Part II)

synopsis: Mariah Carey had spent the early 2000s in a tailspin, with a failed movie, a nervous breakdown and a string of flops that made many write her off, and this album, her tenth, was her attempt at a comeback. The record's lead single, 'We Belong Together', became the biggest hit of her career, spending fourteen weeks at number one, and its blend of her signature ballads with contemporary R&B re-established her as the queen of the charts. 'Shake It Off' and 'Don't Forget About Us' followed it to the top, and the album sold over 10 million copies. It is one of the greatest comebacks in pop history, the sound of a superstar refusing to stay down.

name: Daydream
teaser: 1995 Mariah Carey's fifth album is her most seamless fusion of pop and R&B: 'Fantasy', 'One Sweet Day', and 'Always Be My Baby' are smooth and effortless. The album sold 20 million copies and produced two number-one singles. It is her commercial peak.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the vocals — the album showcases her five-octave range. 'Fantasy' was the first song by a female artist to debut at number one.

synopsis: Mariah Carey had spent her first four albums establishing herself as the best-selling female artist in the world, and this fifth record was the peak of that era. The album's singles, from the hip-hop-inflected 'Fantasy' to the soaring 'One Sweet Day', a duet with Boyz II Men that became the longest-running number one in history, to the tender 'Always Be My Baby', were an unprecedented run of hits. The record fused her signature ballads with R&B and hip-hop in a way that was ahead of its time, and it sold over 20 million copies. It is the album where Mariah Carey perfected her formula of pop perfection and vocal acrobatics.

name: Music Box
teaser: 1993 Mariah Carey's third album made her a global superstar: 'Dreamlover', 'Hero', and 'Without You' are ballads and dance-pop at their most polished. The album sold 28 million copies. It remains one of the best-selling albums of all time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the ballads — 'Hero' became an anthem of personal strength. The album's production is immaculate mid-90s pop.

tracks.title: Just to Hold You Once Again

synopsis: Mariah Carey had become a star with her first two albums, but this third record was the one that made her a global phenomenon. The album's lead single, 'Dreamlover', was an instant smash, and 'Hero', a ballad she was reluctant to record, became one of her signature songs and an anthem of inspiration around the world. The record sold over 25 million copies and topped charts for months, and her voice, with its astonishing range, was at its peak. It is the album that turned the young singer from a promising newcomer into the best-selling female artist of her generation.

name: The Bodyguard
teaser: 1992 Whitney Houston's soundtrack album is the best-selling soundtrack of all time: 'I Will Always Love You', 'I Have Nothing', and 'Run to You' showcase her voice at its peak. The album sold 45 million copies. Dolly Parton's song became Houston's signature.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Will Always Love You' — the a cappella opening builds into one of the greatest vocal performances ever recorded. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys.

tracks.title: Even If My Heart Would Break
It's Gonna Be a Lovely Day
(What's So Funny 'Bout) Peace, Love, and Understanding

synopsis: Whitney Houston was at the absolute peak of her powers in 1992, the best-selling female artist in the world, and this soundtrack to her film debut became the biggest-selling soundtrack of all time. The movie, a thriller about a singer who hires a bodyguard, was a hit, but it was the music that made history, led by 'I Will Always Love You', a Dolly Parton song that Houston transformed into a six-minute showstopper that spent fourteen weeks at number one. The album also includes 'I'm Every Woman' and 'Run to You', and it sold over 45 million copies. It is the sound of the greatest voice of her generation at the height of its glory.

name: Whitney
teaser: 1987 Whitney Houston's second album made her the first woman to debut at number one: 'I Wanna Dance with Somebody', 'Didn't We Almost Have It All', and 'So Emotional' are pop-soul anthems. The album sold 20 million copies and produced four number-one singles.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Narada Michael Walden's arrangements gave the album its polished sound. The album cemented Houston as the decade's biggest female star.

tracks.title: Saving All My Love for You
Nobody Loves Me Like You Do
Take Good Care of My Heart

synopsis: Whitney Houston had conquered the world with her debut album, and this follow-up, released just two years later, confirmed that she was not a flash in the pan but a phenomenon. The album made history by debuting at number one, the first time a female artist had ever achieved that feat, and its singles, from the anthemic 'I Wanna Dance with Somebody' to the soaring 'Didn't We Almost Have It All' to the gospel-tinged 'So Emotional', were an unprecedented run of hits. The record sold over 20 million copies and won a Grammy, and Houston's voice, with its astonishing power and range, was the defining instrument of the decade. It is the sound of a superstar at the peak of her reign.

name: Whitney Houston
teaser: 1985 Whitney Houston's debut made her an overnight star: 'Saving All My Love for You', 'How Will I Know', and 'Greatest Love of All' showcase her voice and elegance. The album sold 25 million copies and produced three number-one singles. It is one of the best-selling debuts ever.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album displays her gospel-trained voice across pop, R&B, and ballads. 'Greatest Love of All' became an anthem of self-esteem.

tracks.title: Saving All My Love for You
Nobody Loves Me Like You Do
Take Good Care of My Heart

synopsis: Whitney Houston had been singing since she was a child, first in the church choir and then as a model and backup singer, but nothing prepared the world for this debut album, released in 1985 when she was 21. The record introduced her voice, one of the most powerful and versatile instruments ever recorded, and its singles, from 'Saving All My Love for You' to 'How Will I Know' to 'The Greatest Love of All', became an unprecedented run of hits. The album sold over 25 million copies and won a Grammy, and its blend of pop, R&B and gospel made Houston the most important new voice of the decade. It is the record that started one of the greatest careers in pop history.

name: I'm Your Baby Tonight
teaser: 1990 Whitney Houston's third album embraced new jack swing: 'I'm Your Baby Tonight', 'All the Man That I Need', and 'Miracle' are sleek and confident. The album sold 10 million copies and produced three number-one singles. It modernized her sound for the new decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — L.A. Reid and Babyface gave the album a contemporary R&B edge. The title track is a new jack swing showcase.

tracks.title: All the Man That I Need

synopsis: Whitney Houston had spent the 80s as the queen of pop ballads, and this third album found her adapting to the new sound of the early 90s. Working with producers including L.A. Reid and Babyface, Houston embraced new jack swing, and the record's title track and 'All the Man That I Need' showed she could move with the times without losing her voice. The album also contains the enduring ballad 'Miracle' and the funky 'My Name Is Not Susan'. It was another massive hit, selling over 10 million copies, and while it is often overlooked next to her earlier triumphs, it showed Houston evolving as an artist on the eve of her greatest success.

teaser: 2015 Adele's third album addressed motherhood and maturity: 'Hello', 'When We Were Young', and 'Send My Love (To Your New Lover)' are polished and emotional. The album sold 22 million copies and won Album of the Year. 'Hello' broke streaming records on release.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Greg Kurstin and Max Martin crafted a more restrained sound. 'Hello' was written about reaching out to people from the past.

tracks.title: Send My Love (To Your New Lover)

synopsis: Adele had spent four years following up her record-breaking album 21, and the pressure was immense, but this third record, made in the aftermath of motherhood and a divorce, found her wiser and more assured. The album's lead single, 'Hello', with its enormous chorus, became one of the fastest-selling singles in history, and 'When We Were Young' and 'Send My Love (To Your New Lover)' showed her range. The record sold over 20 million copies in a year, an almost impossible number in the streaming era, and won the Grammy for Album of the Year. It is the sound of an artist who had grown up, singing about love and loss with a new depth of feeling.

teaser: 2008 Adele's debut introduced her voice to the world: 'Chasing Pavements', 'Hometown Glory', and 'Make You Feel My Love' are folk and soul ballads. The album won a Grammy for Best New Artist. It sold 9 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the debut is simpler than her later work, letting her voice carry the songs. 'Hometown Glory' was written about London at 18.

tracks.title: That’s It, I Quit, I'm Moving On

synopsis: Adele had been writing songs since she was a teenager, and this debut album, recorded when she was just 19 and still in school, introduced her extraordinary voice to the world. The record is built on her gift for turning heartbreak into anthems, and its lead single, 'Chasing Pavements', became a global hit, winning a Grammy. The album also contains 'Hometown Glory', a tribute to her native London, and the devastating 'Someone Like You', which would later become a phenomenon on her next record. It won the Mercury Prize and sold over 10 million copies, and its blend of classic soul and modern pop made Adele the most exciting new voice in years.

name: The Fame
teaser: 2008 Lady Gaga's debut made electro-pop a movement: 'Just Dance', 'Poker Face', and 'Paparazzi' are hook-filled and theatrical. The album sold 15 million copies and won a Grammy. It introduced her as pop's most ambitious new star.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — RedOne's beats gave the album its dance-floor energy. 'Poker Face' was a global number one and remains her signature.

tracks.title: Eh, Eh (Nothing Else I Can Say)

synopsis: Lady Gaga had spent years as a songwriter for other artists before she decided to make her own music, and this debut album, released in 2008, announced her arrival with a bang. The record's blend of electro-pop, dance and theatrical glamour was unlike anything on the radio, and its singles, from 'Just Dance' to 'Poker Face' to 'Paparazzi', were an unprecedented run of hits. Gaga's persona, part Andy Warhol, part David Bowie, was as important as her music, and the album made her the biggest new star in pop. It is the record that turned electro-pop into a global movement and made Gaga the most talked-about artist of her generation.

name: Born This Way
teaser: 2011 Lady Gaga's second album is a maximalist statement of self-acceptance: 'Born This Way', 'Judas', and 'Edge of Glory' are dance anthems about identity. The album debuted at number one in 20 countries. It is her most ambitious pop statement.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album mixes rock guitars, disco, and industrial beats. The title track became an anthem for the LGBTQ community.

synopsis: Lady Gaga had spent her debut album building a persona of fame and excess, and this second record turned the volume up to maximum. The album is a maximalist statement of self-acceptance, built on enormous choruses, industrial beats and lyrics about being born different and proud of it, and its title track, with its pro-immigrant, pro-gay message, became an anthem. 'Judas', 'The Edge of Glory' and 'You and I' showed her range, and the record debuted at number one in nearly every country in the world. It sold over 20 million copies and confirmed Gaga as the defining pop star of her era, an artist who used her platform to celebrate the outcasts.

name: Joanne
teaser: 2016 Lady Gaga's fifth album is her most personal: 'Million Reasons', 'Joanne', and 'Perfect Illusion' are stripped-back country-pop about family and loss. The album was named after her aunt who died at 19. It won a Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the shift — the album trades her dance sound for acoustic guitars and raw vocals. 'Million Reasons' became a fan favorite and live staple.

synopsis: Lady Gaga had spent her career as a larger-than-life pop star, but this fifth album, named for her aunt Joanne, who died of lupus before Gaga was born, found her stripping back the artifice. Working with producers including Mark Ronson and Florence Welch, Gaga made a record rooted in classic rock and country, singing with a new directness about family, loss and love. 'Million Reasons' and the title track became hits, and the album's centerpiece, 'Joanne', is a tribute to the aunt she never met. It divided fans who wanted the old Gaga, but it showed an artist willing to be vulnerable, and its authenticity won over many skeptics. It is the most personal record of her career.

name: Chromatica
teaser: 2020 Lady Gaga's sixth album returned to pure dance pop: 'Stupid Love', 'Rain on Me', and '911' are euphoric and escapist. The album was recorded during a period of personal struggle. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — BloodPop and Burns crafted a cohesive electronic sound. 'Rain on Me' with Ariana Grande won a Grammy.

synopsis: Lady Gaga had spent the late 2010s moving away from pure pop, with a jazz album, an Oscar-winning film role and a country-tinged record, and this sixth album was her return to the dance floor. The record is a pure, unapologetic celebration of dance music, built on the sounds of the 90s house and disco that made her fall in love with pop, and its lead single, 'Stupid Love', and the Elton John duet 'Sine from Above' showed her joy in the music. The album's release was overshadowed by the pandemic, but its message of finding joy in darkness made it the soundtrack many people needed. It is the sound of a superstar remembering why she started.

name: The Fame Monster
teaser: 2009 Lady Gaga's EP expanded her debut's universe: 'Bad Romance', 'Telephone', and 'Alejandro' are dark, theatrical, and iconic. The monster theme references her fears. The EP won three Grammys and sold 6 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the darkness — the songs are more experimental than the debut. 'Bad Romance' is one of the most awarded songs of the decade.

synopsis: Lady Gaga had released her debut album to enormous success, but she had been sitting on a set of songs that were too dark and personal for that record, and this EP, released a year later, was where she let them out. The record's eight tracks are built around two themes, fame and its monsters, and its lead single, 'Bad Romance', became one of the defining pop songs of the decade, with its chanted chorus and its video's surreal imagery. 'Telephone', a duet with Beyoncé, and 'Alejandro' continued the run, and the EP sold over 10 million copies, an almost unheard-of number for a six-song release. It is the record that turned Gaga from a pop star into a phenomenon.

name: Section.80
teaser: 2011 Kendrick Lamar's debut album introduced his storytelling: 'HiiiPower', 'A.D.H.D', and 'Rigamortus' are socially conscious West Coast rap. The album was released independently and built his underground following. It set the stage for his major-label masterpieces.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album is a concept piece about a generation. 'A.D.H.D' became an anthem for his peers.

synopsis: Kendrick Lamar had spent years building a following in his native Compton with a series of mixtapes, and this debut album, released independently in 2011, was his introduction to the wider world. The record is a stunning display of his storytelling, with songs about the crack epidemic, the war on drugs and the cycle of violence in his neighborhood, anchored by his extraordinary rapping and the production of his mentor Dr. Dre and others. 'HiiiPower', with its triumphant horn line, became an anthem, and the album's centerpiece, 'Keisha's Song', tells the devastating story of a sex worker. It sold poorly at first but built the foundation for the greatest career in modern rap.

name: It Was Written
teaser: 1996 Nas's second album traded Illmatic's rawness for cinematic scope: 'If I Ruled the World', 'Street Dreams', and 'I Gave You Power' are grand and ambitious. The album sold 2.5 million copies. It is often debated as nearly the equal of his debut.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — 'I Gave You Power' is told from the perspective of a gun. The production by Trackmasters gave the album a mafioso feel.

tracks.title: If I Ruled the World (Imagine That)

synopsis: Nas had spent two years following his legendary debut Illmatic, and this second album, made with producers including Dr. Dre and the Trackmasters, was his attempt to reach a wider audience without losing his edge. The record trades Illmatic's raw street poetry for cinematic scope, with songs about the mafia, the afterlife and the burdens of fame, and its lead single, 'If I Ruled the World (Imagine That)', a duet with Lauryn Hill, became his biggest hit. 'The Message' and 'I Gave You Power', a song narrated by a gun, are among the greatest tracks of his career. It was a massive success, and while purists preferred his debut, it showed Nas could be both an artist and a star.

name: Stillmatic
teaser: 2001 Nas's fifth album reasserted his dominance: 'Ether', 'One Mic', and 'Got Ur Self a Gun' are combative and focused. The album was a response to rival Jay-Z's attacks. It re-established Nas as a top-tier rapper.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the diss — 'Ether' is one of the most brutal diss tracks in hip-hop history. The album's title signaled a return to his debut's spirit.

synopsis: Nas had spent the late 90s in a creative slump, releasing records that critics and fans alike dismissed, and by 2001 his career was in jeopardy. This fifth album was his comeback, and its lead single, 'Ether', a devastating diss track aimed at his rival Jay-Z, became one of the most famous battles in rap history. The album also contains 'One Mic', a stunning meditation on violence and faith, and 'Got Ur Self A...', and its title, a reference to his claims to be the best rapper alive, captured its defiant mood. It re-established Nas as one of the greatest rappers in the world, and its title track remains one of his signature songs.

name: God's Son
teaser: 2002 Nas's sixth album blends street wisdom with spiritual reflection: 'Made You Look', 'I Can', and 'Dance' are incisive and personal. The album was released after his mother's death. It is among his most emotionally direct work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'I Can' — the song teaches children self-worth over a Beethoven sample. The album's title honors his mother.

synopsis: Nas had spent his career as the poet of the streets, and this sixth album found him turning toward spirituality. Made in the aftermath of his mother's death, the record is full of songs about faith, mortality and the search for meaning, from the introspective 'Made You Look' to the gospel-tinged 'Dance' and the title track, a prayer for his mother. The album also contains 'Book of Rhymes' and the fierce 'Get Down', showing he had lost none of his edge. It is regarded as one of the best albums of his later period, a record that balances street wisdom with genuine reflection, made by a man who had lived long enough to have something to say.

name: The Score
teaser: 1996 The Fugees' second album fused hip-hop, soul, and reggae: 'Killing Me Softly', 'Fu-Gee-La', and 'Ready or Not' made them international stars. The album sold 18 million copies and won two Grammys. It remains the best-selling hip-hop album of its era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — 'Killing Me Softly' turned a Roberta Flack classic into a global hit. The album's genre blend was unprecedented.

synopsis: The Fugees had spent their first album as a promising but overlooked hip-hop group, and this second record, made after they nearly broke up, was their transformation into superstars. The album is a stunning fusion of hip-hop, soul, reggae and R&B, built around the extraordinary voices of Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean, and its centerpiece, a cover of Roberta Flack's 'Killing Me Softly', became one of the biggest hits of the decade. 'Ready or Not', 'Fu-Gee-La' and their version of Bob Marley's 'No Woman, No Cry' completed the run. The album sold over 20 million copies and made the Fugees the most successful hip-hop group in history, and its influence is still felt today.

teaser: 1999 Dr. Dre's second album proved the G-funk architect still ruled: 'Still D.R.E.', 'The Next Episode', and 'Forgot About Dre' are West Coast anthems. The album relaunched Snoop and Eminem alongside Dre. It is the definitive West Coast album of its era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — every track is immaculately crafted. 'Still D.R.E.' features one of the most recognizable piano riffs in rap.

tracks.title: Fuck You (censored as F*** You in the edited version)
Bitch Niggaz (censored as Bi*** Ni**az in the edited version)

synopsis: Dr. Dre had spent the early 90s as the most important producer in hip-hop, the architect of G-funk and the man behind Snoop Dogg's debut, but he had not released an album of his own in seven years. This record, his second, was his declaration that he still ruled, and it is a masterpiece of West Coast hip-hop, full of the slow, sinister grooves that made his reputation. 'Still D.R.E.', with Snoop Dogg, 'Forgot About Dre', with Eminem, and 'The Next Episode' became instant classics, and the album's guest list, including Mary J. Blige and Xzibit, showed his reach. It sold over 20 million copies and proved the G-funk architect had lost nothing.

name: Compton
teaser: 2015 Dr. Dre's third album ended a 16-year gap: 'Talking to My Diary', 'One Shot One Kill', and 'Deep Water' are dense and cinematic. The album was released alongside the film Straight Outta Compton. It is his final statement as a rapper.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album features contributions from Kendrick Lamar and Anderson .Paak. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

synopsis: Dr. Dre had spent sixteen years as the most successful producer in hip-hop without releasing an album of his own, and this record, his third and final, was both a return and a farewell. Made with a new generation of producers including Anderson .Paak and Kendrick Lamar, who appears on several tracks, the album finds Dre looking back on his life in Compton, from the violence of his youth to the success of his later years. 'Talking to My Diary' and 'One Shot One Kill' are among the most personal songs he ever made, and the record's title, a reference to his hometown, gave it the weight of a homecoming. It is a fitting epitaph for one of the greatest careers in hip-hop.

name: The Documentary
teaser: 2005 The Game's debut, executive-produced by Dr. Dre, made him a star: 'Hate It or Love It', 'How We Do', and 'Westside Story' are G-funk updates for the new century. The album sold 5 million copies. It is the last great West Coast debut.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Dre's beats anchor the album. 'Hate It or Love It' with 50 Cent became an anthem of rivalry.

synopsis: The Game had spent years as a protege of Dr. Dre, the legendary producer who had not launched a new star in over a decade, and this debut album, executive produced by Dre, was his coming out party. The record is a stunning showcase for his talents, with his laid-back flow and his gift for storytelling carrying songs about the streets of Compton, and its centerpiece, 'Hate It or Love It', a duet with 50 Cent, became an anthem. 'Westside Story' and 'How We Do' completed the run, and the album sold over five million copies. It made the Game a star and confirmed that Dre's Midas touch had not faded.

name: Food & Liquor
teaser: 2006 Lupe Fiasco's debut is one of the most literate rap albums ever: 'Kick, Push', 'Daydreamin'', and 'Hurt Me Soul' are intricate and political. The album won a Grammy for Best Urban/Alternative Performance. It established him as hip-hop's poet.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — Lupe's lyrics are dense with references and double meanings. 'Kick, Push' is a love song about skateboarding.

synopsis: Lupe Fiasco had spent years as one of the most respected underground rappers in Chicago, and this debut album, released in 2006, brought his literate, socially conscious style to a wider audience. The record is one of the most intelligent rap albums ever made, full of references to history, philosophy and popular culture, and its lead single, 'Kick, Push', a song about skateboarding that became an unlikely hit, introduced his worldview. 'Daydreamin' and 'Hurt Me Soul' showed his range, and the album was nominated for a Grammy. It made Lupe the standard bearer for a new generation of conscious rap, an artist who proved that intelligence and commercial success were not opposites.

name: The Cool
teaser: 2007 Lupe Fiasco's second album expanded his debut's concept: 'Superstar', 'Paris, Tokyo', and 'The Cool' explore the characters he created. The album's production by Kanye West and others is cinematic. It is his most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album follows the characters Michael Young History and The Cool. 'Superstar' became his biggest hit.

synopsis: Lupe Fiasco had spent his debut album establishing himself as the most literate rapper of his generation, and this second record expanded on its themes. The album is built around a concept, the story of a man named The Cool who dies and is resurrected as a hustler, and its songs explore the seductions and dangers of the street life, from the anthemic 'Superstar' to the devastating 'The Coolest'. The record also contains 'Paris, Tokyo' and 'Hip-Hop Saved My Life', a celebration of the music that gave him purpose. It is a rare example of a concept album that works on every level, and it confirmed Lupe as one of the most ambitious artists in rap.

name: 808s & Heartbreak
