teaser: 2008 Kanye West's fourth album traded rapping for autotuned singing: 'Love Lockdown', 'Heartless', and 'Street Lights' are sparse and melancholic. The album's grief after his mother's death and his broken engagement defined it. It influenced a decade of emo rap.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the 808 drums and minimal synth pads created a new template for rap. 'Love Lockdown' has no chorus in the traditional sense.

synopsis: Kanye West had spent his first three albums establishing himself as the greatest producer and one of the greatest rappers of his generation, and this fourth record was a radical departure. Made in the aftermath of his mother's death and his broken engagement, the album trades rapping for Auto-Tuned singing, and its songs are built on the spare, cold production of 808 drums and electronic textures. 'Love Lockdown' and 'Heartless' became hits, and the album's centerpiece, 'Welcome to Heartbreak', is one of the most vulnerable songs ever made by a major rapper. It divided fans on release, but its influence has been enormous, reshaping the sound of pop and rap for the next decade.

name: Yeezus
teaser: 2013 Kanye West's sixth album is his most abrasive: 'Black Skinhead', 'New Slaves', and 'Blood on the Leaves' are industrial, confrontational, and brilliant. The album was produced in six weeks with a team including Daft Punk. It is his most divisive work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the textures — the album is built from industrial noise, punk energy, and minimalist beats. 'Black Skinhead' has no traditional chorus.

synopsis: Kanye West had spent his career making records of increasing grandeur, and this sixth album was his most abrasive and confrontational. The record is built on industrial beats, distorted vocals and some of the angriest raps of his career, and its songs, from 'Black Skinhead' to 'New Slaves' to 'Blood on the Leaves', are full of fury at racism, consumerism and the music industry. West rapped about his own arrogance and genius with a lack of filter that made the album both thrilling and uncomfortable. It debuted at number one and was hailed as a masterpiece by many critics, and its uncompromising vision confirmed West as the most unpredictable artist in pop.

name: The Life of Pablo
teaser: 2016 Kanye West's seventh album was revised and re-released repeatedly: 'Ultralight Beam', 'Famous', and 'Waves' are gospel, hip-hop, and chaos. The album's ever-changing nature was a statement about art in the streaming age. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the gospel — the album opens with church choir and Chance the Rapper. The tracklist changed even after release, a first for a major album.

synopsis: Kanye West had spent his career as a perfectionist who controlled every detail of his releases, but this seventh album was different: he was still tweaking it after its release, re-uploading new versions and changing track lists, a process that turned the album itself into a statement about art in the digital age. The record is a sprawling, gospel-inflected meditation on faith, family and fame, from the opener 'Ultralight Beam' to the controversial closer 'Saint Pablo', and its guest list, including Kendrick Lamar, Chance the Rapper and Rihanna, reads like a who's who of modern music. It is messy, contradictory and brilliant, the sound of an artist making it up as he goes.

name: Donda
teaser: 2021 Kanye West's tenth album was named for his late mother: 'Hurricane', 'Jail', and 'Moon' are gospel-tinged and grandiose. The album was unveiled at three listening events in stadiums. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the scale — the album is a two-hour gospel-rap epic. The listening events were as much performance art as music.

synopsis: Kanye West had spent years turning his concerts into church-like spectacles, and this tenth album, named for his late mother Donda West, was his most explicitly religious record. The album went through a legendary series of delays and revisions, including three stadium listening events that were streamed to millions, before its release, and its songs, from the opener 'Donda' to 'Hurricane' to 'Jail', are full of gospel choirs, prayers and West's struggles with faith and family. The record is sprawling and inconsistent, but its best moments are among the most powerful of his career, and its 27 tracks gave his fans more than enough to argue about. It is the sound of a genius in crisis, working it out in public.

name: Watch the Throne
teaser: 2011 Jay-Z and Kanye West's collaboration album is a celebration of success: 'N****s in Paris', 'Otis', and 'No Church in the Wild' are maximalist and luxurious. The album sold over a million copies and won three Grammys. 'Paris' became a live spectacle.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album features samples of Otis Redding and James Brown. The live performances of 'Paris' were legendary for their repeated encores.

synopsis: Jay-Z and Kanye West had spent a decade as friends, rivals and collaborators, and this joint album, released in 2011, was the summit of their partnership. The record is a celebration of success, full of songs about wealth, power and the cost of both, and its production, overseen by West with help from a team of producers, is among the most luxurious in rap history. 'Otis', built on an Otis Redding sample, 'Niggas in Paris', which became a live anthem, and 'No Church in the Wild' are highlights, and the album sold over a million copies in its first week. It is the sound of two legends at the top of their game, enjoying every minute of it.

name: Kids See Ghosts
teaser: 2018 Kanye West and Kid Cudi's collaboration is a seven-track meditation on mental health: 'Reborn', '4th Dimension', and 'Kids See Ghosts' are raw and redemptive. The album was recorded in Wyoming in a week. It is one of the most acclaimed releases of its year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arc — the album moves from chaos to peace. 'Reborn' is an anthem about recovery and growth.

synopsis: Kanye West and Kid Cudi had been friends and collaborators for years, with Cudi's singing style a major influence on West's music, and this joint album, released in 2018, was a product of their mutual healing. Both artists had been through very public struggles, West with his mental health and Cudi with his depression, and the record's seven tracks are a meditation on that journey, from 'Feel the Love' to the cathartic 'Reborn'. The album is full of the experimental, gospel-tinged production that defined West's late work, and Cudi's voice, floating over it all, gives the record a sense of peace. It was hailed as a return to form for both artists, a record about finding light in darkness.

name: Meddle
teaser: 1971 Pink Floyd's sixth album foreshadowed their masterpiece: 'Echoes', 'One of These Days', and 'Fearless' are atmospheric and ambitious. The 23-minute 'Echoes' closes the album with their most complete statement to that point. It is the bridge to Dark Side of the Moon.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Echoes' — the song's underwater guitar and slow build define the band's sound. The album was recorded in bits across many studios.

synopsis: Pink Floyd had spent the late 60s as Syd Barrett's band, and after his breakdown they were adrift, unsure whether they could continue. This sixth album, recorded in fits and starts over a year, found them rebuilding, and its centerpiece, 'Echoes', a 23-minute suite that takes up the entire second side, pointed the way to their future. The record also contains 'One of These Days', an instrumental built on a menacing bass riff, and 'Fearless', a gentle song with a Liverpool crowd singing 'You'll Never Walk Alone' at its end. It is a transitional record, but its best moments foreshadowed the greatness of Dark Side of the Moon, still two years away.

name: Obscured by Clouds
teaser: 1972 Pink Floyd's soundtrack for the film La Vallee is an underrated gem: 'Wot's... Uh the Deal', 'Childhood's End', and 'Free Four' are melodic and relaxed. The album was recorded during a pause in the Dark Side sessions. It is their most underrated record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songs — the album is more straightforward than their epics. 'Childhood's End' is the only Pink Floyd song to mention a UFO.

synopsis: Pink Floyd had been asked to write music for a French film called La Vallée, about a group of travelers searching for a lost valley in New Guinea, and this soundtrack, recorded quickly between their other projects, is one of the most underrated records of their career. The music is lighter and more melodic than their epic work, full of the acoustic textures and gentle songs that they rarely had room for elsewhere, and it features some of David Gilmour's most beautiful guitar playing. 'Wot's... Uh the Deal' and 'Childhood's End' are among the best songs they ever recorded. It is a record that many fans overlook, but it rewards attention, and it stands as a bridge between their early experimentation and their later mastery.

name: Atom Heart Mother
teaser: 1970 Pink Floyd's fifth album features the 23-minute title suite with a choir and orchestra: 'Atom Heart Mother', 'If', and 'Summer '68' show the band moving toward their epic sound. The album reached number one in the UK. It is a transitional work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title suite — its orchestral and choral sections were controversial among fans. The album's cow cover is among the most famous in music.

tracks.title: Alan's Psychedelic Breakfast" :I. "Rise and Shine (3:33) :II. "Sunny Side Up (4:12) :III. "Morning Glory

synopsis: Pink Floyd had spent the late 60s as one of the most experimental bands in Britain, and this fifth album was their most ambitious statement yet, built around a 23-minute title suite that took up the entire first side. The piece, scored for the band and a choir, moves through several movements, from a pastoral opening to a thundering climax, and its recording process, which involved dragging a piano into a field and recording it through a PA system, was typical of the band's willingness to try anything. The album was a hit in Britain, and while the band later disowned it, its ambition pointed the way to the epics that would make them legends. It is a fascinating artifact of a band finding its way.

name: A Saucerful of Secrets
teaser: 1968 Pink Floyd's second album was their first without Syd Barrett: 'Set the Controls for the Heart of the Sun', 'A Saucerful of Secrets', and 'Remember a Moment' show the band finding a new direction. The title track is a 12-minute instrumental epic. It is the beginning of their progressive era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — it builds from quiet murmurs to a full-band climax. The album was recorded as the band transformed.

tracks.title: Set the Controls for the Heart of the Sun
A Saucerful of Secrets :I. "Something Else (3:57) :II. "Syncopated Pandemonium (3:07) :III. "Storm Signal (1:34) :IV. "Celestial Voices

synopsis: Pink Floyd had been shattered by the departure of their founder Syd Barrett, whose mental illness had made him unable to continue, and this second album, their first without him, was made in the shadow of that loss. The band, now led by the bassist Roger Waters and the guitarist David Gilmour, had to reinvent themselves, and the album's centerpiece, the 12-minute title track, is a suite that moves from eerie calm to thunderous noise, a reflection of the chaos they had lived through. The rest of the record, from the gentle 'Remember a Moment' to the psychedelic 'See Emily Play' outtake 'Apples and Oranges', shows a band searching for a new identity. It is a difficult, transitional record, but it contains the seeds of their greatness.

name: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn
teaser: 1967 Pink Floyd's debut is the sound of Syd Barrett's psychedelic genius: 'Astronomy Domine', 'Interstellar Overdrive', and 'Bike' are playful, strange, and revolutionary. The album was recorded at Abbey Road while the Beatles worked on Sgt. Pepper. It is the definitive psychedelic record.

exploreAction.targetName: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn (1967) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Barrett's imagination — the songs mix nursery rhymes, space travel, and acid rock. The album's influence on psychedelia is immeasurable.

tracks.title: Take Up Thy Stethoscope and Walk

synopsis: Pink Floyd's debut album is the sound of Syd Barrett's psychedelic genius at its peak, a record that captured the spirit of London's underground scene in 1967. Barrett wrote nearly all of the songs, from the surreal 'Astronomy Domine' to the whimsical 'The Gnome' to the legendary 'Interstellar Overdrive', an improvised instrumental that became the band's live centerpiece, and his childlike imagination and gift for strange, beautiful melodies defined the record. It was a hit in Britain and made the band stars of the psychedelic movement, but Barrett's mental health was already deteriorating, and he would be gone from the band within a year. It is the sound of a genius at the moment of his greatest clarity.

name: A Momentary Lapse of Reason
teaser: 1987 Pink Floyd's first album without Roger Waters: 'Learning to Fly', 'On the Turning Away', and 'Sorrow' are polished and optimistic. David Gilmour led the band into a new era. The album sold 7 million copies.

exploreAction.targetName: A Momentary Lapse of Reason (1987) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded largely on a houseboat studio. 'Learning to Fly' is about Gilmour's new pilot's license.

synopsis: Pink Floyd had spent the decade after Dark Side of the Moon locked in a legal battle over the use of the band's name, and this album, the first made without Roger Waters, was David Gilmour's attempt to rebuild the group from the wreckage. The record is more polished and commercial than the band's epic work, and its lead single, 'Learning to Fly', about Gilmour's new passion for aviation, became a hit. 'On the Turning Away' and 'One Slip' showed the new direction, and while the album was criticized for lacking Waters' vision, it proved the band could survive without him. It is a record of rebirth, made by a band determined to carry on.

name: The Division Bell
teaser: 1994 Pink Floyd's final studio album: 'High Hopes', 'Marooned', and 'Take It Back' are atmospheric and elegiac. The album sold 12 million copies and won a Grammy for Best Rock Instrumental. It is a fitting farewell.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'High Hopes' — the song closes the album and the band's career with a sense of farewell. The album's title came from the gap between the band members.

tracks.title: What Do You Want from Me

synopsis: Pink Floyd's final studio album was made a decade after their last record, and it found the band, now reduced to David Gilmour, Nick Mason and Richard Wright, in a reflective mood. The record is full of songs about communication, or the lack of it, from the opener 'Cluster One' to the centerpiece 'High Hopes', a wistful look back at the band's early days that became their epitaph. 'Marooned' won a Grammy, and the album's title, a reference to the peace bell, captured its mood of reconciliation. It was a massive hit, debuting at number one around the world, and it stands as a gentle, elegiac farewell from a band that had spent three decades as giants of rock.

name: Led Zeppelin
teaser: 1969 Led Zeppelin's debut redefined rock with its heaviness: 'Good Times Bad Times', 'Dazed and Confused', and 'Communication Breakdown' are blues-rock at maximum power. The album was recorded in 36 hours on a budget of 1,780 pounds. It sold 10 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dynamics — the album's loud-quiet shifts were revolutionary. 'Dazed and Confused' was played live for over a decade.

synopsis: Led Zeppelin had spent years as session musicians and members of other bands, and when they came together in 1968, they had no idea they were about to change rock history. This debut album, recorded in a matter of days, introduced their formula of crushing riffs, wailing vocals and virtuoso musicianship, from the proto-metal of 'Good Times Bad Times' to the epic 'Dazed and Confused' to the folk-tinged 'Babe I'm Gonna Leave You'. Jimmy Page's guitar, Robert Plant's voice, John Paul Jones's bass and John Bonham's drums, the legendary 'Bonham beat', were all fully formed from the start. It redefined what rock could be, and its heaviness made it a founding document of heavy metal.

name: Led Zeppelin II
teaser: 1969 Led Zeppelin's second album was recorded while touring: 'Whole Lotta Love', 'Heartbreaker', and 'Ramble On' are riff-driven and raw. The album's heavy blues sound defined hard rock. It sold 12 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the riffs — the album is built on Jimmy Page's heaviest guitar work. 'Whole Lotta Love' was built on a Willie Dixon blues song.

tracks.title: What Is and What Should Never Be
Living Loving Maid (She's Just a Woman)

synopsis: Led Zeppelin had taken the world by storm with their debut, and this second album, recorded between tour dates in a series of studios across America, captured the band at its most ferocious. The record's centerpiece is 'Whole Lotta Love', built on one of the greatest riffs in rock history and a middle section of pure psychedelic chaos, and it also contains the blues of 'The Lemon Song', the epic 'Ramble On' and the frantic 'Moby Dick', a showcase for John Bonham's drumming. Jimmy Page's production, full of innovative recording techniques, gave the album a power that redefined what rock could sound like. It topped the charts on both sides of the Atlantic and made Zeppelin the biggest band in the world.

name: Led Zeppelin III
teaser: 1970 Led Zeppelin's third album surprised fans with acoustic songs: 'Immigrant Song', 'Since I've Been Loving You', and 'Tangerine' balance electric and folk. The album was recorded at a Welsh cottage. It is their most varied early work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — from the metal of 'Immigrant Song' to the folk of 'Tangerine'. The album's cover features hidden images when rotated.

synopsis: Led Zeppelin had spent a year as the heaviest band in rock, and this third album surprised everyone by opening with an acoustic guitar. Recorded at a cottage in Wales, where the band retreated to escape the madness of touring, the record alternates between the heavy rock of 'Immigrant Song' and 'Celebration Day' and the folk of 'Gallows Pole', 'That's the Way' and 'Tangerine', showing a depth that their critics had not expected. Page's production is more varied and subtle than before, and Robert Plant's lyrics, full of mythology and nature, matched the new direction. It was initially dismissed by fans who wanted more of the same, but it is now recognized as one of their most adventurous records.

name: Houses of the Holy
teaser: 1973 Led Zeppelin's fifth album expanded beyond hard rock: 'The Song Remains the Same', 'No Quarter', and 'The Rain Song' are progressive and epic. The album was their first without a title. It sold 11 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the textures — the album incorporates reggae, funk, and orchestral elements. 'No Quarter' is one of their most atmospheric songs.

tracks.title: Over the Hills and Far Away

synopsis: Led Zeppelin had spent their first four albums defining hard rock, and this fifth record found them expanding beyond it. The album is their most varied yet, from the reggae-tinged 'D'yer Mak'er' and the funk of 'The Crunge' to the gorgeous ballad 'The Rain Song' and the epic 'No Quarter', and it contains one of their most beloved songs, 'The Ocean'. The record also features 'The Song Remains the Same' and its companion piece 'The Rain Song', which open the album with a suite of extraordinary ambition. The band, now at the height of its fame, was free to experiment, and the result is one of the most adventurous records of its era.

name: Presence
teaser: 1976 Led Zeppelin's seventh album was recorded during Robert Plant's recovery from a car crash: 'Achilles Last Stand', 'Nobody's Fault but Mine', and 'For Your Life' are relentless and guitar-driven. The album is their most intense work. It divided critics but has aged well.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Achilles Last Stand' — the song's galloping rhythm and layered guitars are a masterclass. The album was recorded in just three weeks.

synopsis: Led Zeppelin had spent the mid-70s as the biggest band in the world, but this seventh album was made under terrible circumstances: Robert Plant was recovering from a car accident that had nearly killed him, and the band recorded in a rushed, tense atmosphere to keep their tour dates. The album's songs, written in the shadow of Plant's ordeal, are among the darkest and most direct of their career, from the relentless 'Achilles Last Stand', a nine-minute epic that many consider their greatest track, to the eerie 'Nobody's Fault but Mine'. It is a difficult, claustrophobic record, but its best moments are as powerful as anything they ever made. It stands as a testament to a band that would not be stopped.

name: In Through the Out Door
teaser: 1979 Led Zeppelin's final album: 'Fool in the Rain', 'All My Love', and 'I'm Gonna Crawl' show a band experimenting with keyboards and Latin rhythms. The album's packaging featured hidden images revealed by water. It sold 7 million copies despite mixed reviews.

exploreAction.targetName: In Through the Out Door (1979) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experimentation — John Paul Jones's keyboards dominate the album. 'Fool in the Rain' features a samba section that showed their range.

synopsis: Led Zeppelin's final album was recorded in 1978, a year after their last record, and it found the band, now reduced to a shell of its former self, struggling to find its way. The album was dominated by John Paul Jones, who contributed the record's best songs, including the jazzy 'Fool in the Rain' and the beautiful 'All My Love', a tribute written by Plant for his young son who had died the year before. The band was falling apart, with John Bonham's drinking out of control, and the record has a tired, elegiac quality. It was a massive hit, but within a year Bonham was dead and the band was finished. It stands as a gentle, melancholy farewell from giants.

name: Coda
teaser: 1982 Led Zeppelin's posthumous collection of outtakes: 'We're Gonna Groove', 'I Can't Quit You Baby', and 'Wearing and Tearing' are raw and unfinished. The album was released after John Bonham's death. It is a coda in the musical sense — a closing passage.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the raw takes — the album captures the band's live energy. 'Wearing and Tearing' was written in response to punk.

synopsis: When Led Zeppelin broke up in 1980 after the death of drummer John Bonham, they left behind a mountain of unreleased recordings, and this collection, released in 1982, gathered the best of what remained. The record includes 'We're Gonna Groove', a live favorite, the blues of 'I Can't Quit You Baby' and the epic 'Wearing and Tearing', which was written for the Knebworth shows, and it also features the instrumental 'Bonzo's Montreux', a showcase for Bonham's drumming recorded shortly before his death. The album was assembled by the surviving members as a tribute and a farewell, and its title, the musical term for a concluding passage, was fitting. It is the last word from one of the greatest bands in rock history.

name: Fleetwood Mac
teaser: 1975 Fleetwood Mac's self-titled album with newcomers Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks transformed the band: 'Rhiannon', 'Landslide', and 'Say You Love Me' are California pop-rock at its best. The album sold 5 million copies and launched their golden era. It is the perfect introduction to the band.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — Buckingham and Nicks added a new dimension to the band's sound. 'Rhiannon' was inspired by Welsh mythology.

synopsis: Fleetwood Mac had spent the late 60s as one of the most successful blues bands in Britain, but by 1974 they were in crisis, with their founding members gone and their manager pushing them to find a new sound. The solution came when Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks, a young couple from California, joined the band, and this album, their first with the new lineup, was the beginning of their transformation. The record mixes the band's blues roots with the pop sensibilities of the newcomers, and its best songs, including Buckingham's 'Monday Morning' and Nicks's 'Rhiannon', pointed the way to the superstardom that was just two years away. It is the sound of a band being reborn.

name: Then Play On
teaser: 1969 Fleetwood Mac's third album is their last with Peter Green: 'Oh Well', 'Rattlesnake Shake', and 'Coming Your Way' are blues-rock at its most inventive. The album marks the end of the band's original era. It is a bridge between blues and rock.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Oh Well' — its flamenco-style guitar section was revolutionary for a blues band. The album's title reflects the band's improvisational approach.

synopsis: Fleetwood Mac had spent their first two albums as one of the most successful blues bands in Britain, and this third record, their last with the founding guitarist Peter Green, found them expanding beyond the blues. Green, who was struggling with mental illness and drug use, contributed the record's best songs, including the haunting 'Oh Well' and the instrumental 'The Green Manalishi', and the band's new members, including Danny Kirwan and Jeremy Spencer, pushed them toward a more melodic sound. It is a transitional record, caught between the blues band they had been and the pop band they would become, and its best moments show a band of extraordinary talent beginning to fragment. Green left the band shortly after its release.

name: Kiln House
teaser: 1970 Fleetwood Mac's fourth album without Peter Green: 'Station Man', 'Jewel Eyed Judy', and 'This Is the Rock' are rockabilly and blues. The band carried on with guitarist Jeremy Spencer and Danny Kirwan. The album is transitional but charming.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the rockabilly — the album is lighter than the band's blues work. The cover art features a famous pinup illustration.

tracks.title: Tell Me All the Things You Do

synopsis: Fleetwood Mac had been shattered by the departure of their leader Peter Green, whose mental illness had made him unable to continue, and this fourth album was their attempt to rebuild. The band, now led by the guitarists Danny Kirwan and Jeremy Spencer, retreated to a more stripped-down sound, and the record's songs, from the rocking 'Station Man' to the delicate 'Jewel-Eyed Judy', showed a band searching for a new identity. The album is best known for its cover art, a series of paintings by Spencer, and it sold modestly, but it kept the band alive through its darkest period. It is a record of survival, made by a band determined not to let its founder's tragedy end its story.

name: Rubber Soul
teaser: 1965 The Beatles' sixth album raised pop's ambitions: 'Norwegian Wood', 'In My Life', and 'Nowhere Man' are literate and introspective. The album's folk-rock sound and studio craft influenced everyone from the Beach Boys to Dylan. It is the album where the Beatles became artists.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — 'In My Life' is one of the greatest songs ever written, with its harpsichord-style piano solo. The album was recorded in a month.

synopsis: The Beatles had spent 1965 at the peak of Beatlemania, but they were growing tired of the endless touring and hungry for something more, and this sixth album captured that restlessness. Recorded quickly between tour dates, the record shows Paul McCartney and John Lennon beginning to experiment, from the sitar on 'Norwegian Wood', one of the first uses of the instrument in pop, to the surreal lyrics of 'Nowhere Man'. The album also contains 'In My Life', one of the greatest songs Lennon ever wrote, and its blend of folk, rock and new sounds raised pop's ambitions. Bob Dylan reportedly played it for the Byrds and told them to listen to the lyrics. It is the album where the Beatles began their transformation from pop stars into artists.

name: Help!
teaser: 1965 The Beatles' fifth album is a bridge from their pop era to their artistic peak: 'Help!', 'Ticket to Ride', and 'Yesterday' show growing sophistication. 'Yesterday' features a string quartet, a first for the band. The album accompanied their second film.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Yesterday' — Paul McCartney's ballad with a string quartet was a pop first. The album marks the start of the Beatles' most creative period.

tracks.title: You've Got to Hide Your Love Away
You're Going to Lose That Girl

synopsis: The Beatles' fifth album was recorded in early 1965, between their film Help! and their second appearance on Ed Sullivan, and it captures the band in transition. The record is a bridge from their early pop era to the artistic ambitions of Rubber Soul, with the title track, written for the film, showing their new confidence, and 'Ticket to Ride' and 'You've Got to Hide Your Love Away' pointing toward deeper waters. The album also contains their version of 'Yesterday', a song so famous it barely needs introduction, and its blend of pop and experimentation made it a massive hit. It is the sound of a band on the verge of its greatest period.

name: Beatles for Sale
teaser: 1964 The Beatles' fourth album leans country and rockabilly: 'Eight Days a Week', 'I'll Follow the Sun', and 'No Reply' are melodic and assured. The album was recorded between tours. It shows the band's versatility beyond Beatlemania.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the country influence — the album includes covers of Carl Perkins and Buddy Holly. 'Eight Days a Week' was their first song with a fade-in.

tracks.title: I Don't Want to Spoil the Party
Everybody's Trying to Be My Baby

synopsis: The Beatles had spent 1964 conquering America, but by the end of the year they were exhausted, and this fourth album, recorded between tours, found them leaning on their roots. The record is full of country and rockabilly songs, both covers like 'Rock and Roll Music' and originals like 'I'll Follow the Sun' and 'Baby's in Black', and it shows the band retreating to the music they had grown up on. John Lennon later dismissed the album, calling it a collection of leftovers, but it contains some gems, including 'Eight Days a Week' and 'No Reply'. It is the sound of the biggest band in the world taking a breather, and it remains a fan favorite.

name: A Hard Day's Night
teaser: 1964 The Beatles' third album is the only one with all original songs: 'A Hard Day's Night', 'Can't Buy Me Love', and 'And I Love Her' are confident and catchy. The album accompanied their film of the same name. It is Beatlemania at its peak.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the opening chord — the album's first chord has been analyzed by musicians for decades. The film made the band global icons.

tracks.title: I'm Happy Just to Dance with You

synopsis: The Beatles had conquered Britain and were about to conquer America when they recorded this, their third album, and it is the only one of their records to consist entirely of original songs. Written to accompany their first film, the record was composed in a burst of creativity that John Lennon later called their 'purest' period, and its title track and 'Can't Buy Me Love' became anthems. The album also contains 'And I Love Her' and 'Things We Said Today', and its confidence and energy captured the moment when Beatlemania was at its peak. It was a massive hit around the world, and its all-original song list was a first in pop history.

name: With the Beatles
teaser: 1963 The Beatles' second album mixed originals with covers: 'All My Loving', 'It Won't Be Long', and 'Please Mr. Postman' show their R&B roots. The album's stark black-and-white cover was iconic. It spent 21 weeks at number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — the band's versions of Motown and girl-group songs reveal their influences. 'All My Loving' became a live staple.

tracks.title: You Really Got a Hold on Me

synopsis: The Beatles had become the biggest phenomenon in Britain with their debut, and this second album, recorded in the fall of 1963, was rushed out to capitalize on their success. The record mixes eight originals with six covers, from the R&B of 'Please Mr. Postman' to the Motown of 'You Really Got a Hold on Me', and its original songs, including 'All My Loving', 'It Won't Be Long' and 'I Wanna Be Your Man', showed the band's rapid growth as writers. The album's cover, with the band's faces half in shadow, became iconic, and its success in Britain, where it topped the charts for 21 weeks, was unprecedented. It is the sound of a band at the start of its reign, still finding its voice but already extraordinary.

name: Please Please Me
teaser: 1963 The Beatles' debut was recorded in a single day: 'I Saw Her Standing There', 'Love Me Do', and 'Twist and Shout' capture the band's raw live energy. The album launched Beatlemania. It spent 30 weeks at number one in the UK.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — 'Twist and Shout' was recorded last, when John Lennon's voice was nearly gone. The album was recorded in 585 minutes.

tracks.title: Do You Want to Know a Secret

synopsis: The Beatles recorded their debut album in a single marathon day in February 1963, knocking out ten songs in under ten hours between live appearances, and the record captures the raw energy of the band's early live shows. The album mixes original songs like 'I Saw Her Standing There' and 'Love Me Do' with covers of the R&B and rock and roll songs that had shaped them, from 'Twist and Shout' to 'Boys', and the band's enthusiasm is infectious. It topped the British charts and stayed there for 30 weeks, and its blend of wit, charm and pure rock and roll energy made it one of the most influential debut albums in history. It is the sound of a revolution beginning.

name: The Beatles
teaser: 1968 The Beatles' White Album is a double album of the band pulling apart: 'While My Guitar Gently Weeps', 'Blackbird', and 'Helter Skelter' show four solo careers in one record. The album's minimalist white cover was a reaction to Sgt. Pepper's excess. It is their most diverse work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — from the folk of 'Blackbird' to the metal of 'Helter Skelter'. Each member wrote alone, making it a collection of four voices.

tracks.title: The Continuing Story of Bungalow Bill
Why Don't We Do It in the Road?
Everybody's Got Something to Hide Except Me and My Monkey

synopsis: The Beatles recorded this sprawling double album in 1968, during the most turbulent year of their lives, and it is a document of a band pulling apart in real time. The record's thirty songs range from the raw rock of 'Back in the U.S.S.R.' and 'Helter Skelter' to the tenderness of 'Blackbird' and 'Julia' to the avant-garde noise of 'Revolution 9', and they were recorded separately, with each Beatle bringing in his own songs while the others drifted in and out. Ringo briefly quit during the sessions, and the friction is audible. It is messy, inconsistent and endlessly fascinating, the sound of four geniuses who had outgrown the band that made them famous.

teaser: 2000 The Beatles' compilation of all 27 of their UK number-one singles: 'Hey Jude', 'Yesterday', and 'Let It Be' trace their entire career. The album sold 31 million copies, making it the best-selling album of the 2000s. It is the definitive Beatles introduction.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the evolution — from 'Love Me Do' to 'The Long and Winding Road', the compilation shows the band's transformation. The album was remastered from the original tapes.

tracks.title: I Want to Hold Your Hand
The Ballad of John and Yoko

synopsis: The Beatles had spent the 60s as the most successful band in history, and this compilation, released in 2000, gathered all 27 of their UK number-one singles into a single record. The track list is a document of the most extraordinary run in pop history, from 'Love Me Do' and 'I Want to Hold Your Hand' through 'Hey Jude' and 'Let It Be', and listening to it in sequence is like watching the 60s unfold in an hour. The album sold over 30 million copies, reintroducing the Beatles to a new generation, and its simple, elegant presentation, with no liner notes or extras, let the music speak for itself. It is the essential Beatles collection, a single disc that contains more greatness than most artists' entire catalogs.

name: Smile
teaser: 2011 The Beach Boys' legendary unfinished album, finally released: 'Good Vibrations', 'Heroes and Villains', and 'Surf's Up' are Brian Wilson's most ambitious work. The album was abandoned in 1967 and reconstructed decades later. It is pop's greatest lost masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the studio craft — the album's fragments were assembled from hours of sessions. 'Good Vibrations' alone took six months and cost $50,000.

tracks.title: I Love to Say Da Da
Old Master Painter" / "You Are My Sunshine
Child Is Father of the Man
I'm in Great Shape" / "I Wanna Be Around" / "Workshop

synopsis: The Beach Boys had been forced to abandon their legendary Smile album in 1967 after Brian Wilson's breakdown, and for decades its fragments haunted the band and their fans. This album, finally assembled and completed in 2011 from the original sessions, is the closest we will ever come to hearing what Wilson had planned. The record includes the masterpiece 'Good Vibrations', 'Heroes and Villains', 'Surf's Up' and the extraordinary 'Cabinessence', and its suite-like structure and lyrical themes of America, childhood and innocence show how far Wilson had pushed pop music. It was hailed on release as one of the greatest albums ever made, a lost masterpiece finally found. It is the sound of a genius's vision, restored at last.

name: Sunflower
teaser: 1970 The Beach Boys' first album on their own label: 'Add Some Music to Your Day', 'This Whole World', and 'Forever' are warm and beautifully arranged. The album was a critical favorite that sold poorly. It is now regarded as one of their best.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the album features some of the band's most intricate vocal arrangements. 'Forever' was later covered by Dennis Wilson's friends.

tracks.title: Add Some Music to Your Day

synopsis: The Beach Boys had spent the 60s as one of the biggest bands in the world, but by 1970 they were in crisis, with Brian Wilson's mental health failing and their label dropping them. This album, their first on their own label, was a fresh start, and it found the band, now led by the brothers Carl and Dennis Wilson, making some of the most beautiful music of their career. Songs like 'Add Some Music to Your Day' and 'Forever' showed a new warmth and maturity, and the album's harmonies were as gorgeous as anything they had recorded. It sold poorly, but it has since been recognized as one of the great lost albums of the era, a record of gentle, heartfelt beauty made by a band fighting for survival.

name: Holland
teaser: 1973 The Beach Boys' ambitious album was recorded in the Netherlands: 'Sail On, Sailor', 'California Saga', and 'Funky Pretty' are sprawling and adventurous. The album was a modest hit and a critical favorite. It is the end of their classic era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sail On, Sailor' — the song's build is one of the band's best. The album was recorded at a Dutch studio the band had to build themselves.

synopsis: The Beach Boys had been asked to perform in the Netherlands, and they decided to record their next album there, setting up in a studio in Amsterdam and writing new songs on the spot. The record that resulted is one of their most ambitious, full of the orchestral arrangements and studio experimentation that Brian Wilson had pioneered, and its centerpiece, 'Sail On, Sailor', with its soulful lead vocal by the session singer Blondie Chaplin, became one of their most beloved songs. The album also contains 'The Trader' and 'California Saga', and its Dutch sojourn gave it a sense of adventure. It sold modestly but has since been recognized as one of the best records of their later period.

teaser: 1969 The Beach Boys' album assembled unreleased tracks: 'Do It Again', 'I Can Hear Music', and 'Bluebirds over the Mountain' are polished pop. The album was the last with Brian Wilson's full participation for years. It closed the 60s for the band.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — the album includes a version of Phil Spector's 'I Can Hear Music'. The tracklist was assembled from scattered sessions.

synopsis: The Beach Boys had spent the late 60s in disarray, with Brian Wilson's Smile project abandoned and the band struggling to find direction, and this album, their first of the new decade, gathered a collection of unreleased and half-finished tracks. The record's best songs, including 'Do It Again', a nostalgic return to their surf roots that became a hit, and 'I Can Hear Music', a beautiful cover produced by Carl Wilson, showed that the band could still make magic. The album is uneven, a patchwork of sessions from different eras, but its best moments are as good as anything they recorded. It is a transitional record, but it kept the band alive into the new decade.

name: Friends
teaser: 1968 The Beach Boys' gentle album of domestic bliss: 'Friends', 'Busy Doin' Nothin'', and 'Little Bird' are soft and experimental. The album was a commercial flop but a critical favorite. It is the band's most understated work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the calm — the album is a retreat from the psychedelic excess of the era. The recording sessions were some of the band's most relaxed.

tracks.title: When a Man Needs a Woman

synopsis: The Beach Boys had spent 1967 in chaos, with Brian Wilson's Smile project collapsing and the band scrambling to find a new direction, and this gentle, domestic album was their quiet answer. The record is full of songs about home, family and simple pleasures, from the title track to 'Busy Doin' Nothin'' and 'Diamond Head', and its warmth was a deliberate retreat from the psychedelic excesses of the era. Wilson produced the album himself, and its understated beauty has made it a favorite of connoisseurs. It sold poorly on release, but it has since been recognized as one of the most charming and personal records of the band's career.

name: Wild Honey
teaser: 1967 The Beach Boys' stripped-back album of R&B covers and originals: 'Wild Honey', 'Darlin'', and 'Mama Says' are funky and direct. The album was recorded at home in two months. It was a reaction to the complexity of Smile.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the simplicity — the album was recorded on a home tape machine. 'Darlin'' became a favorite live song.

tracks.title: I Was Made to Love Her
I'd Love Just Once to See You

synopsis: The Beach Boys had spent the previous year making the most ambitious music of their career, and this stripped-back album was a deliberate reaction against that complexity. Recorded quickly at home, the record is full of R&B covers and simple, soulful originals, from the title track, a cover of a Stevie Wonder song, to Wilson's own 'Darlin'' and 'Country Air'. The band sounds relaxed and joyful, and the album's lack of pretension is its strength. It sold modestly, but it has since been recognized as a return to the band's roots, a record of pure, unadorned pop made by a band recovering from its own ambition.

name: Smiley Smile
teaser: 1967 The Beach Boys' album released in place of Smile: 'Good Vibrations', 'Heroes and Villains', and 'She's Goin' Bald' are strange and beautiful. The album baffled fans at release but has grown in reputation. It is the sound of an unfinished masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the weirdness — the album's stripped-down versions of Smile songs sound like demos from another dimension. 'Good Vibrations' became their biggest hit.

tracks.title: Fall Breaks and Back to Winter (W. Woodpecker Symphony)

synopsis: The Beach Boys had spent years working on Brian Wilson's masterpiece Smile, only to abandon it in 1967, and this album, released in its place, has long been seen as a disappointment. But the record contains some of the most extraordinary music the band ever made, including 'Good Vibrations', Wilson's psychedelic masterpiece, and a version of 'Heroes and Villains', and its strange, homemade sound, full of tape effects and odd transitions, was ahead of its time. The band's label and fans were confused by it, and it sold poorly, but its influence has been enormous, and it is now seen as a fascinating document of a genius's breakdown. It is the sound of an album that never was, and the one that took its place.

name: The Beach Boys Today!
teaser: 1965 The Beach Boys' album marked their artistic leap: 'California Girls', 'When I Grow Up', and 'Please Let Me Wonder' are sophisticated and personal. The album's second side was all ballads, a first for rock. It is their transition to genius.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — Brian Wilson's production and lyrics matured dramatically. 'California Girls' is one of the most famous intros in pop.

tracks.title: When I Grow Up (To Be a Man)
In the Back of My Mind

synopsis: The Beach Boys had spent their early career as a surf band, but this 1965 album marked their artistic leap into maturity. The record's centerpiece is 'California Girls', one of the greatest songs of the decade, and it also contains 'Please Let Me Wonder', 'She Knows Me Too Well' and the devastating 'In the Back of My Mind', all of which showed Brian Wilson's growing sophistication as a songwriter and producer. The album was recorded as Wilson was beginning to use the studio as an instrument, layering vocals and instruments in ways that pointed toward Pet Sounds. It is the record where the Beach Boys stopped being a surf band and became the most important group in American pop.

name: All Summer Long
teaser: 1964 The Beach Boys' album of summer songs: 'I Get Around', 'All Summer Long', and 'Wendy' are sunny and sophisticated. The album spent five weeks at number one. It is the peak of their early surf era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the band's vocal blend was unmatched. 'I Get Around' was their first number-one single.

synopsis: The Beach Boys had conquered the world with their surf songs, and this 1964 album, their fourth, was the peak of that era. The record is full of summer anthems, from 'I Get Around', their first number one, to 'All Summer Long' and 'Little Honda', and its songs about cars, girls and the beach captured the California dream at its most innocent. Brian Wilson's production was growing more sophisticated, with layered harmonies and inventive arrangements that pointed toward his future masterpieces. It was a massive hit, and its title captured the band's whole worldview: a permanent summer of fun, sun and endless good times.

name: Surfer Girl
teaser: 1963 The Beach Boys' third album features their first self-produced single: 'Surfer Girl', 'Catch a Wave', and 'The Surfer Moon' are gentle and harmonic. The album shows Brian Wilson's growing studio ambition. It is a milestone of surf pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its melody was inspired by a song Wilson heard in a dream. The album's production shows his early genius.

tracks.title: South Bay Surfer (The Old Folks at Home)

synopsis: The Beach Boys' third album was their first to be produced entirely by Brian Wilson, who took over from the label's session producers, and it marked his emergence as a studio visionary. The record's centerpiece is 'Surfer Girl', a beautiful ballad that Wilson wrote as a teenager, and it also contains 'Catch a Wave', 'The Surfer Moon' and their version of 'The Lord's Prayer'. The album's harmonies, led by Wilson's increasingly sophisticated arrangements, were the most advanced in pop, and its blend of surf rock and balladry made it a hit. It is the record where the band's leader began to become a genius.

name: Surfin' U.S.A.
teaser: 1963 The Beach Boys' second album of surf anthems: 'Surfin' U.S.A.', 'Shut Down', and 'Surfer's Rule' are energetic and catchy. The album's title track borrowed Chuck Berry's melody. It made the band national stars.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album captures the surf craze at its peak. 'Surfin' U.S.A.' was a top-five hit.

synopsis: The Beach Boys' second album, released just months after their debut, found them consolidating their success and refining their sound. The record's centerpiece is the title track, an anthem that became their signature song, and it also contains 'Shut Down', a song about drag racing, and 'Farmer's Daughter', and its mix of surf rock and car songs captured the Southern California youth culture that the band embodied. The album sold well, and its success established the Beach Boys as the most popular band in America, the only group that could rival the Beatles. It is the sound of a phenomenon taking hold.

name: Surfin' Safari
teaser: 1962 The Beach Boys' debut captured the California surf scene: 'Surfin' Safari', '409', and 'Ten Little Indians' are energetic and naive. The album made the band local heroes. It is the beginning of the surf rock era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the innocence — the album is a time capsule of early 60s California. '409' celebrates the engine of a Chevy.

synopsis: The Beach Boys' debut album captured the sound of the Southern California surf scene in 1962, and it introduced the world to the most important American band of the decade. The record's title track, which the Wilson brothers had written as teenagers, became a hit, and the album's blend of surf rock, vocal harmonies and teenage energy made it a sensation. Brian Wilson, only 20, was already showing the arranging genius that would define his career, and the band's harmonies were unlike anything in rock. It is a record of pure, innocent fun, the sound of a movement beginning, and its influence on everything that followed is incalculable.

name: Brian Wilson
teaser: 2004 Brian Wilson's long-awaited solo album finally matched his legend: 'Love and Mercy', 'Gettin' in Over My Head', and 'Good Timin'' are warm and redemptive. The album was released after decades of struggle. It was his first fully realized solo work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was produced with members of the Wondermints. 'Love and Mercy' became his anthem of hope.

tracks.title: Baby Let Your Hair Grow Long
Meet Me in My Dreams Tonight

synopsis: Brian Wilson had spent thirty years as rock's most famous broken genius, the man who made Pet Sounds and then fell apart, and this solo album, his first in decades, was his attempt to finally match his legend. The record was produced with a team of young musicians who worshipped him, and its songs, mostly collaborations with his therapist and various writers, are full of reflections on his life, his music and his long struggle with mental illness. The album's centerpiece, a reworking of the Smile song 'Love and Mercy', became his anthem, and its release marked the beginning of his long-overdue rehabilitation. It is the sound of a legend coming home.

name: Frank
teaser: 2003 Amy Winehouse's debut introduced her retro soul sound: 'Stronger Than Me', 'Take the Box', and 'Fuck Me Pumps' are jazzy and sharp. The album won a Brit Award and a Mercury Prize nomination. It showcased her voice and songwriting before her fame.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the jazz — the album's production is more understated than her later work. The lyrics are witty and confessional.

tracks.title: Amy Amy Amy / "Outro" / "Brother (hidden track) / "Mr Magic (Through the Smoke)
Amy Amy Amy / "Outro" / "Moody's Mood for Love (hidden track) / "Know You Now

synopsis: Amy Winehouse had grown up in London listening to her parents' record collection, and this debut album, released when she was 19, introduced her extraordinary voice and her love of classic soul. The record's blend of jazz, soul and hip-hop was unlike anything else in British pop, and its songs, from the confessional 'Stronger Than Me' to the swinging 'Take the Box', showed a young woman with the voice of a 60s soul singer and the sensibility of a modern one. The album was nominated for the Mercury Prize, and while it sold modestly, it established Winehouse as the most exciting new voice in Britain. It is the sound of a talent that was just beginning to flower.

name: Lioness: Hidden Treasures
teaser: 2011 Amy Winehouse's posthumous collection of unreleased songs: 'Our Day Will Come', 'Between the Cheats', and 'Half Time' show her range beyond the hits. The album was compiled by her friends and producers. It is a bittersweet final document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the outtakes — the album includes early versions and unreleased gems. 'Our Day Will Come' was a 1963 pop song she made her own.

tracks.title: Will You Still Love Me Tomorrow?

synopsis: Amy Winehouse had died in 2011 at the age of 27, leaving behind a legend and a mountain of unreleased recordings, and this collection, assembled by her family and label, gathered the best of what remained. The record includes 'Our Day Will Come', a reggae-tinged cover that became a posthumous hit, and a series of demos and outtakes from the Back to Black sessions, all showing the extraordinary voice that had made her a star. The album is a bittersweet document, a reminder of what was lost, and its title, taken from a song about a woman waiting for her man, captures the melancholy of her story. It is a farewell from one of the greatest voices of her generation.

name: In the Lonely Hour
teaser: 2014 Sam Smith's debut made heartbreak a global anthem: 'Stay with Me', 'I'm Not the Only One', and 'Lay Me Down' are soulful and sad. The album won four Grammys including Best Pop Vocal Album. It sold 12 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the emotion — Smith's voice carries the album's ache. 'Stay with Me' was written about a one-night stand.

synopsis: Sam Smith had spent their early career as a featured vocalist on dance tracks, but this debut album, released when they were 22, made them a star in their own right. The record is built on Smith's extraordinary voice, a high, aching instrument that can break your heart with a single note, and its songs are almost all about unrequited love and loneliness. 'Stay with Me' became a global anthem, and 'I'm Not the Only One' and 'Lay Me Down' showed the same gift for turning pain into beauty. The album sold over 12 million copies and won four Grammys, and its confessional intimacy made Smith the voice of a generation of the heartbroken.

name: Divide
teaser: 2017 Ed Sheeran's third album is a global smash: 'Shape of You', 'Castle on the Hill', and 'Perfect' blend pop, folk, and R&B. The album sold 26 million copies and was the best-selling album of 2017. 'Shape of You' became one of the most-streamed songs ever.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Benny Blanco and Steve Mac crafted radio-perfect hooks. The album's emotional songs became wedding staples.

synopsis: Ed Sheeran had spent years building his following one acoustic show at a time, and this third album, released in 2017, was the payoff, becoming one of the best-selling records in history. The album's lead single, 'Shape of You', with its dancehall groove, became one of the biggest songs of the decade, and 'Castle on the Hill' and 'Galway Girl' showed his range. The record sold over 30 million copies, and its blend of pop, folk, rap and R&B made Sheeran the most commercially successful artist of his generation. It is a record of pure, relentless populism, made by a songwriter with an uncanny gift for writing songs the whole world wants to hear.

name: Sweetener
teaser: 2018 Ariana Grande's fourth album processed grief into pop: 'God Is a Woman', 'Breathin'', and 'No Tears Left to Cry' are buoyant and vulnerable. The album won a Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album. It marked her artistic maturation.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Pharrell Williams contributed several tracks with his signature sound. 'No Tears Left to Cry' was her first song after the Manchester bombing.

synopsis: Ariana Grande had spent her career as a pop princess, but this fourth album was made in the aftermath of the Manchester Arena bombing at her concert, and it found her processing grief in public. The record's title, a reference to her own journey toward happiness, captures its mood, and its songs, from the soaring 'God Is a Woman' to the vulnerable 'Breathin' and the Pharrell-produced 'Sweetener', are full of her extraordinary voice and her determination to find light in darkness. The album won a Grammy, its first for Grande, and its blend of pop, R&B and trap showed her evolution as an artist. It is the sound of a survivor, refusing to be defined by tragedy.

name: Thank U, Next
teaser: 2019 Ariana Grande's fifth album was recorded in two weeks: 'Thank U, Next', '7 Rings', and 'Break Up with Your Girlfriend' are confident and personal. The album debuted at number one and its title track broke streaming records. It is her most honest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded quickly, giving it a raw energy. '7 Rings' samples the Sound of Music's 'My Favorite Things'.

tracks.title: Break Up with Your Girlfriend, I'm Bored

synopsis: Ariana Grande had spent 2018 reeling from the Manchester bombing at her concert and the death of her ex-boyfriend Mac Miller, and she channeled all of it into this album, her fifth, which she recorded in just two weeks with producers including Tommy Brown and Max Martin. The record is her most direct and personal, from the title track, a letter to her exes that became her first number one without a feature, to the devastating 'Ghostin', about grieving Miller while in a new relationship. It debuted at number one and won a Grammy, and its raw honesty, delivered in her extraordinary voice, made it her most acclaimed work. It is the sound of a superstar processing trauma in real time.

name: Positions
teaser: 2020 Ariana Grande's sixth album explores intimacy and lockdown life: 'Positions', '34+35', and 'POV' are smooth and playful. The album debuted at number one. It is her most mature and mellow work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends trap, R&B, and pop seamlessly. 'POV' closes the album with vulnerability.

synopsis: Ariana Grande recorded this album during the pandemic, mostly at home with her then-boyfriend Dalton Gomez, and its title and songs reflect that intimate, locked-down setting. The record is her most sexually explicit and playful, full of songs about domestic bliss and desire, and its blend of R&B, trap and pop, led by the title track and '34+35', showed a new side of her artistry. Grande also stepped into the producer's chair for the first time, and the album's warm, understated production was a departure from her earlier pop maximalism. It debuted at number one, her fifth in a row, and its cozy, horny mood captured the strange intimacy of lockdown life.

name: Eternal Sunshine
teaser: 2024 Ariana Grande's seventh album is a confessional return: 'Yes, And?', 'We Can't Be Friends', and 'The Boy Is Mine' are danceable and direct. The album was inspired by the film of the same name. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the dance influences — the album blends 90s house with modern pop. 'We Can't Be Friends' was a global hit.

synopsis: Ariana Grande titled this album after the 2004 film Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, and its songs, inspired by the end of her marriage, explore the same territory: the pain of erasing a love from your memory versus the ache of keeping it. The record is a confessional return to her pop roots, full of soaring ballads and dance tracks, and its lead single, 'Yes, And?', a house-inspired anthem about ignoring the gossip, set the tone. 'We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)' and 'Bye' became hits, and the album debuted at number one, her sixth consecutive chart-topper. It is the sound of a pop star processing heartbreak with wit, warmth and total vocal command.

name: Yours Truly
teaser: 2013 Ariana Grande's debut introduced her as pop's new voice: 'The Way', 'Baby I', and 'Tattooed Heart' blend doo-wop and R&B. The album was recorded over three years with multiple producers. It set the stage for her superstardom.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the vocals — Grande's four-octave range is on full display. 'The Way' with Mac Miller was her breakthrough single.

synopsis: Ariana Grande had spent her teenage years on Broadway and Nickelodeon, and this debut album, released when she was 20, introduced her to the pop world as a fully formed vocalist. The record is built on her astonishing voice, a four-octave instrument with a whistle register that drew immediate comparisons to Mariah Carey, and its blend of pop, R&B and doo-wop, led by the hit 'The Way' with Mac Miller, was a breath of fresh air. The album also contains the ballad 'Honeymoon Avenue' and the soaring 'Tattooed Heart', and it debuted at number one, making Grande the fifteenth female artist to top the charts with a debut. It is the sound of a generational voice arriving.

name: My Everything
teaser: 2014 Ariana Grande's second album expanded her sound: 'Problem', 'Break Free', and 'Love Me Harder' are electro-pop anthems. The album debuted at number one and produced four top-ten singles. It made her a global star.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Max Martin and Zedd contributed to the album. 'Break Free' with Zedd became a dance anthem.

tracks.title: Just a Little Bit of Your Heart

synopsis: Ariana Grande had spent her debut establishing herself as pop's most exciting new voice, and this second album, released a year later, expanded her sound into full pop territory. The record's lead single, 'Problem', with its saxophone hook and Iggy Azalea verse, became one of the biggest songs of 2014, and 'Break Free' and 'Bang Bang' continued the run of dance-pop anthems. The album also showed her ballad side with 'My Everything' and 'Just a Little Bit of Your Heart', and its production, from Max Martin and others, was bigger and glossier than her debut. It debuted at number one and made Grande, still only 21, one of the most reliable hitmakers in pop.

name: Dangerous Woman
teaser: 2016 Ariana Grande's third album is her most confident: 'Dangerous Woman', 'Into You', and 'Side to Side' are sleek and seductive. The album debuted at number two and produced several hits. It is her artistic peak of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends pop, R&B, and dance with polish. 'Into You' is often cited as her best single.

synopsis: Ariana Grande had spent her first two albums as pop's sweetheart, and this third record, her first without her signature ponytail on the cover, marked her transformation into a confident, sexual adult artist. The album is her most cohesive and assured, from the title track's smoky declaration of independence to the trap-pop of 'Into You' and the reggae-tinged 'Side to Side' with Nicki Minaj. Grande co-wrote nearly every song, and her voice, richer and more controlled than ever, carried material about desire and power with total conviction. It debuted at number one and earned her a Grammy nomination, and it remains the favorite of many of her fans.

name: reputation
teaser: 2017 Taylor Swift's sixth album is a dark reinvention: 'Look What You Made Me Do', 'Delicate', and '...Ready for It?' address her public battles with venom and wit. The album sold 4.5 million copies and debuted at number one. It is her most defiant work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Max Martin and Shellback crafted a darker electronic sound. 'Look What You Made Me Do' announced her new era.

tracks.title: Look What You Made Me Do
This Is Why We Can't Have Nice Things

synopsis: Taylor Swift had spent 2016 in a very public feud with Kanye West and Kim Kardashian that turned much of the world against her, and she responded by disappearing for a year and then returning with this album, a dark reinvention of her whole image. The record trades her country-pop innocence for a moody, trap-tinged sound, and its songs are full of snakes, revenge and carefully chosen enemies, from the opener '...Ready for It?' to the notorious 'Look What You Made Me Do' and the devastating 'Getaway Car'. It debuted at number one, and its lead single's video, full of versions of herself, announced the new Taylor. It is the sound of a pop star weaponizing her own narrative.

teaser: 2014 Taylor Swift's fifth album was her full pivot to pop: 'Shake It Off', 'Blank Space', and 'Style' are shimmering synth-pop. The album sold 10 million copies and won Album of the Year at the Grammys. It is one of the best-selling albums of all time.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Max Martin and Shellback crafted the album's polished pop sound. 'Blank Space' satirized her media image.

tracks.title: All You Had to Do Was Stay

synopsis: Taylor Swift had spent her career as country's most successful crossover, but this fifth album, released in 2014, was her full, unapologetic pivot to pop. Working with producers Max Martin and Shellback, Swift built a record of immaculate synth-pop, and its singles, from 'Shake It Off' to 'Blank Space' to 'Bad Blood', were among the biggest of the decade. The album sold over 10 million copies in its first year, making it the fastest-selling record in over a decade, and it won Album of the Year at the Grammys, the first time a pop album had taken the prize in over 20 years. It is the record that turned the country star into the biggest pop artist in the world.

name: Speak Now
teaser: 2010 Taylor Swift's third album is entirely self-written: 'Mine', 'Back to December', and 'Enchanted' are confessional and mature. The album sold 5 million copies and debuted at number one. It is her most personal early work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the songwriting — Swift wrote every song alone, a rarity for a major pop album. 'Enchanted' became a fan favorite about a crush.

synopsis: Taylor Swift had written every song on her first two albums, but she had always collaborated on production, and this third album, released when she was 20, was the first she wrote and produced entirely alone. The record is a statement of independence, full of songs about love, heartbreak and the perils of growing up in public, from the opening 'Mine' to the revenge fantasy 'Better Than Revenge' and the acoustic closer 'Long Live'. It debuted at number one and sold over a million copies in its first week, and its title, a reference to the moment when a young person finds their voice, captured the album's theme. It is the sound of a songwriter taking full control of her art.

name: Fearless
teaser: 2008 Taylor Swift's second album made her a superstar: 'Love Story', 'You Belong with Me', and 'Fifteen' are country-pop perfection. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys, making her the youngest winner ever. It sold 12 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the hooks — the album's choruses are built for stadiums. 'Love Story' was inspired by Romeo and Juliet with a happy ending.

tracks.title: Fearless Tour 2009 First Show Behind the Scenes

synopsis: Taylor Swift had spent her debut establishing herself as country's newest star, and this second album, released in 2008, made her a phenomenon. The record's lead single, 'Love Story', with its Romeo and Juliet narrative, became one of the biggest country-pop crossover hits in history, and 'You Belong with Me' and 'White Horse' continued the run. The album spent more weeks on the Billboard 200 than any record in history, and it won Album of the Year at the Grammys, making Swift, at 20, the youngest winner of the award. It is the record that turned the teenage songwriter into a superstar, and its blend of country storytelling and pop melodies defined her sound for years.

name: Taylor Swift
teaser: 2006 Taylor Swift's debut introduced country's new star: 'Tim McGraw', 'Teardrops on My Guitar', and 'Our Song' are teenage country-pop gems. The album sold 7 million copies. It is the beginning of her unprecedented career.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the innocence — the debut captures her teenage perspective. 'Our Song' was written for a school talent show.

synopsis: Taylor Swift had moved to Nashville as a teenager with a demo tape and a dream, and this debut album, released when she was 16, was the payoff. The record is full of the teenage love stories and small-town observations that would define her career, from the opening 'Tim McGraw', a song about a boy who reminded her of the singer, to 'Teardrops on My Guitar' and 'Our Song'. Swift wrote or co-wrote every track, an unusual feat for a debut, and her plain, direct delivery made the songs feel personal. The album sold steadily for years, and its success made Swift, still in high school, country's newest star.

name: Midnights
teaser: 2022 Taylor Swift's tenth album is a late-night meditation: 'Anti-Hero', 'Lavender Haze', and 'Karma' are moody and introspective. The album sold 5 million copies in its first year and won Album of the Year at the Grammys. It is her most personal album in years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jack Antonoff and Aaron Dessner crafted a cohesive synth-pop sound. 'Anti-Hero' is her most self-deprecating hit.

synopsis: Taylor Swift had spent 2022 re-recording her old albums and dominating the charts, and this tenth record, announced with almost no warning, was her most introspective yet. The album is a late-night meditation, full of songs about sleeplessness, regret and the things that keep you up, and its lead single, 'Anti-Hero', with its frank look at her own insecurities, became one of the biggest songs of her career. 'Lavender Haze', 'Maroon' and 'Karma' showed her range, and the record debuted at number one, selling more copies in its first week than any album in years. It won Album of the Year at the Grammys, making Swift the first artist to win the award four times.

name: Evermore
teaser: 2020 Taylor Swift's ninth album is folklore's darker sister: 'Willow', 'Champagne Problems', and 'Coney Island' are folk songs about regret and winter. The album was recorded in the same quarantine sessions as folklore. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — the album's songs are more narrative than folklore's. 'Champagne Problems' is a fan-favorite about a rejected proposal.

synopsis: Taylor Swift had spent 2020 releasing the surprise album Folklore, a quarantine project that won Album of the Year, and this companion record, released just five months later, was its darker sister. The album explores similar territory, full of fictional characters, small-town stories and songs about the weight of memory, but its mood is more melancholy and its arrangements more spare. 'Willow', the lead single, became her seventh number one, and 'Champagne Problems', 'Coney Island' and 'Marjorie', a tribute to her late grandmother, showed her songwriting at its most personal. It is a quieter, stranger record than its sister, and many fans consider it the better one.

name: Lover
teaser: 2019 Taylor Swift's seventh album is a celebration: 'Lover', 'Cruel Summer', and 'ME!' are bright and colorful. The album debuted at number one and sold 3 million copies. It is her most joyful work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jack Antonoff and Swift crafted a pop sound with indie touches. 'Cruel Summer' became a sleeper hit years after release.

tracks.title: It's Nice to Have a Friend

synopsis: Taylor Swift had spent years cultivating a good-girl image, and this seventh album, released in 2019, was her attempt to shed it and celebrate love openly. The record is a bright, colorful collection of pop songs about being happy, from the title track's declaration of devotion to the disco-tinged 'Cruel Summer' and the anthemic 'You Need to Calm Down'. It also contains the devastating ballad 'Soon You'll Get Better', about her mother's cancer, and the record's release marked the beginning of her battle with her label over her master recordings. It is a record of joy shadowed by real pain, made by an artist about to fight for her own work.

name: The Tortured Poets Department
teaser: 2024 Taylor Swift's eleventh album is a double record about heartbreak: 'Fortnight', 'Down Bad', and 'So Long, London' are literate and raw. The album's surprise second half doubled its runtime. It sold 2.6 million copies in its first week, a record.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Jack Antonoff and Aaron Dessner split the album's two halves. 'Fortnight' with Post Malone was the lead single.

tracks.title: My Boy Only Breaks His Favorite Toys
Who's Afraid of Little Old Me?
I Can Fix Him (No Really I Can)
I Can Do It with a Broken Heart
The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived

synopsis: Taylor Swift had spent 2023 as the most dominant force in popular culture, with her Eras Tour breaking records around the world, and this eleventh album, released in 2024, was the most personal record of her career. The double album, whose title is a cheeky reference to a phrase her ex Joe Alwyn reportedly used, is full of songs about the end of their long relationship, and its lyrics are the most explicit and raw she has ever written, from the opening 'Fortnight' to the devastating 'So Long, London' and the confessional 'The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived'. It sold two million copies in its first week, breaking every record, and it confirmed Swift as the defining artist of her era.

name: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers
teaser: 2022 Kendrick Lamar's fifth album is a therapy session: 'N95', 'Die Hard', and 'Father Time' confront trauma, fame, and growth. The album debuted at number one and won a Grammy. It is his most personal and uncomfortable work.

exploreAction.targetName: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers (2022) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album is structured as a therapy session with interludes. 'Auntie Diaries' addresses trans identity with empathy.

synopsis: Kendrick Lamar had spent his career as the most acclaimed rapper of his generation, but this fifth album, his first in five years, found him doing something unprecedented: turning his own life into a therapy session, on record. The album is a sprawling, uncomfortable examination of his family, his faith and his own flaws, full of songs about generational trauma, infidelity and the difficulty of healing, and it features appearances from his fiancée Whitney Alford and his cousin Carl, who speak on the recordings. 'N95', 'Die Hard' and 'The Heart Part 5' showed his range, and the record's unflinching honesty divided fans who wanted the old Kendrick. It is the sound of a genius turning his gaze inward.

name: GNX
teaser: 2024 Kendrick Lamar's sixth album arrived unannounced: 'Squabble Up', 'TV Off', and 'Luther' are West Coast bangers with political edge. The album debuted at number one amid his feud with Drake. It is his most direct album in years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album is built on West Coast G-funk samples. 'Squabble Up' became an instant hit.

synopsis: Kendrick Lamar had spent 2024 in the middle of the biggest rap feud of the decade, trading increasingly vicious diss tracks with Drake, and when he released this surprise album in November, the world was still reeling. The record is named for a limited-edition Buick Regal, a symbol of West Coast pride, and it is full of the fury and confidence of a man who had just won the biggest battle in hip-hop history. 'Squabble Up', 'TV Off' and the Drake-dissing 'Not Like Us' showed Lamar at his most aggressive, and the album debuted at number one. It is a victory lap, taken at full speed, by the greatest rapper of his generation.

name: Untitled Unmastered
teaser: 2016 Kendrick Lamar's collection of outtakes from To Pimp a Butterfly: 'Untitled 02', 'Untitled 05', and 'Untitled 08' are as strong as the album itself. The tracks were recorded during the TPAB sessions. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the jazz — the collection continues TPAB's free-jazz energy. 'Untitled 02' features jazz vocalist Bilal.

synopsis: Kendrick Lamar had recorded enough material for his masterpiece To Pimp a Butterfly to fill several albums, and this collection, released in 2016, gathered eight of the outtakes. The record is looser and more experimental than its parent album, full of jazz-funk jams and spoken word passages, and its tracks, most of which have no proper titles, feel like sketches from a genius's notebook. 'untitled 02' and 'untitled 05' became fan favorites, and the album's quality, for a collection of leftovers, was extraordinary. It debuted at number one and confirmed that even Lamar's castoffs were better than most artists' best work.

name: A Star Is Born
teaser: 2018 Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper's soundtrack became a phenomenon: 'Shallow', 'Always Remember Us This Way', and 'I'll Never Love Again' are raw and powerful. The album won a Grammy for 'Shallow'. It sold 6 million copies.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Shallow' — the song's build from a whisper to a roar won the Oscar for Best Original Song. The album's country-rock production fits the film.

tracks.title: I Don't Know What Love Is
I'll Never Love Again (extended version) (performed by Gaga)

synopsis: Bradley Cooper had spent years preparing to remake A Star Is Born, the story of a fading musician who discovers a young singer, and when he recruited Lady Gaga to co-star, he got far more than an actress. The film's soundtrack, on which Cooper and Gaga sing together, became a phenomenon, led by 'Shallow', a duet that won the Oscar for Best Original Song and became one of the biggest hits of the decade. The album also contains Gaga's solo performances of 'Always Remember Us This Way' and 'I'll Never Love Again', and its blend of country, rock and pop captured the film's heartbreak. It sold over six million copies and turned the movie into a cultural event.

name: Love for Sale
teaser: 2021 Lady Gaga and Tony Bennett's final collaboration: 'Love for Sale', 'I Get a Kick Out of You', and 'Night and Day' are classic standards sung by legends. The album won a Grammy for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album. It is Bennett's final album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the duets — Bennett's voice and Gaga's blend beautifully on the standards. The album was recorded between Bennett's Alzheimer's diagnosis sessions.

tracks.title: I Get a Kick Out of You

synopsis: Tony Bennett and Lady Gaga had become an unlikely duo when they recorded their first jazz album together in 2014, and this follow-up, recorded when Bennett was 95 and struggling with Alzheimer's, was their farewell.
