The record consists of Cole Porter songs, the same material Bennett had sung on his own 1950s debut, and Gaga's presence seems to bring out the best in the aging singer, who sounds remarkably alert on tracks like 'I Get a Kick Out of You'. The album won a Grammy, making Bennett the oldest Grammy winner in history. It is a tender, bittersweet document of a remarkable friendship, recorded while Bennett could still remember the songs he had sung for seventy years.

name: Cheap Thrills
teaser: 1968 Big Brother and the Holding Company's second album captured Janis Joplin at her peak: 'Piece of My Heart', 'Summertime', and 'Ball and Chain' are raw, bluesy, and volcanic. The cover was drawn by underground cartoonist R. Crumb. The album reached number one and made Joplin a star.
byline: Big Brother and the Holding Company

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to Joplin's voice — it rasps, wails, and soars with unmatched power. The album was recorded live in the studio with the band playing together.

tracks.title: I Need a Man to Love

synopsis: Janis Joplin had spent years as the most electrifying singer in the San Francisco scene, and this album, her second with Big Brother and the Holding Company, captured her at the peak of her powers. The record's centerpiece is her version of 'Piece of My Heart', a song she made entirely her own with a vocal performance of raw, desperate power, and it also contains the blues of 'Summertime' and the frantic 'Ball and Chain'. Joplin's voice, a gravelly howl that could break into a tender croon, was unlike anything in rock, and the album's success made her a star. She died two years later, at 27, and this record stands as the definitive document of her genius.

name: After the Gold Rush
teaser: 1970 Neil Young's third solo album is a masterpiece of longing: 'After the Gold Rush', 'Only Love Can Break Your Heart', and 'Southern Man' are folk-rock songs about love, apocalypse, and hope. The album was recorded in a basement with pianist Nils Lofgren. It defined his delicate, high voice.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — Lofgren played many parts while Young focused on guitar and voice. 'Southern Man' sparked a response from Lynyrd Skynyrd.

tracks.title: Only Love Can Break Your Heart
Don't Let It Bring You Down
When You Dance I Can Really Love

synopsis: Neil Young had spent his first two solo albums finding his voice, and this third record, recorded with a group of session musicians including the future members of Crazy Horse, is where he found it completely. The album is a masterpiece of longing, full of songs about love, loss and the search for meaning, from the title track's apocalyptic vision to the tender 'Only Love Can Break Your Heart' and the elegiac 'Birds'. Young's voice, high and fragile, and his acoustic guitar carry songs of extraordinary intimacy, and the record's blend of folk, country and rock made it his commercial breakthrough. It is one of the essential albums of the singer-songwriter era.

name: Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere
teaser: 1969 Neil Young's second album introduced Crazy Horse: 'Cinnamon Girl', 'Cowgirl in the Sand', and 'Down by the River' are long, loud, and raw. The album was recorded in three days with the garage band. It is the sound of Young finding his electric voice.

exploreAction.targetName: Everybody Knows This Is Nowhere (1969) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitar interplay — Young and Danny Whitten trade solos throughout. 'Down by the River' is nine minutes of slow-burning tension.

synopsis: Neil Young had spent his solo debut finding his feet, and this second album, recorded with a new band he called Crazy Horse, found him fully formed. The record is built on long, loose jams, with guitarist Danny Whitten's harmonies and the band's ragged, live-in-the-studio sound giving Young's songs a new power, and its centerpiece is 'Cinnamon Girl', 'Cowgirl in the Sand' and the nine-minute 'Down by the River', all instant classics. Young's guitar playing, full of sustained notes and feedback, was a revelation, and the album's blend of country melodies and heavy rock made it a landmark. It is the record where the singer-songwriter became a rock star.

name: On the Beach
teaser: 1974 Neil Young's bleak masterpiece: 'Walk On', 'On the Beach', and 'Revolution Blues' are sardonic and weary. The album was a deliberate downer after his commercial peak. It has become a cult favorite among his fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the despair — the album was Young's response to the failures of the counterculture. 'Revolution Blues' is about the Manson murders.

tracks.title: See the Sky About to Rain

synopsis: Neil Young had spent the early 70s as one of the most successful singer-songwriters in the world, but by 1974 he was adrift, alienated from the counterculture he had helped create and surrounded by the wreckage of his friends' excesses. This album, his fifth, is the sound of that despair, full of songs about isolation, betrayal and the death of the 60s dream, from the weary 'Walk On' to the devastating title track and the acid-tinged 'Revolution Blues'. Young has called it one of his darkest records, and it sold poorly on release, but it has since been recognized as a masterpiece, the sound of a man watching his generation destroy itself.

name: Zuma
teaser: 1975 Neil Young and Crazy Horse reunited for a loose, powerful album: 'Cortez the Killer', 'Lookin' for a Love', and 'Barstool Blues' are long, loud, and lyrical. The album was recorded quickly after years of strain. 'Cortez the Killer' is among his greatest songs.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitars — Young's solos on 'Cortez the Killer' are among his most emotional. The album was recorded live in the studio with few overdubs.

synopsis: Neil Young had spent two years making increasingly bleak and personal records, and this album, his seventh, found him reuniting with Crazy Horse for a looser, more hopeful sound. The record was made quickly, with the band playing live in the studio, and its songs, from the roaring 'Don't Cry No Tears' to the elegiac 'Stupid Girl' and the epic 'Cortez the Killer', are full of the ragged energy that only Young and Crazy Horse could produce. The title track, a love song to a place he had once lived with his lover Carrie Snodgress, is one of his most beautiful compositions. It is the sound of a genius recovering his joy.

name: Comes a Time
teaser: 1978 Neil Young's gentle country album: 'Comes a Time', 'Goin' Back', and 'Motorcycle Mama' are warm and acoustic. The album was recorded with a country band and a string section. It is his most accessible work of the 70s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — Nicolette Larson sings throughout the album. The title track is a meditation on change.

synopsis: Neil Young had spent the late 70s making increasingly hard-edged music, and this gentle country album was a deliberate change of pace. The record is full of the warm, acoustic songs that Young had always written alongside his rockers, from the title track to 'Goin' Back' and the duet 'Motorcycle Mama' with Nicolette Larson, and its relaxed, pastoral mood made it a favorite of fans who preferred his softer side. The album was recorded with a cast of country session players and features some of Young's most straightforward love songs. It sold well and reminded everyone that the angry rocker was also one of the most tender voices in American music.

name: Rust Never Sleeps
teaser: 1979 Neil Young's live album with studio overdubs: 'My My, Hey Hey (Out of the Blue)', 'Powderfinger', and 'Welfare Mothers' capture his acoustic and electric sides. The album was recorded live with Crazy Horse. It is the sound of punk and classic rock meeting.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the acoustic-electric split — the album opens quiet and closes loud. 'Powderfinger' is a story song about a family tragedy.

tracks.title: My My, Hey Hey (Out of the Blue)
Hey Hey, My My (Into the Black)

synopsis: Neil Young had spent the late 70s on a series of ambitious but commercially disappointing records, and this album, recorded live with Crazy Horse and then overdubbed in the studio, was his comeback. The record is built on the contrast between its acoustic first half, which includes 'My My, Hey Hey (Out of the Blue)', a meditation on death and rock and roll inspired by the Sex Pistols' Sid Vicious, and its electric second half, which features the full-band version of the song and the anthemic 'Hey Hey, My My (Into the Black)'. It was hailed as a return to form and made Young relevant again for the punk generation. It is the sound of an old rocker proving he was still dangerous.

name: Freedom
teaser: 1989 Neil Young's comeback album: 'Rockin' in the Free World', 'Crime in the City', and 'No More' are loud and political. The album marked his return to the electric sound after a decade of detours. It re-established him as a rock icon.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the anger — 'Rockin' in the Free World' is a protest anthem with a screaming guitar solo. The album was a bridge to the 90s grunge era.

tracks.title: Crime in the City (Sixty to Zero Part I)

synopsis: Neil Young had spent the 80s wandering through experiments with synthesizers and rockabilly that alienated his fans, and this album, released in 1989, was his return to the sound that made him a legend. The record is full of the hard, melodic rock that Young had perfected with Crazy Horse, from the political anthem 'Rockin' in the Free World', which became a signature song, to the tender 'Crime in the City' and the elegiac 'Hangin' on a Limb'. The album was a critical and commercial success, and its title captured its mood of liberation after a decade of wandering. It is the sound of a legend reclaiming his throne.

name: Fleet Foxes
teaser: 2008 Fleet Foxes' debut made indie folk a movement: 'White Winter Hymnal', 'Ragged Wood', and 'Blue Ridge Mountains' are lush, harmonic, and timeless. The band's layered vocal harmonies evoked the Beach Boys and Appalachian choirs. The album was a critical and commercial breakthrough.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the harmonies — the band stacks voices in intricate arrangements. 'White Winter Hymnal' was built around a simple, nursery-rhyme melody.

synopsis: Fleet Foxes had spent years playing in the Seattle folk scene, and this debut album, recorded in 2008, introduced their extraordinary harmonies to the world. The band, led by Robin Pecknold, makes music that sounds like it could have been recorded in a cathedral or a forest, full of interlocking vocal harmonies, acoustic guitars and lyrics full of nature and mythology. 'White Winter Hymnal', 'Ragged Wood' and 'He Doesn't Know Why' became instant classics, and the album's blend of folk, rock and baroque pop made it one of the most acclaimed debuts of the decade. It made Fleet Foxes the leaders of a folk revival and set an impossibly high bar for their follow-ups.

name: Helplessness Blues
teaser: 2011 Fleet Foxes' second album deepened their sound: 'Helplessness Blues', 'Bedouin Dress', and 'The Shrine/An Argument' are ambitious and introspective. The album explores identity and uncertainty. It is their most complete statement.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the arrangements — the band moved beyond folk into chamber pop and psychedelia. The title track is a meditation on purpose.

synopsis: Fleet Foxes had spent their debut establishing themselves as the most exciting new folk band in the world, and this second album, recorded over two years, deepened and darkened their sound. The record is more ambitious and more personal than its predecessor, full of songs about doubt, identity and the difficulty of connection, and its arrangements, from the title track's orchestral swell to the a cappella opening of 'The Plains/Bitter Dancer', are more intricate than ever. Pecknold's lyrics, full of existential questions and natural imagery, reward deep listening, and the album's blend of beauty and unease made it a masterpiece. It is the record where a great band became a great one.

name: Crack-Up
teaser: 2017 Fleet Foxes' third album was their most experimental: 'Third of May/Odaigahara', 'If You Need to, Keep Time on Me', and 'On Another Ocean (January/June)' are long and intricate. The album was inspired by F. Scott Fitzgerald's essay of the same name. It is their most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the song structures — many tracks shift between movements. The album rewards patient, focused listening.

tracks.title: I Am All That I Need / Arroyo Seco / Thumbprint Scar
If You Need to, Keep Time on Me

synopsis: Fleet Foxes had spent six years between albums, and frontman Robin Pecknold spent much of that time in a state of crisis, questioning whether he wanted to continue making music. This third album, named for F. Scott Fitzgerald's essay about the crack-up, is the sound of that crisis, and it is the band's most experimental record, full of sudden shifts, jazz textures and songs that refuse to resolve. 'Third of May/Odaigahara', 'If You Need to, Keep Time on Me' and the haunting 'Kept Woman' showed Pecknold pushing his music into stranger territory. It divided fans who wanted more of the old sound, but its ambition was undeniable. It is the sound of an artist breaking himself open.

name: Shore
teaser: 2020 Fleet Foxes' fourth album arrived on the autumn equinox: 'Can I Believe You', 'Sunblind', and 'Featherweight' are warm and hopeful. The album was recorded with collaborators across the globe during lockdown. It is their most optimistic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the collaborations — the album features contributions from many indie artists. 'Sunblind' is a tribute to musicians the band lost.

tracks.title: A Long Way Past the Past

synopsis: Fleet Foxes had spent years on their experimental third album, and this fourth record, released on the autumn equinox of 2020, was a deliberate return to warmth. Recorded with a large cast of collaborators, including members of other bands and a full string section, the record is full of the soaring harmonies and natural imagery that made the band famous, but its mood is gentler and more grateful. 'Can I Believe You', 'Sunblind' and 'A Long Way Past the Past' are among the loveliest songs they have written, and the record's title, a reference to the shore where the tide meets the land, captures its sense of arrival. It is the sound of a band finding peace.

name: Hail to the Thief
teaser: 2003 Radiohead's sixth album balanced their experimental side with rock songs: 'There There', '2 + 2 = 5', and 'Sail to the Moon' are urgent and uneasy. The album was recorded in a church in two weeks. It is their last album with a traditional band sound for years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the tension — the album was written in the shadow of the Iraq war. 'There There' became their biggest single in years.

tracks.title: Where I End and You Begin.

synopsis: Radiohead had spent their first five albums zigzagging between rock and electronic experimentation, and this sixth record found them trying to balance both sides of their identity. The album was written quickly, in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks, and its songs are full of the paranoia and dread of that moment, from the opener '2 + 2 = 5' to the political 'A Punchup at a Wedding' and the eerie 'There There'. The record's blend of guitars and electronics, with Thom Yorke's voice floating over both, made it their most accessible work since OK Computer. It debuted at number one and is often cited by the band themselves as one of their favorites.

name: A Moon Shaped Pool
teaser: 2016 Radiohead's ninth album is their most elegiac: 'Burn the Witch', 'Daydreaming', and 'True Love Waits' are slow, string-laden, and beautiful. The album was five years in the making. 'True Love Waits' had been played live for two decades before finally being recorded.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the strings — the London Contemporary Orchestra plays throughout. The album closes with a piano ballad about loss.

tracks.title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Sailor Rich Man Poor Man Beggar Man Thief

synopsis: Radiohead had spent five years between albums, and this ninth record, released in 2016, was made after the death of the band's longtime producer and mentor, which gave the music an elegiac weight. The album is full of songs about loss and letting go, from the opening 'Burn the Witch', with its strings and paranoia, to the devastating 'Daydreaming', a piano ballad about the end of a relationship, and the closing 'True Love Waits', a song the band had been performing live for twenty years. The record's arrangements, built on strings and sparse electronics, are among the most beautiful the band has made. It is a quiet, heartbroken masterpiece, the sound of a great band saying goodbye to something.

name: Pablo Honey
teaser: 1993 Radiohead's debut introduced 'Creep', their accidental global hit: 'Creep', 'Anyone Can Play Guitar', and 'Stop Whispering' are grunge-era rock. The band was unhappy with the album's generic sound. It set the stage for their later genius.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Creep' — its sudden loud chorus was the band's breakthrough. The album is best heard as a rough sketch of what came next.

synopsis: Radiohead had spent their early years as one of the most promising bands in the Oxford scene, and this debut album, released in 1993, introduced them to the world with a song they had written in frustration and nearly thrown away. 'Creep', with its grunge guitars and Thom Yorke's self-lacerating lyrics, became an accidental global hit, making the band stars whether they liked it or not. The rest of the album, from 'Stop Whispering' to 'Anyone Can Play Guitar', shows a band still finding its voice, caught between the grunge of the moment and the art rock ambitions that would define them. It is a flawed, fascinating debut, remembered mostly for the song that made its creators uncomfortable.

name: The King of Limbs
teaser: 2011 Radiohead's eighth album is a study in rhythm: 'Lotus Flower', 'Bloom', and 'Codex' are built on looping, fractured beats. The album was recorded with the band's live looping techniques. It is their most rhythm-focused work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the drums — the album is built around drum loops and percussion. 'Lotus Flower' became famous for Thom Yorke's dance in the video.

synopsis: Radiohead had spent their career making albums of ever-increasing complexity, and this eighth record, released in 2011, was a deliberate exercise in restraint. The album runs barely 37 minutes, and its songs are built on rhythm, with drummer Phil Selway's patterns and the band's loops and samples taking the lead. 'Lotus Flower', with Thom Yorke's strange, twitching dance in its video, became an unlikely hit, and 'Bloom' and 'Codex' showed the band's mastery of atmosphere. It was greeted with disappointment by fans who expected another Kid A, but its dense, knotty rhythms have aged well. It is the sound of a great band making music for themselves.

name: Harlequin
teaser: 2024 Lady Gaga's companion album to Joker: Folie a Deux: 'Folie a Deux', 'Happy Mistake', and 'The Joker' are torch songs and jazz standards. The album showcases her voice without pop production. It is a stylistic departure.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the vocals — the album strips away production to showcase her range. 'Folie a Deux' is an original song for the film.

tracks.title: If My Friends Could See Me Now

synopsis: Lady Gaga had spent years preparing to play Harley Quinn in the sequel to Joker, and this companion album, released alongside the film, collects the songs her character performs in the movie, mostly jazz standards from the American songbook. The record is a showcase for Gaga's extraordinary versatility, from her duets with Joaquin Phoenix on 'Folie à Deux' and 'The Joker' to her versions of 'That's Entertainment' and 'Get Happy', and it captures the strange, tragic romance of the film. It is a minor entry in her catalog, but it shows the range that has made her one of the most versatile stars in pop, equally at home in a stadium or a smoky jazz club.

name: Mayhem
teaser: 2025 Lady Gaga's seventh studio album is a return to maximalist pop: 'Disease', 'Abracadabra', and 'Garden of Eden' blend her early electro sound with new textures. The album was announced as a homecoming to her roots. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends her signature electro-pop with live instruments. 'Abracadabra' became an instant fan favorite.

tracks.title: How Bad Do U Want Me

synopsis: Lady Gaga had spent the first half of the 2020s making a country record, a jazz album and a film soundtrack, and this seventh studio album was her return to the maximalist pop that made her famous. The record is a celebration of her whole career, full of the dance-pop anthems, theatrical ballads and glam-rock stomps that defined her sound, and its singles, including 'Abracadabra' and 'Disease', were among her most confident in years. Gaga called the album 'a love letter to pop music', and its songs about fame, desire and survival showed an artist at peace with her own legacy. It debuted at number one and was hailed as her best album in over a decade.

name: Cheek to Cheek
teaser: 2014 Lady Gaga and Tony Bennett's first duet album: 'Anything Goes', 'Cheek to Cheek', and 'I Can't Give You Anything but Love' are jazz standards sung with relish. The album won a Grammy for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album. It introduced Gaga's voice to a new audience.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the chemistry — Bennett's mentoring shines through the duets. The album was recorded live with a jazz band.

tracks.title: I Can't Give You Anything but Love
Let's Face the Music and Dance
It Don't Mean a Thing (If It Ain't Got That Swing)
Bang Bang (My Baby Shot Me Down)
On a Clear Day (You Can See Forever)

synopsis: Tony Bennett had spent decades as one of the greatest interpreters of the American songbook, and Lady Gaga had grown up listening to her grandfather's jazz records, so this duet album, their first together, was a meeting of generations. The record consists of jazz standards, from 'Anything Goes' to 'I Can't Give You Anything but Love', and Gaga, singing in a warm, swinging style that surprised everyone who knew only her pop persona, holds her own alongside the 88-year-old master. The album won a Grammy and was followed by a joint tour, and its success introduced Bennett's music to a new generation. It is a record of pure, joyful musicianship, made by two singers who clearly adored each other.

name: White Light/White Heat
teaser: 1968 The Velvet Underground's second album is their loudest: 'White Light/White Heat', 'Sister Ray', and 'I Heard Her Call My Name' are harsh, noisy, and confrontational. The album was recorded in a day. It is noise rock's founding document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the chaos — 'Sister Ray' is a 17-minute jam about sailors and drugs. The album's guitar feedback was a decade ahead of punk.

tracks.title: I Heard Her Call My Name

synopsis: The Velvet Underground had spent their debut album making some of the most influential music of the decade, and this follow-up, recorded in 1968, was even more extreme. The record is their loudest and harshest, built on the amplifier abuse of guitarist John Cale and the relentless pounding of Maureen Tucker's drums, and its centerpiece, the seventeen-minute 'Sister Ray', is a brutal, chaotic jam about sailors, drugs and debauchery that still sounds shocking today. 'White Light/White Heat' and 'The Gift', a ten-minute spoken word story, complete the assault. It sold almost nothing on release, but its influence on punk, noise and everything in between has been immeasurable. It is the sound of a band pushing itself to the edge.

name: The Modern Lovers
teaser: 1976 The Modern Lovers' sole album was recorded in 1972 but released four years later: 'Roadrunner', 'Pablo Picasso', and 'She Cracked' are proto-punk songs about Boston and girls. The album's naive sound influenced punk and new wave. It is a cult classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the simplicity — the album is built on two chords and Jonathan Richman's deadpan vocals. 'Roadrunner' became an anthem of teenage freedom.

synopsis: The Modern Lovers, led by Jonathan Richman, recorded this album in 1972 with producer John Cale, but the record was shelved and the band broke up before it could be released, and it did not appear until 1976. The delay did nothing to date the music, which sounds like a blueprint for everything that came after: the proto-punk of 'Roadrunner', with its two-chord roar and its ode to the Boston night, the deadpan genius of 'Pablo Picasso', and the sweet awkwardness of 'Someone I Care About'. Richman's songs are about cars, girls and the joy of being alive, delivered with a childlike wonder that made him a cult hero. It is one of the most influential albums ever released, the sound of punk before punk had a name.

name: Adventure
teaser: 1978 Television's second album is softer and more polished than their debut: 'Foxhole', 'Glory', and 'Ain't That Nothin'' are melodic and intricate. The album was a commercial disappointment but has aged well. It is the band's farewell for decades.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the melodies — the album is more song-oriented than Marquee Moon. 'Glory' is a wry comment on the band's fame.

synopsis: Television had spent their debut album Marquee Moon establishing themselves as the most inventive band in the New York punk scene, and this follow-up, recorded with a new producer, found them polishing their sound. The record is softer and more melodic than its predecessor, with the twin guitars of Tom Verlaine and Richard Lloyd weaving together in ever more intricate patterns, and songs like 'Foxhole' and 'Glory' showed the band's growing confidence. It was poorly received on release, with critics and fans alike comparing it unfavorably to its masterpiece predecessor, and the band broke up shortly after. Time has been kinder, and its gentle, lyrical guitar music is now seen as a worthy follow-up to one of the greatest debuts in rock.

name: Moondance
teaser: 1970 Van Morrison's second album is his most accessible: 'Moondance', 'Crazy Love', and 'Into the Mystic' are warm, jazzy, and romantic. The album blended R&B, jazz, and folk into a new sound. It sold 4 million copies and is his best-selling work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the horn arrangements — the album's jazz-tinged R&B is infectious. 'Into the Mystic' is among the most loved songs in pop.

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent his previous album Astral Weeks making the most uncompromising music of his career, and this follow-up, recorded in New York with a group of jazz musicians, was his attempt to reach a wider audience. The record is his most accessible, full of warm, swinging songs about love, nature and spiritual longing, and its title track, 'Moondance', 'Crazy Love' and 'Into the Mystic' became instant classics. Morrison's voice, a keening instrument of extraordinary range, had never sounded more joyful, and the album's blend of soul, jazz and Celtic folk made it a massive hit. It is the album where the mystic of Astral Weeks learned to dance, and it remains his most beloved work.

name: Tupelo Honey
teaser: 1971 Van Morrison's fifth album is warm and rootsy: 'Tupelo Honey', 'Wild Night', and 'These Dreams of You' are soulful and celebratory. The album was recorded with a band in a cabin. It is his most relaxed work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album was recorded live in a studio built in a cabin. 'Wild Night' became a cover favorite.

tracks.title: (Straight to Your Heart) Like a Cannonball
When That Evening Sun Goes Down

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the early 70s making some of the most acclaimed music of his career, and this fifth album, recorded in California with a group of musicians including his wife Janet, is his warmest and most rootsy record. The album's title track, a love song to his wife, became one of his signature tunes, and 'Wild Night' and the joyous '(Straight to Your Heart) Like a Cannonball' showed his gift for pure, uncomplicated joy. The record also contains the epic 'Almost Independence Day', a ten-minute meditation on freedom, and its blend of country, soul and folk made it a fan favorite. It is the sound of a man content with his life, and it remains one of his most beloved albums.

name: Saint Dominic's Preview
teaser: 1972 Van Morrison's sixth album spans soul, jazz, and Celtic folk: 'Jackie Wilson Said', 'Saint Dominic's Preview', and 'Almost Independence Day' are ambitious and varied. The album was recorded in multiple cities. It is his most eclectic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album moves from funk to folk to rock. 'Almost Independence Day' is a 10-minute epic about the Northern Ireland troubles.

tracks.title: Jackie Wilson Said (I'm in Heaven When You Smile)

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the early 70s as one of the most acclaimed singer-songwriters in the world, and this sixth album found him expanding his sound to take in soul, jazz and Celtic folk. The record's centerpiece is 'Jackie Wilson Said (I'm in Heaven When You Smile)', a tribute to the soul singer that became one of his most joyful recordings, and it also contains the epic 'Listen to the Lion', an eleven-minute meditation on identity that is among the strangest and most beautiful things he ever recorded. Morrison's voice, at the height of its powers, carries songs of love, longing and spiritual searching, and the album's blend of styles made it a critical favorite. It is the sound of a restless genius refusing to stand still.

name: Veedon Fleece
teaser: 1974 Van Morrison's ninth album is his most introspective: 'Veedon Fleece', 'You Don't Pull No Punches, But You Don't Push the River', and 'Streets of Arklow' are long, poetic, and mystical. The album was inspired by a trip to Ireland. It is a cult favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the poetry — the album's lyrics are among Morrison's most abstract. 'Veedon Fleece' is a meditation on wandering.

tracks.title: You Don't Pull No Punches, but You Don't Push the River

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent years making increasingly mystical and sprawling records, and this ninth album, recorded on a trip to Ireland, is his most introspective and personal. The record is full of songs about memory, roots and the pull of home, and its centerpiece, 'Veedon Fleece', is a ten-minute meditation on love and loss that ranks among his greatest compositions. 'You Don't Pull No Punches, but You Don't Push the River' and 'Bulbs' complete a record of unusual depth and beauty. Morrison has said he was trying to recapture the feeling of his childhood in Belfast, and the album's Celtic soul, full of fiddle and flute, reflects that search. It sold poorly and he went silent for three years after its release.

name: Wavelength
teaser: 1978 Van Morrison's album marked his turn to a rock band sound: 'Wavelength', 'Kingdom Hall', and 'Checkin' It Out' are polished and direct. The album was his first with a horn section in years. It reached number 28 on the Billboard chart.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded in Los Angeles with a full band. 'Wavelength' was inspired by a song he heard on the radio.

tracks.title: Take It Where You Find It

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the mid-70s silent, releasing nothing between 1974 and 1977 while he renegotiated his contract and searched for a new direction. This album, his first in four years, marked his return with a new sound, built around a full rock band and the soul and R&B that had always been at the heart of his music. The title track and 'Kingdom Hall' showed the new energy, and 'Natalie' and the epic closer 'Take It Where You Find It' demonstrated that his songwriting had lost none of its depth. The album was a commercial success and pointed the way to the more polished sound of his later career. It is the sound of a legend returning.

name: Into the Music
teaser: 1979 Van Morrison's album of spiritual longing: 'Bright Side of the Road', 'Into the Music', and 'Full Force Gale' are joyful and mystical. The album marked a return to his Celtic roots. It is a fan favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the gospel influence — the album's backing singers lift every song. 'Bright Side of the Road' became a live staple.

tracks.title: You Make Me Feel So Free
It's All in the Game (Charles Dawes, Carl Sigman)
You Know What They're Writing About

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the late 70s making rock records, and this album, his twelfth, found him turning back toward the spiritual longing that had defined his best work. The record is full of songs about transcendence and the search for meaning, from the opener 'Bright Side of the Road' to the devotional 'Full Force Gale' and the epic closer 'It Must Be You'. Morrison's voice, still in magnificent shape, carries the material with total conviction, and the album's blend of soul, gospel and Celtic folk made it a favorite of fans who preferred his mystical side. It is the sound of a man seeking God through music, and it remains one of his most beloved records.

name: Common One
teaser: 1980 Van Morrison's most mystical album: 'When Heart Is Open', 'Summertime in England', and 'Satisfied Mind' are long, meditative, and transcendental. The album was recorded in a French monastery. It divided critics but has a devoted following.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the length — the songs run 10-15 minutes each, built on meditative grooves. The album rewards patience and solitude.

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the 70s as one of the most prolific and acclaimed singer-songwriters in the world, and this album, his thirteenth, is his most mystical and uncompromising. The record consists of just six long songs, most of them built on a single, hypnotic groove over which Morrison improvises and chants like a man possessed, and its centerpiece, the nineteen-minute 'Summertime in England', is one of the strangest and most transcendent recordings of his career. The album's jazz textures, with Mark Isham's trumpet and Pee Wee Ellis's saxophone, give the music a meditative, almost religious quality. It was dismissed by critics on release, but it has since been recognized as a unique document of a genius following his own vision.

name: Beautiful Vision
teaser: 1982 Van Morrison's album of spiritual devotion: 'Vanlose Stairway', 'Cleaning Windows', and 'Dweller on the Threshold' are tender and luminous. The album reflects his growing mysticism. It is among his most beautiful records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the piano — the album features Mark Isham's trumpet and a contemplative mood. 'Cleaning Windows' is a nostalgic portrait of youth.

tracks.title: Across the Bridge Where Angels Dwell

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the early 80s making increasingly mystical records, and this album, his fourteenth, found him refining that sound into something more accessible. The record is full of songs of spiritual devotion, from the autobiographical 'Vanlose Stairway', about his relationship with his Danish lover, to the transcendent 'Scandinavia' and the gorgeous closer 'Dweller on the Threshold'. Morrison's voice, full of longing and joy, carries the material with total conviction, and the album's blend of Celtic folk, jazz and gospel made it one of his most commercially successful records of the decade. It is the sound of a mystic finding a wider audience.

name: Avalon Sunset
teaser: 1989 Van Morrison's album of duets and devotion: 'Whenever God Shines His Light', 'Have I Told You Lately', and 'I'd Love to Write Another Song' are warm and spiritual. The album was his biggest hit in years. 'Have I Told You Lately' became a wedding standard.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the duets — Cliff Richard joins him on 'Whenever God Shines His Light'. The album's spiritual themes are front and center.

tracks.title: Whenever God Shines His Light (duet with Cliff Richard)
I'd Love to Write Another Song
When Will I Ever Learn to Live in God

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the 80s as one of the most respected figures in popular music, and this album, his nineteenth, found him in a reflective, devotional mood. The record is full of songs about faith, mortality and the simple joys of life, and its centerpiece, 'Whenever God Shines His Light', a duet with Cliff Richard, became one of his biggest hits in years. 'Have I Told You Lately', a love song that would later be covered by Rod Stewart, and 'I'd Love to Write Another Song' completed a record of unusual warmth and accessibility. It was a massive commercial success, his best-selling album in over a decade, and it reminded the world of his gift for simple, profound songwriting.

name: Enlightenment
teaser: 1990 Van Morrison's album of midlife reflection: 'Enlightenment', 'Real Real Gone', and 'In the Days Before Rock 'n' Roll' are witty and warm. The album's title track asks what enlightenment is. It is among his most personal works.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — Morrison's lyrics are at their most playful. The album balances jazz, R&B, and Celtic sounds.

tracks.title: In the Days Before Rock 'N' Roll (Durcan, Morrison)

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the 80s making increasingly devotional records, and this album, his twentieth, found him turning his attention to the secular concerns of middle age. The record is full of songs about reflection, contentment and the passing of time, from the title track's wry observation that enlightenment is just another word for acceptance to the jazzy 'Real Real Gone' and the tender 'See Me Through'. Morrison's voice, richer and more lived-in than in his youth, suits the material perfectly, and the album's blend of jazz, R&B and Celtic soul made it a commercial success. It is the sound of a man making peace with his life.

name: Hymns to the Silence
teaser: 1991 Van Morrison's double album is his most sprawling: 'When Will I Learn to Learn to Stop and Start?', 'I Need Your Kind of Loving', and 'See Me Through' span blues, gospel, and jazz. The album is a compendium of his influences.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the double album covers every style he has touched. 'When Will I Learn' is a standout meditation.

tracks.title: I Can't Stop Loving You – (Gibson) – 3:54 (With The Chieftains)
See Me Through, Pt. 2 (Just a Closer Walk with Thee) – (Traditional)
Be Thou My Vision – (Traditional) – 3:49 (With The Chieftains)
I Need Your Kind of Loving

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the late 80s making increasingly polished records, and this double album, his twenty-first, was a return to the sprawling ambition of his early career. The record is his most varied, full of the blues, gospel, jazz and Celtic folk that had always been his raw materials, and its songs, from the autobiographical 'Why Must I Always Explain?' to the devotional 'Hymns to the Silence', show every side of his genius. Morrison was in a period of personal turmoil, with his marriage ending, and the record's mixture of joy and anguish gives it an unusual depth. It is a sprawling, uneven masterpiece, the sound of a legend working through his pain in public.

name: Days Like This
teaser: 1995 Van Morrison's return to form: 'Days Like This', 'Perfect Fit', and 'No Religion' are warm, confident, and melodic. The album was his most accessible in years. The title track became an anthem of contentment.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the groove — the album's band plays with ease. 'Days Like This' became his signature late-career song.

tracks.title: You Don't Know Me (Eddy Arnold, Cindy Walker)
I'll Never Be Free (Bennie Benjamin, George David Weiss)

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the early 90s making increasingly personal and difficult records, and this album, his twenty-fourth, was a return to the accessible soul that had made him famous. The record is full of warm, melodic songs about love and gratitude, from the title track, a celebration of ordinary happiness that became his biggest hit in years, to 'Perfect Fit' and the jazzy 'No Religion'. The album's relaxed, professional production and Morrison's rich, assured vocals made it his most commercially successful record in a decade. It is the sound of a legend reconnecting with his audience, and its warmth is contagious.

name: The Healing Game
teaser: 1997 Van Morrison's album of deep grooves: 'The Healing Game', 'Rough God Goes Riding', and 'Fire in the Belly' are bluesy, earthy, and hypnotic. The album was recorded live in the studio. It is among his best late-period records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album was cut live with a tight group. 'The Healing Game' is built on a slow, patient groove.

tracks.title: Piper at the Gates of Dawn

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the mid-90s making increasingly polished records, and this album, his twenty-fifth, found him returning to the deep, hypnotic grooves of his early career. The record's title track, built on a slow, simmering funk groove, is one of the most powerful things he had recorded in years, and 'Rough God Goes Riding' and 'Waiting Game' continued the mood of quiet intensity. Morrison's voice, full of grit and soul, carries the material with total authority, and the album's jazz and blues textures gave it a timeless quality. It is the sound of a master craftsman at work, and it stands as one of the best records of his later period.

name: Back on Top
teaser: 1999 Van Morrison's bluesy return: 'Back on Top', 'Goin' Down Geneva', and 'Precious Time' are loose, funny, and direct. The album was his most immediate in years. It is a fan favorite.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the horns — the album's backing band includes a full horn section. 'Back on Top' has a swagger missing from his spiritual albums.

tracks.title: When the Leaves Come Falling Down
Valley of Tears – 5:02 (Fats Domino, arranged Morrison)

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent the late 90s making increasingly serious records, and this album, his twenty-sixth, was a return to the bluesy, good-time music of his youth. The record is full of loose, swinging songs about love, music and the pleasures of the road, from the title track to 'Goin' Down Geneva' and the cover of the standard 'Precious Time', and Morrison sounds like he is having fun for the first time in years. The album's stripped-down production, with his band playing live in the studio, gave the music a warmth his recent records had lacked. It was hailed as a return to form and remains one of his most enjoyable records.

name: Keep It Simple
teaser: 2008 Van Morrison's album of stripped-back songs: 'Keep It Simple', 'Behind the Ritual', and 'End of the Land' are gentle and reflective. The album was recorded quickly with a small band. It is his most direct work of the 2000s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the simplicity — the album avoids the mystical length of his other work. The title track is a statement of intent.

synopsis: Van Morrison had spent decades making increasingly elaborate records, and this album, released in 2008, was a deliberate return to simplicity. The record is built on stripped-back arrangements, mostly acoustic, with Morrison's voice and the songs themselves carrying the weight, and its title track and 'Behind the Ritual' showed his gift for quiet, meditative songwriting. The album was recorded quickly, with a small band, and its lack of studio polish was the point: after years of horns and strings, Morrison wanted to prove the songs could stand alone. It was a modest commercial success, but its intimacy made it a favorite of longtime fans. It is the sound of a legend stripping back to essentials.

name: Erotica
teaser: 1992 Madonna's fifth album is her most explicit: 'Erotica', 'Deeper and Deeper', and 'Rain' are dance music about desire and intimacy. The album was tied to her book Sex, causing controversy. It is now considered one of her most daring records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Shep Pettibone's house beats give the album its pulse. 'Deeper and Deeper' became a dance classic.

synopsis: Madonna had spent the 80s as the queen of pop, but by the early 90s she was determined to shock, and this fifth album, released alongside her book Sex and her film Body of Evidence, was her most explicit statement yet. The record is built on the sounds of deep house and hip-hop, and its title track, a song about the art of seduction, and 'Deeper and Deeper' showed a new sophistication. But it was the album's frank sexuality, from 'Where Life Begins' to the S&M of 'Erotica' itself, that made headlines. The backlash was fierce, and the album, while a hit, marked the beginning of a commercial decline. It has since been reappraised as one of her boldest records.

name: Bedtime Stories
teaser: 1994 Madonna's sixth album softened her image: 'Secret', 'Take a Bow', and 'Bedtime Story' are smooth R&B ballads. The album was a response to the backlash against Erotica. It is her most tender work of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album blends R&B with ambient textures. 'Take a Bow' with Babyface was her longest-running number one.

synopsis: Madonna had spent 1992 courting controversy with her erotic book and album, and this sixth record was a deliberate softening of her image. The album is full of quiet, R&B-influenced ballads, a response to the criticism she had received, and its lead single, 'Secret', and the soaring 'Take a Bow', which spent seven weeks at number one, were among the biggest hits of her career. The record also contains the Babyface duet 'Forbidden Love' and the reflective 'Inside of Me', and its warm, understated production showed a new maturity. It is the album where the queen of shock proved she could also be the queen of heartbreak.

name: Prairie Wind
teaser: 2005 Neil Young's album of reflection, recorded before his brain surgery: 'The Painter', 'When God Made Me', and 'Prairie Wind' are gentle, nostalgic, and grateful. The album was recorded in Nashville. It is his most personal work of the decade.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album was recorded with a full band including Emmylou Harris. The title track looks back at his prairie childhood.

tracks.title: Falling Off the Face of the Earth

synopsis: Neil Young had spent the early 2000s making political records and touring with his friends, but this album, released in 2005, was something more personal. Recorded in Nashville with producer Ben Keith, the record is full of songs about mortality, memory and the American heartland, from the elegiac 'The Painter' to the title track's meditation on the prairie wind, and it was made in the shadow of Young's brain aneurysm, which struck just after the sessions and almost killed him. The album's gentle, country-tinged sound, full of pedal steel and close harmonies, was a deliberate tribute to the music of his youth, and its songs about family and home took on new weight after his near-death. It is the sound of a man facing his own mortality with grace.

name: Sleeps with Angels
teaser: 1994 Neil Young and Crazy Horse's dark album about the death of Kurt Cobain: 'Sleeps with Angels', 'Change Your Mind', and 'Blue Eden' are long, slow, and haunted. The album was recorded in the studio where Cobain died. It is their heaviest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album is a meditation on mortality. The title track was directly inspired by Cobain's suicide note.

synopsis: Neil Young had spent the early 90s at the height of his commercial and critical powers, and this album, recorded with Crazy Horse in 1994, was made in the shadow of Kurt Cobain's suicide. Cobain had quoted a Young lyric in his suicide note, and Young, devastated, channeled his grief into this dark, sprawling record, whose title track is a haunting meditation on the death of the grunge icon. The album's other songs, from the eleven-minute 'Change Your Mind' to the eerie 'Safeway Cart', continue the mood of unease, and its recording sessions, full of improvisation and tension, produced some of the strangest music of Young's career. It is a difficult, harrowing record, the sound of a legend processing the death of the generation that had adopted him.

name: Little Broken Hearts
teaser: 2012 Norah Jones' fifth album, produced by Danger Mouse, is her most adventurous: 'Happy Pills', 'Little Broken Hearts', and 'Miriam' are moody, cinematic, and slightly sinister. The album was written during a breakup. It is a departure from her jazz-pop comfort zone.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Danger Mouse built the album's sparse, dark sound. 'Happy Pills' has a sinister edge beneath its catchy melody.

synopsis: Norah Jones had spent her career as the queen of mellow, jazzy pop, but this fifth album, produced by Danger Mouse, was a sharp turn into darker territory. The record is built on the sounds of 60s girl groups, spy movies and psychedelic pop, and its songs are mostly about heartbreak and revenge, from the opening 'Good Morning' to the devastating 'Miriam' and the title track's tale of a woman who collects her lovers' broken hearts. Jones's voice, usually warm and comforting, takes on a cool, menacing edge, and the album's lush, cinematic production was unlike anything she had made before. It was hailed as a reinvention, and it proved that the queen of cozy could also be the queen of cool.

name: American Pie
teaser: 1971 Don McLean's album featuring the epic 'American Pie' — an eight-minute allegory about the death of rock and roll. 'Vincent', 'Crossroads', and 'Castles in the Air' are folk songs of loss and reflection. The title track is one of the most analyzed songs in pop.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — 'American Pie' is a coded history of the 1960s. 'Vincent' is a tribute to Van Gogh written after reading his letters.

synopsis: Don McLean had been struggling as a folk singer when he wrote the eight-and-a-half-minute epic that would make him famous, a cryptic, elegiac meditation on the death of Buddy Holly, which he called 'the day the music died'. The song's dense, allusive lyrics, full of references to the history of rock and roll, made it a phenomenon, and this album, his second, was built around it. The rest of the record, from the gentle 'Vincent', a tribute to Vincent van Gogh, to the title track's folk rock, showed a songwriter of real gifts, and the album's blend of folk, pop and poetry made it one of the best-selling records of 1972. It is remembered for its epic, but it contains much more than that.

name: Squeeze
teaser: 1973 The Velvet Underground's final album without Lou Reed: 'Little Jack', 'She'll Make You Cry', and 'Sweet Bonnie Brown' are demo-quality rock. The album was rejected by the label and shelved for a decade. It is a curiosity for completists.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the raw demos — the album was recorded after the band's core had left. It is best understood as a coda to their story.

synopsis: The Velvet Underground had spent their career making the most influential music in rock, but after Lou Reed left in 1970, the band's bassist Doug Yule kept the name alive for two more albums. This second of those, recorded with a new lineup, is a strange relic, full of polished pop songs that sound nothing like the band's earlier work, and its centerpiece is 'Little Jack', a song that Yule had originally recorded for a children's album. The record was a commercial failure and is generally regarded as an embarrassment by fans, but it has a strange, kitschy charm, and its story, of a legendary band reduced to a shadow of itself, is a cautionary tale. It is the sound of a great name outliving its creators.

name: Live Rust
teaser: 1979 Neil Young's live double album with Crazy Horse: 'Hey Hey, My My', 'Powderfinger', and 'Like a Hurricane' capture the band's power on stage. The album was recorded during the Rust Never Sleeps tour. It is the definitive live Neil Young document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — Crazy Horse at their loudest and loosest. The album closes with a version of 'Tonight's the Night'.

tracks.title: My My, Hey Hey (Out of the Blue)
When You Dance I Can Really Love
The Needle and the Damage Done
Hey Hey, My My (Into the Black)

synopsis: Neil Young had spent 1978 touring with Crazy Horse, and this live double album, released the following year, captured the power of those shows. The record's first disc is acoustic, with Young performing solo versions of his classics, and its second disc is pure electric chaos, with the full band tearing through 'Cortez the Killer', 'Like a Hurricane' and the epic 'Hey Hey, My My (Into the Black)'. The album was released alongside his studio record Rust Never Sleeps, and together they marked his triumphant return to relevance. It is one of the great live albums of the era, the sound of a legend and his band at the peak of their powers.

name: The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan
teaser: 1963 Bob Dylan's second album made him the voice of a generation: 'Blowin' in the Wind', 'A Hard Rain's A-Gonna Fall', and 'Don't Think Twice, It's All Right' are protest songs and love songs. The album sold 10 million copies. It is the beginning of his legend.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the writing — the album marked his leap from folk covers to original genius. 'Blowin' in the Wind' became an anthem of the civil rights movement.

tracks.title: Don't Think Twice, It's All Right
Honey, Just Allow Me One More Chance
Let Me Die in My Footsteps

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent his debut album performing mostly covers, and this second record, released in 1963, was where he became a songwriter for the ages. The album's songs, from 'Blowin' in the Wind' to 'A Hard Rain's A-Gonna Fall' to 'Don't Think Twice, It's All Right', announced a new kind of folk music, full of poetic imagery and political urgency, and Dylan's voice, nasal and untrained but utterly compelling, made them feel like dispatches from a prophet. The record made him the voice of the civil rights movement and the folk revival, and its influence on everything that followed is incalculable. It is one of the most important albums ever made, the sound of a generation finding its voice.

name: The Times They Are A-Changin'
teaser: 1964 Bob Dylan's third album is his most political: 'The Times They Are A-Changin'', 'The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll', and 'Only a Pawn in Their Game' are protest songs of rare power. The album captures the civil rights era. It is his most committed work.

exploreAction.targetName: The Times They Are A-Changin' (1964) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the anger — the album is entirely acoustic and entirely political. 'The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll' tells a true story of injustice.

tracks.title: Only a Pawn in Their Game
The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent 1963 as the voice of the folk revival, and this third album, released in 1964, was his most explicitly political statement. The record's title track, with its famous chorus about the times being a-changin', became an anthem of the civil rights movement, and songs like 'The Lonesome Death of Hattie Carroll', about a real murder, and 'Only a Pawn in Their Game', about the assassination of Medgar Evers, showed Dylan engaging directly with the news of the day. The album is full of the moral urgency of its moment, and its blend of protest and poetry made it the definitive document of the early 60s folk revival. It is the sound of a young man who believed his songs could change the world.

name: Bringing It All Back Home
teaser: 1965 Bob Dylan's fifth album mixed acoustic songs with his first electric recordings: 'Mr. Tambourine Man', 'Subterranean Homesick Blues', and 'It's Alright, Ma' are a bridge between folk and rock. The album's electric side changed music history. It is the hinge of his career.

exploreAction.targetName: Bringing It All Back Home (1965) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the transition — side one is electric, side two is acoustic. 'Subterranean Homesick Blues' introduced his rapid-fire lyrical style.

tracks.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent years as the acoustic voice of the folk revival, and this fifth album, released in 1965, was his declaration of independence. The record's first side is electric, full of the rock and roll energy that would scandalize his folk fans, from the opener 'Subterranean Homesick Blues' to 'Maggie's Farm' and 'It's Alright, Ma (I'm Only Bleeding)', and its second side returns to acoustic balladry, including 'Mr. Tambourine Man' and 'Gates of Eden'. The album's blend of poetry and rock, its surreal imagery and its sheer musical invention, made it a landmark. It is the record where Dylan stopped being a folk singer and became the most important artist in popular music.

name: John Wesley Harding
teaser: 1967 Bob Dylan's quiet album after his motorcycle crash: 'All Along the Watchtower', 'I Dreamed I Saw St. Augustine', and 'The Ballad of Frankie Lee and Judas Priest' are spare, biblical, and mysterious. The album was a radical retreat from the psychedelic era. It is among his most enduring works.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the restraint — the album is acoustic trio recordings with no production. 'All Along the Watchtower' was made famous by Jimi Hendrix's cover.

tracks.title: As I Went Out One Morning
I Dreamed I Saw St. Augustine
The Ballad of Frankie Lee and Judas Priest

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent 1966 on the most legendary tour in rock history, playing electric music to audiences who booed him, and he had just completed the sessions for his next album when he crashed his motorcycle in July 1966 and disappeared from public life. This album, his eighth, recorded in secret in Nashville during his recovery, was the quietest music he had ever made, full of simple, biblical songs about faith, sin and redemption, from 'All Along the Watchtower', which Jimi Hendrix would soon make immortal, to 'I Dreamed I Saw St. Augustine' and the title track, a portrait of an outlaw. Its spare, country-tinged sound was a complete departure, and its themes of spiritual searching defined the rest of his career. It is the sound of a man who had died and been reborn.

name: Nashville Skyline
teaser: 1969 Bob Dylan's country album with Johnny Cash: 'Lay Lady Lay', 'Girl from the North Country', and 'Tonight I'll Be Staying Here with You' are warm, melodic, and unexpected. Dylan sang in a new, softer voice. The album was a commercial success.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the voice — Dylan's new country croon surprised everyone. The duet with Johnny Cash on 'Girl from the North Country' is a historic meeting.

tracks.title: Tell Me That It Isn't True
Tonight I'll Be Staying Here with You

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the late 60s making increasingly quiet and personal records, and this ninth album, recorded in Nashville with a group of country session players, was his most straightforwardly musical in years. The record's songs are mostly love songs, sung with a warmth and clarity that surprised fans used to his nasal bark, and its centerpiece, 'Lay Lady Lay', with its famous organ part, became one of his biggest hits. The album also contains a duet with Johnny Cash on 'Girl from the North Country' and the rollicking 'Country Pie', and its relaxed, joyful mood was a deliberate reaction against the heaviness of his recent work. It is the sound of a genius taking a holiday, and it remains one of his most charming records.

name: New Morning
teaser: 1970 Bob Dylan's gentle album after years of retreat: 'If Not for You', 'New Morning', and 'Sign on the Window' are warm and domestic. The album was a return to simplicity. It is among his most relaxed records.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the calm — the album was recorded with a small band including George Harrison on guitar. 'If Not for You' was covered by George Harrison.

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent three years in seclusion after his motorcycle crash, and this tenth album, released in 1970, was his gradual return to public life. The record is his gentlest and most domestic, full of love songs and celebrations of simple pleasures, from the opening 'If Not for You', which George Harrison would soon cover, to 'The Man in Me', 'Day of the Locusts' and 'Went to See the Gypsy', a song inspired by an encounter with Elvis Presley. Dylan's voice is warm and relaxed, and the album's country-tinged sound, recorded in Nashville, matched its contented mood. It was a modest hit and is often overlooked, but its quiet charm has made it a favorite of his fans.

name: Planet Waves
teaser: 1974 Bob Dylan's album with the Band: 'Forever Young', 'Something There Is About You', and 'Going, Going, Gone' are warm and rootsy. The album was recorded in three days. 'Forever Young' became a standard.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the Band — their backing gives the album a lived-in sound. 'Forever Young' is one of Dylan's most beloved songs.

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the early 70s making quiet, unambitious records, and this fourteenth album, recorded with the Band, was his attempt to return to the rock and roll of his youth. The record was made quickly, with the Band providing the loose, rootsy backing that they had perfected over a decade of collaboration with Dylan, and its songs, from the opener 'On a Night Like This' to the epic 'Forever Young', which became one of his most beloved compositions, showed a songwriter at ease. The album topped the charts, his first number one, and its title, a reference to the astrological age, captured its sense of renewal. It is the sound of a legend reconnecting with his roots.

name: The Basement Tapes
teaser: 1975 Bob Dylan and the Band's legendary basement recordings: 'I Shall Be Released', 'You Ain't Goin' Nowhere', and 'The Mighty Quinn' were recorded in 1967 at the Band's house. The songs were circulated as bootlegs for years before official release. They defined the Americana genre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the intimacy — the recordings capture friends playing in a basement. 'The Mighty Quinn' became a hit for Manfred Mann.

tracks.title: Yea! Heavy and a Bottle of Bread
Crash on the Levee (Down in the Flood)

synopsis: In 1967, after his motorcycle crash, Bob Dylan retreated to a house in Woodstock, New York, with his band, and the recordings they made in the basement became the most legendary bootlegs in rock history. This collection, released in 1975, gathered many of those songs, from 'I Shall Be Released' and 'Tears of Rage' to 'The Weight' and 'This Wheel's on Fire', and it revealed a songwriter at the peak of his powers, writing songs that the Band would soon claim as their own. The recordings, loose and full of laughter, captured a moment of creative freedom, and their influence on the roots rock of the following decade was enormous. It is one of the most important archival releases in rock history.

name: Desire
teaser: 1976 Bob Dylan's album of long, cinematic story songs: 'Hurricane', 'One More Cup of Coffee', and 'Sara' are sweeping and theatrical. The album was recorded in five days with violinist Scarlet Rivera. 'Hurricane' tells the story of boxer Rubin Carter.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the violin — Rivera's playing weaves through every song. 'Hurricane' is a 9-minute protest song about a wrongful conviction.

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the mid-70s on his famous Rolling Thunder Revue tour, and this fifteenth album, recorded with producer Rob Stoneman and a cast of musicians including Scarlet Rivera on violin, was written during that whirlwind. The record is full of long, cinematic story songs, from 'Hurricane', a protest against the wrongful conviction of boxer Rubin Carter, to 'Isis', 'One More Cup of Coffee' and the epic 'Sara', a desperate love letter to his wife as their marriage was collapsing. Dylan's voice, ragged and urgent, and the record's gypsy-folk arrangements made it his most theatrical album. It was a huge hit, and its blend of romance and politics remains unique in his catalog.

name: Street-Legal
teaser: 1978 Bob Dylan's album of hot-rodded gospel rock: 'Changing of the Guards', 'Baby, Stop Crying', and 'Is Your Love in Vain?' are dense, theatrical, and intense. The album's production was controversial. It has been reassessed as a strong late-70s work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the horns and female backing vocals — the album's sound is unlike anything else in his catalog. 'Changing of the Guards' is an epic opener.

tracks.title: Where Are You Tonight? (Journey Through Dark Heat)

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the mid-70s on tour and in the studio, and this eighteenth album, released in 1978, was his attempt to make a rock record for the disco era. The album's sound is bigger and more polished than anything he had made before, with a full band, horns and female backing singers, and its songs, from the opener 'Changing of the Guards' to the epic 'Where Are You Tonight? (Journey Through Dark Heat)', show a songwriter in transition. The record was poorly received by critics, but its best songs, including the sardonic 'Baby, Stop Crying' and 'New Pony', have aged well, and its story, of a man on the eve of a religious conversion, is fascinating in hindsight.

name: Slow Train Coming
teaser: 1979 Bob Dylan's first gospel album: 'Gotta Serve Somebody', 'Slow Train', and 'Precious Angel' are born-again Christian songs with a funky band. The album won a Grammy for Best Male Rock Vocal. It divided fans but is musically strong.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — Mark Knopfler of Dire Straits plays guitar. 'Gotta Serve Somebody' was covered by many artists.

tracks.title: Gonna Change My Way of Thinking
Do Right to Me Baby (Do Unto Others)
Man Gave Names to All the Animals

synopsis: Bob Dylan had been raised in a Jewish family but had long been interested in Christianity, and in 1979 he surprised the world by releasing this, his first gospel album, full of songs about Jesus, sin and salvation. The record's blend of rock, soul and gospel, with its superb band and Dylan's urgent, born-again lyrics, made it an instant classic, and 'Gotta Serve Somebody', which won a Grammy, and 'Slow Train' and 'Precious Angels' showed his new conviction. Many fans were alienated by his preaching, but the music itself was among his most powerful in years, and the album's influence on Christian rock has been enormous. It is the sound of a seeker who had found what he was looking for.

name: Oh Mercy
teaser: 1989 Bob Dylan's return to critical favor: 'Everything Is Broken', 'Most of the Time', and 'Man in the Long Black Coat' are produced by Daniel Lanois. The album's swampy, mysterious sound was his best in a decade. It re-established him.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Lanois gave the album its atmospheric, haunted sound. 'Man in the Long Black Coat' is a voodoo-tinged mystery.

tracks.title: Man in the Long Black Coat

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the 80s making increasingly erratic records, and by 1989 his career was at a low ebb, with critics writing him off and his label losing faith. This album, his first with producer Daniel Lanois, was his return to form, and its atmospheric sound, full of murky textures and Dylan's weathered voice, made it his most acclaimed record in over a decade. 'Everything Is Broken', 'Political World' and the majestic 'Most of the Time' showed a songwriter who had lost none of his gifts, and the album's title, a line from an old blues song, captured its mood of desperation. It was hailed as a comeback, and it set the stage for the greatest late-career renaissance in rock history.

name: Time Out of Mind
teaser: 1997 Bob Dylan's late-career masterpiece: 'Love Sick', 'Not Dark Yet', and 'Make You Feel My Love' are brooding, world-weary, and profound. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys, his first since 1970. It began his late renaissance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album was recorded with producer Daniel Lanois in sessions that became legendary. 'Not Dark Yet' is a meditation on mortality.

tracks.title: Til I Fell in Love with You

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the 90s making records that critics ignored, and he was widely considered a spent force when he released this album, his first of new songs in seven years, in 1997. The record, produced by Daniel Lanois and recorded over several years, is a meditation on mortality, love and the passing of time, full of songs of extraordinary depth and beauty, from the opening 'Love Sick' to the devastating 'Not Dark Yet' and the epic closer 'Highlands', a sixteen-minute monologue about the emptiness of modern life. It won three Grammys, including Album of the Year, and it is regarded as the beginning of his late-career renaissance, the record where the old master proved he was still the greatest songwriter alive.

name: Love and Theft
teaser: 2001 Bob Dylan's thirtieth album: 'Mississippi', 'Summer Days', and 'Tweedle Dee & Tweedle Dum' are funny, bluesy, and loose. The album was recorded in two weeks with his touring band. It is his most playful work of the modern era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the band — the album was cut live in the studio. 'Mississippi' was rejected from Time Out of Mind and became a highlight here.

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent his late-career renaissance making increasingly acclaimed records, and this thirtieth album, released in 2001, was the summit of that period. The record is a loose, playful collection of songs in the American roots tradition, full of blues, country, jazz and Tin Pan Alley references, and its centerpiece, 'Mississippi', is one of the greatest songs he ever wrote. 'Summer Days', 'Sugar Baby' and the devastating 'High Water (for Charley Patton)' complete a record of remarkable range and vitality. Dylan's voice, ravaged by age but full of character, suits the material perfectly, and the album won a Grammy. It is the sound of an old master enjoying himself, and it remains one of his best records.

name: Modern Times
teaser: 2006 Bob Dylan's third album of his late renaissance: 'Thunder on the Mountain', 'When the Deal Goes Down', and 'Ain't Talkin'' are blues, folk, and country songs about love and the end of the world. The album debuted at number one, his first in 30 years.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the age — Dylan's voice is a gravelly instrument that carries the songs. The album's apocalyptic undertones are unmistakable.

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the early 2000s making acclaimed roots records, and this thirty-second album, released in 2006, was the third in his late renaissance trilogy. The record is built on the blues, with Dylan's voice, now a ravaged growl, front and center, and its songs, from the opening 'Thunder on the Mountain', a tribute to Alicia Keys, to the epic 'Ain't Talkin'', show a songwriter still finding new things to say. The album debuted at number one, making Dylan the oldest artist ever to top the charts, and its blend of humor, menace and hard-won wisdom made it a critical favorite. It is the sound of a legend who had become an American monument.

name: Together Through Life
teaser: 2009 Bob Dylan's album of Tex-Mex blues: 'Beyond Here Lies Nothin'', 'Life Is Hard', and 'I Feel a Change Comin' On' are warm, funny, and seasoned. The album was written quickly with Grateful Dead lyricist Robert Hunter. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the accordion — the album has a Mexican border feel. The lyrics were co-written with Robert Hunter of the Grateful Dead.

tracks.title: If You Ever Go to Houston
I Feel a Change Comin' On

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent the 2000s making increasingly bluesy records, and this thirty-third album, released in 2009, continued in that vein, with a sound inspired by the Tex-Mex music of the border. The record's songs, mostly co-written with Robert Hunter of the Grateful Dead, are full of the accordions, guitars and romantic fatalism of that tradition, from the opening 'Beyond Here Lies Nothin'' to 'If You Ever Go to Houston' and the beautiful closer 'It's All Good'. Dylan's voice, warm and weathered, suits the material, and the album's relaxed, roadhouse mood made it a modest success. It is a minor entry in his catalog, but a thoroughly enjoyable one.

name: Tempest
teaser: 2012 Bob Dylan's 35th album: 'Duquesne Whistle', 'Pay in Blood', and 'Tempest' are long, dark, and masterful. The album's 14-minute title track recounts the Titanic sinking. It is among his most forceful late works.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the storytelling — the album is filled with narratives of murder, love, and disaster. 'Tempest' is a grim epic.

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent his late career making increasingly acclaimed records, and this thirty-fifth album, released in 2012, was another high point. The record's songs are mostly long, brooding meditations on mortality and American history, from the opening 'Duquesne Whistle' to the fourteen-minute 'Tempest', a retelling of the sinking of the Titanic, and the album's title track, and they are delivered with a fury that belied his 71 years. 'Pay in Blood', 'Narrow Way' and the murder ballad 'Tin Angel' complete a record of unusual darkness and power. It was hailed as one of his best late records, and its themes of death and judgment suggested a man contemplating his own end.

name: Rough and Rowdy Ways
teaser: 2020 Bob Dylan's first album of new songs in eight years: 'Murder Most Foul', 'I Contain Multitudes', and 'Key West (Philosopher Pirate)' are long, literary, and profound. The 17-minute 'Murder Most Foul' about the JFK assassination was a surprise hit. It is his late masterpiece.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the poetry — the album's lyrics are among his most dense and allusive. 'Murder Most Foul' references dozens of songs and events.

tracks.title: I've Made Up My Mind to Give Myself to You

synopsis: Bob Dylan had spent eight years without releasing a new album, touring constantly and seeming content to be a living monument, and this thirty-ninth record, released in 2020, was a shock: his first album of new songs since 2012. The record is a meditation on mortality, history and the American song, from the seventeen-minute epic 'Murder Most Foul', about the assassination of John F. Kennedy, which became his first number one single, to the tender 'I Contain Multitudes' and the title track, a bluesy reflection on his own journey. Dylan's voice, now a deep, cracked whisper, gives the songs an almost biblical weight. It is a late masterpiece, the sound of the greatest songwriter in American history summing up his life.

name: Check Your Head
teaser: 1992 The Beastie Boys' fourth album returned to their roots: 'So What'cha Want', 'Pass the Mic', and 'Gratitude' blend rap with live funk. The band played their own instruments for the first time. It is their most organic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the live band — the album was recorded with the group playing real instruments. 'Pass the Mic' is a dense, playful manifesto.

synopsis: The Beastie Boys had spent their first three albums moving from frat-boy rap to dense sample collages, and this fourth record, released in 1992, was a return to their roots as musicians. The album was recorded after the trio learned to play their instruments, and it finds them playing live in the studio, mixing rap with funk, punk and jazz, and its highlights include the funky 'So What'cha Want', the punk of 'Time for Livin'' and the jazzy instrumental 'In 3's'. It was a hit and confirmed that the Beasties were more than a novelty act.

name: Ill Communication
teaser: 1994 The Beastie Boys' fifth album mixed rap, punk, and funk: 'Sabotage', 'Sure Shot', and 'Root Down' are furious and fun. The album debuted at number one. 'Sabotage' became famous for its music video.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album jumps from hardcore punk to smooth jazz. 'Sabotage' is a hardcore blast with a legendary video.

tracks.title: B-Boys Makin' with the Freak Freak

synopsis: The Beastie Boys had spent their fourth album learning to play their instruments, and this fifth record found them integrating those skills into their music completely. The album's centerpiece is 'Sabotage', a blast of hard rock fury with a legendary music video, and it also contains the funky 'Get It Together' with Q-Tip, the jazzy 'Root Down' and the mellow 'Sure Shot', which samples a flute solo by his mother. The record debuted at number one and won a Grammy, and its blend of rap, punk and funk made it the definitive statement of the trio's musicianship. It is the sound of a band that had grown up without losing its sense of fun.

name: Hello Nasty
teaser: 1998 The Beastie Boys' sixth album was their most futuristic: 'Intergalactic', 'Body Movin'', and 'Remote Control' blend sci-fi samples with their signature raps. The album won a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the samples — the album is packed with odd, funky breaks. 'Intergalactic' became a global hit with its robot-voice chorus.

synopsis: The Beastie Boys had spent the 90s as one of the most respected acts in hip-hop, and this sixth album, released in 1998, was their most futuristic. The record's title, a reference to the band's in-joke name for their fan club, and its sci-fi artwork set the tone for an album full of electronic textures and space-age sounds, from the opener 'Super Disco Breakin'' to the hits 'Intergalactic' and 'Body Movin''. The album debuted at number one and won two Grammys, and its blend of old-school rap and futuristic production made it their most successful record. It is the sound of a band that had been around for fifteen years and was still ahead of the curve.

name: To the 5 Boroughs
teaser: 2004 The Beastie Boys' album about New York after 9/11: 'Ch-Check It Out', 'An Open Letter to NYC', and 'Triple Trouble' are political and defiant. The album was their first without Adam Yauch's usual voice. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the message — the album directly addresses the attacks and the city's recovery. 'An Open Letter to NYC' is a love letter to their home.

synopsis: The Beastie Boys had spent the 90s as elder statesmen of hip-hop, and this seventh album, released in 2004, was their response to the September 11 attacks, which had happened a few blocks from their studio. The record is a love letter to New York, full of songs about the city and its resilience, and its political content, from 'Ch-Check It Out' to the anti-war 'Operation Right to Fail', was the most direct of their career. The album's sound, built on the old-school beats and raps that had made them famous, was a deliberate return to basics, and its title, a reference to the five boroughs, captured its civic pride. It was a modest hit and remains a love letter to their hometown.

name: Hot Sauce Committee Part Two
