teaser: 2013 Jay-Z's album of luxury and legacy: 'Holy Grail', 'Picasso Baby', and 'Tom Ford' are grandiose and introspective. The album was released through a Samsung app partnership. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guest list — Justin Timberlake, Beyoncé, and Rick Ross appear. 'Holy Grail' samples Nirvana's 'Smells Like Teen Spirit'.

synopsis: Jay-Z had spent his career as the most successful rapper in history, and this twelfth album, released in 2013, was a meditation on the costs of that success. The record was made with a cast of superstar producers, including Timbaland, Pharrell Williams and Kanye West, and its songs, from 'Holy Grail', a duet with Justin Timberlake, to 'Picasso Baby' and 'Oceans', are full of the luxury and isolation of his life. The album was famously released in partnership with Samsung, giving it away to millions of users, a move that divided the industry. It was a commercial success, and its best songs are among the most reflective of his career. It is the sound of a man counting his blessings and his enemies.

teaser: 2017 Jay-Z's confessional album: '4:44', 'The Story of O.J.', and 'Family Feud' address infidelity, race, and family. The album was released exclusively to Tidal first. It is his most personal work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the honesty — the title track is an apology to Beyoncé. The album's production is sparse and soulful.

synopsis: Jay-Z had spent years as the most successful rapper in history, but this thirteenth album, released in 2017, was his most personal and vulnerable record. The album is a confession, full of songs about his infidelity, his therapy and his family, made in the aftermath of Beyoncé's album Lemonade, which had exposed his cheating to the world. The title track, with its gorgeous beat, and 'The Story of O.J.', a meditation on race and wealth, and 'Family Feud' are among the most honest songs he has ever written. It was hailed as a masterpiece, and its willingness to confront his own failures made it his most acclaimed record in years. It is the sound of a legend finally telling the truth.

name: Infinite
teaser: 1996 Eminem's independent debut: 'Infinite', 'Backstabber', and 'Open Mic' show a young rapper finding his voice. The album sold poorly but caught the attention of Dr. Dre. It is a fascinating origin story.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the evolution — the album shows Em before his Slim Shady persona. 'Infinite' is a showcase of early technical skill.

synopsis: Eminem had spent the early 90s as a struggling rapper in Detroit, and this independent debut, released in 1996, was his first attempt to break through. The record shows the influences that would define his style, from the storytelling of Nas to the wordplay of the Wu-Tang Clan, and its songs, from the title track to 'Backstabber' and 'Open Mic', are full of the technical skill that would later make him famous, though his voice and persona had not yet fully formed. The album sold poorly, and Eminem was on the verge of giving up when he was discovered by Dr. Dre. It is a fascinating document of a genius before he became a star.

name: Encore
teaser: 2004 Eminem's fifth album: 'Just Lose It', 'Mockingbird', and 'Like Toy Soldiers' mix humor, heart, and rage. The album was recorded during his addiction struggles. It is a troubled but revealing work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the emotional tracks — 'Mockingbird' is a song to his daughter, 'Like Toy Soldiers' addresses his feuds. The album's darker songs outshine the comedy.

synopsis: Eminem had spent the early 2000s as the most controversial and successful rapper in the world, and this fifth album, released in 2004, found him struggling with the pressures of fame. The record's lead single, 'Just Lose It', a parody of Michael Jackson, caused a scandal, and 'Mockingbird', a tender song for his daughter, showed the vulnerability beneath the shock tactics. The album was made during a period of intense drug addiction, and its quality suffers as a result, with too many forgettable tracks padding out the record. It was a commercial success, debuting at number one, but it is generally regarded as his weakest work of the decade. It is the sound of a genius losing his way.

name: Relapse
teaser: 2009 Eminem's comeback after his overdose: 'Crack a Bottle', 'Beautiful', and '3 a.m.' are dark, technical, and horror-themed. The album was produced almost entirely by Dr. Dre. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the technical skill — the album showcases Em's best rapping in years. 'Beautiful' is a reflective highlight.

synopsis: Eminem had spent 2005-2007 in a coma and rehab, nearly dying from the drug addiction that had consumed him, and this sixth album, released in 2009, was his attempt to come back. The record was produced largely by Dr. Dre, and its sound, full of the horrorcore imagery and technical rapping of his early work, was a deliberate return to form. 'Crack a Bottle' became his first number one single in years, and 'Beautiful' and the haunting 'Déjà Vu', about his overdose, showed a new honesty. It won a Grammy and was hailed as a comeback, though some critics noted that the Slim Shady persona felt forced. It is the sound of a man clawing his way back from the brink.

name: Recovery
teaser: 2010 Eminem's album of sobriety: 'Not Afraid', 'Love the Way You Lie', and 'No Love' are anthems of survival. The album sold 20 million copies. It is his most commercially successful work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the message — the album is about rebuilding after addiction. 'Love the Way You Lie' with Rihanna was a global smash.

synopsis: Eminem had spent his comeback album Relapse returning to his old persona, and this seventh album, released in 2010, found him embracing sobriety and a new maturity. The record's lead single, 'Not Afraid', became an anthem of recovery, and 'Love the Way You Lie', a duet with Rihanna about domestic violence, became one of the biggest hits of his career. 'No Love' and 'Space Bound' continued the run, and the album's blend of introspection and technical skill made it his most commercially successful record, selling over ten million copies. It won a Grammy and re-established Eminem as the biggest rapper in the world. It is the sound of a man who had been to hell and come back stronger.

name: The Marshall Mathers LP 2
teaser: 2013 Eminem's sequel to his masterpiece: 'Berzerk', 'Rap God', and 'Headlights' revisit his legacy. The album's 12-minute 'Rap God' became famous for its speed. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the references — the album revisits themes and samples from the original. 'Headlights' is a reconciliation with his mother.

synopsis: Eminem had spent his career as the most technically skilled rapper in the world, and this eighth album, released in 2013, was a sequel to the record that had made him a star, The Marshall Mathers LP. The record is full of the rapid-fire rapping and dark humor of his early work, from 'Berzerk', with its Beastie Boys sample, to 'Rap God', a six-minute display of technical virtuosity that became a viral sensation. 'The Monster', a duet with Rihanna, became his fifth number one single, and the album's blend of nostalgia and innovation made it a commercial success. It is the sound of a master showing the young guns how it's done.

name: Revival
teaser: 2017 Eminem's political album: 'Walk on Water', 'River', and 'Untouchable' address race, politics, and his critics. The album received mixed reviews. It is his most contentious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the politics — the album was released during the Trump era. 'Untouchable' addresses racial profiling.

synopsis: Eminem had spent the mid-2010s as an elder statesman of rap, and this ninth album, released in 2017, found him turning political. The record's songs are full of fury at Donald Trump, gun violence and the state of America, from 'Walk on Water', a duet with Beyoncé about the burden of genius, to 'River', with Ed Sheeran, and the album's centerpiece, 'Untouchable'. The album was made with a new producer, Rick Rubin, and its sound, full of rock samples and gospel choirs, was a departure from his usual style. It received mixed reviews, with many critics finding it bloated and unfocused. It is the sound of a legend trying to stay relevant in a changed world.

name: Kamikaze
teaser: 2018 Eminem's surprise diss album: 'The Ringer', 'Lucky You', and 'Fall' attack critics and fellow rappers. The album was released without announcement. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the aggression — the album is a response to criticism of Revival. 'The Ringer' is a relentless opener.

synopsis: Eminem had spent 2017 releasing the poorly received Revival, and when critics and fans turned on him, he responded with this surprise album, released in 2018 with almost no warning. The record is a diss album aimed at the new generation of rappers and critics who had dismissed him, from the opening 'The Ringer' to 'Lucky You' and the infamous 'Fall', and its title, a reference to the kamikaze pilots of World War II, captured its suicidal fury. The album was a commercial success, debuting at number one, and its blend of technical skill and spite reminded everyone why Eminem was still feared. It is the sound of a legend lashing out at his doubters.

name: Music to Be Murdered By
teaser: 2020 Eminem's album with Alfred Hitchcock samples: 'Godzilla', 'Darkness', and 'Premonition' are technical and dark. The album debuted at number one. 'Godzilla' features a legendary rapid-fire verse.

exploreAction.targetName: Music to Be Murdered By (2020) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — the album is packed with dense, rapid rhymes. 'Darkness' addresses the Las Vegas shooting with a twist.

synopsis: Eminem had spent his career making concept albums and alter egos, and this tenth album, released in 2020, was built around samples of Alfred Hitchcock's music and dialogue. The record's songs, from the opener 'Premonition' to 'Godzilla', a display of rapid-fire rapping with the late Juice WRLD, and 'Darkness', a devastating song about the Las Vegas shooting told from the shooter's perspective, are among the most ambitious of his late career. The album was announced with a mock trailer and released on the anniversary of Hitchcock's death, and its blend of horror imagery and social commentary made it a critical success. It is the sound of a legend still finding new ways to surprise.

name: The Death of Slim Shady (Coup de Grâce)
teaser: 2024 Eminem's conceptual farewell to his alter ego: 'Houdini', 'Tobey', and 'Renaissance' kill off Slim Shady in a narrative album. The album debuted at number one. It is his most ambitious late work.

exploreAction.targetName: The Death of Slim Shady (Coup de Grâce) (2024) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the concept — the album is structured as a story about destroying his persona. 'Houdini' became a global hit.

synopsis: Eminem had spent his career rapping as Slim Shady, the outrageous alter ego who had made him famous, and this eleventh album, released in 2024, was his attempt to kill that persona once and for all. The record is a concept album about the death of Slim Shady, with songs like 'Houdini', a tribute to his early hits, and 'Tobey' exploring the relationship between Eminem and the character that made him a star. The album was made with producer Dr. Dre, and its blend of nostalgia and self-examination made it a commercial success. It is the sound of a legend saying goodbye to the monster he created, a farewell to the persona that defined his career.

name: N.W.A and the Posse
teaser: 1987 N.W.A's early compilation: 'Boyz-n-the-Hood', 'Dopeman', and '8 Ball' collect early tracks by Ice Cube and Eazy-E. The album predates the group's official debut. It is a rough sketch of what came next.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the origins — the compilation shows the group before their breakthrough. 'Boyz-n-the-Hood' was an early hit.

tracks.title: Tuffest Man Alive featuring The D.O.C.

synopsis: N.W.A had spent the mid-80s as the most controversial group in rap, and this compilation, released in 1987, was their introduction to the world. The record gathers tracks recorded by the group's members before they officially formed, including the legendary 'Boyz-n-the-Hood', Eazy-E's debut single, and 'Dopeman', and it also features solo tracks by the various members. The album sold well in Los Angeles and helped build the buzz that would explode with the group's debut proper. It is a rough, uneven collection, but it contains the seeds of the revolution that N.W.A would unleash. It is an essential document of the birth of gangsta rap.

name: Efil4zaggin
teaser: 1991 N.W.A's second and final album: 'Alwayz into Somethin'', 'Appetite for Destruction', and 'Findum, Fuckum & Flee' are raw and confrontational. The album was recorded without Ice Cube. It reached number one, a first for gangsta rap.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Dr. Dre's beats are more polished than the debut. The album's lyrics are among the most explicit ever released.

synopsis: N.W.A had spent their debut album Straight Outta Compton shocking the world, and this second and final album, released in 1991, was both a commercial triumph and a farewell. The record's title, the group's name spelled backwards, was a deliberate provocation, and its songs, from 'Alwayz into Somethin'' to 'Appetite for Destruction', continued the group's celebration of violence, misogyny and rebellion. The album was made as the group was falling apart, with Ice Cube having already left and lawsuits flying, and it topped the charts despite being banned from many retailers. It is a difficult, ugly record, but it remains a fascinating document of a group that changed rap forever and then destroyed itself.

name: The Predator
teaser: 1992 Ice Cube's third album: 'It Was a Good Day', 'Check Yo Self', and 'Today Was a Good Day' are West Coast classics. The album was recorded after the LA riots. It debuted at number one.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album blends anger and reflection. 'It Was a Good Day' is one of the most beloved hip-hop songs ever.

tracks.title: We Had to Tear This Mothafucka Up
Say Hi to the Bad Guy

synopsis: Ice Cube had spent his first two solo albums establishing himself as rap's most ferocious political voice, and this third album, released in 1992, was his commercial breakthrough. The record's centerpiece is 'It Was a Good Day', a celebration of a perfect day in South Central Los Angeles that became one of the most beloved rap songs of all time, and 'Check Yo Self', with its unforgettable hook, and 'We Had to Tear This Mothafucka Up' continued the run. The album was released shortly after the Los Angeles riots, which gave its portrait of urban life an urgent resonance, and it sold over two million copies. It is the record where the revolutionary became a star.

name: Lethal Injection
teaser: 1993 Ice Cube's fourth album: 'You Know How We Do It', 'Bop Gun (One Nation)', and 'What Can I Do?' are funkier and more melodic. The album was produced with DJ Pooh. It is his most polished early work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the album samples Parliament and George Clinton. 'You Know How We Do It' is a laid-back classic.

tracks.title: You Know How We Do It
Make It Ruff, Make It Smooth

synopsis: Ice Cube had spent the early 90s as rap's most feared political voice, and this fourth album, released in 1993, found him adding humor and funk to his fury. The record's lead single, 'You Know How We Do It', a laid-back celebration of his success, became one of his biggest hits, and 'Bop Gun (One Nation)', with its Parliament sample, showed a new, party-friendly side. The album also contains 'Really Doe' and the political 'Ghetto Bird', and its blend of street knowledge and good times made it a commercial success. It is the sound of a revolutionary learning to enjoy the fruits of his labor.

name: The Great Adventures of Slick Rick
teaser: 1988 Slick Rick's debut is a storytelling masterpiece: 'Children's Story', 'Hey Young World', and 'Mona Lisa' are witty, detailed, and influential. The album is one of the greatest debuts in hip-hop. It defined narrative rap.

exploreAction.targetName: The Great Adventures of Slick Rick (1988) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the stories — every track is a miniature narrative. 'Children's Story' was covered and sampled countless times.

synopsis: Slick Rick had spent the mid-80s as one of the most distinctive voices in rap, a British-born storyteller with an eye patch and a gift for narrative, and this debut album, released in 1988, is a masterpiece of storytelling. The record's songs, from the epic 'Children's Story', a cautionary tale about a young criminal, to 'Mona Lisa' and 'Hey Young World', are full of the wit, warmth and narrative detail that made him unique, and his voice, smooth and theatrical, carries every tale with total command. The album was a critical and commercial success, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest rap albums of all time. It is the sound of rap's greatest storyteller at the peak of his powers.

name: De La Soul Is Dead
teaser: 1991 De La Soul's dark sequel to their debut: 'A Roller Skating Jam Named 'Saturdays'', 'Ring Ring Ring (Ha Ha Hey)', and 'Millie Pulled a Pistol on Santa' are moody and eclectic. The album rejected their image. It is a bold, strange classic.

exploreAction.targetName: De La Soul Is Dead (1991) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the skits — the album is framed as a continuous radio broadcast. 'Millie Pulled a Pistol on Santa' is a shocking narrative.

tracks.title: Johnny's Dead AKA Vincent Mason (Live from the BK Lounge)
Afro Connections at a Hi 5 (In the Eyes of the Hoodlum)
Millie Pulled a Pistol on Santa
Not Over till the Fat Lady Plays the Demo

synopsis: De La Soul had spent their debut album 3 Feet High and Rising establishing themselves as the playful, positive alternative to hardcore rap, and this second album, released in 1991, was a deliberate darkening of their image. The record's title, a response to critics who had written them off as a novelty act, set the tone, and its songs, from 'A Roller Skating Jam Named Saturdays' to the title track, a bitter meditation on the music industry, are full of the group's trademark wordplay but with a new edge. The album also contains 'Ring Ring Ring (Ha Ha Hey)', a song about the group's frustration with their own success. It is a difficult, rewarding record, the sound of a group fighting for its identity.

name: Buhloone Mindstate
teaser: 1993 De La Soul's jazz-influenced album: 'Ego Trippin' (Part Two)', 'I Am I Be', and 'Patti Dooke' are loose, live, and philosophical. The album was recorded with jazz musicians. It is their most organic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the live instruments — the album features a horn section and Maceo Parker. 'I Am I Be' is a statement of identity.

synopsis: De La Soul had spent their first two albums establishing themselves as rap's most inventive group, and this third record, released in 1993, found them going deeper into jazz and funk. The album's sound, built on live instrumentation and jazz samples, was a departure from the sample-heavy style of their earlier work, and its songs, from 'Ego Trippin' (Part Two)' to 'I Am I Be' and the beautiful 'Patti Dooke', show the group at their most relaxed and confident. The record also contains the brilliant 'Breakadawn', and its overall mood of mellow, psychedelic positivity made it a fan favorite. It is the sound of a group that had stopped trying to please anyone but itself.

name: Stakes Is High
teaser: 1996 De La Soul's album of independence: 'Stakes Is High', 'The Bizness', and 'Itzsoweezee (Hot)' are sample-dense and politically aware. The album was a response to commercial rap. It is their most critically acclaimed later work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — J Dilla contributed beats, including 'Stakes Is High'. The album's title track is a landmark.

tracks.title: Baby Baby Baby Baby Ooh Baby

synopsis: De La Soul had spent the early 90s fighting their label over royalties and their own creative freedom, and this fourth album, released in 1996, was their declaration of independence. The record was the first on their own label, and its title track, a meditation on the state of hip-hop, became an underground anthem, with its famous line about the music losing its soul. The album's sound, built on jazzy, sample-heavy production, was a return to the group's roots, and its songs, from 'The Bizness' to 'Big Brother Beat' and the gorgeous 'Long Island Wildin'', showed a group at the peak of its powers. It is regarded as their masterpiece, the record where they finally took full control.

name: The Grind Date
teaser: 2004 De La Soul's album of maturity: 'Shopping Bags (She Got from You)', 'Church', and 'Much More' are polished and reflective. The album reunited them with producer 9th Wonder. It is their strongest album of the 2000s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — 9th Wonder and Madlib contribute beats. 'Shopping Bags' is a fan favorite.

synopsis: De La Soul had spent the late 90s in a legal and commercial wilderness, and this seventh album, released in 2004 after a four-year silence, was their return. The record is their most mature and polished, full of the grown-up concerns of a group in its forties, and its production, by the duo of 9th Wonder and J Dilla, among others, gives the music a warm, soulful feel. 'Shopping Bags (She Got from You)' and 'Rock Co.Kane Flow', with MF Doom, are highlights, and the album's relaxed confidence showed a group at peace with its legacy. It is a late-career triumph, the sound of veterans proving they still had plenty to say.

name: and the Anonymous Nobody...
teaser: 2016 De La Soul's crowdfunded album: 'Pain', 'Drawn', and 'Property of Spitkool.com' were built from live improvisations. The album was funded by fans on Kickstarter. It is their final album before their catalog hit streaming.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the process — the album was built from jam sessions with live musicians. 'Pain' features a spoken-word intro.

synopsis: De La Soul had spent decades as one of the most beloved groups in hip-hop, and this eighth album, released in 2016, was their most ambitious experiment yet, funded entirely by a crowdfunding campaign. The record was built from live recordings made with a full band over several years, and its sound, full of funk, rock and jazz, was a complete departure from the sample-based hip-hop that had made them famous. 'Pain', 'Drawn' and the epic 'Property of Spitkicker.com' showed the group pushing itself into new territory, and its title, a reference to the anonymous voices that shaped their sound, captured its theme. It is a sprawling, uneven, endlessly interesting record from a group that never stopped experimenting.

name: The Impossible Kid
teaser: 2016 Aesop Rock's solo album: 'Rings', 'Kirby', and 'Lotta Years' are dense, witty, and personal. The album was recorded alone at home. It is his most accessible work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the wordplay — Aesop's dense rhymes reward repeated listens. 'Rings' is about his failed art career.

synopsis: Aesop Rock had spent two decades as one of the most respected underground rappers in the world, and this seventh solo album, released in 2016, was his most personal. The record is full of songs about his life in Portland, his family and his struggles, and its centerpiece, 'Rings', a meditation on his abandoned art career, and 'Kirby', a tribute to his cat, showed a vulnerability that his dense, abstract style usually hid. The production, largely by Aesop himself, is warm and melodic, and the album's blend of technical skill and emotional honesty made it his most accessible work. It is the sound of a genius letting his guard down.

name: Because the Internet
teaser: 2013 Childish Gambino's concept album: '3005', 'Sweatpants', and 'Flight of the Navigator' explore loneliness and internet culture. The album was accompanied by a 72-page screenplay. It is his breakthrough work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the narrative — the album follows a character through isolation. '3005' is a trap-pop classic.

tracks.title: Playing Around Before the Party Starts
II. Earth: The Oldest Computer (The Last Night)
III. Life: The Biggest Troll (Andrew Auernheimer)

synopsis: Childish Gambino, the music persona of actor Donald Glover, had spent his early career as a witty, wordy rapper, and this second album, released in 2013, was his leap into concept territory. The record tells the story of a young man named The Boy, isolated and paranoid in his mansion, and its songs, from '3005' to 'Sweatpants' and the epic closer 'Flight of the Navigator', are full of the loneliness of success. The album was released with a screenplay and a series of videos that expanded its universe, and its blend of rap, R&B and electronic music made it his most ambitious work yet. It is the sound of a restless genius refusing to be categorized.

name: Awaken, My Love!
teaser: 2016 Childish Gambino's funk album: 'Redbone', 'Me and Your Mama', and 'Terrified' are psychedelic soul. The album abandoned rapping for singing. 'Redbone' became a Grammy-winning classic.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the album channels Parliament-Funkadelic. 'Redbone' has one of the most sampled vocals of the decade.

tracks.title: The Night Me and Your Mama Met

synopsis: Childish Gambino had spent his career as one of the most versatile artists in pop, and this third album, released in 2016, found him abandoning rap entirely for funk and soul. The record is a love letter to the music of the 70s, full of the warm, psychedelic sounds of Parliament and Sly Stone, and its centerpiece, 'Redbone', with its eerie falsetto and slow-burning groove, became one of the defining songs of the decade. 'Me and Your Mama' and 'Terrified' showed the album's range, and its blend of nostalgia and menace made it a critical triumph. It is the sound of an artist reinventing himself completely, and it remains his most acclaimed record.

teaser: 2020 Childish Gambino's surprise album: 'Algorhythm', 'This Is America', and 'Time' are experimental and political. The album was released as a stream with a digital artwork. 'This Is America' had won the Grammy for Record of the Year.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experimentation — the album blends funk, gospel, and electronic music. 'Algorhythm' is a dense opener.

synopsis: Childish Gambino had spent years teasing his final album, and this surprise release, dropped without warning in March 2020 as the pandemic was beginning, was it. The record's centerpiece, 'This Is America', which had been released two years earlier and became a cultural phenomenon with its video about gun violence, finally had a home, and the album's other songs, from 'Algorhythm' to 'Time' and 'Feels Like Summer', explore similar themes of race, technology and the American nightmare. The record was released in a deliberately unfinished form, with tracks that run together and titles taken from their file names, and its raw, experimental quality divided listeners. It is a fascinating, frustrating farewell from one of the most ambitious artists of his generation.

name: Camp
teaser: 2011 Childish Gambino's major-label debut: 'Bonfire', 'Heartbeat', and 'Backpackers' are witty, pop-aware rap. The album was produced largely by Ludwig Goransson. It is his most direct work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — Ludwig Goransson's beats are cinematic. 'Bonfire' is a brash statement of arrival.

synopsis: Childish Gambino had spent his early career building a following with mixtapes and viral videos, and this major-label debut, released in 2011, was his introduction to the wider world. The record is full of the sharp, witty rapping and pop culture references that had made him a cult figure, from 'Bonfire' to 'Heartbeat' and 'Backpackers', and its sound, produced by a team that included Ludwig Göransson, mixed rap with indie rock and R&B. The album was a modest commercial success, and its blend of intelligence and humor made it a favorite of critics. It is the record where the comedian became a rapper, and the rapper became a star.

name: Richard D. James Album
teaser: 1996 Aphex Twin's breakthrough: 'Cornish Acid', '4', and 'Girl/Boy Song' blend drill-and-bass rhythms with classical strings. The album was recorded at his home studio. It is his most melodic work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the drum programming — the beats are impossibly fast and precise. 'Girl/Boy Song' has a beautiful string section.

synopsis: Aphex Twin, the pseudonym of Richard D. James, had spent the early 90s as the most radical figure in electronic music, and this fourth album, released in 1996, was his most accessible work yet. The record's sound, full of breakbeats, classical samples and the strange, beautiful melodies that had become his signature, was a perfect fusion of his experimental instincts and his pop sensibility, and its centerpiece, 'Girl/Boy Song', with its intricate percussion, became a cult classic. 'Cornish Acid' and '4' showed his range, and the album's title, a reference to his own name, captured its personal quality. It is the album that made Aphex Twin a star beyond the underground.

name: Drukqs
teaser: 2001 Aphex Twin's double album: 'Vordhosbn', 'Avril 14th', and 'Mt Saint Michel' alternate between frenetic drill-and-bass and delicate piano. The album was recorded over years. It is his most ambitious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the contrast — the album swings between chaos and calm. 'Avril 14th' is one of his most beloved piano pieces.

tracks.title: Mt Saint Michel + Saint Michaels Mount

synopsis: Aphex Twin had spent five years away from the spotlight, and this double album, released in 2001, was his return, a sprawling collection that showed every side of his genius. The record's first disc is full of the frantic, drill-and-bass tracks that had made him famous, from 'Vordhosbn' to 'Mt Saint Michel + Saint Michaels Mount', while its second disc is dominated by the quiet, beautiful piano pieces, including 'Avril 14th', which became one of his most beloved compositions after being used in films and samples by Kanye West. The album was made on a laptop while James traveled, and its mix of chaos and tenderness made it a critical triumph. It is a demanding, rewarding record, the sound of a genius with nothing left to prove.

name: Syro
teaser: 2014 Aphex Twin's return after 13 years: 'Xmas_Evet10', 'minipops 67', and 'Aisatsana' are warm and playful. The album was announced with a blimp over London. It won a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the warmth — the album is more melodic than his abrasive work. It is a fitting comeback.

synopsis: Aphex Twin had spent thirteen years without releasing an album of new material, and this record, released in 2014 with almost no warning, was one of the most anticipated electronic releases in history. The album was delivered in a plain sleeve with no title on the cover, and its music, full of the intricate rhythms and strange melodies that had defined his career, showed that James had lost none of his genius. 'minipops 67' and 'XMAS_EVET10' were instant classics, and the album won a Grammy, a rare honor for such experimental music. It is the sound of a legend returning after a long silence, and it proved that the most original mind in electronic music was still years ahead of everyone else.

name: Geogaddi
teaser: 2002 Boards of Canada's darker follow-up: 'Music Is Math', '1969', and 'The Beach at Redpoint' are eerie, detailed, and occult. The album was rumored to contain hidden messages. It is their most mysterious work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the details — the album is dense with samples and hidden sounds. It rewards repeated, careful listening.

tracks.title: The Devil Is in the Details
A Is to B as B Is to C

synopsis: Boards of Canada had spent their debut album establishing a sound of warm, nostalgic electronic music, and this second album, released in 2002, was its darker shadow. The record is full of the eerie, unsettling textures that lurked beneath the duo's melodies, from the opener 'Ready Let's Go' to 'Music Is Math' and the terrifying '1969', and its themes, drawn from cults, numerology and childhood trauma, gave the music a sense of unease that their debut lacked. It is a difficult, demanding record, but its atmosphere is unmatched, and it is now regarded as one of the greatest electronic albums of all time. It is the sound of nostalgia turning into nightmare.

name: The Campfire Headphase
teaser: 2005 Boards of Canada's album with guitars: 'Dayvan Cowboy', 'Peacock Tail', and 'Chromakey Dreamcoat' blend their electronic sound with folk guitar. The album was a departure for the duo. It is their warmest work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the guitars — the album was the first to feature live instruments prominently. 'Dayvan Cowboy' is a highlight.

synopsis: Boards of Canada had spent their career making electronic music that sounded like memories, and this third album, released in 2005, found them adding a new element: guitars. The record's sound, full of the warm, fuzzy textures of live instrumentation mixed with their trademark synthesizers and tape effects, was a departure from their earlier work, and its centerpiece, 'Dayvan Cowboy', with its epic guitar solo and its famous video of a skydiver, became their best-known song. 'Peacock Tail' and 'Oscar See Through Red Eye' showed the album's range, and its overall mood of pastoral melancholy made it a favorite of fans. It is the sound of a duo expanding its palette without losing its identity.

name: Tomorrow's Harvest
teaser: 2013 Boards of Canada's dystopian album: 'Reach for the Dead', 'Nothing Is Real', and 'Jacquard Causeway' are bleak, cinematic, and precise. The album was teased with a code hidden in vinyl grooves. It is their most political work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the mood — the album imagines a post-collapse world. It rewards headphones and patience.

synopsis: Boards of Canada had spent their career making electronic music that felt like distant memories, and this fourth album, released in 2013 after an eight-year silence, was their darkest and most dystopian record. The album's title, a reference to an obscure horror film, set the tone, and its songs, from the opener 'Reach for the Dead' to 'Nothing Is Real' and the terrifying 'Cold Earth', are full of the imagery of environmental collapse and societal decay. The duo had been inspired by abandoned places and end-of-the-world scenarios, and the record's bleak, cinematic mood was a complete departure from their earlier warmth. It is a difficult, unsettling album, but its atmosphere is unmatched. It is the sound of nostalgia turning to dread.

name: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country
teaser: 2000 Boards of Canada's EP: 'Amo Bishop Roden', 'Kid for Today', and the title track are gentle and hypnotic. The EP was named after a Branch Davidian settlement. It is their most focused release.

exploreAction.targetName: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country (2000) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its simple melody is one of their most memorable. The EP is a perfect entry point.

tracks.title: In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country

synopsis: Boards of Canada had spent the late 90s building a cult following with a series of EPs, and this release, from 2000, is the best of them. The record's title track, 'In a Beautiful Place Out in the Country', with its eerie organ and its invocation of cult leader David Koresh, is one of the most unsettling and beautiful things the duo ever recorded, and 'Kid for Today' and 'Amo Bishop Roden' complete a record of extraordinary atmosphere. The EP is a perfect introduction to the duo's world, full of the warmth, unease and mystery that defined their music. It is a minor entry in their catalog, but its best moments are as powerful as anything on their albums.

name: Thrust
teaser: 1974 Herbie Hancock's follow-up to Head Hunters: 'Actual Proof', 'Palm Grease', and 'Spank-a-Lee' are deep, funky, and complex. The album featured a new lineup. It is a fan favorite among jazz-funk fans.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the interplay — the band locks into complex grooves. 'Actual Proof' is a fusion classic.

synopsis: Herbie Hancock had spent his career as one of the most versatile musicians in jazz, and this 1974 album, his follow-up to the landmark Head Hunters, continued his exploration of funk. The record is full of the electric keyboards, clavinet and bass grooves that had defined his fusion sound, and its centerpiece, 'Actual Proof', with its complex, shifting rhythms, became a favorite of jazz-funk fans, while 'Palm Grease' and the beautiful 'Spank-a-Lee' showed his range. The album was a commercial success, and its blend of jazz sophistication and danceable funk made it a landmark of the genre. It is the sound of a genius at the peak of his fusion powers.

name: Romantic Warrior
teaser: 1976 Return to Forever's fusion masterpiece: 'Medieval Overture', 'Sorceress', and 'The Romantic Warrior' are classically influenced jazz-rock. The album is the peak of 70s fusion. It remains a touchstone for guitarists and bassists.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the virtuosity — the band plays with incredible precision and speed. The album is a gateway to jazz fusion.

tracks.title: Duel of the Jester and the Tyrant (Parts I and II)

synopsis: Return to Forever, led by keyboardist Chick Corea, had spent the early 70s as one of the most ambitious bands in jazz fusion, and this fifth album, released in 1976, was their masterpiece. The record is dominated by guitarist Al Di Meola, whose dazzling, lightning-fast playing defined the band's sound, and its four long pieces, from the opening 'Medieval Overture' to the epic 'Sorceress' and the closing 'Majestic Dance', are full of the virtuosity and drama that made the band legendary. The album topped the jazz charts and crossed over to rock audiences, and its blend of classical structure and electric fire made it a landmark. It is the definitive statement of jazz fusion's golden age.

name: Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy
teaser: 1973 Return to Forever's electric debut: 'Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy', 'After the Cosmic Rain', and 'Space Circus' are cosmic fusion. The album marked the band's turn from acoustic to electric. It is a fusion landmark.

exploreAction.targetName: Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy (1973) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the energy — the album's fast, precise playing defines the genre. 'Space Circus' is a fan favorite.

synopsis: Return to Forever had spent their first two albums as an acoustic, avant-garde band, and this third record, released in 1973, marked their transformation into an electric powerhouse. The album's lineup, featuring guitarist Bill Connors and drummer Lenny White, was the first to feature the band's full electric sound, and its title track, an epic suite, and 'Space Circus' and 'After the Cosmic Rain' showed the new direction. The record's blend of classical forms, rock energy and jazz improvisation made it a landmark of fusion, and its title, a reference to the band's cosmic themes, captured its spirit. It is the album where Return to Forever became the band that would conquer the 70s.

name: Unchained
teaser: 1996 Johnny Cash's second album with Rick Rubin: 'Rusty Cage', 'Mean Eyed Cat', and 'Country Boy' feature Tom Petty's Heartbreakers. The album's cover showed Cash flipping the camera. It won a Grammy for Best Country Album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the covers — Cash transforms Soundgarden's 'Rusty Cage' and Beck's 'Rowboat'. The album is a masterclass in reinterpretation.

tracks.title: The One Rose (That's Left in My Heart)

synopsis: Johnny Cash had spent his American Recordings series rehabilitating his career, and this second album, released in 1996, continued the process. The record is a set of covers, chosen by Cash and producer Rick Rubin, of songs by artists as varied as Soundgarden, Beck and Tom Petty, and Cash's weathered voice transforms them all into something new, from the opening 'Rusty Cage', which turns a grunge song into a blues, to 'Mean Eyed Cat' and the haunting 'I Hung My Head'. The album won a Grammy and was hailed as the equal of its predecessor, and its blend of country, folk and rock showed a legend at home in every genre. It is the sound of an American icon reclaiming his voice.

name: Solitary Man
teaser: 2000 Johnny Cash's third album with Rick Rubin: 'Solitary Man', 'I Won't Back Down', and 'The Mercy Seat' are stark and defiant. The album was recorded as his health declined. It is a powerful statement of endurance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the defiance — Cash covers Neil Diamond and Tom Petty with authority. 'The Mercy Seat' is a Nick Cave cover.

tracks.title: That Lucky Old Sun (Just Rolls Around Heaven All Day)
Would You Lay with Me (In a Field of Stone)

synopsis: Johnny Cash had spent his late-career renaissance making acclaimed records with producer Rick Rubin, and this third American Recordings album, released in 2000, found him in a reflective mood. The record is built on Cash's own compositions and a few carefully chosen covers, from the title track, a Tom Petty song that became a signature, to 'I Won't Back Down' and the gospel-tinged 'Wayfaring Stranger'. Cash's voice, deeper and more weathered than ever, gives every song an autumnal weight, and the album's sparse, intimate production lets his performances shine. It was another critical and commercial success, and its title, a reference to the hermit's life, captured its mood of solitude. It is the sound of a legend facing his own mortality with grace.

name: The Man Comes Around
teaser: 2002 Johnny Cash's final album: 'Hurt', 'The Man Comes Around', and 'We'll Meet Again' are meditations on mortality. The album was released months before his death. 'Hurt', a Nine Inch Nails cover, became his greatest late performance.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Hurt' — the video and performance turned the song into a farewell. The album is a profound final statement.

tracks.title: First Time Ever I Saw Your Face
I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry

synopsis: Johnny Cash had spent his late career making the most acclaimed music of his life, and this fourth American Recordings album, released in 2002, was his final statement. The record's centerpiece is his version of 'Hurt', the Nine Inch Nails song, which he transformed into a devastating meditation on regret and mortality, and its video, filmed months before his death, became one of the most powerful in music history. The title track, 'The Man Comes Around', with its biblical imagery, and 'We'll Meet Again' and 'Bridge over Troubled Water' completed a record of extraordinary gravity. It was released shortly after his wife June Carter's death and months before his own, and its themes of loss and redemption gave it an unbearable weight. It is one of the greatest farewells in music history.

name: Unearthed
teaser: 2003 Johnny Cash's five-disc box set of unreleased American Recordings sessions: 'Long Black Veil', 'The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face', and 'Pocahontas' are raw and intimate. The set includes 60 tracks. It is a treasure trove.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the set covers gospel, country, and rock covers. 'Pocahontas' with Neil Young is a highlight.

tracks.title: Just the Other Side of Nowhere
The Fourth Man in the Fire
Down There by the Train (Alternate Take)
As Long as the Grass Shall Grow
Everybody's Trying to Be My Baby
Bird on a Wire (Live with Orchestra)
The L & N Don't Stop Here Anymore
Hard Times Come Again No More
When The Roll Is Called Up Yonder
If We Never Meet Again This Side of Heaven
Where the Soul of Man Never Dies
Let the Lower Lights Be Burning
When He Reached Down His Hand for Me
I'm Bound for the Promised Land
The One Rose (That's Left in My Heart)

synopsis: Johnny Cash had recorded hundreds of songs with producer Rick Rubin during his late-career renaissance, and this five-disc box set, released in 2003, gathered the best of what had not made the American Recordings albums. The collection is a treasure trove, full of covers and originals that show every side of Cash's genius, from the rollicking 'Big River' and 'Folsom Prison Blues' to the gospel 'I'm a Drifter' and duets with his wife June Carter and others. The set's centerpiece is a live disc recorded at Cash's home, and its intimacy is extraordinary. It is an essential document of the greatest late-career renaissance in music history, the sound of a legend working at full power until the very end.

name: American VI: Ain't No Grave
teaser: 2010 Johnny Cash's posthumous final album: 'Ain't No Grave', 'Redemption Day', and '1 Corinthians 15:55' are spiritual and defiant. The album was completed after his death. It is a fitting close to the American series.

exploreAction.targetName: American VI: Ain't No Grave (2010) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the faith — the album's gospel themes close his career. 'Ain't No Grave' is a powerful statement of belief.

tracks.title: Ain't No Grave (Gonna Hold This Body Down)
Can't Help But Wonder Where I'm Bound
Last Night I Had the Strangest Dream

synopsis: Johnny Cash had died in 2003, and this sixth American Recordings album, released in 2010, was assembled from the recordings he had made with producer Rick Rubin in his final years. The record's title track, 'Ain't No Grave', a gospel song about resurrection, was the last song Cash ever recorded, and its defiant chorus, sung by a man who knew he was dying, is one of the most powerful moments in his catalog. The album also contains 'Redemption Day' and 'I Corinthians 15:55', and its sparse, intimate production gives Cash's voice, ravaged but unbowed, the final word. It is a fitting epitaph for the Man in Black, the sound of a legend singing his way into the light.

name: I Want You
teaser: 1976 Marvin Gaye's album of longing: 'I Want You', 'After the Dance', and 'Since I Had You' are dreamy, layered, and hypnotic. The album's production by Leon Ware is luxurious. It is his most sensual work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the production — the album's arrangements are lush and detailed. 'After the Dance' is a classic.

tracks.title: I Wanna Be Where You Are
Soon I'll Be Loving You Again

synopsis: Marvin Gaye had spent his career as one of the most versatile singers in soul, and this album, released in 1976, was his most explicitly sensual record. The title track, with its hypnotic groove and Gaye's whispered, pleading vocals, is one of the greatest love songs ever recorded, and 'After the Dance' and 'Since I Had You' continue the mood of romantic obsession. The album was made during Gaye's troubled later period, with producer Leon Ware crafting the music, and its blend of funk, soul and eroticism made it a commercial success. It is the sound of a man consumed by desire, and its best moments are among the most beautiful in his catalog.

name: Here, My Dear
teaser: 1978 Marvin Gaye's double album about his divorce: 'Here, My Dear', 'When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You', and 'Anger' are painful, honest, and sprawling. The album's royalties went to his ex-wife. It is his most personal work.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the honesty — the album documents the end of a marriage in real time. It was a commercial failure that became a cult classic.

tracks.title: When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You
When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You (Instrumental)
You Can Leave, But It's Going to Cost You
When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You (Reprise)

synopsis: Marvin Gaye had spent 1976 making the sensual I Want You, and this follow-up, released in 1978, was its opposite: a double album about the end of his marriage, paid for by his ex-wife Anna Gordy as part of their divorce settlement. The record is a sprawling, brutally honest account of the relationship, from the tenderness of 'Here, My Dear' to the fury of 'When Did You Stop Loving Me, When Did I Stop Loving You' and the bittersweet 'Anna's Song'. It was dismissed on release as self-indulgent, but its reputation has grown enormously, and it is now regarded as one of the most personal albums ever made by a major artist. It is the sound of a man pouring his entire life into his music.

name: Midnight Love
teaser: 1982 Marvin Gaye's final album: 'Sexual Healing', 'Midnight Lady', and 'Third World Girl' blend funk, reggae, and electronics. 'Sexual Healing' became his biggest hit and won a Grammy. The album was his comeback before his death.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sexual Healing' — the song's groove and vocal performance made it an instant classic. The album is a bittersweet final chapter.

synopsis: Marvin Gaye had spent years in exile, living in Europe and struggling with addiction and tax problems, and this album, released in 1982, was his triumphant return. The record's centerpiece, 'Sexual Healing', with its synthesizers and Gaye's purring vocals, became the biggest hit of his career and won a Grammy, and its success returned him to the top of the charts after a decade of decline. The rest of the album, from 'Midnight Lady' to the funky 'Rockin' After Midnight', showed a singer reconnecting with his sensuality and his joy. It was his last great record; he was shot and killed by his father two years later. It is a bittersweet farewell from one of the greatest voices in soul.

name: Fulfillingness' First Finale
teaser: 1974 Stevie Wonder's fourth masterpiece in a row: 'Boogie On Reggae Woman', 'You Haven't Done Nothin'', and 'Heaven Is 10 Zillion Light Years Away' are funky and political. The album won Album of the Year at the Grammys.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the range — the album moves from reggae-funk to gentle ballads. 'You Haven't Done Nothin'' was a protest against Nixon.

tracks.title: Heaven Is 10 Zillion Light Years Away
They Won't Go When I Go

synopsis: Stevie Wonder had spent the early 70s in a creative explosion, releasing three masterpieces in a row, and this album, released in 1974, completed the run. The record's first side is full of the political and spiritual songs that had defined his recent work, from 'Smile Please' to the devastating 'You Haven't Done Nothin'', a furious attack on Richard Nixon that became his first number one in years, while its second side, including the gorgeous 'Heaven Is 10 Zillion Light Years Away' and the classic 'Boogie On Reggae Woman', shows his range. It won Album of the Year at the Grammys, and its blend of funk, soul and social commentary made it a landmark. It is the sound of a genius at the height of his powers.

name: Hotter than July
teaser: 1980 Stevie Wonder's most political album: 'Master Blaster (Jammin')', 'Happy Birthday', and 'All I Do' are joyful and committed. 'Happy Birthday' helped make Martin Luther King Jr. Day a national holiday. It is his best-selling album of the 80s.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the politics — the album campaigned for the King holiday. 'Master Blaster' is a reggae tribute to Bob Marley.

tracks.title: Did I Hear You Say You Love Me
I Ain't Gonna Stand for It
As If You Read My Mind

synopsis: Stevie Wonder had spent the 70s as the most acclaimed artist in popular music, and this album, released in 1980, was his most political and personal record of the decade's end. The record's centerpiece is 'Master Blaster (Jammin')', a tribute to Bob Marley and the music of Jamaica that became one of his biggest hits, and it also contains the anthemic 'Happy Birthday', a campaign to make Martin Luther King Jr.'s birthday a national holiday, and the gorgeous ballad 'Lately'. The album was a massive commercial success, and its blend of reggae, funk and soul showed Wonder at his most confident. It is the sound of a genius using his platform to change the world.

name: Music of My Mind
teaser: 1972 Stevie Wonder's first album of full artistic control: 'Superwoman (Where Were You When I Needed You)', 'I Love Every Little Thing About You', and 'Keep On Running' are experimental and personal. The album marked the beginning of his classic period.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the experimentation — the album was recorded with Wonder playing most instruments. It is the start of his golden run.

tracks.title: Superwoman (Where Were You When I Needed You)
I Love Every Little Thing About You

synopsis: Stevie Wonder had spent his career under the control of Motown, and this album, released in 1972, was the first he made with complete artistic freedom, after renegotiating his contract at age 21. The record is a stunning display of his talents, with Wonder playing nearly every instrument and using the synthesizers that would define his next decade, and its songs, from the epic 'Superwoman' to 'I Love Every Little Thing About You' and the beautiful 'Love Having You Around', show a young genius finding his voice. It sold modestly but laid the groundwork for the masterpieces that followed. It is the sound of an artist breaking free, and its importance to his career cannot be overstated.

name: Signed, Sealed & Delivered
teaser: 1970 Stevie Wonder's album with Motown's control loosening: 'Signed, Sealed, Delivered I'm Yours', 'Heaven Help Us All', and 'I Can't Help It' are catchy and heartfelt. The title track became his first pop hit in years. It is his last Motown-controlled album.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the title track — its energy and vocal power made it a classic. The album shows him straining toward independence.

synopsis: Stevie Wonder had spent the late 60s as Motown's most reliable hitmaker, and this album, released in 1970, found him beginning to take control of his music. The record's title track, a joyful celebration of love, became one of his signature songs, and 'Heaven Help Us All' and 'Never Had a Dream Come True' showed his growing sophistication as a writer. The album was recorded as Wonder, now 20, was negotiating for more artistic freedom from Motown, and its best songs point toward the genius that would fully emerge two years later. It is a transitional record, but its warmth and invention made it a fan favorite. It is the sound of a prodigy becoming a master.

name: For Once in My Life
teaser: 1968 Stevie Wonder's album of covers and originals: 'For Once in My Life', 'Shoo-Be-Doo-Be-Doo-Da-Day', and 'I Don't Know Why' are joyful and funky. The title track became his biggest hit. It is his most consistent album of the 60s.

exploreAction.targetName: For Once in My Life (1968) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to the funk — the album's horn arrangements are tight and swinging. 'For Once in My Life' is a Motown classic.
